Journals are append-only — never edited, never deleted — so CreatedDateUTC is a complete incremental watermark.
views.grain: one immutable statutory journal header per posted transaction event (JournalID)

views.label: linked transactions
views.description: The rebilling wiring: each row connects a purchase-side line — an ACCPAY bill line or a SPEND bank-transaction line — to the customer it is recoverable from and, once allocated, to the ACCREC invoice line that recharges it. There are NO amounts on this table; cost lives on the source line and recharge revenue on the target line, so every monetary question is a join. The source join is polymorphic on source_transaction_type_code (ACCPAY vs SPEND) — a single unconditional join silently drops half the links. 'Billable expenses not yet recovered' is status = 'APPROVED'.
views.grain: one billable-expense link from one source purchase line to (at most) one target sales invoice line

views.label: manual journal line tracking
views.description: Tracking pairs attached to manual journal document lines — at most two per line, mirroring the ledger convention. For POSTED journals the same pairs re-materialize on the statutory side in xero_journal_line_tracking; this table exists so drafts can be segmented before posting and so document-side audits reconcile.
views.grain: one tracking category/option pair per (manual journal, line position, tracking category)

views.label: manual journal lines
views.description: The debit/credit lines of manual journal documents. LineAmount is signed like the statutory ledger (debits positive, credits negative) but is a DOCUMENT amount whose tax treatment depends on the parent's LineAmountTypes — it is not automatically the statutory net. Use these lines to inspect drafts and per-line tracking before posting; once the parent is POSTED, the audited numbers live in xero_journal_lines. Lines have no vendor id, so the key is the parent id plus array position.
views.grain: one entry line per (manual journal, zero-based array position)

views.label: manual journals
views.description: Hand-keyed ledger adjustments — accruals, corrections, opening balances — as editable documents with a status lifecycle. Only POSTED manual journals reach the general ledger (where they reappear in xero_journals with source_type MANJOURNAL); DRAFT and ARCHIVED are staging states, and DELETED/VOIDED are dead but still returned by the API. This table's unique value over xero_journals is draft visibility, narration, and availability without the Advanced journals scope — it is NOT a second copy of the ledger to sum.
views.grain: one manual journal document per ManualJournalID

views.label: online invoices
views.description: Per-invoice fan-out from GET /Invoices/{InvoiceID}/OnlineInvoice: the public 'view your invoice online' link Xero hosts for sales invoices. Operational/engagement metadata, not a financial fact. Fetched lazily against the fan-out rate budget, so coverage is best-effort — absence of a row means not-yet-fetched at least as often as not-available.
views.grain: one online-invoice sharing URL per invoice

views.label: organisation actions
views.description: The org's capability/entitlement matrix from GET /Organisation/Actions: named features (e.g. 'UseMulticurrency', 'Payroll', 'AttachFiles') with an ALLOWED/NOT-ALLOWED verdict driven by plan, region and edition. This is the reference to consult BEFORE declaring a data gap: an empty multicurrency, payroll or attachments footprint under a NOT-ALLOWED action is a plan limitation, not a sync failure.
views.grain: one entitlement action per organisation per action name

views.label: organisation addresses
views.description: Normalized explode of Organisation.Addresses. Xero maintains at most one address per type per org, so (organisation_id, address_type) is the true key. POBOX is the postal/mailing address that documents display; STREET is the physical address. Rows are replaced wholesale with each parent refresh — an address cleared in Xero simply stops appearing.
views.grain: one address per organisation per address type (POBOX, STREET or DELIVERY)

views.label: organisation cis settings
views.description: UK Construction Industry Scheme posture per org, fetched by fan-out from GET /Organisation/{OrganisationID}/CISSettings: whether the org operates as CIS contractor and/or subcontractor, and the HMRC-verified deduction rate applied to subcontracted labour. Only meaningful for UK-version orgs — for everyone else the endpoint returns nothing, and absence of a row is the expected state, not a gap.
views.grain: one CIS configuration record per organisation

views.label: organisation external links
views.description: Normalized explode of Organisation.ExternalLinks — the org's website and social profiles (Facebook, Twitter, LinkedIn, GooglePlus, Website). Xero exposes no link id, so the key is a minted array ordinal and rows are replaced per parent on refresh. The array is present only once Organisation settings have been edited in Xero; most orgs have zero rows.
views.grain: one external profile link per organisation per array position

views.label: organisation payment terms
views.description: Normalized explode of Organisation.PaymentTerms: the org-level DEFAULT due-date rules for new sales invoices and new bills, one row per side. These are data-entry defaults three levels removed from reality — contact-level terms override them, and every document ultimately carries its own DueDate. Use this table to describe policy ('we invoice net 20'), never to compute lateness.
views.grain: one default payment-term rule per organisation per document side (SALES or BILLS)

views.label: organisation phones
views.description: Normalized explode of Organisation.Phones, which reuses the accounting API's shared Phone shape (the same object Contacts use, owned by contacts_dir). Xero maintains fixed type slots (DEFAULT, DDI, MOBILE, FAX, OFFICE) with at most one entry per type. A dialable number is the concatenation of country code + area code + number — no single column holds the full number.
views.grain: one phone entry per organisation per phone type slot

views.label: organisations
views.description: The legal-entity master record and the decoder ring for every number in the connector: exactly one row per connected tenant. base_currency is the currency all journal lines and base-converted totals resolve to; financial_year_end_day/month define the fiscal calendar every 'this year' question must respect; version and country_code decide regional semantics (which payroll region exists, what tax_number means). The record carries no UpdatedDateUTC, so the sync refreshes it wholesale and the table is current-state only — settings changes leave no history here. Filter is_demo_company before any cross-org rollup: Xero's demo company ships with realistic invoices that poison portfolio totals.
views.grain: one organisation profile per connected Xero tenant

views.label: overpayment allocations
views.description: The settlement edge between an overpayment and the invoices it pays down: each row moves a slice of excess-payment credit onto exactly one invoice on a given date. Like prepayment allocations these are cash-free settlements — the money moved when the overpayment happened, so allocation amounts must never join collections metrics. Rows are exploded from the parent's Allocations array, re-land wholesale when the parent changes, and carry no independent watermark.
views.grain: one application of overpayment credit to one invoice, keyed by parent overpayment and array position

views.label: overpayments
views.description: Credit created when someone paid MORE than was owed (or paid with nothing owed): Xero books the excess as an overpayment against the contact, to be allocated to invoices or refunded later. Like prepayments it is never revenue — the excess is a liability (customer side) or asset (supplier side) until consumed, and the underlying cash already lives in the bank transaction feed. Direction is carried by type (RECEIVE-*/AR* = customer overpaid you, SPEND-* = you overpaid a supplier); remaining_credit and applied_amount are current-state balances restated every sync.
views.grain: one overpayment credit document per OverpaymentID

views.label: payment services
views.description: Org-level configuration of 'Pay Now' services shown on Xero online invoices — the branded URL a customer clicks to pay. Pure reference data: no amounts, no events. It tells you what payment rails the org OFFERS, not what was used; actual receipts are still xero_payments rows regardless of which service collected them, and the service-to-branding-theme assignment that decides which invoices show which button is not exposed on this read surface.
views.grain: one custom online-payment service configuration per PaymentServiceID

views.label: payments
views.description: Cash application evidence: each row records money moving between a bank/clearing account and exactly one receivable or payable document. A payment is not revenue (that is the invoice line) and not cash in the bank (that is the bank transaction feed) — it is the allocation that connects them. Refunds of credit notes, prepayments and overpayments appear here too, as the six *CREDITPAYMENT/*PREPAYMENTPAYMENT/*OVERPAYMENTPAYMENT PaymentType values (no value literally contains 'REFUND'), so 'payments received' must filter both Status and PaymentType or refunds inflate collections. Batched payments also roll up into xero_batch_payments; count cash from exactly one of the two tables.
views.grain: one payment or refund applied against exactly one invoice, credit note, prepayment or overpayment

views.label: payroll au deduction types
views.description: The catalogue of deduction pay items (DeductionTypes family of GET /PayItems): what can be withheld from employees, and how each behaves against tax, super and W1. ReducesTax marks pre-tax (salary-packaging-style) deductions; DeductionCategory carries the STP classification for union fees and workplace giving. Retired types persist with current_record = false for historical joins.
views.grain: one deduction type pay item per org

views.label: payroll au earnings rates
views.description: The catalogue of earnings pay items (from the EarningsRates family of GET /PayItems): every kind of pay the org can put on a payslip, with its ATO classification. This dimension is what turns anonymous earnings lines into 'ordinary time vs overtime vs allowance vs ETP' — EarningsType is the classification the whole wage analysis hangs on. Retired items remain (current_record = false) so historical payslip lines keep their labels; never inner-filter them away in joins.
views.grain: one earnings rate pay item per org

views.label: payroll au employee bank accounts
views.description: Standing instructions for where an employee's net pay lands: fixed-amount splits plus exactly one remainder account. This is configuration, not money movement — actual paid amounts are on payslips and in the bank feed. Its analytical use is operational (how many employees split pay, disbursement audit), and it is dense with financial PII.
views.grain: one net-pay disbursement split per employee per position in the employee's BankAccounts array

views.label: payroll au employee home addresses
views.description: The employee's declared residential address, normalised out of the employee record. Its analytical job is state attribution — payroll tax and long-service-leave rules are state-based — but note it is where the employee lives, which is not necessarily where they work. Entirely PII apart from the state/postcode level of aggregation.
views.grain: one home address per employee (the employee's single declared HomeAddress)

views.label: payroll au employee leave balances
views.description: The employee's leave balances as reported by Xero at the moment of the last sync — the 'how much annual leave does everyone have' table. It is a snapshot, not a ledger: each ingest replaces the previous balance, and no history of accrual or consumption survives here (leave movements are on payslip leave lines). Units are whatever the leave type says (hours or days), so cross-type sums are only valid within one unit system.
views.grain: one current leave balance per employee per leave type

views.label: payroll au employee super memberships
views.description: The bridge between employees and superannuation funds: each row is one employee's membership of one fund, with the member number the fund knows them by. Pay-template and payslip super lines reference the membership, not the fund — so fund-level contribution questions route through this table.
views.grain: one super fund membership per SuperMembershipID (an employee's enrolment in one fund)

views.label: payroll au employee tax declarations
views.description: The employee's TFN declaration and PAYG withholding settings: residency, tax scale, threshold claim, study-loan flags and withholding variations. This drives how much tax each payslip withholds; it is settings, not amounts — actual tax withheld is on payslip tax lines. Contains the Tax File Number, the most sensitive datum in the connector: pii, never to be surfaced.
views.grain: one tax declaration per employee

views.label: payroll au employees
views.description: The worker dimension for Australian payroll: one row per person (or contractor) the organisation pays through Xero Payroll AU. Every payslip, leave balance, super membership and pay-template line hangs off this spine. Terminated employees are returned forever with Status=TERMINATED, so 'headcount' is a filtered question, never COUNT(*). Payroll is region-exclusive — a tenant runs AU or UK or NZ payroll, never two — so never union this with xero_payroll_uk_employees / xero_payroll_nz_employees; at most one of the three families has rows.
views.grain: one AU payroll employee per EmployeeID

views.label: payroll au leave applications
views.description: Leave requests as employees and admins entered them: one row per application for a span of a leave type, with the payroll processing broken into per-pay-period slices in xero_payroll_au_leave_periods. This is the intent record — whether the leave was actually processed (or rejected) lives on the period statuses, so absence metrics that count applications without checking periods count leave that never happened. Scanned via GET /LeaveApplications/v2, the current revision of the collection; the op exposes no status filter, so requested, scheduled and rejected leave all arrive together and must be separated downstream. A deleted application disappears from the collection outright — there is no cancelled status and no tombstone.
views.grain: one leave application per employee per requested leave span

views.label: payroll au leave periods
views.description: The payroll slicing of a leave application: Xero splits each request into one row per pay period it touches, each carrying the units of leave falling in that period and a processing status. This is where leave becomes quantified and real — PROCESSED rows have hit a posted payslip, SCHEDULED are approved future slices, REQUESTED await approval, REJECTED never happened. Every 'leave taken' number is a filtered SUM over this table.
views.grain: one leave period per leave application per pay period it spans

views.label: payroll au leave types
views.description: The catalogue of leave types (LeaveTypes family of GET /PayItems): each org-defined leave entitlement with its accrual quantum, unit of measure, statutory category and pay behaviour. LeaveCategoryCode is the cross-org normalizer — org-specific names like 'RDO bank' map onto statutory categories (ANNUALLEAVE, PERSONALSICKCARERSLEAVE, LONGSERVICELEAVE...). Joined from leave applications and payslip leave-accrual lines.
views.grain: one leave type pay item per org

views.label: payroll au opening balance deduction lines
views.description: Year-to-date deduction totals migrated at conversion, one row per deduction type. Amount is the meaningful field in this context; the shared DeductionLine shape's other fields are carried but typically null. Conversion-year only.
views.grain: one migrated YTD deduction amount per employee per position in the employee's OpeningBalances.DeductionLines array

views.label: payroll au opening balance earnings lines
views.description: Year-to-date earnings brought over from the previous payroll system at conversion, one row per earnings rate. In this context Xero populates the rate id and the YTD amount; the other EarningsLine fields are carried for shape-fidelity but are typically null. These amounts predate every Xero payslip — they are the missing left-hand side of conversion-year YTD reconciliations.
views.grain: one migrated YTD earnings amount per employee per position in the employee's OpeningBalances.EarningsLines array

views.label: payroll au opening balance leave lines
views.description: Leave balances carried over from the previous system at conversion: leave type plus units. These seed the running balances that xero_payroll_au_employee_leave_balances now reports — they are the historical starting point, not the current balance.
views.grain: one migrated leave-balance amount per employee per position in the employee's OpeningBalances.LeaveLines array

views.label: payroll au opening balance paid leave lines
views.description: STP2 disaggregation of migrated YTD earnings: leave actually paid in the prior system, split by leave type, with the leave-loading portions split by Super Guarantee treatment. Exists so conversion-year STP reporting can categorise paid leave correctly; only present on STP2-migrated employees.
views.grain: one migrated YTD paid-leave earnings amount per employee per position in the employee's OpeningBalances.PaidLeaveEarningsLines array

views.label: payroll au opening balance reimbursement lines
views.description: Year-to-date reimbursements migrated at conversion, one row per reimbursement type. Reimbursements are outside gross wages, so these rarely matter beyond completeness of conversion-year payment summaries.
views.grain: one migrated YTD reimbursement amount per employee per position in the employee's OpeningBalances.ReimbursementLines array

views.label: payroll au opening balance super lines
views.description: Year-to-date super contributions migrated at conversion, one row per membership/contribution type. Amount and contribution_type are the meaningful fields; remaining shared SuperLine fields are carried but typically null. Conversion-year only.
views.grain: one migrated YTD superannuation amount per employee per position in the employee's OpeningBalances.SuperLines array

views.label: payroll au opening balances
views.description: Conversion-time header for an employee migrated into Xero mid-payroll-year: the as-at date and the year-to-date PAYG tax brought across. The per-category YTD amounts live in the opening-balance line tables. These rows exist only for employees who were migrated with history; their absence means the employee's Xero payslips are the complete record. It is not pure reference data: tax is the migrated PAYG measure, additive across employees inside the conversion year and meaningless outside it.
views.grain: one opening-balance header per employee

views.label: payroll au pay runs
views.description: The header of every AU payroll processing event: each row is one run of one payroll calendar over one period, carrying org-level totals (Wages, Deductions, Tax, Super, Reimbursement, NetPay) that Xero computes by summing the run's payslips. DRAFT runs are visible work-in-progress that will change or vanish; only POSTED runs are payroll that actually happened. The embedded payslip roster (PayslipSummary array) is exploded to xero_payroll_au_payslips via the per-payslip fan-out and also kept verbatim here as payslip_summaries. All amounts are AUD — AU payroll has no multi-currency dimension. Deletion is a disappearance rather than a tombstone: PayRunStatus carries only DRAFT and POSTED, so a run deleted in Xero simply stops being returned.
views.grain: one pay run, keyed by PayRunID — one processing of one payroll calendar over one pay period

views.label: payroll au pay template deduction lines
views.description: Recurring deductions configured on the employee's pay template — union fees, child support, salary-packaging and the like — with their calculation basis. Template configuration only: the money actually deducted each pay is on payslip deduction lines. PRETAX vs POSTTAX matters: pre-tax deductions reduce taxable income, post-tax do not.
views.grain: one standing deduction instruction per employee per position in the employee's PayTemplate.DeductionLines array

views.label: payroll au pay template earnings lines
views.description: The employee's recurring earnings setup: which earnings rates apply and how they are calculated (annual salary, entered rate, or the rate's own default). This is the template copied onto each new payslip — expected pay, not actual pay. Actual earnings are payslip earnings lines in the payroll processing domain; use this table for salary-book, FTE and pay-structure questions, not for cost incurred.
views.grain: one standing earnings instruction per employee per position in the employee's PayTemplate.EarningsLines array

views.label: payroll au pay template leave lines
views.description: How each leave type accrues for this employee: the calculation method, annual entitlement units, termination payout treatment and whether the accrual counts as qualifying earnings for super guarantee. This is entitlement configuration — accrued balances live in xero_payroll_au_employee_leave_balances and leave actually taken is on payslip leave lines.
views.grain: one standing leave-accrual instruction per employee per position in the employee's PayTemplate.LeaveLines array

views.label: payroll au pay template reimbursement lines
views.description: Recurring reimbursements on the employee's pay template (e.g. a fixed phone allowance repaid through payroll). Reimbursements are not earnings: they are tax-free repayments of employee outlay and are excluded from gross wages, PAYG and super. Template only — actual reimbursed amounts are on payslip reimbursement lines.
views.grain: one standing reimbursement instruction per employee per position in the employee's PayTemplate.ReimbursementLines array

views.label: payroll au pay template super lines
views.description: Recurring super contributions configured per employee: the statutory SGC line plus any salary-sacrifice, employer-additional or employee-voluntary lines, each pointing at a super membership and the GL accounts it posts to. Configuration, not contributions — amounts actually accrued each pay are on payslip super lines. The contribution_type split is the compliance axis: SGC is the employer's legal obligation; SALARYSACRIFICE reduces the employee's taxable income.
views.grain: one standing superannuation instruction per employee per position in the employee's PayTemplate.SuperLines array

views.label: payroll au payroll calendars
views.description: The org's pay schedules: each row defines a frequency (WEEKLY, FORTNIGHTLY, MONTHLY...) that pay runs are generated from and employees are assigned to. Small reference set. StartDate and PaymentDate describe the UPCOMING period and roll forward every time a run posts — they are 'next period' pointers, not history; historical periods live on the pay runs themselves.
views.grain: one pay schedule, keyed by PayrollCalendarID — an org can define several calendars of the same frequency, so calendar_type is not a key

views.label: payroll au payslip deduction lines
views.description: Employee-side deductions withheld on a payslip (union fees, workplace giving, purchase plans...), exploded from Payslip.DeductionLines. Amounts are positive magnitudes subtracted from gross on the way to net pay — money the employer holds and remits elsewhere, never an employer cost. Join xero_payroll_au_deduction_types for the deduction's name and its pre-tax/W1 treatment.
views.grain: one deduction line per payslip per position in the payslip's DeductionLines array

views.label: payroll au payslip earnings lines
views.description: The wage detail of a payslip: one row per earnings rate applied (ordinary time, overtime, allowances, bonuses...), exploded from Payslip.EarningsLines. This is the table for 'overtime spend', 'allowance cost by type' or hourly-vs-salary splits — join xero_payroll_au_earnings_rates for the rate's EarningsType classification. Salaried employees typically show a single ANNUALSALARY-calculated line; hourly staff show units x rate. Timesheet-generated and leave-generated earnings live in sibling tables, so this table alone understates gross wages.
views.grain: one earnings line per payslip per position in the payslip's EarningsLines array

views.label: payroll au payslip leave accrual lines
views.description: Leave EARNED in the period: each row records units of a leave type accrued on one payslip, exploded from Payslip.LeaveAccrualLines. This is the flow side of leave — accruals in, leave-earnings out — not a balance. Xero does not expose a per-payslip leave balance here; balances live on the employee record in the payroll employees domain, and summing accruals alone reconstructs only the credit side.
views.grain: one leave accrual line per payslip per position in the payslip's LeaveAccrualLines array

views.label: payroll au payslip leave earnings lines
views.description: Wages paid for leave taken (or cashed out) in the period, exploded from Payslip.LeaveEarningsLines. Each row prices leave units at an earnings rate; PayOutType distinguishes leave actually taken from balances cashed out, which behave differently for leave-liability and for headline 'time off' questions. These amounts are already inside the payslip's Wages total.
views.grain: one leave earnings line per payslip per position in the payslip's LeaveEarningsLines array

views.label: payroll au payslip reimbursement lines
views.description: Expense money returned to employees through payroll, exploded from Payslip.ReimbursementLines. Reimbursements ride the payslip but are not remuneration: no PAYG, no super, excluded from W1. They belong in cash-out and expense analyses, never in wage-cost or average-pay figures.
views.grain: one reimbursement line per payslip per position in the payslip's ReimbursementLines array

views.label: payroll au payslip superannuation lines
views.description: The superannuation detail of a payslip, exploded from Payslip.SuperannuationLines: each row is one contribution instruction, pairing a super fund membership with a contribution type. The same membership and type can appear on more than one line, which is why the row key is the array ordinal rather than that pairing. ContributionType is the load-bearing split — SGC and EMPLOYERADDITIONAL are employer-funded cost on top of wages, while SALARYSACRIFICE and EMPLOYEE come out of the employee's gross. Every 'super liability', 'SGC compliance' or 'employer cost' number starts by filtering this column; the payslip's Super total mixes all four.
views.grain: one superannuation line per payslip per position in the payslip's SuperannuationLines array

views.label: payroll au payslip tax lines
views.description: PAYG withholding detail per payslip, exploded from Payslip.TaxLines. Most payslips carry one automatic PAYG line; extra or overridden lines appear for ETPs and schedule-based manual tax (ManualTaxType names which schedule). Amounts are withheld from the employee and owed to the ATO — a liability in transit, not an employer expense. This is the reconciliation table for W2/BAS PAYG figures.
views.grain: one PAYG tax line per payslip per position in the payslip's TaxLines array

views.label: payroll au payslip timesheet earnings lines
views.description: Earnings lines that Xero generated from approved timesheets when the pay run was created, exploded from Payslip.TimesheetEarningsLines (same EarningsLine shape as the manual earnings table). Kept separate because it answers a different question: how much of the wage bill was driven by timesheets versus standing pay templates. Employees paid purely on salary never appear here.
views.grain: one timesheet-generated earnings line per payslip per position in the payslip's TimesheetEarningsLines array

views.label: payroll au payslips
views.description: The employee-level slice of a pay run: each row is one employee's pay for one run, with totals (Wages, Deductions, Tax, Super, Reimbursements, NetPay) that Xero derives from the typed line families exploded into the xero_payroll_au_payslip_* tables. Rows are fetched one-by-one via GET /Payslip/{PayslipID} using the ids from the parent run's roster. A payslip has no status of its own — it is as real as its run, so every aggregate must join xero_payroll_au_pay_runs and filter POSTED.
views.grain: one payslip per employee per pay run

views.label: payroll au reimbursement types
views.description: The catalogue of reimbursement pay items (ReimbursementTypes family of GET /PayItems): the categories of expense money an org repays through payroll, each mapped to a GL expense account. A small reference dimension joined from payslip reimbursement lines; retired types persist with current_record = false.
views.grain: one reimbursement type pay item per org

views.label: payroll au settings
views.description: Org-wide AU payroll configuration: the payroll year's day count, STP Phase 2 enablement, and which tracking categories classify employees and timesheets. Singleton per tenant. The GL account wiring inside Settings is normalised into xero_payroll_au_settings_accounts.
views.grain: one payroll settings record per organisation (the endpoint returns exactly one)

views.label: payroll au settings accounts
views.description: The GL accounts AU payroll posts to — the wiring between payroll and the general ledger: wages expense, wages payable, PAYG liability, super expense and super liability. The payroll-specific Type values are the roles; join to xero_accounts for the full chart-of-accounts context. This is where 'which GL account holds unpaid super' resolves.
views.grain: one payroll control-account wiring entry per settings singleton per AccountID + Type in Settings.Accounts

views.label: payroll au super fund products
views.description: Reference catalogue of APRA-regulated super fund products, fetched by looking up the ABN/USI of funds the organisation uses. It exists to give regulated funds their official product name and to validate USIs — it is industry reference data, not tenant data, and carries no amounts.
views.grain: one regulated super fund product per ABN + USI

views.label: payroll au super funds
views.description: The organisation's registry of destination super funds: APRA-regulated funds (identified by USI) and self-managed funds (SMSF, identified by ABN plus their own bank details). The two types populate disjoint field sets — treat Type as a schema switch. Employees connect here via super memberships; contribution amounts never live on this table.
views.grain: one superannuation fund per SuperFundID registered in the organisation's payroll

views.label: payroll au timesheet lines
views.description: The per-rate detail of a timesheet: each line books hours against one earnings rate, optionally tagged to a tracking option for cost-centre attribution. NumberOfUnits is NOT a scalar — it is an ARRAY with one element per day of the timesheet period, in day order starting at the timesheet's StartDate, stored here as jsonb. Daily and per-line hour analysis expands the array; the parent timesheet's Hours column is the pre-summed shortcut.
views.grain: one timesheet line per timesheet per position in its TimesheetLines array — a line pairs one earnings rate with one optional tracking option, but the same pairing can legitimately appear twice, so the ordinal is what makes the key

views.label: payroll au timesheets
views.description: Hours as entered: one timesheet record per employee per period, with a total Hours figure and per-rate daily detail in xero_payroll_au_timesheet_lines. Status is the trust boundary — DRAFT and REQUESTED are unvetted claims, APPROVED is signed off, PROCESSED has been consumed by a posted pay run, REJECTED was refused — and it is also what keeps the grain honest, since a rejected submission and the corrected resubmission both survive for the same employee and period. Hours only become wages when a run picks the timesheet up, at which point they surface as TimesheetEarningsLines on payslips. Deletion is a disappearance, not a status: TimesheetStatus has no DELETED value, so a removed timesheet simply stops being returned and only a full identity scan retires the staged row.
views.grain: one timesheet record, keyed by TimesheetID — normally one per employee per period, but employee + period is NOT a key because a refused or superseded submission persists alongside its replacement

views.label: payroll nz deductions
views.description: The org's catalogue of voluntary deduction types (payroll giving, KiwiSaver voluntary contributions, superannuation top-ups, other) and the liability account each posts to. Definitions only: amounts actually deducted from pay are payslip deduction lines in the pay-run domain. Note the category overlap trap: KiwiSaverVoluntaryContributions here is EXTRA voluntary saving — the standard employee KiwiSaver deduction is a statutory deduction, not this.
views.grain: one org-level deduction pay item per deduction id

views.label: payroll nz earnings rates
views.description: The org's catalogue of ways people can be paid: ordinary earnings, overtime multipliers, allowances, bonuses, holiday pay and the rest, each with its calculation mechanics (rate-per-unit, multiple-of-ordinary, fixed) and the GL expense account it posts to. Every timesheet line, salary record, pay-template line and payslip earnings line points here — it is the decoding dimension for all NZ earnings analysis. Definitions only; earned dollars live on payslips.
views.grain: one org-level earnings rate (pay item) per earnings rate id

views.label: payroll nz employee bank accounts
views.description: The bank accounts an electronically-paid employee's net pay is split into, with the split rule per account: a FixedAmount account takes dollar_amount each pay and the Balance account absorbs the remainder. Highly sensitive PII (account numbers). dollar_amount is a per-pay split INSTRUCTION, not money that has moved — summing it across employees estimates configured splits, not actual payroll cash.
views.grain: one wage-destination bank account per employee, keyed by employee and array position

views.label: payroll nz employee leave
views.description: Leave events: each row is one employee's request to take a specific leave type over a start/end date span. The per-pay-period splits, unit counts and approval status live in xero_payroll_nz_employee_leave_periods — this header has NO units column, so 'days of leave taken' must come from the periods table, never from counting header rows or date arithmetic on the span (which counts weekends and part-days wrongly). The canonical workforce_leave fact is sourced from the periods table for exactly that reason; treating this header as a second source of the same concept counts every request twice at a grain that carries no quantity.
views.grain: one leave request (a dated span of one leave type) per employee

views.label: payroll nz employee leave balances
views.description: Point-in-time leave balances: how many units of each leave type each employee holds as of the last sync. A snapshot, not a ledger — Xero returns only the current value, so there is no balance history and summing across syncs or time double-counts. Balances can be negative (leave taken in advance).
views.grain: one current leave balance per employee per leave type

views.label: payroll nz employee leave periods
views.description: The quantity-bearing grain of leave: each leave request is split into the pay periods it touches, with units scheduled (number_of_units) and units actually taken (number_of_units_taken) plus the period's approval status. This is THE table for 'how much leave' questions. Statuses matter: Estimated periods are forecasts that a pay run has not confirmed; only Approved/Completed periods represent real leave.
views.grain: one pay-period slice of one leave request, keyed by leave request and array position

views.label: payroll nz employee leave types
views.description: The per-employee accrual contract for each leave type the employee is enrolled in: how it accrues, at what annual quantity, caps, opening balance and NZ-specific holiday-pay flags. This is configuration, not consumption — actual leave taken is in leave periods and current balances in leave balances. The same leave_type_id appears for many employees with DIFFERENT accrual values, which is exactly why this table exists separately from the org-level xero_payroll_nz_leave_types.
views.grain: one leave-type assignment (with its accrual configuration) per employee per leave type

views.label: payroll nz employee opening balances
views.description: Pre-Xero earnings history typed in at migration so NZ Holidays Act calculations (ordinary weekly pay, average weekly earnings) are correct from the org's first Xero pay run. Each row is one prior pay period's gross earnings with the days paid and unpaid weeks that period contributes to the divisor. It describes the time BEFORE the org used Xero payroll, so it is disjoint from payslip earnings rather than overlapping them: unioning the two does not double count, it silently changes the basis of a 'total earnings' answer from 'calculated and paid through Xero' to 'partly unaudited figures a human keyed in at go-live'. Report the two series separately and label which is which.
views.grain: one historical pay-period opening-balance line per employee, keyed by employee and array position

views.label: payroll nz employee pay template earnings
views.description: The employee's standing pay template: the earnings lines Xero pre-loads into each new pay run draft (e.g. 40 ordinary hours at $X, plus a standing allowance). Template lines are defaults, not payments — a pay run can override or remove them, so 'what someone was paid' comes from payslips while 'what someone is set up to be paid' comes from here and from xero_payroll_nz_salary_and_wages.
views.grain: one earnings template line per employee pay template, keyed by its payTemplateEarningID

views.label: payroll nz employee payment methods
views.description: How the employee is paid: Electronically (bank transfer), Cheque or Manual. The bank accounts the money splits into are exploded to xero_payroll_nz_employee_bank_accounts. Pure configuration — no amounts flow through this table; actual wage payments are pay-run artifacts in the payroll pay-run domain.
views.grain: one payment-method record per employee

views.label: payroll nz employee tax
views.description: The employee's IRD tax settings and KiwiSaver membership: tax code, special rates, student loan position and contribution percentages. This is the employee-side view of KiwiSaver (membership status and rates); the org-side scheme definitions live in xero_payroll_nz_superannuations and the deduction categories in xero_payroll_nz_statutory_deductions — do not sum or double-count across the three, none of them is a paid amount. Xero returns only the current record: changes overwrite in place, so there is no tax-code history here.
views.grain: one current tax configuration record per employee

views.label: payroll nz employee working patterns
views.description: Header of an employee's regular-week working pattern, effective from a date; the actual hours-per-weekday grid lives in xero_payroll_nz_employee_working_weeks. Patterns are effective-dated like salaries: the pattern in force at date D is the one with the greatest effective_from <= D per employee. Only employees whose salary record uses work_pattern_type RegularWeek have meaningful patterns.
views.grain: one effective-dated working pattern per employee

views.label: payroll nz employee working weeks
views.description: The hours grid of a working pattern: hours to be worked on each weekday. A pattern can repeat over multiple weeks (alternating rosters), hence one row per week in the cycle. Contracted hours, not hours worked — actuals come from timesheets; comparing this grid with timesheet lines finds overtime and under-utilization.
views.grain: one week of a working pattern's repeating cycle, keyed by pattern and array position

views.label: payroll nz employees
views.description: The worker master for NZ Payroll v2: identity, home address, employment dates and the payroll calendar the person is paid on. This is heavy-PII reference data — names, DOB, address, contact details — not a fact table. Employment status is inferred, not declared: an employee with a null end_date is current; a populated end_date is a termination effective that day. A tenant has AU or UK or NZ payroll, never two — if this table is empty the org simply doesn't run NZ payroll, and no cross-region union with xero_payroll_au_employees/xero_payroll_uk_employees is ever valid.
views.grain: one employee record per person employed under the tenant's NZ payroll

views.label: payroll nz leave types
views.description: The org's leave-type catalogue: annual, sick, bereavement, public holidays, unpaid and custom types, with whether they are paid and how their units are expressed. The org-wide definition — per-employee accrual quantities live in xero_payroll_nz_employee_leave_types, and this table's typeOfUnits is the decoding key for all leave-unit aggregation.
views.grain: one org-level leave type per leave type id

views.label: payroll nz pay run calendars
views.description: The org's pay cycles: frequency (weekly through annual), the CURRENT period's start/end and the payment date. Every employee is attached to exactly one calendar, and pay runs are generated per calendar per period. The period dates roll forward as runs are posted — they describe the next/current period, not a fixed anchor, so period math for history must come from pay runs themselves.
views.grain: one pay-run calendar (pay frequency definition) per payroll calendar id

views.label: payroll nz pay runs
views.description: The header record for every time NZ payroll was (or is being) processed, and the ONLY place this domain carries dates and a posting status. totalCost is Xero's own employer-cost figure for the run and totalPay is the net cash that reaches employees; they answer different questions and differ by every withholding and employer-side contribution, so never present one as the other. Draft runs are returned by the API alongside Posted ones and their numbers change until posting, so every payroll total must filter pay_run_status = 'Posted'. NZ payroll runs entirely in NZD: there are no currency or rate columns anywhere in this domain, and none are needed. These tables are populated only for tenants whose payroll region is NZ.
views.grain: one NZ pay run — a single processing (scheduled, unscheduled, or earlier-year-update) of one payroll calendar period

views.label: payroll nz payslip deduction lines
views.description: Non-statutory deductions withheld from pay: payroll giving, social club, union fees, employee super top-ups beyond KiwiSaver minima. Rolls up to PaySlip.totalDeductions. Statutory withholdings (student loan, child support, employee KiwiSaver) are NOT here — they live in the statutory-deduction-lines table — so 'everything withheld from staff' must union both families.
views.grain: one voluntary/contractual deduction line on one payslip (position within PaySlip.deductionLines)

views.label: payroll nz payslip earnings lines
views.description: Ordinary (non-leave, non-timesheet) earnings detail: salary, ordinary hours, allowances, bonuses — one row per earnings rate applied on the payslip. amount is the authoritative paid figure; ratePerUnit × numberOfUnits does not always reproduce it (rounding, average-daily-pay substitution, fixed-amount rates), so aggregate amount and treat rate/units as explanatory. This family alone is NOT gross pay — leave and timesheet earnings live in their sibling tables and the three partition PaySlip.grossEarnings.
views.grain: one ordinary earnings line on one payslip (position within PaySlip.earningsLines)

views.label: payroll nz payslip employee tax lines
views.description: Tax withheld FROM the employee — PAYE under the payslip's tax code — one row per tax component, rolling up to PaySlip.totalEmployeeTaxes. The sibling employer-tax table shares the identical TaxLine shape but means money the EMPLOYER owes on top of pay; the two tables must never be unioned into a single 'tax' number without labelling direction.
views.grain: one employee-side tax line on one payslip (position within PaySlip.employeeTaxLines)

views.label: payroll nz payslip employer tax lines
views.description: Tax the EMPLOYER owes on top of pay — in NZ practice, ESCT on employer superannuation contributions — one row per component, rolling up to PaySlip.totalEmployerTaxes. Identical TaxLine shape to the employee-tax table but opposite direction: these amounts never touch the employee's net pay, and they belong in employer-cost analysis (gross + employer taxes + employer super).
views.grain: one employer-side tax line on one payslip (position within PaySlip.employerTaxLines)

views.label: payroll nz payslip leave accrual lines
views.description: Leave ENTITLEMENT EARNED this pay period, per leave type — the accrual side of leave, with no dollar amounts. Units are whatever the leave type is configured in (NZ annual leave is commonly tracked in weeks or hours, sick leave in days or hours), so units must never be summed across leave types. This table is a period-by-period movement, not a balance: current leave balances live on the employee record in the NZ payroll employees domain, and summing accruals without subtracting leave taken does not produce a balance.
views.grain: one leave accrual line on one payslip — units of one leave type accrued in one pay period (position within PaySlip.leaveAccrualLines)

views.label: payroll nz payslip leave earnings lines
views.description: Pay for leave TAKEN in the period — annual leave, sick leave, public holidays — one row per leave earnings rate on the payslip. This is the money side of leave; the units-accrued side is xero_payroll_nz_payslip_leave_accrual_lines and the two must not be conflated. Amounts here are already inside PaySlip.grossEarnings: leave pay is a composition slice of gross, never an addition to it.
views.grain: one leave earnings line on one payslip (position within PaySlip.leaveEarningsLines)

views.label: payroll nz payslip payment lines
views.description: How the payslip's NET pay was distributed to bank accounts — one row per destination account, summing to PaySlip.totalPay. Purely a cash-distribution breakdown: no earnings semantics at all, and the row carries raw bank account details, making this the most PII-sensitive table in the domain. Use it to reconcile payroll against the bank feed and to detect split-pay arrangements.
views.grain: one bank payment split of one payslip's net pay (position within PaySlip.paymentLines)

views.label: payroll nz payslip reimbursement lines
views.description: Non-taxable repayments of employee out-of-pocket expenses, paid through payroll and rolled up to PaySlip.totalReimbursements. Added to net pay AFTER tax — reimbursements are part of cash paid to employees but are neither earnings nor labour cost; leaving them in average-pay or wage-cost analysis inflates both.
views.grain: one reimbursement line on one payslip (position within PaySlip.reimbursementLines)

views.label: payroll nz payslip statutory deduction lines
views.description: Withholdings required by law, deducted from the employee's pay and rolled up to PaySlip.totalStatutoryDeductions: student loan repayments, child support, employee KiwiSaver contributions. Legally distinct from voluntary deductions and kept in a separate family by Xero — 'all deductions from pay' is this table plus the deduction-lines table. Amounts reduce net pay but are NOT tax lines, even though most are remitted to IRD.
views.grain: one statutory deduction line on one payslip (position within PaySlip.statutoryDeductionLines)

views.label: payroll nz payslip superannuation lines
views.description: EMPLOYER superannuation contributions per payslip — in NZ practice, employer KiwiSaver — rolling up to PaySlip.totalSuperannuation. This is an employer cost on top of gross pay: the employee's own KiwiSaver contribution is a statutory deduction, and ESCT on these contributions sits in the employer tax lines. Treating these amounts as withheld from the employee misstates both take-home and cost.
views.grain: one superannuation line on one payslip (position within PaySlip.superannuationLines)

views.label: payroll nz payslip timesheet earnings lines
views.description: Earnings generated from approved timesheets — the third and final slice of gross pay alongside ordinary and leave earnings. For hourly workforces this family, not earningsLines, is where most wages appear; 'wages by hours worked' questions sum number_of_units and amount here. Amounts are already inside PaySlip.grossEarnings.
views.grain: one timesheet-sourced earnings line on one payslip (position within PaySlip.timesheetEarningsLines)

views.label: payroll nz payslips
views.description: The employee-level payroll fact: every totals column here is the roll-up of one typed line family below it. Take-home is expected to reconcile as total_pay = gross_earnings − total_employee_taxes − total_deductions − total_statutory_deductions + total_reimbursements, and employer-side amounts (total_employer_taxes, total_superannuation) sit outside take-home entirely. Validate that identity on a sample payslip before publishing anything built on it — the spec's wording for totalDeductions is loose enough to read as an aggregate, and a tenant where it already contains statutory withholdings would make 'all deductions = both columns' double-count. totalEarnings and grossEarnings are the same number for NZ (the spec says so) — never add them. This row carries NO dates and NO status: join xero_payroll_nz_pay_runs for both, and filter pay_run_status = 'Posted' on every aggregate. TaxSettings and GrossEarningsHistory (single nested objects, not arrays) are flattened onto this row.
views.grain: one payslip — one employee's pay within one pay run

views.label: payroll nz reimbursements
views.description: Catalogue of expense-reimbursement pay items (mileage, tools, phone...) paid through payroll, with GST treatment and calculation mechanics. Reimbursements are repayments of employee outlay, not remuneration: exclude them from earnings, tax and KiwiSaver bases in any wage analysis. Amounts actually reimbursed are payslip reimbursement lines.
views.grain: one org-level reimbursement type per reimbursement id

views.label: payroll nz salary and wages
views.description: The employee's base-pay history: each row is a salary/hourly arrangement effective from a date, with status Active (current), Pending (future-dated) or History (superseded). This is the table for 'what is X's salary' and for pay-rise analysis, and it is semi-additive — annual_salary adds up across PEOPLE at one moment to give a wage bill, but adding it across an employee's successive arrangements sums every raise they ever received into the total. Every current-pay query therefore reduces to one row per employee first.
views.grain: one effective-dated salary or wage arrangement per employee, identified by its salaryAndWagesID

views.label: payroll nz settings accounts
views.description: The org's payroll posting map: which GL accounts NZ payroll posts PAYE liabilities, wages payable, wage expense and the payroll bank account to. Rows are payroll ROLES pointing at GL accounts — the role (type) is the key, because nothing stops an org pointing two roles at the same GL account, so account_id alone does not guarantee uniqueness. This is plumbing for reconciling payroll to the ledger — the account master itself is xero_accounts in ledger_config.
views.grain: one payroll posting role (PAYE liability, wages payable, wages expense, payroll bank) per tenant

views.label: payroll nz statutory deductions
views.description: Legally-mandated deduction types the org can process: attachment/earnings orders (court fines, child support, MSD repayments, IR arrears), student loan variants and KiwiSaver. These are employer obligations triggered by government notice, unlike the voluntary types in xero_payroll_nz_deductions. Definitions and GL routing only — deducted amounts are payslip lines.
views.grain: one org-level statutory deduction type per id

views.label: payroll nz superannuations
views.description: Employer superannuation schemes the org contributes to: KiwiSaver, complying funds and other schemes, with the calculation rule (fixed amount vs percentage of taxable earnings), default rates, employer cap and the two GL accounts (expense for the employer cost, liability until remitted). The spec models these records with an object literally named 'Benefit' while the endpoint and envelope are Superannuations, so every column below cites payroll_nz:Benefit.* for a table nothing in the payload calls a benefit — that mismatch is spec naming, not a design error. Scheme definitions only: contributed dollars are payslip superannuation lines.
views.grain: one org-level superannuation benefit scheme per id

views.label: payroll nz timesheet lines
views.description: The atomic worked-time fact for NZ payroll: date, earnings rate, optional tracking category option and units (hours). This is the grain for daily-hours, overtime and labour-allocation analysis; roll up to the timesheet for period totals. Status lives on the parent — every aggregate over lines must join the header and filter its status, or draft hours pollute actuals.
views.grain: one day's units against one earnings rate (and optional tracking item) within one timesheet

views.label: payroll nz timesheets
views.description: Header of an employee's timesheet for one pay-calendar period, with lifecycle status and Xero's own totalHours rollup. The employee+period pair is NOT unique — a resubmission creates a second timesheet over the same window, so only timesheetID is the key and period totals must not blindly sum duplicate windows. Hours-by-day detail is in xero_payroll_nz_timesheet_lines. Status is the truth filter: Draft and Requested timesheets are unconfirmed, Approved is ready for payroll, Completed has been consumed by a posted pay run — 'hours worked' analysis over all statuses counts unapproved and possibly abandoned drafts.
views.grain: one submitted timesheet document, identified by timesheetID — an employee can hold more than one covering the same pay-calendar period when a timesheet is resubmitted

views.label: payroll nz tracking categories
views.description: Singleton configuration naming which of the org's two accounting tracking categories payroll uses: one to group employees (cost-center reporting of wages) and one to tag timesheet lines (labour allocation). The ids point at xero_tracking_categories in ledger_config; their options are what timesheet_lines.tracking_item_id values belong to. Both ids null means payroll tracking is off and labour-allocation questions are unanswerable from tracking.
views.grain: one payroll tracking-category configuration record per tenant

views.label: payroll uk benefits
views.description: Org-level employer benefit definitions — in the UK API these are overwhelmingly employer PENSION schemes (the spec literally describes the fields as 'the employer pension'). Each row defines how the employer contribution is computed (fixed vs percentage of gross, qualifying-earnings basis) and which GL accounts it posts to. This is the catalogue; amounts actually contributed per employee per period are payslip benefit lines in the pay-run domain.
views.grain: one employer benefit (pension) pay item per benefit id

views.label: payroll uk deductions
views.description: Org-level deduction definitions: employee pension contributions, salary sacrifice, student/postgraduate loan items, childcare vouchers, court-order style repayments and other before/after-tax deductions. Rows are the catalogue and calculation rules; amounts actually deducted are payslip deduction lines in the pay-run domain. The subject-to flags decide whether a deduction reduces taxable/NIC-able gross — the essence of salary-sacrifice economics.
views.grain: one deduction pay item per deductionId

views.label: payroll uk earnings orders
views.description: Org-level attachment/earnings-order definitions — court-mandated deductions (child support, court fines, creditor orders) applied to employees' pay. The enum is shared across Xero's regions, so NZ/US values (KiwiSaver, USChildSupport) appear as legal enum members but never occur in UK data. Amounts actually withheld are payslip lines in the pay-run domain; this table exists to classify them.
views.grain: one attachment-of-earnings order pay item per earnings order id

views.label: payroll uk earnings rates
views.description: The org's catalogue of ways people earn: regular pay, overtime, bonuses, commission, tips, termination pay and the full family of statutory pay types (SSP, SMP, SPP...). Every earnings line on every payslip and timesheet references one of these, making this the classification dimension for gross-pay composition. rate_type gates which of the three rate fields applies — reading the wrong one produces nonsense rates.
views.grain: one earnings rate pay item per earningsRateID

views.label: payroll uk employee bank accounts
views.description: The bank accounts an electronically-paid employee's net pay is sent to. More than one row per employee means the net pay is split across accounts — but the payload carries only the account identity (name, number, sort code) and NO amount or percentage per account, so how the split divides is not derivable here: the count of accounts is the only fact this table supports. Every column is sensitive financial PII (UK sort code + account number); this table exists for completeness and payment-ops questions, not for analytics, and should never be surfaced without an explicit request.
views.grain: one net-pay destination bank account per employee per array position

views.label: payroll uk employee contracts
views.description: The authoritative employment-episode history: each row is a contract (full/part-time/zero-hour, employee vs worker status, fixed-term window, optional apprenticeship). This — not the flat start/end dates on the employee row — is what re-hires, FTE mix and contract-type analyses should read. The contract start_date is locked once the employee has been paid, making it the most trustworthy hire date in the domain.
views.grain: one employment contract episode per employee per array position

views.label: payroll uk employee leave
views.description: Booked leave (holiday, unpaid leave, org-defined types) per employee. Each request spans start_date..end_date but the quantified time off — units per pay period — lives in xero_payroll_uk_employee_leave_periods; this table alone cannot tell you how many hours were taken. Statutory family leave and SSP episodes are tracked separately in the statutory leave tables, so 'all absence' questions need both families.
views.grain: one leave request per leaveID

views.label: payroll uk employee leave balances
views.description: The employee's leave balances as of the last sync — a point-in-time snapshot that each sync overwrites. Balances are last-value measures: summing them over time or across syncs double-counts, and there is no history here (trend questions need the periods table plus accrual rules). Units differ per leave type, so cross-type sums are unit soup.
views.grain: one current leave balance per employee per leave type

views.label: payroll uk employee leave periods
views.description: How each leave request is carved across payroll periods, with the number of units actually deducted from the balance in each period. This is the additive quantity table for non-statutory leave: SUM(number_of_units) is hours (or the type's unit) of leave taken. Slices follow the employee's PAYROLL calendar, so a calendar-month report must aggregate by the slice dates, not assume slices equal months.
views.grain: one pay-period slice of one leave request

views.label: payroll uk employee leave types
views.description: The per-employee accrual configuration for each leave type the employee is enrolled in: accrual schedule, annual hours, caps and opening balance. This is the RULE; the resulting number lives in xero_payroll_uk_employee_leave_balances. Distinct from the org-level catalogue xero_payroll_uk_leave_types, which defines the types themselves — join it for names and paid/statutory flags.
views.grain: one leave-type enrolment (accrual rule) per employee per leave type

views.label: payroll uk employee ni categories
views.description: The employee's NI category letter history, exploded from the employee record. The category letter decides the employer and employee NIC rates (A standard, C over state pension age, M/Z under 21, H apprentice under 25, V veteran, F/I/L/S Freeport, N/E/K/D Investment Zone), so any employer-NIC cost model keys off the CURRENT letter: the row with the latest start_date. Rows are assignments over time, not a point-in-time attribute — joining all rows to payslips multiplies pay.
views.grain: one effective-dated National Insurance category assignment per employee per array position

views.label: payroll uk employee opening balances
views.description: Fiscal year-to-date statutory pay amounts the employee had ALREADY received before the organisation started (or re-based) Xero payroll, plus the prior employer's staff number. These carry-in figures exist so statutory pay caps (e.g. 28 weeks SSP) compute correctly mid-year. Any 'statutory pay this tax year' total must be payslip amounts PLUS these openings, or mid-year-migrated orgs under-report.
views.grain: one migration-time opening balance record per employee

views.label: payroll uk employee pay template earnings
views.description: The employee's pay template: standing earnings instructions (regular allowances, fixed amounts, default units) that seed each new pay run. These are TEMPLATES, not actual pay — the payslip earnings lines in the sibling pay-run domain are the actuals, and a run can be edited after seeding. Use this table for 'who has a standing allowance' and expected-pay modelling, never for amounts actually paid.
views.grain: one standing earnings line per employee's pay template (payTemplateEarningID)

views.label: payroll uk employee payment methods
views.description: How each employee's net pay leaves the business: electronically (BACS file), by cheque, or recorded as paid manually. The destination bank accounts for electronic payment live in the child table xero_payroll_uk_employee_bank_accounts. Operationally load-bearing for 'who is in the bank file' questions; analytically a small but telling dimension of payroll process maturity.
views.grain: one net-pay payment method configuration per employee

views.label: payroll uk employee salary and wages
views.description: The employee's pay basis history: each row fixes an annual salary or hourly arrangement from an effective date, with exactly one Active row per employee at a time (Pending = future-dated change, History = superseded). This is the table for salary bill, pay-rise and pay-basis questions. annual_salary is a stock, not a flow: it is safe to add ACROSS employees once you have picked one row per employee (status = 'Active', or the latest effective_from at the date in question), and never safe to add across an employee's own rows — summing annual_salary without that filter adds every historical salary the employee ever had.
views.grain: one effective-dated salary or wage basis record per salaryAndWagesID

views.label: payroll uk employee statutory leave balances
views.description: Remaining statutory entitlement (SSP, SMP, SPP, SAP, ShPP, bereavement, neonatal care) per employee, fetched one leave type at a time with an explicit as-of date. The ingester must enumerate LeaveType values per employee, so coverage depends on the scan plan — treat absence of a row as 'not fetched', not 'no entitlement'. Because the endpoint answers a question ('what is left on this date?') rather than returning a stored record, the AsOfDate the scan passed is part of the row's identity: two passes on different dates produce two legitimately different rows for the same employee and type. Balances are expressed in Hours even though statutory entitlements are legally defined in weeks.
views.grain: one statutory leave balance per employee per statutory leave type per as-of date the scan requested

views.label: payroll uk employee tax
views.description: The employee's live HMRC tax settings: tax code, W1/M1 basis, starter declaration, P45 carry-in figures, student/postgraduate loan flags and director NIC treatment. This is CURRENT STATE ONLY — Xero returns no tax-code history, so questions about what code applied to a past payslip cannot be answered from here; the payslip's own tax lines are the record of what was actually deducted.
views.grain: one current PAYE tax configuration per employee

views.label: payroll uk employees
views.description: The master roster of everyone the organisation pays through Xero UK Payroll: current staff, leavers, and off-payroll workers. This is the anchor of the whole UK payroll domain — every leave, tax, salary, timesheet and payslip row hangs off employee_id. Headcount questions must filter end_date (null means still employed) AND is_off_payroll_worker, or contractors inflate the number. Note start_date/end_date are the employment dates 'at the time it was requested' — a convenience snapshot; the authoritative employment episode history is xero_payroll_uk_employee_contracts. These tables are only populated for tenants running UK payroll; a tenant has AU or UK or NZ payroll, never two, so never union across regions.
views.grain: one current or former UK payroll employee per employeeID within the organisation

views.label: payroll uk leave types
views.description: The organisation's catalogue of leave types (holiday, sickness, unpaid leave...), with the flags that change how leave costs and displays: paid vs unpaid, statutory vs org-defined, active vs retired. Employee leave requests, balances and per-employee accrual rules all join here for names and flags. Distinct from the per-employee enrolment table xero_payroll_uk_employee_leave_types.
views.grain: one org-level leave type per leaveTypeID

views.label: payroll uk pay run calendars
views.description: The org's pay schedules: frequency (weekly through annual), the CURRENT period's start/end and its payment date. Employees and timesheets reference a calendar, making this the dimension that splits the workforce into pay-frequency populations. The period dates roll forward as pay runs post — they describe the current period at sync time, not a fixed anchor, so never treat them as the schedule's first-ever period.
views.grain: one payroll calendar (pay frequency schedule) per payrollCalendarID

views.label: payroll uk pay runs
views.description: The processing container for UK payroll. Each row is one run of one payroll calendar, carrying run-level totals: total_cost is what the employer spent (gross pay plus employer NI and other on-costs), total_pay is what employees actually took home (net). Draft runs are provisional and mutate freely until posted; only Posted runs represent money that moved and RTI submissions that happened. EarlierYearUpdate runs are HMRC corrections to a PREVIOUS tax year and must never be counted as current-period cost. A payroll calendar period can hold more than one run (an Unscheduled run alongside the Scheduled one), so never assume period dates uniquely identify a run.
views.grain: one UK payroll pay run: one processing of one payroll calendar over one pay period

views.label: payroll uk payslip benefit lines
views.description: Non-earnings compensation applied on the payslip — the spec's own framing is fringe benefits and perks provided in addition to normal earnings. These amounts sit outside the gross-to-net bridge entirely: not in gross_earnings, not in total_pay, so no benefit line is cash the employee received. The analytically dangerous part is that one array carries two different economic things — an employer contribution that IS new spend, and a payrolled benefit value that is only tax bookkeeping on something already paid for — and the spec gives no flag to tell them apart. Only benefit_type_id and display_name, interpreted against how this org configured its benefit types, can separate them, so treat any sum over this table as unclassified until that mapping is known.
views.grain: one benefit line per payslip per position in its benefitLines array

views.label: payroll uk payslip court order lines
views.description: Statutory attachments the employer must divert from the employee's pay under a court or agency order — attachment of earnings orders (AEOs), child maintenance DEOs and similar. Deducted after tax on the way to net; the money is the employee's, redirected — never an employer cost and never a voluntary deduction. Sensitive by nature: rows reveal that an employee is under a court order, so aggregate rather than list employees wherever possible.
views.grain: one court order line per payslip per position in its courtOrderLines array

views.label: payroll uk payslip deduction lines
views.description: Configured deductions taken from the employee's own pay on the way from gross to net — typically employee pension contributions, salary sacrifice, union fees and loan repayments, though what a given org actually configures here is visible only through deduction_type_id. Every amount on this table is the employee's money being redirected, never employer cost. subject_to_tax is the one semantic hinge the spec does give: it states whether the deducted amount remains subject to tax, which separates deductions that shrink taxable pay from those taken after tax has been calculated. Statutory tax and court orders are deliberately NOT here — Xero keeps them in their own arrays and their own payslip totals.
views.grain: one deduction line per payslip per position in its deductionLines array

views.label: payroll uk payslip earnings lines
views.description: Regular (non-leave, non-timesheet) earnings detail: salary, hourly wages, bonuses, overtime and other configured earnings rates, one row per rate application on a payslip. This family is only PART of gross pay — leave-paid earnings and timesheet-driven earnings live in their own sibling tables, so summing amount here alone understates gross for any org using leave or timesheets. amount is the settled value (ratePerUnit x numberOfUnits, or fixedAmount for Fixed-rate types); the rate and unit columns are inputs and must never be summed.
views.grain: one regular earnings line per payslip per position in its earningsLines array

views.label: payroll uk payslip employee tax lines
views.description: Statutory tax withheld FROM the employee: PAYE income tax and employee (primary Class 1) National Insurance, one row per tax component. These amounts are inside gross_earnings and reduce it to net — they are not employer cost. The description text ('PAYE', 'Employee NIC'...) is the practical PAYE-vs-NI splitter; global_tax_type_id is the stable code. This table and xero_payroll_uk_payslip_employer_tax_lines materialize two different Payslip arrays of the same TaxLine object — never union them without labeling the payer.
views.grain: one employee tax line per payslip per position in its employeeTaxLines array

views.label: payroll uk payslip employer tax lines
views.description: Tax the EMPLOYER owes on top of gross pay: employer (secondary Class 1) National Insurance and Apprenticeship Levy, one row per component. This is the on-cost wedge — add it to gross_earnings for true employment cost; it never touches the employee's pay. Same TaxLine shape as the employee table but a different Payslip array; the split by array is what keeps 'tax burden on staff' and 'tax cost to the business' from contaminating each other. Note that run-level reliefs like Employment Allowance are settled with HMRC and may not be visible per payslip.
views.grain: one employer tax line per payslip per position in its employerTaxLines array

views.label: payroll uk payslip leave accrual lines
views.description: Leave entitlement EARNED in this pay run, in units (hours or days per the leave type) — no money on this table at all. It is a flow, not a balance: summing number_of_units gives cumulative accrual over a window, but remaining entitlement also needs leave taken, which this table does not carry. Paid leave consumption is recorded in the leave earnings lines table (amount plus its own numberOfUnits), but those units are defined by the pricing earnings rate, not by this table's leave type — the two unit systems need not match, so netting accruals against leave-earnings units without confirming both definitions is unsafe. Presenting a sum of accruals as 'leave balance' is the wrong-answer mode to avoid.
views.grain: one leave accrual line per payslip per position in its leaveAccrualLines array

views.label: payroll uk payslip leave earnings lines
views.description: Pay for leave actually taken in the period — holiday pay, statutory sick/parental pay priced through leave-linked earnings rates. These amounts are INSIDE gross_earnings (they are earnings, paid instead of worked time), so 'cost of leave' from this table must not be added on top of gross. Distinguish from xero_payroll_uk_payslip_leave_accrual_lines, which records entitlement units earned, not money paid.
views.grain: one leave earnings line per payslip per position in its leaveEarningsLines array

views.label: payroll uk payslip payment lines
views.description: How the payslip's NET pay is disbursed: one row per destination bank account, carrying employee bank details (account number, sort code, account name — all PII). Employees can split pay across accounts, so SUM(amount) per payslip — not any single row — should equal the slip's total_pay for electronically paid slips. This is a disbursement instruction, not compensation: never use it for pay analysis, only for payment reconciliation and split-payment questions.
views.grain: one payment line per payslip per position in its paymentLines array

views.label: payroll uk payslip reimbursement lines
views.description: Non-taxable repayments of out-of-pocket expenses settled through payroll. Reimbursements are ADDED to net pay but are not earnings: they sit outside gross_earnings and outside tax. The two classic mistakes are counting them as compensation (inflates wage analysis) and forgetting them in the gross-to-net bridge (net looks too high). description is free text from the payroll admin — useful for eyeballing, unreliable for classification.
views.grain: one reimbursement line per payslip per position in its reimbursementLines array

views.label: payroll uk payslip timesheet earnings lines
views.description: Earnings sourced from approved timesheets: hours captured on timesheets, priced at an earnings rate and settled on the payslip. Inside gross_earnings like its sibling families. This domain's ground truth contains no Timesheet object, so within these tables this family is the only record of paid worked time — number_of_units is the paid-hours measure and amount the paid value — but it is the payroll settlement of timesheets, not the timesheets themselves, and a timesheets domain elsewhere in the connector would be the authority on hours worked. What is here is time PAID, which can lag or aggregate the time actually worked when a timesheet spans periods.
views.grain: one timesheet earnings line per payslip per position in its timesheetEarningsLines array

views.label: payroll uk payslips
views.description: The per-employee settlement of a pay run: header totals for gross, net, taxes, deductions, reimbursements, court orders and benefits, with the line-level detail exploded into eleven child tables. The critical trap is total_pay: it is NET take-home, not gross — employment cost per head is gross_earnings + total_employer_taxes. Payslips carry no status of their own; whether the money is real is decided by the parent run's pay_run_status, so almost every query joins xero_payroll_uk_pay_runs. Names are denormalized snapshots at pay time — identity questions must key on employee_id.
views.grain: one payslip per employee per pay run

views.label: payroll uk reimbursements
views.description: Org-level reimbursement definitions — non-taxable repayments of employee expenses routed through payroll (mileage, tools, expenses). Rows are the catalogue; amounts actually reimbursed are payslip reimbursement lines in the pay-run domain. Reimbursements are not earnings: they sit outside gross pay, tax and NIC, so including them in wage-cost or gross-pay metrics inflates both.
views.grain: one reimbursement pay item per reimbursementID

views.label: payroll uk settings accounts
views.description: The payroll settings' GL account map: which general-ledger accounts UK payroll posts wages expense, wages payable, PAYE and NIC liabilities and the payment bank account to. The row's type is the payroll ROLE and the true row key — the settings payload carries one entry per role, and nothing stops an org pointing two roles (say PAYELIABILITY and NICLIABILITY) at the same GL account, so accountID can repeat. The accountID is the same id as xero_accounts, so this table is the bridge between payroll amounts and where they appear in the P&L and balance sheet.
views.grain: one payroll GL account mapping per payroll account role (type) for the organisation

views.label: payroll uk statutory leave summaries
views.description: Every statutory leave episode (maternity, paternity, adoption, shared parental, bereavement, neonatal care, sickness) recorded for each employee, with its date span, entitlement verdict and lifecycle status. This is the discovery index for statutory absence: sick episodes fan further out to xero_payroll_uk_statutory_sick_leaves for SSP detail. Note the endpoint requires payroll.settings scope — not payroll.employees — so this family can be absent while ordinary employee data synced fine.
views.grain: one statutory leave episode per statutoryLeaveID

views.label: payroll uk statutory sick leaves
views.description: Full SSP detail for sick episodes discovered in the summaries table: entitlement weeks requested/qualified/remaining, work pattern, pregnancy linkage, notice compliance and failure reasons. The weeks fields are entitlement arithmetic, not time worked — they answer 'how much SSP runway is left', never 'how many hours were missed'. Fetched per StatutorySickLeaveID, so it exists only where the optional detail scan ran.
views.grain: one statutory sick pay (SSP) episode per statutoryLeaveID

views.label: payroll uk timesheet lines
views.description: The daily detail behind each timesheet: units (per the earnings rate's unit type, normally hours) worked on a specific date under a specific earnings rate, optionally tagged to a tracking option.
