This is the workforce time-entry fact of the UK payroll domain — hours by day, by overtime vs regular, by department all resolve here. The payability filter lives on the PARENT: always join the timesheet header and filter its status.
views.grain: one timesheet line per timesheetLineID: one employee's units for one date and one earnings rate

views.label: payroll uk timesheets
views.description: Timesheet headers, each covering one employee for one payroll-calendar period and carrying the total hours plus the approval lifecycle. Hours become payable only as the timesheet moves Draft → Approved → Completed (processed in a pay run); Draft hours are unvetted data entry. The key is timesheetID alone — (employee_id, start_date) is NOT a key, because an employee can hold more than one timesheet for the same period. total_hours duplicates the sum of the line units — use header OR lines in one query, never both.
views.grain: one timesheet per timesheetID: one employee's submitted hours for one payroll-calendar period

views.label: payroll uk tracking categories
views.description: A single-row pointer table: which two ACCOUNTING tracking categories UK payroll uses — one for employee groups (org-structure reporting on pay runs) and one for timesheet lines (department/cost-centre tagging of hours). It contains ids only; the categories' names and options live in xero_tracking_categories / xero_tracking_options. This is NOT a payroll copy of the accounting tracking tables — it is the glue that says which of them payroll uses.
views.grain: one payroll tracking configuration record per organisation

views.label: prepayment allocations
views.description: The settlement edge between a prepayment and the invoices it pays down: each row moves a slice of held credit onto exactly one invoice on a given date. Allocations are how invoices get PAID WITHOUT CASH MOVING — treating allocation amounts as receipts double-counts the cash that already arrived when the prepayment was created. Rows are exploded from the parent document's Allocations array and re-land whenever the parent changes; they have no independent watermark.
views.grain: one application of prepayment credit to one invoice, keyed by parent prepayment and array position

views.label: prepayments
views.description: Money received (or paid) BEFORE any invoice exists: a prepayment is created from a bank transaction and sits as credit against the contact until allocated to invoices or refunded. It is never revenue or expense by itself — recognition happens on the invoice lines it eventually offsets, so counting prepayment totals as sales double-counts the later invoice. Direction is carried by type (RECEIVE-*/AR* = customer credit you hold, SPEND-*/AP* = credit you hold with a supplier), mirroring the ACCREC/ACCPAY split that runs through the whole connector. remaining_credit and applied_amount are current-state balances restated on every sync, not history.
views.grain: one prepayment credit document per PrepaymentID

views.label: project tasks
views.description: The work-item and billing-line level of a project: each task carries its charge model (charge_type plus the rate Amount pair) and Xero-maintained to-date rollups of minutes and value split by invoiced state. Chargeability is decided HERE — time entries have no value of their own and inherit everything from the task they are logged against. The rollups are balances that already summarize xero_project_time_entries; add task totals to time-entry sums and every hour counts twice. Deleted tasks vanish from the API rather than gaining a status.
views.grain: one task (a billable or non-billable work item) on one project per taskId

views.label: project time entries
views.description: The only transaction-grain fact in the projects domain: one row per block of minutes a user logged against a task, fully additive across every dimension. duration is integer minutes — divide by 60.0 for hours or Postgres integer division floors the answer. The row itself carries no value and no chargeability: join xero_project_tasks for charge_type and rate, and price duration/60.0 times rate for TIME tasks only. date_utc is the day the work was done (the business axis); date_entered_utc is when it was keyed in (the audit axis) — aggregate on the former.
views.grain: one logged block of minutes by one user against one task per timeEntryId

views.label: project users
views.description: Roster dimension of everyone who can appear in Xero Projects time data — the join target that turns a time entry's user_id into a person. Presence here means access, not activity: utilization answers must LEFT JOIN from this roster or zero-hour people silently disappear. The roster is also current-state only, so it can be narrower than history — someone removed from Projects stops being returned while their logged hours remain, which makes an inner join in the other direction lose real time. It carries personal name and email, the only PII in the projects domain.
views.grain: one Xero user with access to Xero Projects in the org per userId

views.label: projects
views.description: The client-job dimension of Xero Projects and the fastest place to answer job-profitability questions: every monetary column is a Xero-maintained to-date rollup — a balance, not a transaction stream — denominated in the project's own currency_code. The rollups already contain everything in xero_project_tasks and xero_project_time_entries, so they must never be added to aggregates built from those child tables. Expenses have no child endpoint in this API version, which makes the expense rollups here the ONLY view of project expenses. CLOSED projects keep returning with full financial history: lifetime questions keep them, WIP and pipeline questions filter status = 'INPROGRESS'. Deletion is hard: a removed project stops being returned rather than gaining a DELETED status, and no field on this object carries a modified watermark, so staging only sheds it on a full identity rescan.
views.grain: one Xero Projects project (a client job) per projectId

views.label: purchase order line items
views.description: The queryable grain of committed procurement: what is being ordered, from which GL account and catalog item, at what price, carrying the order's tracking dimensions. Lines have no status of their own — every aggregate must join xero_purchase_orders and filter the parent's status, or DELETED and DRAFT orders pollute committed spend. Whether line_amount includes tax depends on the parent's line_amount_types, so tax-safe rollups need a CASE on that flag.
views.grain: one line item on one purchase order

views.label: purchase orders
views.description: The commitment ledger of procurement: each row is an order placed (or drafted) with a supplier, with tax-normalized header totals in the document's own currency. Nothing here is actual expenditure — when a purchase order reaches status BILLED the same value re-materializes as an ACCPAY invoice in xero_invoices, so adding PO totals to bill totals double-counts procurement. Open commitment is status AUTHORISED; DRAFT/SUBMITTED are unapproved intent; DELETED orders keep arriving from the API and must be excluded from every aggregate. Line-level detail (GL accounts, items, tracking) lives in xero_purchase_order_line_items.
views.grain: one purchase order document raised against one supplier contact

views.label: quote line items
views.description: Proposed-value lines exploded from Quote.LineItems: what was offered, at what price, before anything was billed. Nothing here is revenue — quotes only become revenue when invoiced (parent status INVOICED and a real invoice exists). Currency and LineAmountTypes come from the parent xero_quotes row, and the quote enum spells LineAmountTypes in UPPERCASE unlike invoices.
views.grain: one line item on one quote per LineItemID

views.label: quotes
views.description: Pre-revenue sales pipeline: quotes are offers, always customer-facing (no ACCREC/ACCPAY split here), and none of their value is billed until an invoice is raised. Status is the whole story — DRAFT/SENT are open pipeline, ACCEPTED is won-but-unbilled, INVOICED is converted, DECLINED/DELETED are dead. There is no key linking a quote to the invoice it became; conversion analysis works off status and matching by contact/date/amount.
views.grain: one quote document per QuoteID

views.label: receipt line items
views.description: The GL-categorized grain of employee out-of-pocket spend: each row says which account (and optionally which catalog item and tracking dimensions) a slice of a receipt hits. Lines carry no status — join xero_receipts and filter the parent's status or declined/voided spend pollutes every sum. Amounts are org base currency; whether line_amount includes tax follows the parent's line_amount_types. These are categorizations awaiting the claims workflow, not ledger postings — the statutory record is journal lines once the claim is processed.
views.grain: one line item on one expense receipt

views.label: receipts
views.description: Employee out-of-pocket spend documents: who spent, at which merchant, on what date, with tax-normalized totals in org base currency (receipts carry no currency fields). This is the spend-evidence side of the claims workflow — the reimbursement liability lives on the claim, and cash leaves via xero_expense_claim_payments. Receipts are neither bills nor bank transactions: once reimbursed, the same economic spend also surfaces as a payment against the claim, so mixing receipts with ACCPAY invoices or the bank feed double-counts employee spend. Approved company spend is status AUTHORISED only.
views.grain: one expense receipt captured by one org user in the classic expense-claims workflow

views.label: repeating invoice line items
views.description: The composition of each recurring template: which products/services and GL accounts every generated invoice will carry. Values are per-occurrence template amounts, so like the parent they are non-additive until normalized by the parent's schedule. Realized recurring line detail lives on xero_invoice_line_items of generated invoices, not here.
views.grain: one line item on one repeating invoice template per LineItemID

views.label: repeating invoices
views.description: Templates that GENERATE invoices on a schedule — recurring billing (ACCREC) or recurring bills (ACCPAY), with the Schedule object flattened into schedule_* columns. Template totals are per-occurrence values: a $100 weekly template is not comparable to a $100 monthly one until normalized by schedule_unit/schedule_period, which is why this table is non-additive. Realized recurring revenue lives on xero_invoices rows whose repeating_invoice_id points here; only AUTHORISED templates generate anything.
views.grain: one repeating invoice template per RepeatingInvoiceID

views.label: tax rate components
views.description: The parts a tax rate is built from — e.g. Canadian GST + PST as two components of one rate. IsCompound marks components calculated on top of tax-inclusive subtotals, which is exactly why the parent's EffectiveRate can exceed the arithmetic sum of component rates. Components have no ids and no watermark; they re-land with each parent rescan.
views.grain: one constituent component per (tax rate, zero-based array position)

views.label: tax rates
views.description: The org's tax rate definitions, keyed by the TaxType code that journal lines, document lines and account defaults all reference. EffectiveRate is the rate the calculation engine actually applies (compounding included); DisplayTaxRate is the label the UI shows — they diverge exactly when a component compounds. Rates have no uuid and no update watermark: the tiny unpaged set is fully re-scanned each sync, and DELETED/ARCHIVED rates must be kept because historical lines cite them forever.
views.grain: one org tax rate per TaxType code

views.label: tracking categories
views.description: The org's self-defined analysis dimensions — 'Department', 'Region', 'Cost Centre' — of which at most two can be ACTIVE at once. These are how Xero users encode structure the chart of accounts does not carry, applied per line via tracking pairs; treat each category as a first-class reporting axis. The ingester passes includeArchived=true, so ARCHIVED categories referenced by history are present; hard-deleted ones are detected only by full identity rescan.
views.grain: one tracking category (analysis dimension) per TrackingCategoryID

views.label: tracking options
views.description: The value list of each tracking category — the 'East', 'West', 'Marketing' a line can be stamped with. Options are the actual segment members reports group by; ARCHIVED options stay bound to historical lines, so segment dimensions must keep them or old segments disappear from breakdowns.
views.grain: one selectable option per TrackingOptionID within its tracking category

views.label: users
views.description: Everyone who can act inside the org — staff, external accountants and practice-side logins — with their permission tier. This is the roster history records' free-text actor names resolve against, and the source for access/security questions. It is NOT a headcount table: advisers and managed-client logins inflate it, and the same human appears once per connected org. REMOVED users keep appearing in the payload after losing access.
views.grain: one user login with access to the connected organisation

dimensions.label: sale id
dimensions.description: Immutable numeric ticket id, unique within the account. The join key for every child table (lines, payments, voids, CC charges, ShipTo, quotes). NOT the human receipt number the customer sees — the Refund endpoint accepts a ticketNumber in its URL path, but no ticketNumber field is published on this object.

dimensions.label: completed
dimensions.description: True once the ticket was finalised: inventory has been deducted and payments sum to the total. False = an open/parked ticket sitting on a register (or the working sale behind a saved quote) with NO payments at all. Almost every money question must filter completed = true; omitting it silently mixes unpaid shopping carts into revenue.

dimensions.label: voided
dimensions.description: True when the sale was voided. Documented meaning: voided sales do not count toward totals or payments received and all inventory was restocked — but the money columns on this row are NOT zeroed out, so a voided sale still carries a full calcTotal. Summing without voided = false inflates revenue by the value of every reversed ticket.

dimensions.label: archived
dimensions.description: True when the sale is archived (hidden from the POS UI). Archived is NOT voided: an archived completed sale was real revenue and must stay in the numbers. See the VERIFIED LIVE gotcha — the archived=true query filter is silently ignored on this endpoint.

dimensions.label: create time
dimensions.description: When the ticket was first opened at the register, store-local, read-only. This is when shopping started, not when money changed hands — on layaways and parked tickets it can precede completion by months. Never use it as the revenue period.

dimensions.label: complete time
dimensions.description: When the sale was completed — THE canonical revenue timestamp, store-local. Empty/NULL on open tickets, so any date predicate on this column implicitly drops uncompleted sales. Documented as changeable (staff can back-date a completion), so it is not monotonic with sale_id and a re-run of last month's report can legitimately move.

dimensions.label: update time
dimensions.description: Last modification, read-only, store-local. Use for incremental mirroring only, never for reporting periods — a two-year-old sale touched by a refund gets today's stamp. Note the reference field table spells it `updatetime` (lower-case t) while the live payload and query parameter are `updateTime`.

dimensions.label: reference number
dimensions.description: Order number assigned by the external system that created the sale (webstore, Amazon, marketplace). Empty for tickets rung up in-store. Free text, not guaranteed unique, and not a Lightspeed identifier — never join on it without also matching reference_number_source.

dimensions.label: reference number source
dimensions.description: Name of the external system that owns reference_number. The nearest thing to a sales-channel dimension on this object: empty means the sale originated in the POS, non-empty names the ecommerce/marketplace channel. Values are whatever the integration writes, so normalise before grouping.

dimensions.label: tax2 rate
dimensions.description: Default second tax rate as a fraction, for jurisdictions with two components (e.g. GST + PST). 0 in single-tax territories such as AU/NZ. Total tax collected on the sale is calc_tax1 + calc_tax2, never a rate multiplication.

dimensions.label: change given
dimensions.description: Cash handed back to the customer; cash sales only. Purely informational — it is already reflected inside the cash SalePayment amount and is NOT a deduction from revenue. Subtracting it from totals double counts.

dimensions.label: tip enabled
dimensions.description: True when the tipping feature was active on this ticket. A configuration flag, not evidence a tip was actually left: the money is in calc_tips and SalePayment.tipAmount. Can be true with calc_tips = 0.

dimensions.label: enable promotions
dimensions.description: True when automatic Promotions were run against every line added to this sale. Write-once: settable only at creation and immutable thereafter, so it describes how the ticket was priced historically, not a toggle you can reason about as current config.

dimensions.label: calc discount
dimensions.description: Total money discounted on the sale, store currency, as a POSITIVE number representing value given away. Aggregates line-level markdowns plus the sale-level discount from ANY source — named rule, automatic price rule, loyalty redemption, manual override. Therefore it is NOT attributable to discount_id alone.

dimensions.label: calc taxable
dimensions.description: Subtotal of only the lines that were actually taxed (SaleLine.tax = true AND their TaxClass carries a rate). calc_taxable + calc_non_taxable should reconcile to calc_subtotal; a gap means mixed tax treatment worth investigating.

dimensions.label: calc non taxable
dimensions.description: Subtotal of the non-taxable lines (tax-exempt customers, zero-rated goods, some labour classes). The reason tax collected is usually less than subtotal x rate — quote this rather than accusing the data of being wrong.

dimensions.label: calc tax1
dimensions.description: Tax collected at the first rate across all lines, in store currency. A money amount, not a rate — the name pairs confusingly with tax1_rate.

dimensions.label: calc tax2
dimensions.description: Tax collected at the second rate, in currency; 0 in single-tax jurisdictions. Total tax on the sale = calc_tax1 + calc_tax2.

dimensions.label: calc payments
dimensions.description: Sum of every SalePayment.amount on this sale, tips included. On a completed sale this equals the total; on a layaway or on-account sale it is only the portion paid so far. This is takings, not revenue — the two diverge whenever deposits or instalments exist.

dimensions.label: calc tips
dimensions.description: Sum of SalePayment.tipAmount across the sale. Tips are INSIDE the payment amounts, not additional to them, so merchandise money taken = calc_payments - calc_tips. Tips are not revenue and are typically owed to tip_employee_id.

dimensions.label: displayable total
dimensions.description: total plus gift-card deposits. Issuing a gift card is not revenue, so its face value is excluded from total but must still be printed on the receipt. Use this only to reproduce a printed receipt; using it for revenue double counts every gift card once at issue and again at redemption.

dimensions.label: balance
dimensions.description: total - calc_payments: money still owed on the ticket. Non-zero on layaways, special orders and on-account sales, ~0 on a settled ticket. The ONE non-additive column in this table — it is an outstanding balance at a point in time, so summing it across a date range mixes in layaways that were subsequently paid off.

dimensions.label: employee id
dimensions.description: Employee who processed (rang up) the ticket — the attribution for 'sales by staff member'. Distinct from ls_sale_lines.employee_id (which can differ when several staff touch one ticket) and from tip_employee_id.

dimensions.label: tip employee id
dimensions.description: Employee assigned the whole tip amount for this sale. Frequently 0/NULL even when calc_tips > 0, because tipping is often configured without an assignee. Never use it as the seller.

dimensions.label: quote id
dimensions.description: The Quote this sale was created from. Non-zero means the ticket originated as a saved quote — THIS is the direction to measure quote conversion from, because the inverse pointer (Quote.saleID) is reassigned on every quote edit and is meaningless for conversion.

dimensions.label: register id
dimensions.description: Register (till) the sale was processed on. Maps to the `register` canonical entity. 0/NULL for sales created via the API or an integration with no register context, so register splits will show an unattributed bucket for ecommerce orders.

dimensions.label: ship to id
dimensions.description: The ShipTo (shipment/delivery) record for this sale, present when goods were shipped rather than carried out. Non-zero is the practical marker of a delivered order — there is no explicit fulfilment-type field on Sale.

dimensions.label: shop id
dimensions.description: Shop (physical location) where the sale was processed — the `location` dimension for every revenue split. Note lines carry their own shopID, so a multi-shop ticket is technically possible and line-level splits can disagree with this.

dimensions.label: tax category id
dimensions.description: TaxCategory governing which tax rates apply to this sale; it is what determines the tax1_rate/tax2_rate defaults. 0 when the account has a single implicit category. Maps to the `tax_code` canonical entity.

dimensions.label: sale line id
dimensions.description: Unique numeric id for the line. Stable across edits to the parent sale; the target of parent_sale_line_id on refund lines and of ls_sale_accounts.sale_line_id on gift-card lines.

dimensions.label: sale id
dimensions.description: The sale this line sits on. This table has no completed/voided/complete_time of its own, so every revenue query MUST join ls_sales through this key (or carry those three columns down at load time).

dimensions.label: create time
dimensions.description: When the line was first added to the ticket, store-local. On a parked ticket or a layaway this can be days or months before the sale completes — it is 'when the item was put in the basket', not the sale date.

dimensions.label: time stamp
dimensions.description: When the line was last modified. Not the sale date: a line touched during a later exchange gets a fresh stamp, so filtering revenue periods on it back-dates nothing and double counts amended sales. Filter on the parent sale's complete_time instead.

dimensions.label: normal unit price
dimensions.description: Per-unit price before any price rules were applied — the 'was' price. (normal_unit_price - unit_price) * unit_quantity approximates automatic markdown only; manually keyed discounts land in discount_amount / calc_line_discount instead, so the two measures do not add up.

dimensions.label: discount amount
dimensions.description: Dollar discount entered on the line. Mutually exclusive with discount_percent — exactly one of the two is non-zero. This is the operator's INPUT, not the resulting money off; the realised money off is calc_line_discount.

dimensions.label: taxed
dimensions.description: Whether the line is taxed at all. If false, no tax applies regardless of any rate. If true, tax still only applies when the line's TaxClass actually carries a rate — so taxed = true does NOT guarantee calc_tax1 > 0, and using it as a proxy for 'tax was collected' overstates taxable turnover.

dimensions.label: tax1 rate
dimensions.description: First tax rate for THIS line as a fraction, after TaxClass and TaxCategory customisation. Overrides the sale's tax1Rate — this is why a mixed basket cannot have its tax reconstructed from the sale-level rate.

dimensions.label: tax2 rate
dimensions.description: Second tax rate for this line as a fraction, where the jurisdiction has one. 0 in single-tax territories.

dimensions.label: is layaway
dimensions.description: Line sits on a layaway: goods are reserved (see ls_sale_line_inventory_allocations) and paid for over time, so the money is a balance rather than settled revenue. Settable only via the SaleLine endpoint or the app, never through the Sale endpoint.

dimensions.label: is workorder
dimensions.description: Line originated from a workshop/service job — the marker that separates SERVICE revenue from goods revenue. Effectively read-only: the docs state it must not be set through the Sale or SaleLine endpoints and cannot be used to create a workorder.

dimensions.label: is special order
dimensions.description: Line is a special order (stock brought in for a named customer); setting it creates a SpecialOrder record. Settable only via the SaleLine endpoint or the app. Special-order lines can sit on an open ticket for weeks, so they distort 'time to sell' metrics.

dimensions.label: displayable subtotal
dimensions.description: Receipt-facing line subtotal, documented as (unitQuantity * unitPrice) - discount. Use it to reproduce a printed receipt. For analytics prefer calc_subtotal so the tax treatment is unambiguous — but note the two differ by exactly the line discount (see the calc_subtotal gotcha).

dimensions.label: displayable unit price
dimensions.description: The unit price shown to the customer after price-rule PERCENTAGE discounts ONLY — fixed-amount price rules are deliberately excluded. Because of that exclusion it can disagree with unit_price; never use it as the cash-per-unit basis for revenue.

dimensions.label: calc line discount
dimensions.description: Money taken off by the line's own discount, in currency. Only half the story: add calc_transaction_discount to get the total markdown on the line, otherwise whole-sale discounts are invisible at line grain.

dimensions.label: calc transaction discount
dimensions.description: This line's allocated share of a whole-sale (transaction-level) discount. calc_line_discount + calc_transaction_discount summed across lines reconciles to Sale.calcDiscount; using either alone under-reports markdown.

dimensions.label: calc total
dimensions.description: Line revenue INCLUDING tax, after all discounts. Sums across lines to the sale's calc_total. Negative on refund lines.

dimensions.label: calc tax1
dimensions.description: Tax charged on this line at the first rate, in currency. A money amount, not a rate.

dimensions.label: calc tax2
dimensions.description: Tax charged on this line at the second rate, in currency; 0 in single-tax jurisdictions.

dimensions.label: tax class id
dimensions.description: TaxClass of the line, which determines its specific rates. The practical dimension for goods-vs-labour tax splits (accounts commonly define a 'Labor' tax class). Maps to the `tax_code` canonical entity.

dimensions.label: discount id
dimensions.description: The named Discount rule applied to this line specifically. Joins ls_discounts. NULL/0 for automatic price rules, loyalty and manual markdowns, so it explains only part of calc_line_discount.

dimensions.label: employee id
dimensions.description: Employee responsible for this line, which can differ from the sale's employee when staff split a ticket or a workshop tech adds parts. Use this for per-line commission and the sale's employee_id for per-ticket attribution — mixing them double counts.

dimensions.label: item id
dimensions.description: Catalog item the line charges for; maps to the `product`/`product_variant` canonical entities. VERIFIED LIVE: 0/absent on non-catalog lines (miscellaneous charges, some labour), so product rankings must filter item_id IS NOT NULL or an unnamed bucket tops the chart. On write an itemCode (UPC/EAN, or the itemID itself) may be sent in its place, but reads always return itemID.

dimensions.label: note id
dimensions.description: The single Note object attached to this line; notes print on the receipt. At most one per line by design, so this is a scalar FK not an array. The Note object's own fields are not published in this extract.

dimensions.label: parent sale line id
dimensions.description: For a REFUND line, the original sale line it reverses — the API uses it to stop cumulative refunds exceeding the original quantity. Non-null is the most reliable marker of a refund line, more reliable than sign alone (rebate lines are also negative-valued). NULL on ordinary lines.

dimensions.label: shop id
dimensions.description: Shop where the line was added. Normally equal to the parent sale's shopID, but it is stored per line, so a cross-shop ticket is representable and line-level location splits can disagree with sale-level ones.

dimensions.label: tax category id
dimensions.description: TaxCategory applied to this line — the jurisdiction-level container that sits above TaxClass. Together they resolve tax1_rate/tax2_rate.

dimensions.label: item fee id
dimensions.description: The ItemFee this line represents, when the line is a fee rather than merchandise (e.g. a recycling or environmental levy attached by category). Non-null means this row is a surcharge: it inflates unit counts and distorts average selling price if treated as a product.

dimensions.label: line type
dimensions.description: Descriptor of what the line represents. Explicitly NOT a discriminator for layaway/special-order/workorder — the docs say so outright, and using it that way returns zero rows. Use is_layaway / is_special_order / is_workorder for those, and line_type only to isolate item-fee rows.

dimensions.label: require full reservation
dimensions.description: Request-payload-only flag that makes a write FAIL if there is not enough inventory to reserve the whole unitQuantity. Layaway lines only, defaults false. It carries no analytical meaning on read — expect it absent or false on every stored row and never filter on it.

dimensions.label: completed
dimensions.description: Parent sale completion flag, projected so a line maps standalone.

dimensions.label: voided
dimensions.description: Parent sale voided flag, projected so a line maps standalone.

dimensions.label: complete time
dimensions.description: Parent sale completion time, projected for trading-date attribution.

dimensions.label: sale payment id
dimensions.description: Unique numeric id for this tender line. The reference calls it 'the unique numerical ID for the payment type', which is a documentation error — it identifies the PAYMENT, not the payment type (that is payment_type_id). Target of ref_payment_id on reversals and of ls_processing_fees.sale_payment_id.

dimensions.label: create time
dimensions.description: When the payment was taken, store-local. On layaways and on-account sales this can be far later than the sale's createTime and is the correct date for 'takings by day' / cash-up reconciliation, whereas revenue uses the sale's complete_time.

dimensions.label: archived
dimensions.description: Archived payments are effectively voided and, per the docs, must NOT count toward totals. This is INDEPENDENT of the parent sale's voided flag: a perfectly live sale can carry an archived (reversed and re-taken) payment. Filter archived = false on every takings figure or you count reversed tenders twice.

dimensions.label: remote reference
dimensions.description: Optional client-generated unique identifier supplied by an integration when creating the payment — an idempotency key for reconciling against an external system. Empty for POS-entered payments; not a Lightspeed identifier and not guaranteed unique unless the integration enforces it.

dimensions.label: payment id
dimensions.description: Reference to the charge held by the payment SERVICE (the processor's own handle). A string despite the -ID suffix, and unrelated to sale_payment_id — never join or cast it numerically.

dimensions.label: sale id
dimensions.description: The sale this payment settles. Join to ls_sales for the completed/voided filters — this table has none of its own.

dimensions.label: payment type id
dimensions.description: Tender type of this payment or refund (Cash, Credit Card, Gift Card, Credit Account, ...). The tender-mix dimension; the PaymentType reference table lives in the org domain. Its value is what flips the sign convention on amount when credit_account_id is set.

dimensions.label: cc charge id
dimensions.description: The CCCharge (gateway transaction) backing this payment, when the card ran through Lightspeed's integrated processing. VERIFIED LIVE: NULL/0 on every card payment at stores using an external EFTPOS terminal — absence does NOT mean the payment was not a card.

dimensions.label: ref payment id
dimensions.description: Points at the ORIGINAL salePaymentID this row reverses; set when refunding a previous credit card charge. The only reliable way to pair a refund tender with the payment it reverses — matching on amount and card last-four is guesswork.

dimensions.label: register id
dimensions.description: Register the payment was received at. Can legitimately differ from the parent sale's registerID — a layaway instalment is often paid at a different till from where the ticket was opened, which is why cash-ups must group by THIS column, not the sale's.

dimensions.label: employee id
dimensions.description: Employee who received the payment; may differ from the employee who rang the sale. Use this for till accountability and the sale's employee_id for sales attribution.

dimensions.label: credit account id
dimensions.description: The CreditAccount (store credit or gift card) this deposit/withdrawal applies to. Sign semantics are documented and easy to invert: with paymentType = Credit Account, POSITIVE amount = debit FROM the account (customer spends stored value), NEGATIVE = deposit TO it. With Cash/Check/Credit Card and this set, a positive amount is a REFUND of the customer's deposit paid out in that tender.

dimensions.label: completed
dimensions.description: Parent sale completion flag, projected so a payment maps standalone.

dimensions.label: voided
dimensions.description: Parent sale voided flag, projected so a payment maps standalone.

dimensions.label: complete time
dimensions.description: Parent sale completion time, projected for trading-date attribution.

dimensions.label: shop id
dimensions.description: Parent sale shop, projected because a payment carries no location of its own.

dimensions.label: sale account id
dimensions.description: Primary key of the link record. Has no business meaning on its own — it exists only to identify the association.

dimensions.label: credit account id
dimensions.description: The CreditAccount (gift card / store credit account) used in the SalePayment. This is the identity of the physical gift card, and the key that lets you follow one card's balance across issue, top-up and redemption on different sales.

dimensions.label: sale payment id
dimensions.description: The SalePayment linked to the sale line — specifically the NEGATIVE-amount payment that created or topped up the gift card. Relationship is documented one-to-one, so this is effectively an alternate key: at most one SaleAccount per payment.

dimensions.label: sale line id
dimensions.description: The SaleLine that sold the gift card. This is the half that makes the record useful: pairing the line (what was sold) with the payment (money in) is the ONLY reliable way to classify a gift-card issue versus a redemption.

dimensions.label: sale payment signature id
dimensions.description: Primary key of the signature record. Addressable at SalePayment/{salePaymentID}/SalePaymentSignature/{id} — it is a child resource of the payment, not a top-level collection.

dimensions.label: create time
dimensions.description: When the signature was captured, store-local. Normally within seconds of the payment's createTime; a large gap indicates a signature added retrospectively, which is exactly what a chargeback investigation cares about.

dimensions.label: sale payment id
dimensions.description: The payment this signature was captured for — the ONLY link this table has to the rest of the domain. There is no sale_id, so reaching the sale requires going through ls_sale_payments.

dimensions.label: inventory sale id
dimensions.description: Unique numeric identifier for the allocation. The only field on this object that is stable — quantity is rewritten in place while the parent line is open.

dimensions.label: create time
dimensions.description: When the allocation or reservation was made, store-local. For a layaway this is when stock was ring-fenced, which can precede the sale completing by months — so it is the right date for 'how long has this stock been tied up' and the wrong date for COGS periods.

dimensions.label: inventory id
dimensions.description: The Inventory lot the units were pulled from. The join key into the inventory domain and the reason this table exists: it is the only published link between a sale line and the specific cost lot behind its FIFO cost.

dimensions.label: sale line id
dimensions.description: The sale line this allocation belongs to. NOT a field on the InventorySale object itself — it is carried down from the explode parent. Without it the row has no grain and no meaning, which is why this object cannot be loaded from a standalone collection.

dimensions.label: sale id
dimensions.description: The sale the allocation ultimately belongs to, carried down from the top-level Sale envelope. Denormalised purely so allocations can be filtered by sale state without a second hop through ls_sale_lines.

dimensions.label: sale void id
dimensions.description: Unique numeric id of the void record. Note the resource is keyed on the VOID, not the sale, so counting rows is not the same as counting voided sales.

dimensions.label: create time
dimensions.description: When the void happened, store-local. This is the VOID date, not the original sale date — a ticket rung Monday and voided Tuesday appears in Monday's sales history and Tuesday's void report. Use it for 'voids by day/shift/staff member'.

dimensions.label: reason
dimensions.description: Free-text note the operator gave for the void. No enum — values are whatever staff typed, including empty. Loss-prevention gold: blank or boilerplate reasons on high-value voids are the classic fraud signal, so never coalesce empty to a placeholder before analysing.

dimensions.label: sale id
dimensions.description: The sale that was voided; joins ls_sales where voided = true. Because the resource is keyed on saleVoidID, a sale can in principle carry more than one void record — COUNT(DISTINCT sale_id), not COUNT(*), when counting voided sales.

dimensions.label: employee id
dimensions.description: Employee who PERFORMED the void — frequently NOT the employee who rang the original sale (that is ls_sales.employee_id). Comparing the two is the standard void-abuse check, and treating this as the seller misattributes every manager override.

dimensions.label: shop id
dimensions.description: Shop where the void was performed. Can differ from the original sale's shopID when a void is processed at a different location, so location-based void rates must decide which of the two they mean.

dimensions.label: cc charge id
dimensions.description: Unique numeric id for the charge attempt. ls_sale_payments.cc_charge_id joins here. Existence of a row does not imply money moved — check declined, voided and auth_only.

dimensions.label: gateway trans id
dimensions.description: The processor's own transaction id — the key for reconciling against a merchant statement. Opaque string whose format varies by gateway, so never parse it or assume it is numeric.

dimensions.label: response
dimensions.description: Raw response received from the gateway. Documented as possibly XML, a URL, or another format — unparsed, bulky, and not analytics data. VERIFIED LIVE caveat: the docs' own sample response returns this blob under the key `rawResponse`, so extraction against `response` can yield NULL on some accounts.

dimensions.label: voided
dimensions.description: The charge was voided AT THE GATEWAY before settlement — no money ever moved. INDEPENDENT of Sale.voided: a gateway-voided charge can sit under a perfectly live sale (the customer simply re-tapped) and a voided sale can contain a settled charge that was refunded separately.

dimensions.label: amount
dimensions.description: The original amount authorised/captured on the card. The current remaining balance of the charge is amount - refunded. Includes any tip that was added at the terminal, so it can exceed the sale total.

dimensions.label: auth only
dimensions.description: True when the transaction was an AUTHORISATION HOLD only and was never captured. No money settled. Counting auth-only rows as takings inflates card revenue, and they are common on pre-auth flows (workshop deposits, hire bonds).

dimensions.label: auth code
dimensions.description: Authorisation code returned by the gateway on approval. Presence is a weak approval signal; use declined = false as the actual test.

dimensions.label: time stamp
dimensions.description: When the record was last modified, store-local. The closest thing to a charge timestamp this resource exposes, but it MOVES when a refund is later applied — so it is not the original charge time. For the payment date use ls_sale_payments.create_time.

dimensions.label: declined
dimensions.description: True when the gateway declined the charge. DECLINED ATTEMPTS STILL CREATE ROWS. Settled card money requires declined = false AND voided = false AND auth_only = false — omitting any one of the three overstates card volume.

dimensions.label: sale id
dimensions.description: The sale this card payment belongs to. A single sale can have many charges (retries after declines, split tender, tip adjustments), so this is many-to-one.

dimensions.label: entry method
dimensions.description: CONFLICTED FIELD: the reference documents it as 'The card type: Visa, Mastercard, etc.' while the field name says how the card was presented (swipe/chip/contactless/keyed). One of the two is wrong. Treat values as untrusted until observed on a live gateway-integrated account, and never build a card-brand mix on it without verifying first.

dimensions.label: communication key
dimensions.description: Undescribed in the reference — gateway plumbing, most likely a credential or session handle. No analytical meaning, and it should be treated as a secret: never expose it in output or logs.

dimensions.label: sale payment processing fee id
dimensions.description: Unique identifier of the processing fee record. Note the sortable-fields list for this endpoint is truncated in the reference ('salePaymentProcessingFeeID, ---'), so assume this is the only safe sort key.

dimensions.label: sale payment id
dimensions.description: The SalePayment the fee was assessed on. The endpoint supports a direct ?salePaymentID= lookup, making per-payment fee retrieval cheap without a full scan.

dimensions.label: processing fee ref
dimensions.description: The processor's external reference id for this fee line — the key for tying a fee back to a line on a processor statement. Opaque; format is processor-specific.

dimensions.label: processor
dimensions.description: Name of the payment processor handling the transaction. Only populated for integrated-payments merchants, and the grouping dimension if an account has moved between processors — fee rates are not comparable across processors.

dimensions.label: fixed fee
dimensions.description: The fixed, per-transaction component of the fee, in store currency. Together with variable_fee this is the actual money the merchant lost on the payment.

dimensions.label: variable fee
dimensions.description: The rate-based component of the fee, in store currency. Total fee for the payment = fixed_fee + variable_fee; the interchange_* and scheme_* columns explain how that total was composed, they are not additional charges.

dimensions.label: interchange fees fixed fee
dimensions.description: Fixed portion of the interchange component (the part paid to the card-issuing bank). A BREAKDOWN of the total fee, not an addition to it — adding it to fixed_fee double counts.

dimensions.label: interchange fees variable fee
dimensions.description: Variable portion of interchange, in currency. Breakdown component; do not add it to variable_fee.

dimensions.label: interchange fees variable pct
dimensions.description: The rate behind the variable interchange portion. Same fraction-vs-percentage uncertainty as variable_pct — unverified live.

dimensions.label: scheme fees fixed fee
dimensions.description: Fixed portion of card-scheme fees (the part paid to the Visa/Mastercard network, distinct from interchange). Breakdown component.

dimensions.label: scheme fees variable fee
dimensions.description: Variable portion of card-scheme fees, in currency. Breakdown component.

dimensions.label: scheme fees variable pct
dimensions.description: The rate behind the variable scheme portion. Format unverified live, same caveat as variable_pct.

dimensions.label: processing time
dimensions.description: When the processor remotely processed the fee — the settlement-side date. It LAGS the payment date and determines which processor statement period the fee lands in, so statement reconciliation must use this column, not create_time.

dimensions.label: create time
dimensions.description: When the fee record was created inside Lightspeed. A sync artefact: it tracks when Lightspeed learned about the fee, not when the fee was charged.

dimensions.label: update time
dimensions.description: Last modification of the fee record. Fees CAN be restated by the processor after the fact, so a fee report re-run for a closed month may legitimately change — use this column to detect restatements.

dimensions.label: quote id
dimensions.description: Unique numeric id of the quote — the ONLY stable identifier here. ls_sales.quote_id back-references it when a quote is turned into a sale, and that reference is what conversion should be measured on.

dimensions.label: issue date
dimensions.description: When the quote was issued, store-local. The only date on the object: there is no expiry, no accepted-at and no converted-at field, so quote age can only be computed as issue_date to now, and 'time to convert' must come from the converted sale's complete_time.

dimensions.label: notes
dimensions.description: Free-text notes on the quote. Usually the ONLY human description of what was quoted, because the line detail lives on the linked sale — so this is what a rep actually reads when reopening a quote.

dimensions.label: archived
dimensions.description: True when the quote is retired. Archived does NOT mean lost: staff routinely archive quotes AFTER they convert as well as when they go cold. Open-pipeline questions need archived = false AND no completed sale referencing the quote — the flag alone is not a lost/won signal.

dimensions.label: employee id
dimensions.description: Employee who started the quote. The attribution for quote-pipeline-by-rep. Note this is who CREATED it — the employee who eventually completes the resulting sale is on ls_sales.employee_id and can be a different person.

dimensions.label: sale id
dimensions.description: The Sale record CURRENTLY holding this quote's contents. The reference states outright that a quote gets a NEW saleID every time it is modified, so this is a content pointer, not a conversion signal. Read the quote's value, customer and lines through it; measure conversion from ls_sales.quote_id on completed sales instead.

dimensions.label: discount id
dimensions.description: Unique numeric identifier for the discount rule. Both ls_sales.discount_id (deprecated, sale-level) and ls_sale_lines.discount_id (line-level) point here.

dimensions.label: name
dimensions.description: The merchant-defined description/name staff see when applying the rule. Names can carry trailing whitespace — TRIM before grouping or the same rule splits into two rows in every report.

dimensions.label: discount amount
dimensions.description: Dollar amount off, in store currency. A rule is EITHER an amount or a percentage, never both — the unused side sits at 0. Documented as required to be > 0.00 when this is the active side.

dimensions.label: require customer
dimensions.description: True when a customer must be attached to the sale before the rule can be applied (club, trade and loyalty rules). Explains why these discounts never appear on walk-in tickets, which otherwise looks like staff ignoring them.

dimensions.label: archived
dimensions.description: True when the rule is retired. VERIFIED LIVE: DELETE archives rather than deletes, and Discount.json accepts archived=true to retrieve them. Historical sales keep referencing archived rules, so an INNER join filtered to archived = false silently drops old markdowns from reports.

dimensions.label: source id
dimensions.description: What KIND of discount this is. Mislabelling a loyalty redemption (1) as a promotional markdown (2) misstates both gross margin and the cost of the loyalty programme, because loyalty is a redemption of a previously accrued liability rather than a price concession.

dimensions.label: time stamp
dimensions.description: When the rule record was last modified, store-local. It moves on every edit and can be bulk-set during a platform migration, so it is NOT reliable evidence of when the discount was introduced.

dimensions.label: item id
dimensions.description: Stable primary key of the SKU across the whole account; the join target for sale lines, stock rows, images, serial numbers and order lines. Survives archiving (items are never hard-deleted), so historical sale lines always resolve.

dimensions.label: system sku
dimensions.description: The barcode Lightspeed generates and prints on shelf labels (e.g. 210000000004). Documented as an integer but it is an identifier, never a quantity — store and compare as text or leading zeros and precision are lost. Read-only; distinct from custom_sku (the shop's own code) and upc/ean (the manufacturer's barcodes).

dimensions.label: taxable
dimensions.description: True when sales tax/GST is charged on this item at the register. Governs whether the price already carries tax in a tax-inclusive jurisdiction; get it wrong and margin on zero-rated goods is understated by the tax rate.

dimensions.label: archived
dimensions.description: True when the item has been retired. The published doc text for this field reads 'Whether this discount is archived' — a copy-paste error in the Lightspeed docs; it refers to the item. Archiving is the ONLY form of delete (a DELETE request archives) and it irreversibly zeroes the item's inventory. Cannot be set via update. Filter false for the live range.

dimensions.label: discountable
dimensions.description: True when cashiers may apply a discount to this line at the register. False on fixed-price or contract lines; explains why some items never appear in discount analysis.

dimensions.label: item type
dimensions.description: What kind of thing the SKU is, which decides whether its stock number means anything. non_inventory rows (labour, services, fees) carry stock quantities that are noise and must be excluded from unit and value totals. box/assembly rows are built from ls_item_components children.

dimensions.label: serialized
dimensions.description: True when every unit gets a serial number captured at sale. Independent of item_type — it may be true on any type — but must be true before item_type can be set to serialized or serialized_assembly. Serial records live in ls_serialized.

dimensions.label: description
dimensions.description: The product name printed on receipts and labels. For matrix variants Lightspeed composes it as '<matrix description> <attribute1> <attribute2> <attribute3>', so a LIKE on the family name catches every size/colour. Not a long marketing description — that is ecom_long_description.

dimensions.label: upc
dimensions.description: UPC barcode, 11-14 digits. Text, not a number: leading zeros are significant. Also one of the three values the itemCode single-read query matches against.

dimensions.label: ean
dimensions.description: EAN barcode, 11-14 digits — the international sibling of upc, usually empty when upc is populated. Also matched by the itemCode query.

dimensions.label: custom sku
dimensions.description: The shop's own internal SKU, entered by staff. Frequently empty and free-text, so never assume uniqueness or a format.

dimensions.label: manufacturer sku
dimensions.description: The manufacturer's own part number. The most reliable key for matching against supplier catalogues and price lists — join it to ls_catalog_vendor_items.manufacturer_number.

dimensions.label: updated at
dimensions.description: When the item RECORD was last edited. Documented to exclude changes to related records, so it does not move when stock, ItemShops or related prices change. Using it to find 'recently received' or 'recently sold' products is the classic wrong answer here — use the inventory movement log instead.

dimensions.label: created at
dimensions.description: When the SKU was first created in the catalogue. A good proxy for when the shop began ranging the product; unaffected by later edits.

dimensions.label: publish to ecom
dimensions.description: Flag requesting publication to Lightspeed eCom. A catalogue intent flag only — it is not proof the item is live on a webstore, and it is independent of ecom_list_on_store.

dimensions.label: category id
dimensions.description: The single category node this item hangs off, at any depth of the tree. 0 is written when uncategorised — map to NULL, otherwise uncategorised items join a non-existent category 0.

dimensions.label: tax class id
dimensions.description: Which tax class governs the item's rate. 0 when unset. Together with taxable it decides the effective rate; a wrong reading silently shifts tax-exclusive margin.

dimensions.label: item matrix id
dimensions.description: The variant family this SKU belongs to: all sizes/colours of one product share it. 0 (map to NULL) means a standalone item, not a variant. The key to collapsing variant rows into products.

dimensions.label: manufacturer id
dimensions.description: Who MAKES the product (brand). Not the supplier the shop buys from — that is default_vendor_id. 0 when unset.

dimensions.label: default vendor id
dimensions.description: The supplier the shop reorders this item from by default. A plain scalar field, NOT a loadable relation — there is no 'Vendor' load_relations name on Item. An item may have many vendor SKUs (ls_item_vendor_nums) but only one default vendor. 0 when unset.

dimensions.label: tax class json
dimensions.description: Raw tax-class object as returned. Kept as JSON because the ground truth publishes no field table for TaxClass, so no sub-field can be traced to a documented column. Read the rate/name out of it only after probing a live response.

dimensions.label: note json
dimensions.description: Raw note object attached to the item (staff notes; public notes also print on receipts). JSON because Note has no published field table. Usually absent.

dimensions.label: custom field values json
dimensions.description: Raw account-defined custom field values. Shape is account-specific and has no published field table, so it stays JSON — treat any key you find as unstable across accounts.

dimensions.label: attribute 1
dimensions.description: First variant axis VALUE for a matrix item, conventionally the colour. Meaningless without attribute_name_1, which names the axis. NULL for standalone items (the ItemAttributes subtree is absent).

dimensions.label: attribute 2
dimensions.description: Second variant axis value, conventionally the size. NULL for standalone items and for single-axis matrices.

dimensions.label: attribute 3
dimensions.description: Third variant axis value; only used by the '3 Attributes' attribute set. Almost always NULL.

dimensions.label: item attribute set id
dimensions.description: Which attribute-set definition explains this item's attribute_1/2/3. Documented as a string but it is a numeric FK to ls_item_attribute_sets. NULL/absent for non-variant items.

dimensions.label: attribute name 1
dimensions.description: Label for variant axis 1 (typically 'Color'). Pair with attribute_1 to render 'Color: Black'. Empty when the set does not use axis 1.

dimensions.label: attribute name 2
dimensions.description: Label for variant axis 2 (typically 'Size').

dimensions.label: attribute name 3
dimensions.description: Label for variant axis 3 ('Attribute 3'). Rarely populated.

dimensions.label: ecom item ecommerce id
dimensions.description: Id of the item's eCommerce info record. Its presence means an eCom record exists at all; NULL means the item was never given web content or dimensions.

dimensions.label: ecom long description
dimensions.description: Long-form marketing copy for the item. The docs explicitly note the itemECommerce fields are NOT used by Lightspeed eCommerce, so treat this as free-text storage, not as what a webstore renders.

dimensions.label: ecom short description
dimensions.description: Short marketing blurb. Same caveat: not consumed by Lightspeed eCommerce.

dimensions.label: weight
dimensions.description: Item weight. The API publishes no unit — it follows whatever the account entered (lb or kg), so never aggregate weights across an account without confirming the unit. 0 means unset.

dimensions.label: width
dimensions.description: Item width, unitless per the API — same unit caveat as weight. 0 means unset, not zero-width.

dimensions.label: height
dimensions.description: Item height, unitless per the API. 0 means unset.

dimensions.label: length
dimensions.description: Item length, unitless per the API. 0 means unset. This plus width/height/weight is the only place shipping dimensions exist in the catalogue.

dimensions.label: ecom list on store
dimensions.description: Whether the item is flagged to be sold online. Documented as not settable in the user interface, so it is often stale or false even on items that are for sale online. Distinct from publish_to_ecom.

dimensions.label: item shop id
dimensions.description: Primary key of this item-in-shop stock record. Either this or shopID must be supplied when writing an update, which is why it exists at all — analytically it is just a surrogate.

dimensions.label: item id
dimensions.description: The item this stock row belongs to. Also available on the parent Item envelope when exploding; joins ls_items.item_id.

dimensions.label: shop id
dimensions.description: The shop holding the stock — EXCEPT 0, which is documented as a summary record containing the QOH for all shops combined. 0 is a sentinel, not a location and not a null. Whole-business questions use shop_id = 0; per-shop breakdowns use shop_id > 0; using both double counts every unit in the account.

dimensions.label: sellable
dimensions.description: Units the POS will let you sell: identical to qoh except it clamps at 0 when qoh is negative. The gap (sellable - qoh) is therefore exactly the size of the negative-inventory problem for that item.

dimensions.label: backorder
dimensions.description: Units already committed on a purchase order but not yet received — 'on order' in shop language. Zero or positive only. Incoming stock, so it must not be added to qoh when reporting what is physically present.

dimensions.label: component backorder
dimensions.description: Additional units obtainable from boxes/assemblies that are currently on order rather than in stock. Doubly notional: potential units from stock that has not arrived. 0 for normal items.

dimensions.label: reorder point
dimensions.description: Threshold: when qoh is at or below this, the item is considered due for reorder in this shop. 0 means no reorder point was configured, NOT 'reorder at zero' — an unfiltered qoh <= reorder_point flags every out-of-stock item in the account.

dimensions.label: reorder level
dimensions.description: Target stock level to reach when reordering: an automatic reorder adds (reorder_level - qoh) units. Suggested order quantity is derived, never stored.

dimensions.label: updated at
dimensions.description: When this stock record last changed. Unlike ls_items.updated_at this DOES move on stock movements, making it the only freshness signal in the catalogue for inventory. It cannot be pushed down when scanning via the Item endpoint, whose timeStamp filter applies to the item record.

dimensions.label: item description
dimensions.description: Denormalised product name from the parent item, so stock rows are readable without a join.

dimensions.label: item archived
dimensions.description: Parent item's archived flag. Archived items were inventory-zeroed at archive time, so any non-zero stock on an archived row is historical noise.

dimensions.label: item type
dimensions.description: Parent item type, carried here because non_inventory rows must be excluded from every stock count and valuation — their quantities are meaningless.

dimensions.label: category id
dimensions.description: Parent item's category. Pushing this down makes category-scoped stock scans dramatically cheaper than filtering after the fact.

dimensions.label: manufacturer id
dimensions.description: Parent item's brand, for brand-level stock rollups without a join.

dimensions.label: item id
dimensions.description: The item the price belongs to. NOT unique in this table — each item contributes one row per configured level, so an unpinned join to ls_items multiplies item rows by the number of levels.

dimensions.label: use type id
dimensions.description: Numeric FK to the pricing level definition (ls_price_levels.price_level_id). The stable half of the key: use it for grouping because use_type names can be renamed by the account at any time.

dimensions.label: use type
dimensions.description: Human name of the price level, which also indicates how the level is applied. Documented behaviour: an amount set at this level OVERRIDES the amount that would otherwise be generated dynamically from cost via the level's calculation — so a stored row means someone pinned the price.

dimensions.label: item component id
dimensions.description: Primary key of the component line. Surrogate — the meaningful identity is (assembly_item_id, component_item_id, component_group).

dimensions.label: assembly item id
dimensions.description: The parent: the box or assembly item being built. Joins ls_items.item_id. Its item_type will be box, assembly or serialized_assembly.

dimensions.label: component item id
dimensions.description: The child: the single item consumed to build the parent. Joins ls_items.item_id. Also the row you would deduct stock from when a box is broken down.

dimensions.label: item vendor num id
dimensions.description: Primary key of the item-vendor cross-reference row.

dimensions.label: item id
dimensions.description: The shop's item this vendor SKU refers to. Joins ls_items.item_id. Not unique here — one item can be stocked by several vendors.

dimensions.label: vendor id
dimensions.description: The supplier that uses this SKU. Joins the Vendor/supplier domain. Compare with ls_items.default_vendor_id to see whether the shop buys from the cheapest listed source.

dimensions.label: vendor sku
dimensions.description: The vendor's own part number for the item — the string you put on a purchase order. Free text: formats differ per supplier and duplicates across vendors are normal.

dimensions.label: updated at
dimensions.description: When this cross-reference row was last modified. The freshest available signal of when a supplier's price for the item was last touched.

dimensions.label: item matrix id
dimensions.description: Primary key of the variant family. ls_items.item_matrix_id points here; ls_images.item_matrix_id attaches family-level photos here.

dimensions.label: description
dimensions.description: Family-level product name. Documented composition rule: each child item's description is '<this description> <attribute1> <attribute2> <attribute3>', so this string is the stable prefix for matching every variant.

dimensions.label: item type
dimensions.description: Type default inherited by the family's items. Same enumeration as ls_items.item_type; the authoritative value for stock logic is on the child item, not here.

dimensions.label: serialized
dimensions.description: True when units in this family carry serial numbers (typical for bike model families). Must be true before item_type can be serialized or serialized_assembly.

dimensions.label: taxable
dimensions.description: Whether tax is charged on this family's items. A default; the child item's own flag is what the register applies.

dimensions.label: model year
dimensions.description: Model year of the family (e.g. 2024). Stored as 0 when unset — map to NULL before filtering by year.

dimensions.label: archived
dimensions.description: True when the family is retired. The published doc text says 'Whether this discount is archived', a copy-paste error — it refers to the matrix. Archiving the family does not by itself guarantee every child item is archived; check ls_items too.

dimensions.label: category id
dimensions.description: Category default for the family. 0 when unset. Children may sit in a different category, so category rollups should use the item rows.

dimensions.label: tax class id
dimensions.description: Tax class default for the family. 0 when unset.

dimensions.label: manufacturer id
dimensions.description: Brand of the family (who makes it), not the supplier. 0 when unset.

dimensions.label: default vendor id
dimensions.description: Default supplier for the family. 0 when unset.

dimensions.label: item attribute set id
dimensions.description: Which attribute-set definition shapes the family's variant axes (Color/Size, Size, Color, 3 Attributes). Documented as a string but it is a numeric FK to ls_item_attribute_sets. Tells you how many axes the children actually use.

dimensions.label: updated at
dimensions.description: When the matrix record was last modified. There is NO createTime on ItemMatrix (unlike Item), so family age is not directly knowable — approximate it with MIN(created_at) of the child items.

dimensions.label: attribute name 1
dimensions.description: Label of the family's first variant axis (typically 'Color'); pairs with ls_items.attribute_1 on the children.

dimensions.label: attribute name 2
dimensions.description: Label of the second variant axis (typically 'Size').

dimensions.label: attribute name 3
dimensions.description: Label of the third variant axis; only meaningful for the '3 Attributes' set.

dimensions.label: tax class json
dimensions.description: Raw tax-class object. JSON because the ground truth publishes no field table for TaxClass — no sub-field can be traced to a documented column.

dimensions.label: custom field values json
dimensions.description: Raw account-defined custom field values on the matrix. Shape is account-specific with no published field table, so it stays JSON.

dimensions.label: item attribute set id
dimensions.description: Primary key. ls_items.item_attribute_set_id and ls_item_matrices.item_attribute_set_id point here (both are documented as strings on those objects but are numeric ids).

dimensions.label: name
dimensions.description: Name of the set. Documented as a closed vocabulary — 'Color/Size', 'Size', 'Color', '3 Attributes' are the only allowed values for now, so it is safe to branch on but not to treat as extensible.

dimensions.label: attribute name 1
dimensions.description: Label for the first axis — documented as 'Color' or the generic 'Attribute 1'. Read alongside an item's attribute_1 value to render a variant properly.

dimensions.label: attribute name 2
dimensions.description: Label for the second axis — documented as 'Size' or 'Attribute 2'. Empty for single-axis sets such as 'Color'.

dimensions.label: attribute name 3
dimensions.description: Label for the third axis — 'Attribute 3'. Only populated for the '3 Attributes' set.

dimensions.label: item fee id
dimensions.description: Primary key of the fee definition.

dimensions.label: name
dimensions.description: Fee name as shown at the register and on the receipt line. The only way to recognise the fee's sale lines, since sale lines carry no itemFeeID.

dimensions.label: calculation method
dimensions.description: How the fee amount is derived. Currently only fixed_amount exists, so fee_value is always a flat per-item charge — do not build percentage logic against this field.

dimensions.label: taxable
dimensions.description: True when tax is charged ON the fee itself. Misreading it shifts the tax base on every transaction that carries the fee, which is why it is load bearing despite being configuration.

dimensions.label: archived
dimensions.description: True when the fee is retired and can no longer be used within a transaction. Historical sale lines from before archiving still exist, so archived fees still appear in past revenue.

dimensions.label: created at
dimensions.description: When the fee was configured — the earliest date its sale lines can appear.

dimensions.label: updated at
dimensions.description: When the fee was last updated. Note the raw API field is lowercase 'timestamp' on this endpoint alone; every other object in this domain uses 'timeStamp'. A case-sensitive extractor written for the rest of the domain silently returns NULL here.

dimensions.label: item fee categories json
dimensions.description: Raw list of the item categories the fee attaches to. Kept as JSON because the ground truth publishes no field table for ItemFeeCategories; the category ids inside can be matched against ls_categories only after probing a live response.

dimensions.label: image id
dimensions.description: Primary key of the image record.

dimensions.label: item id
dimensions.description: The single item this photo belongs to, or NULL/0 when the photo is attached at matrix level instead. Exactly one of item_id and item_matrix_id is meaningful on any row.

dimensions.label: item matrix id
dimensions.description: The variant family this photo belongs to, or NULL/0 when it is attached to a single item. A matrix-level photo implicitly covers every variant in the family, which is why coverage checks must test both columns.

dimensions.label: description
dimensions.description: Caption or alt text for the image. Usually empty in real data; do not rely on it for search.

dimensions.label: filename
dimensions.description: Original filename of the upload. Its extension indicates the source format, which is not necessarily the format Cloudinary serves.

dimensions.label: ordering
dimensions.description: Display sequence among a product's images. The lowest ordering is the primary/hero photo — ties are possible, so break them with image_id for determinism.

dimensions.label: public id
dimensions.description: The Cloudinary public id used to retrieve the image. It is not a URL by itself: it must be concatenated onto the Cloudinary base URL with a file extension to resolve.

dimensions.label: serialized id
dimensions.description: Primary key of the serial record.

dimensions.label: serial
dimensions.description: The serial number stamped on the unit. Frequently an EMPTY STRING in real data because staff logged the machine without reading the number — filtering serial <> '' silently drops most of a customer's units. Match case-insensitively and trimmed.

dimensions.label: description
dimensions.description: Free-text identity used when the record is NOT connected to a catalogue item — typically a customer's own bike ('black planet x'). For service-heavy stores this is the only identity most rows have.

dimensions.label: color name
dimensions.description: Colour of the unit as typed by staff. Free text, often empty, unrelated to the matrix attribute vocabulary.

dimensions.label: size name
dimensions.description: Size of the unit (frame size for bikes) as typed by staff. Free text, often empty; not the matrix Size attribute.

dimensions.label: item id
dimensions.description: The catalogue item this serial is an instance of, when the unit was sold from stock. Stored as 0 (map to NULL) for customer-owned units logged free-text — which is the MAJORITY of rows in service-heavy stores, so an inner join to ls_items quietly hides most customer machines.

dimensions.label: sale line id
dimensions.description: The sale line where this unit was sold, or 0/NULL if it never went through the POS. Join it to recover the sale date, price and salesperson for the specific physical unit.

dimensions.label: updated at
dimensions.description: When the record last changed. A rough proxy for when the unit was last touched in the system (sold, serviced, re-tagged), not when it was manufactured or acquired.

dimensions.label: tag id
dimensions.description: Primary key of the tag.

dimensions.label: name
dimensions.description: The tag text itself. Free text entered by staff, so typos and near-duplicates are normal; VERIFIED LIVE stores often adopt a 'group:value' convention (color:black, size:318mm, year:2018) that the API does not enforce or parse.

dimensions.label: name
dimensions.description: The tag group's name. The only usable key: no numeric id is published for tag groups, so renaming a group breaks any stored reference. Undocumented type — inferred as a string from the example payload.

dimensions.label: manufacturer id
dimensions.description: Primary key of the brand. ls_items.manufacturer_id and ls_item_matrices.manufacturer_id point here.

dimensions.label: name
dimensions.description: Brand name. VERIFIED LIVE: real accounts have inconsistent casing (VITTORIA vs Elite) and occasional duplicate rows for the same brand — group on UPPER(TRIM(name)) or a single brand splits across several ids.

dimensions.label: created at
dimensions.description: When the brand was added to the account. A reasonable proxy for when the shop started ranging that brand — earlier than any of its items' created_at.

dimensions.label: updated at
dimensions.description: When the brand record was last modified (typically a rename). Does not move when the brand's items change.

dimensions.label: category id
dimensions.description: Primary key of the node. ls_items.category_id and ls_item_matrices.category_id point here.

dimensions.label: name
dimensions.description: The node's OWN name only, not its path (e.g. 'Service'). Ambiguous across branches — several branches can each contain a 'Parts' — so grouping by name silently merges unrelated categories.

dimensions.label: full path name
dimensions.description: Slash-delimited path from the root to this node (e.g. 'Workshop/Service'). The standard rollup key: LIKE 'Bikes%' selects an entire subtree, which category_id alone cannot do because items attach at any depth. Precomputed by Lightspeed, so it goes stale only when the tree is reshuffled.

dimensions.label: parent id
dimensions.description: The node directly above this one. 0 (map to NULL) marks a top-level category. Recursive CTEs walk this; for a single-query subtree filter, full_path_name is cheaper.

dimensions.label: node depth
dimensions.description: How many ancestors the node has: 0 = top level, 1 = one parent, and so on. Documented with type string — cast before numeric comparison. Equals the number of '/' separators in full_path_name.

dimensions.label: left node
dimensions.description: Nested-set left bound. A node's descendants all have left_node strictly between this node's left_node and right_node — the O(1) subtree test. Renumbered wholesale when the tree is edited, so never persist it as a key.

dimensions.label: right node
dimensions.description: Nested-set right bound, the closing partner of left_node. (right_node - left_node - 1) / 2 gives the descendant count without a join.

dimensions.label: created at
dimensions.description: When the node was created.

dimensions.label: updated at
dimensions.description: When the node was last modified. Tree reshuffles renumber left/right bounds across MANY nodes at once, so a burst of identical updated_at values means a restructure, not real editing.

dimensions.label: name
dimensions.description: The option's identifier. The only available key: no numeric id is published for Option, so a renamed option breaks any stored reference. The set of legal names is not documented anywhere in the ground truth.

dimensions.label: value
dimensions.description: The option's value, always delivered as a string even when it represents a boolean or a number. Cast explicitly and never rely on truthiness — '0' and 'false' are both non-empty strings.

dimensions.label: price level id
dimensions.description: Primary key of the price level. ls_item_prices.use_type_id is documented as the foreign key for the pricing level and resolves here.

dimensions.label: name
dimensions.description: Display name of the level (Default, MSRP, Online, or an account-defined label). Renameable, so never key logic on the string — use price_level_id.

dimensions.label: archived
dimensions.description: True when the level is retired. Archived levels can still appear on existing ls_item_prices rows, so an archived level does not mean the amounts vanished.

dimensions.label: can be archived
dimensions.description: Whether Lightspeed permits archiving this level — false on built-in levels such as Default. Documented as having NO effect when set, so it is a read-only capability hint, not a control.

dimensions.label: type
dimensions.description: The kind of price level. Documented as an enumeration but the ground truth publishes no member list, so treat observed values as account-specific until confirmed against a live response.

dimensions.label: calculation json
dimensions.description: Raw parameters used to derive a price from cost (markup/margin rules). Kept as JSON because the ground truth publishes no field table for Calculation. It explains the documented ItemPrice behaviour: a stored amount OVERRIDES the amount this calculation would otherwise generate — so an item with no explicit amount is priced by these rules, not by a NULL.

dimensions.label: catalog vendor item id
dimensions.description: Primary key of the catalogue entry. Also the id you POST to import the entry and create an Item in the account — so it is a write handle, not just an analytic key.

dimensions.label: catalog vendor id
dimensions.description: Which vendor CATALOGUE the entry belongs to. This is a catalogue-service id, NOT the account's own vendor/supplier id — joining it to the supplier domain produces silently wrong attributions. Unless specified, queries are limited to the catalogues currently configured for the account.

dimensions.label: vendor number
dimensions.description: The part number the VENDOR assigns — what goes on a purchase order to that supplier. Join it to ls_item_vendor_nums.vendor_sku.

dimensions.label: manufacturer number
