dimensions.description: The part number the MANUFACTURER assigns. The most reliable key for matching a catalogue entry to ls_items.manufacturer_sku, because it survives changing supplier.

dimensions.label: description
dimensions.description: Name/description of the product as the vendor writes it. Will not match the shop's own item description; do not use it as a join key.

dimensions.label: category
dimensions.description: The VENDOR's suggested category as free text (e.g. 'Trunk Racks'). It is not a node in the shop's tree and does not join ls_categories.

dimensions.label: brand
dimensions.description: Brand of the product per the catalogue. Compare against ls_manufacturers.name for range-gap analysis, with the same casing caveats.

dimensions.label: model
dimensions.description: Model designation; the docs note it is usually a year. Overlaps confusingly with the separate 'year' field, which is also a model year — expect one or the other to be populated, not both.

dimensions.label: year
dimensions.description: Model year of the item as text (not a number, so no arithmetic or range filters without casting). Often empty; see also 'model'.

dimensions.label: upc
dimensions.description: Universal Product Code. The other reliable join key to ls_items.upc — compare as TEXT, since leading zeros are significant and numeric casting corrupts the match.

dimensions.label: ean
dimensions.description: International Article Number for the entry; the international counterpart of upc.

dimensions.label: ean2
dimensions.description: An alternate EAN. Its existence means a barcode match must test upc, ean AND ean2 before concluding the shop does not stock the product.

dimensions.label: color name
dimensions.description: Colour as published by the vendor. Free text — unrelated to matrix attribute vocabularies, so do not expect it to match ls_items.attribute_1.

dimensions.label: size name
dimensions.description: Size as published by the vendor. Same caveat: free text, not the matrix Size attribute.

dimensions.label: unit of measurement
dimensions.description: How multiple quantities are grouped for ordering — EA, box, pair. The label that explains retail_unit.

dimensions.label: cost level 3
dimensions.description: Second discounted cost tier. 0 means not published.

dimensions.label: cost level 4
dimensions.description: Final discounted cost tier — the best published terms. 0 means not published.

dimensions.label: break qty
dimensions.description: Order quantity at which the first bulk price break applies. 0 = no break published.

dimensions.label: break price
dimensions.description: Unit price once at least break_qty is ordered. Documented as the price for items ABOVE breakQty — a step function, not a discount percentage.

dimensions.label: break qty 2
dimensions.description: Second bulk break quantity. 0 = none published.

dimensions.label: break price 2
dimensions.description: Unit cost at the second break quantity. The docs call it the 'cost of breakQty2' — it is a per-unit figure at that tier, not a line total.

dimensions.label: break qty 3
dimensions.description: Third bulk break quantity. 0 = none published.

dimensions.label: break price 3
dimensions.description: Unit cost at the third break quantity.

dimensions.label: status
dimensions.description: The vendor's lifecycle status for the entry. VERIFIED LIVE: 'current' is the common value; anything else generally signals a discontinued or superseded line, which is when replacement becomes meaningful.

dimensions.label: replacement
dimensions.description: Vendor part number of the suggested successor when this entry is superseded. A pointer into vendor_number within the same catalogue — the supersession chain can be walked by self-joining.

dimensions.label: replacement description
dimensions.description: Description of the suggested replacement. VERIFIED LIVE: often a terse marker such as 'SUBSTITUTE' rather than a product name, so it is not a substitute for looking the replacement part number up.

dimensions.label: last price change
dimensions.description: When the vendor last changed pricing on this entry. Documented as a date, but VERIFIED LIVE the API sends a full datetime — parse as a timestamp. The freshest signal of supplier cost inflation.

dimensions.label: archived
dimensions.description: True when the catalogue entry itself is archived. Independent of ls_items.archived — the shop may still stock a product the vendor has retired.

dimensions.label: catalog vendor json
dimensions.description: Raw catalogue-owner object. Kept as JSON because the ground truth publishes no field table for CatalogVendor. VERIFIED LIVE: it arrives inline without requesting the relation and carries a human-readable catalogue name.

dimensions.label: inventory log id
dimensions.description: Unique id of the movement event. Monotonically ascending with time, so it is the correct tiebreaker when two movements share a created_at to the second.

dimensions.label: created at
dimensions.description: When the stock change happened, store-local time. The real event clock of this table — always range-filter on it. VERIFIED LIVE: usable as a server-side pushdown filter even though the docs list only inventoryLogID and itemID as sortable.

dimensions.label: automated
dimensions.description: true when Lightspeed itself made the change (a sale deducting stock, a PO receive posting); false when a human typed an adjustment. automated = false with every document FK null is the signature of 'someone edited stock by hand' — the first place to look for shrinkage.

dimensions.label: reason
dimensions.description: Machine-named cause of the change. These are internal method names, not a tidy business enum, and the vocabulary differs by account — GROUP BY reason to discover what exists before hard-coding a filter. Classify movements on the document FK columns first and use reason only to sub-classify.

dimensions.label: caused negative
dimensions.description: true when this specific event pushed the item's on-hand below zero in that shop — the exact moment an oversell happened. A data-hygiene flag, not a movement measure: never sum or net it against qoh_change.

dimensions.label: employee id
dimensions.description: Employee who made or triggered the change. The accountability column for adjustment and shrinkage questions. 0/NULL on purely system-generated rows, so absence does not mean 'unknown staff member', it means 'no staff member'.

dimensions.label: item id
dimensions.description: Item whose stock changed. Joins the catalogue item table. VERIFIED LIVE: arrives as 0 rather than null on non-item events (cancelled special orders observed) — normalise 0 to NULL or an inner join to the catalogue silently deletes those rows from your result.

dimensions.label: shop id
dimensions.description: Shop where the change happened; 0/NULL means unattributed. Do NOT carry over the ItemShop convention where shopID 0 is the account-wide aggregate row — this log has no aggregate rows, so summing every row here is correct whereas summing every ItemShop row double counts.

dimensions.label: order id
dimensions.description: Purchase order whose receiving caused the change. A supplier PO id from the purchasing domain — never a sale id, despite 'order' being the retail word for a customer order in other systems. Non-null with positive qoh_change = goods inwards.

dimensions.label: transfer id
dimensions.description: Inter-shop transfer that caused the change. One transfer produces at least two rows at different times: a negative at the origin shop when sent and a positive at the destination when received. Netting them to zero across shops is expected, not an error.

dimensions.label: sale id
dimensions.description: Sale that caused the change. Set for both directions — a sale consuming stock (negative) and a refund returning it (positive) — so read the sign of qoh_change, not the presence of this id, to tell them apart.

dimensions.label: inventory count id
dimensions.description: Stocktake that caused the change. Non-null rows are count corrections and are the raw material of a shrinkage report. There is no InventoryCount header object anywhere in the R-Series inventory docs, so this id is groupable but not resolvable to a count's name, shop or date.

dimensions.label: vendor return id
dimensions.description: Vendor return (RMA) that caused the change: stock sent back to a supplier, so qoh_change is normally negative. No VendorReturn object is documented in this domain, so treat it as an opaque grouping id rather than a joinable key.

dimensions.label: item import id
dimensions.description: Bulk item import that caused the change — a spreadsheet load setting stock levels. Big clusters of rows sharing one item_import_id are data migrations, not trading activity; exclude them from shrinkage, receiving and movement analysis or a single import will dwarf a year of real movement.

dimensions.label: inventory count calc id
dimensions.description: Unique id of this item's rollup within a count. Surrogate only — the meaningful key is (inventory_count_id, item_id).

dimensions.label: updated at
dimensions.description: Modified date/time of this rollup: the last time a count entry was recorded for THIS item in THIS count. A per-item watermark inside the count, not the count's start date, not its end date and not the reconcile date.

dimensions.label: inventory count id
dimensions.description: The stocktake this rollup belongs to. Groupable but not resolvable: no InventoryCount header object is documented, so the count's name, shop, status and date are unavailable in this domain.

dimensions.label: item id
dimensions.description: The item this rollup is for. Joins the catalogue item table for description, category and cost so variance can be valued.

dimensions.label: inventory count item id
dimensions.description: Unique id of this single count entry.

dimensions.label: counted at
dimensions.description: The date/time at which the count was made. The only genuine event clock in the count tables (the calc table's timestamp is a rollup watermark), so use it to measure how long a stocktake took and when each aisle was walked.

dimensions.label: inventory count id
dimensions.description: The stocktake this entry belongs to. No count header object exists in the docs, so this is a grouping id only.

dimensions.label: item id
dimensions.description: The item that was counted. Joins the catalogue item table.

dimensions.label: employee id
dimensions.description: Employee who physically made this count entry. The accountability trail: pair it with the resulting reconcile variance to find who is counting badly or who was on the floor when a discrepancy appeared.

dimensions.label: inventory count reconcile id
dimensions.description: Unique id of this reconcile posting.

dimensions.label: reconciled at
dimensions.description: When the reconcile was performed — the moment the books actually moved. This is the event date for shrinkage reporting; the counting itself happened earlier (ls_inventory_count_items.counted_at), sometimes much earlier.

dimensions.label: inventory count id
dimensions.description: The stocktake being reconciled. Group by it to price a whole count's shrinkage. No count header object is documented, so the id is not resolvable to a count name or shop.

dimensions.label: item id
dimensions.description: The item adjusted. Note the write-side asymmetry: a POST WITH itemID reconciles only that item, a POST WITHOUT itemID reconciles the entire count and produces a row per item.

dimensions.label: transfer id
dimensions.description: Unique id of the transfer document. Joins ls_transfer_items.transfer_id and ls_inventory_logs.transfer_id.

dimensions.label: is sent
dimensions.description: true once the origin store has dispatched the transfer. Renamed from the API's plain 'sent' to avoid a dangerous collision: TransferItem.sent is a QUANTITY while this is a flag. is_sent AND NOT is_received = stock in transit, sitting on nobody's shelf.

dimensions.label: is received
dimensions.description: true once the receiving store has checked the transfer in. Stock levels do not change until this happens — an unreceived transfer's units are still counted at the origin shop's on-hand, which is why unreceived transfers make two shops' stock look wrong at once.

dimensions.label: note
dimensions.description: Free-text note for the store. The docs type this field 'integer', which is a documentation error — the same docs describe it as 'Text notes for the store'. Treat as text and cast defensively.

dimensions.label: archived
dimensions.description: true when the transfer is filed away as done. Documented as 'integer' but behaves as a 0/1 flag. Means finished/hidden, NOT cancelled — there is no cancelled state, so an abandoned transfer is indistinguishable from one that was never started. Filter archived = false for the live worklist.

dimensions.label: transfer from id
dimensions.description: Key of the origin-side sub-record whose three payload fields are flattened onto this row as sent_on, sent_by_employee_id and from_shop_id. Rarely useful directly; kept so the API shape is traceable.

dimensions.label: transfer to id
dimensions.description: Key of the destination-side sub-record, flattened onto this row as need_by, received_by_employee_id and to_shop_id. Rarely useful directly.

dimensions.label: order id
dimensions.description: Purchase Order this transfer was attached to for centralized ordering (head office buys once, then transfers stock out to shops). A supplier purchase order id from the purchasing domain, never a sale. NULL for ordinary shop-to-shop transfers, and non-null rows should not be double counted as separate procurement.

dimensions.label: sent on
dimensions.description: Date/time the transfer left the origin shop. The genuine event date for outbound flow — bucket transfers by this, never by updated_at. NULL while the transfer is still being picked.

dimensions.label: sent by employee id
dimensions.description: Employee who sent the transfer from the origin shop. Distinct from received_by_employee_id; the pair is the chain of custody for stock lost in transit.

dimensions.label: from shop id
dimensions.description: Origin shop — where the stock leaves. Swapping this with to_shop_id inverts every inbound/outbound flow report, which is easy to do because both sub-records call the field simply 'shopID'.

dimensions.label: need by
dimensions.description: OVERLOADED, exactly as documented: while pending it is the date the transfer must be received BY; once received it is the date it WAS received. Always read it together with is_received or you will report completed receipts as future deadlines and vice versa.

dimensions.label: updated at
dimensions.description: Last modification to the transfer record, store-local. Moves whenever anything on the document changes, including line edits, so it is a staleness signal only: it is NOT the send date (sent_on) and NOT the receive date (need_by once received).

dimensions.label: transfer item id
dimensions.description: Unique id of this transfer line. Also the target of ls_special_orders.transfer_item_id when a special order is fulfilled from another shop.

dimensions.label: transfer id
dimensions.description: The transfer document this line belongs to. Origin shop, destination shop and all dates live on the parent, not here.

dimensions.label: item id
dimensions.description: The item being transferred. Joins the catalogue item table.

dimensions.label: comment
dimensions.description: Free-text note on the line — usually where staff explain a short shipment or damage. Worth reading whenever sent <> received.

dimensions.label: updated at
dimensions.description: Last modification to this line, store-local. Not a send or receive date: an old line edited today would count its whole quantity as today's movement if you bucket by it.

dimensions.label: special order id
dimensions.description: Unique id of the special order.

dimensions.label: contacted
dimensions.description: true once someone has told the customer their special order has arrived. contacted = false with the goods already in is the 'the customer does not know it is here' backlog — the single most valuable operational query on this table.

dimensions.label: completed
dimensions.description: true when the special order has been closed out (collected and rung up on the originating sale line). This is the filter that separates the live backlog from history. It does not by itself mean the customer paid — payment lives on the sale.

dimensions.label: shop id
dimensions.description: Shop where the special order was raised and where the customer will collect. The only location column on this table — the supplying shop, when a transfer fulfils it, is on the parent transfer of transfer_item_id.

dimensions.label: sale line id
dimensions.description: The sale line the special order was started from and where it will be completed — the customer's side of the deal, carrying the price, deposit and sale date. Joins the sales domain's sale-line table; it is also the only way to date a special order, since this object has no timestamp field.

dimensions.label: order line id
dimensions.description: The purchase order line where the item is being bought from the supplier — the supply side. NULL when the item has not been ordered yet OR when it is being fulfilled by an inter-shop transfer instead. Joins the purchasing domain's order-line table.

dimensions.label: transfer item id
dimensions.description: The transfer line fulfilling this special order when another shop supplies it rather than a supplier. NULL on the normal supplier route. Reports that only look at order_line_id classify these as unsourced and generate false 'we never ordered it' alarms.

dimensions.label: transfer from id
dimensions.description: Primary key of the origin record. Referenced by ls_transfers.transfer_from_id.

dimensions.label: transfer to id
dimensions.description: Primary key of the destination record. Referenced by ls_transfers.transfer_to_id.

dimensions.label: order id
dimensions.description: Unique id of the purchase order and the join key for every child table (lines, shipments). Lightspeed exposes no separate human-facing PO number — this integer IS the PO number staff see; ref_number is the VENDOR's number, not ours.

dimensions.label: ordered at
dimensions.description: When the order was placed WITH the vendor. This is the business date for supplier-spend and commitment reporting. Empty/null on drafts that were never sent, so a spend report keyed on this date silently excludes drafts (correctly) but also excludes any PO where the buyer never filled it in.

dimensions.label: received at
dimensions.description: The date the order actually arrived. A single header stamp: for a PO that arrived in several deliveries the docs do not say whether this is the first or the last, so use ls_order_shipments.received_at for real goods-inwards timing. Null while nothing has been received.

dimensions.label: expected arrival at
dimensions.description: The date the order is EXPECTED to arrive — a promise/ETA typed by staff, not a system-computed date and not evidence anything arrived. Null unless someone entered it, so 'late orders' queries must handle nulls explicitly rather than treating them as on time.

dimensions.label: ref number
dimensions.description: Free-text external reference, often the vendor's own order or invoice number. Not unique, not validated, frequently blank. Never use as a key.

dimensions.label: ship instructions
dimensions.description: Free-text instructions for the VENDOR or shipper about how to ship the order (carrier, consolidation, drop-ship address). Outbound-facing prose; carries no structured meaning.

dimensions.label: stock instructions
dimensions.description: Free-text instructions for the RECEIVING employees about how to stock the goods once they land (which bay, label runs, hold for customer). Internal-facing counterpart to ship_instructions; easily confused with it.

dimensions.label: is complete
dimensions.description: True once the order is marked complete, which usually happens after check-in finishes. It is a workflow flag, NOT proof that every unit arrived: buyers routinely close POs short. Open on-order stock = is_complete = false AND is_archived = false.

dimensions.label: is archived
dimensions.description: True when the PO is archived. Lightspeed itself excludes archived orders from backorder/on-order totals, so any 'what is on order' answer that ignores this flag overstates incoming stock. Archived POs remain valid history for spend reporting.

dimensions.label: vendor id
dimensions.description: Supplier the PO is for; joins ls_vendors.vendor_id. VERIFIED LIVE: legacy/imported POs carry 0 rather than null and the Vendor relation does not embed for them, so treat 0 as NULL — otherwise per-vendor spend quietly drops those orders and a phantom 'vendor 0' appears in group-bys.

dimensions.label: vendor name
dimensions.description: Denormalised supplier name from the embedded Vendor relation, for readable grouping without a join. VERIFIED LIVE: null whenever vendor_id is 0/absent because the relation does not embed. Group by vendor_id AND this column, never by name alone — the same brand can exist under several vendor_id values.

dimensions.label: note id
dimensions.description: Foreign key to the Note record holding the PO's free-text note. Only the id is exposed; the note body requires load_relations=Note and is not modelled here. 0 means no note.

dimensions.label: shop id
dimensions.description: The shop (location) the stock is being ordered FOR, i.e. where it will be checked in — not necessarily where the buyer sits. Joins the locations domain (ls_shops.shop_id / canonical `location`). 0 behaves as null.

dimensions.label: created by employee id
dimensions.description: Employee who CREATED the PO — the buyer, not the person who later received it (that is ls_order_shipments.employee_id). Joins the workforce domain (canonical `worker`). 0/null on migrated or API-created orders.

dimensions.label: custom field values
dimensions.description: Raw JSON of the account-defined custom fields attached to this PO. Kept as JSON because the field set is defined per merchant and the ground-truth documentation exposes no member-field table to model — so there are no stable column names to promise. Empty/absent on accounts that define no PO custom fields.

dimensions.label: created at
dimensions.description: When the PO RECORD was created. On migrated accounts this is the data-import timestamp, not when the buyer raised the order, so it can cluster thousands of historic POs on one day. Prefer ordered_at for business dating and keep this for record-level auditing.

dimensions.label: updated at
dimensions.description: Last modification of the record — the correct high-water mark for incremental syncs, and meaningless as a business date (a PO from 2019 touched yesterday shows yesterday). One of only two documented sort keys on this endpoint.

dimensions.label: vendor currency code
dimensions.description: Currency code of the purchase order, defaulting to the vendor's currency (e.g. 'USD'). Tells you which of each *_vendor_currency column pair is meaningful; absent on legacy rows with no vendor. Never assume it equals the merchant currency.

dimensions.label: shipping cost method
dimensions.description: How ship_cost is distributed to the lines. 'total' means the freight stays at ORDER level and is NOT allocated down, so ls_purchase_order_lines.shipping_cost will be empty and any landed-cost-per-line built from the lines alone understates by the whole freight bill.

dimensions.label: has shipments
dimensions.description: True when the PO has any shipment records. False does NOT mean nothing arrived — POs received before the merchant adopted the shipments workflow can have no shipment rows, with receiving represented only in line-level check-in counters.

dimensions.label: discount method
dimensions.description: How the order-level discount is distributed to the lines, mirroring shipping_cost_method. 'total' means the discount is held at order level and the per-line discount_money_value allocations are not populated.

dimensions.label: discount is percent
dimensions.description: True when the buyer typed the order discount as a percentage, false when as a fixed amount. Tells you which of discount_percent_value / discount_money_value was the INPUT — both may still be populated as derived values, which is exactly how double-discount bugs start.

dimensions.label: costs modified after shipment
dimensions.description: True when the shipping cost or discount changed AFTER the first shipment was created. That means the per-shipment freight/discount splits already written into ls_order_shipments and ls_order_shipment_items are stale relative to this header — landed-cost answers for those POs need a caveat or a recompute.

dimensions.label: b2b order uid
dimensions.description: Opaque unique identifier of this order in NuORDER (Lightspeed's B2B wholesale platform). Populated only for POs that originated in NuORDER; empty everywhere else, which makes non-empty a decent proxy for 'ordered through B2B'.

dimensions.label: b2b order number
dimensions.description: Human-readable order number in NuORDER, the display counterpart to b2b_order_uid. Empty unless the PO came through NuORDER; it is the vendor-platform number, not our order_id and not ref_number.

dimensions.label: order line id
dimensions.description: Unique id of the PO line. Stable across edits to the line, and the target of SpecialOrder.orderLineID in the sales domain — that is how 'this customer's item is on PO 4821' is expressed.

dimensions.label: order id
dimensions.description: Parent purchase order; joins ls_purchase_orders.order_id. The line carries no open/complete/archived state of its own, so every 'is this still on order' question has to reach the header through this key.

dimensions.label: item id
dimensions.description: The product being ordered; joins the products domain (canonical `product_variant`, since a Lightspeed Item is the sellable variant). 0 behaves as null. The same item can appear on several lines of one PO, which breaks naive one-line-per-item assumptions.

dimensions.label: discount percent value
dimensions.description: The order-level discount percentage as it lands on this line, in whole-percent units (5 = 5%). Derived from the header, not a line-specific negotiation.

dimensions.label: created at
dimensions.description: When the line was added to the PO — which can be later than the order's own created_at when a buyer appends items, and can be the migration timestamp on imported history.

dimensions.label: updated at
dimensions.description: Last modification of the line and the sync high-water mark. In practice this is when receiving last touched the line (check-in mutates the counters), which makes it a rough but unreliable proxy for receipt date — use the shipment tables when the date matters.

dimensions.label: vendor id
dimensions.description: Parent order vendor, projected so a line maps standalone.

dimensions.label: shop id
dimensions.description: Parent order destination shop, projected so a line maps standalone.

dimensions.label: complete
dimensions.description: Parent order completion flag, projected for received-quantity semantics.

dimensions.label: ordered date
dimensions.description: Parent order date, projected for business-date attribution.

dimensions.label: received date
dimensions.description: Parent order received date, projected for lifecycle status.

dimensions.label: archived
dimensions.description: Parent order archive flag, projected for cancellation semantics.

dimensions.label: vendor currency code
dimensions.description: Parent order vendor currency, projected for line cost currency.

dimensions.label: order shipment id
dimensions.description: Unique id of the shipment across the whole account (not per order — that is sequence_number). Join key for ls_order_shipment_items.

dimensions.label: order id
dimensions.description: The purchase order this delivery was received against; joins ls_purchase_orders.order_id. Every vendor, shop and ordered-date attribute of the receipt has to be reached through this key — the shipment itself carries no vendor or shop.

dimensions.label: sequence number
dimensions.description: The delivery's number WITHIN its purchase order (1 = first delivery, 2 = second). Unique only relative to the order, so it is never a global key; sequence_number > 1 identifies split/backordered deliveries.

dimensions.label: currency code
dimensions.description: The merchant's DEFAULT currency code at the time this shipment was created (e.g. 'AUD') — the unit for every non-vendor money column here. Frozen at creation, so it does not follow later account changes.

dimensions.label: vendor currency code
dimensions.description: The vendor's currency code, the unit for every *_vendor_cost / *_vendor_value column on this row. Equal to currency_code for domestic suppliers, which is why the two column families look redundant until an import PO appears.

dimensions.label: created at
dimensions.description: When the shipment RECORD was created (keyed by staff). Frequently close to but not equal to received_at, and it is the wrong column for goods-inwards periods — a delivery keyed a week late lands in the wrong month.

dimensions.label: payment due date
dimensions.description: Date the supplier's invoice for this delivery falls due — a DATE with no time component, populated only when the receiver entered the invoice terms. This is the domain's only accounts-payable signal; null means 'unknown', never 'due now'.

dimensions.label: shipment packing ref num
dimensions.description: Reference number for the shipment as typed by staff — in practice the packing slip or supplier invoice number. Free text, not unique, often blank; it is how a receipt gets matched to a paper invoice, not a key.

dimensions.label: updated at
dimensions.description: Last update of the shipment record and the incremental-sync high-water mark. Changes when costs are re-split after the fact, so it is not a receiving date.

dimensions.label: employee id
dimensions.description: Employee who received/checked in this delivery; joins the workforce domain (canonical `worker`). Distinct from ls_purchase_orders.created_by_employee_id, which is the buyer — attributing receiving errors to the buyer is a classic mix-up.

dimensions.label: received at
dimensions.description: When the goods were actually received. THE date for goods-inwards volume, lead time and receiving-by-period reporting — preferred over both created_at here and the header stamp on ls_purchase_orders.

dimensions.label: shipping cost method
dimensions.description: How the freight charged to this shipment was spread across its items. 'total' means it stayed at shipment level and the per-item shipping_cost values are not populated, so per-item landed cost built from the items alone understates.

dimensions.label: discount method
dimensions.description: How the discount charged to this shipment was spread across its items, mirroring shipping_cost_method. 'total' leaves it at shipment level with no per-item allocation.

dimensions.label: discount percent value
dimensions.description: Discount percentage applied on the shipment, in whole-percent units (5 = 5%). Documented on this object as 'the discount percent value of the item', but it sits on the shipment header — the per-item figure is the same-named column on ls_order_shipment_items.

dimensions.label: status
dimensions.description: Lifecycle state of the shipment, constrained by the docs to two values. 'received' does not mean the PO is fully satisfied — more deliveries may follow; 'finished' closes receiving for it. Neither value means the shipment was cancelled: there is no cancelled state.

dimensions.label: order shipment item id
dimensions.description: Unique id of this item-within-shipment row. Unique account-wide despite the nested URL, so it is a safe primary key.

dimensions.label: order shipment id
dimensions.description: Parent shipment; joins ls_order_shipments.order_shipment_id. This is the ONLY route from an item receipt to its purchase order, vendor, receive date and receiving employee — none of those exist on this row.

dimensions.label: discount percent value
dimensions.description: Discount percentage applied to this item, in whole-percent units (5 = 5%). Inherited from the shipment/PO allocation rather than negotiated per item.

dimensions.label: currency code
dimensions.description: The merchant's default currency code for this row's non-vendor money columns, frozen when the shipment was created. Repeated from the parent shipment for self-containment.

dimensions.label: vendor currency code
dimensions.description: The vendor's currency code — the unit for every *_vendor_* money column on this row. Identical to currency_code for domestic suppliers, which hides the distinction until an import receipt appears.

dimensions.label: created at
dimensions.description: When this item row was created, i.e. when the line was keyed during check-in. The actual goods-inwards date lives on the parent shipment (received_at); use this only for record auditing.

dimensions.label: updated at
dimensions.description: Last update of this item row and the sync high-water mark. Moves when costs are re-split after the fact, so it is not a receipt date.

dimensions.label: item id
dimensions.description: The product received; joins the products domain (canonical `product_variant`). This is the only product key on the row — there is no orderLineID, so attribution back to a specific PO line is inferred, not given.

dimensions.label: item vendor id
dimensions.description: The VENDOR's own SKU for this item — a STRING despite the '...ID' name, and not a foreign key to anything in Lightspeed. Never join on it; it is for matching supplier paperwork and can be blank or duplicated across items.

dimensions.label: item description
dimensions.description: The item's description as captured on this receipt — a point-in-time snapshot, so it can differ from the product's current name after a rename. This is the field the API exposes for sorting under the key `description`.

dimensions.label: vendor id
dimensions.description: Unique supplier id; the target of ls_purchase_orders.vendor_id and ls_vendor_returns.vendor_id. Note that 0 is used as an 'absent vendor' sentinel on those tables and will never match a row here.

dimensions.label: name
dimensions.description: Supplier name exactly as the shop typed it — a brand or a distributor. Not normalised and not unique: VERIFIED LIVE, the same brand can exist as several vendor records (bought direct and through a distributor), so summing spend by name silently merges or splits suppliers.

dimensions.label: archived
dimensions.description: True when the supplier is retired from the picker. Archived vendors still own all their historical purchase orders, so filtering them out of a spend report deletes real history — filter them only from 'who can we order from today' questions.

dimensions.label: price level
dimensions.description: Name of the pricing tier the business trades on with this supplier — usually '1','2','3' running from HIGHEST price to lowest, so a numerically larger level is normally the better deal. A free-text label, not an enforced enum, and it does not by itself price anything.

dimensions.label: update price
dimensions.description: Behaviour switch: when true, adding a catalogue item to a purchase order refreshes the item's RETAIL price from the catalogue MSRP. It changes future data, it is not a description of past orders.

dimensions.label: update cost
dimensions.description: Behaviour switch: when true, adding a catalogue item to a purchase order refreshes the item's COST from the catalogue entry. Vendors with this off are where stale item costs (and therefore wrong margins) accumulate.

dimensions.label: update description
dimensions.description: Behaviour switch: when true, adding a catalogue item to a purchase order overwrites the item's description from the catalogue entry — which is how carefully edited local descriptions get reverted.

dimensions.label: share sell through
dimensions.description: True when the shop has agreed that this vendor may receive sell-through data. A data-sharing consent flag with commercial consequences; it says nothing about how much is bought from them.

dimensions.label: b2b seller uid
dimensions.description: The vendor's unique identifier in NuORDER (Lightspeed's B2B platform). Non-empty is a reliable marker that this supplier is wired for B2B ordering; it pairs with ls_purchase_orders.b2b_order_uid on the resulting orders.

dimensions.label: purchasing currency code
dimensions.description: Currency the shop buys from this supplier in (e.g. 'USD'). It seeds ls_purchase_orders.vendor_currency_code but does not override it — an existing PO keeps the code it was raised with.

dimensions.label: purchasing currency symbol
dimensions.description: Display symbol for the purchasing currency (e.g. '$'). Presentation only, and ambiguous across currencies that share a glyph — never use it to identify a currency; use purchasing_currency_code.

dimensions.label: updated at
dimensions.description: Last modification of the vendor record and the incremental-sync high-water mark. Not a trading date — it moves when someone edits an address, not when an order is placed.

dimensions.label: vendor return id
dimensions.description: Unique id of the vendor return document. There is no separate human-facing RMA number in Lightspeed — the supplier's RMA is typed into ref_number.

dimensions.label: vendor id
dimensions.description: Supplier the stock is being sent back TO; joins ls_vendors.vendor_id. As on purchase orders, treat 0 as null so a supplier-less legacy record does not appear as a phantom 'vendor 0'.

dimensions.label: shop id
dimensions.description: The shop the stock is LEAVING — the location that loses the inventory, not the vendor's address. Joins the locations domain (canonical `location` / `stock_location`).

dimensions.label: ref number
dimensions.description: Free-text external reference, in practice the supplier's RMA or credit-note number. Not unique, not validated, often blank; a blank one on a sent return usually means nobody has chased the credit.

dimensions.label: status
dimensions.description: Lifecycle state of the return. The docs give only examples ('open', 'sent') rather than a closed set, so unseen values are possible and must not be treated as errors. There is no documented 'credited' state — receipt of the supplier credit is not tracked on this object at all.

dimensions.label: sent at
dimensions.description: When the return was dispatched to the vendor. NULL while the return is still open, so any 'returns this quarter' figure must state whether it counts dispatch date (this) or last activity (updated_at) — the two give different answers for returns still being assembled.

dimensions.label: hide vendor details
dimensions.description: True when the vendor's details are suppressed on the printed return document. A presentation switch only — it has no effect on the data returned by the API and none on the value of the return.

dimensions.label: archived
dimensions.description: True when the return has been archived. Archived returns are settled or abandoned paperwork; leaving them in an 'outstanding credits' report overstates what is owed to the shop.

dimensions.label: vendor name
dimensions.description: Denormalised supplier name from the embedded Vendor relation for readable grouping. Null when vendor_id is absent or 0, exactly as on purchase orders.

dimensions.label: updated at
dimensions.description: Last modification of the record and the incremental-sync high-water mark. This object documents no createTime, so updated_at and sent_at are the ONLY timestamps available — there is no way to know when a return was first raised.

dimensions.label: customer id
dimensions.description: Unique numeric id of this POS customer identity. Load-bearing distinction: it identifies a RECORD, not a person — the register, webstore and workshop each mint their own record, so one human often owns several customer_ids. Never null, never reused. Join target for ls_credit_accounts.customer_id, ls_ship_tos.customer_id and (sales domain) sale.customerID.

dimensions.label: archived
dimensions.description: True when the customer has been archived. Deleting a customer in the POS archives it (and its credit account) rather than removing it, and plain list responses exclude archived rows unless you ask for them. Any all-time customer count must decide explicitly whether archived rows are in scope.

dimensions.label: create time
dimensions.description: When the customer record was created, i.e. when this identity first entered the system. The correct basis for new-customer counts, but because duplicates exist it counts new RECORDS, not new humans. Immutable.

dimensions.label: updated at
dimensions.description: Last modification of the record. Bumps on any edit including bulk/integration updates, so it is NOT a last-visit or last-purchase proxy — deriving recency from it silently overstates engagement. Use it only for incremental sync and change detection.

dimensions.label: credit account id
dimensions.description: Foreign key to the customer's store credit account in ls_credit_accounts. Sentinel: the API returns 0 when the customer has no account — normalise 0 to NULL, otherwise counts of 'customers with store credit' include everyone.

dimensions.label: customer type id
dimensions.description: Foreign key to ls_customer_types (the segment: VIP, Club, Wholesale, Staff...). Sentinel: 0 means untyped and must be normalised to NULL. In most stores the majority of customers are untyped, so any segmentation report needs an explicit 'No type' bucket or it silently drops most of the base.

dimensions.label: discount id
dimensions.description: Foreign key to the Discount (pricing domain) auto-applied at the register for this customer. Sentinel 0 = no discount, normalise to NULL. Load-bearing for margin analysis: these customers' sale totals are systematically lower with no manual discount ever recorded on the sale.

dimensions.label: tax category id
dimensions.description: Foreign key to the TaxCategory (tax domain, canonical tax_code) that overrides normal tax for this customer, e.g. tax-exempt bodies or export customers. Sentinel 0 = standard tax applies, normalise to NULL. Misreading this makes tax-collected reconciliations plausible but wrong.

dimensions.label: contact id
dimensions.description: Id of the Contact block carrying this customer's emails, phones, postal address and marketing opt-outs. Join key to ls_contacts.contact_id. Only present when the Contact relation was requested; live responses also echo a top-level customerID-adjacent contactID.

dimensions.label: contact id
dimensions.description: Unique numeric id of the contact block. Join key from ls_customers.contact_id, ls_credit_accounts.contact_id and ls_ship_tos.contact_id, and the parent key of ls_contact_emails / ls_contact_phones / ls_contact_websites.

dimensions.label: no email
dimensions.description: True when the contact has opted OUT of email messages. Note the negative sense: no_email = false means emailable. Every outbound email audience must filter no_email = false or the store sends to people who unsubscribed.

dimensions.label: no mail
dimensions.description: True when the contact has opted OUT of postal mail. Independent of no_email — a customer can accept post and refuse email.

dimensions.label: no phone
dimensions.description: True when the contact has opted OUT of phone calls. Apply to call and SMS lists; the API has no separate SMS flag.

dimensions.label: updated at
dimensions.description: Last modification of the contact block. Changes when any email, phone, address or opt-out changes, so it is useful for consent-change auditing but says nothing about customer activity.

dimensions.label: contact id
dimensions.description: Owning contact block. Join to ls_contacts.contact_id, and through it to the customer.

dimensions.label: entry index
dimensions.description: Zero-based position of this address inside the parent's email container, needed only because the API gives email entries no id of their own. Position is not stable across syncs — never store it as a durable key outside a single load.

dimensions.label: use type
dimensions.description: Which slot this address occupies: Primary or Secondary. Distinct from the phone useType enum on the same object. Treat 'Primary' as the send-to address; when absent, fall back to the lowest entry_index.

dimensions.label: contact id
dimensions.description: Owning contact block. Join to ls_contacts.contact_id.

dimensions.label: entry index
dimensions.description: Zero-based position within the parent's phone container; phone entries carry no id of their own. Not stable across reloads — use it for ordering within a single snapshot only.

dimensions.label: use type
dimensions.description: What kind of number this is: Home, Work, Mobile, Pager or Fax. Distinct enum from the email useType on the same Contact object. Mobile is the SMS-capable slot; Fax and Pager rows must be excluded from any contact campaign.

dimensions.label: contact id
dimensions.description: Owning contact block. Join to ls_contacts.contact_id.

dimensions.label: entry index
dimensions.description: Zero-based position within the parent's website container; website entries carry no id. Snapshot-local only.

dimensions.label: customer type id
dimensions.description: Unique numeric id of the segment. Referenced by ls_customers.customer_type_id, where 0 means untyped and must be read as NULL.

dimensions.label: name
dimensions.description: Description/name of the customer type as shown in the POS Type field. Free text that may carry stray leading or trailing whitespace, so trim before grouping or matching by name.

dimensions.label: tax category id
dimensions.description: Foreign key to the TaxCategory automatically applied at the register when a customer of this type is attached — the mechanism behind tax-exempt segments. Sentinel 0 = none, normalise to NULL. Canonical target tax_code.

dimensions.label: discount id
dimensions.description: Foreign key to the Discount automatically applied at the register for this type. Sentinel 0 = none, normalise to NULL. Load-bearing for margin work: sales to these customers arrive already discounted with no per-sale discount record to explain the gap.

dimensions.label: credit account id
dimensions.description: Unique numeric id of the credit account or gift card. Referenced by ls_customers.credit_account_id and by SalePayment.creditAccountID in the payments domain.

dimensions.label: gift card
dimensions.description: True = a gift card (bearer code with monetary value, no customer), false = a customer store account. The single most load-bearing filter in this table: gift card float and accounts receivable are different money and summing them together produces a plausible, wrong liability figure.

dimensions.label: archived
dimensions.description: True when the account is archived. Archiving cascades from the owning customer being archived (i.e. deleted in the POS), and the balance survives archiving. An accounts-receivable or gift-card-liability audit that filters archived = false can therefore miss real outstanding money.

dimensions.label: contact id
dimensions.description: Contact block attached to the account, available only when the Contact relation is requested. Rarely useful for customer accounts (the customer already has one) and normally absent on gift cards. Joins ls_contacts.contact_id.

dimensions.label: updated at
dimensions.description: Last modification of the record, which in practice means the last time the balance moved. The nearest thing to a 'last activity' date for an account, but it cannot distinguish a payment from a metadata edit.

dimensions.label: ship to id
dimensions.description: Unique numeric id of the shipment record. The only reliably populated key on the row.

dimensions.label: shipped
dimensions.description: True once the parcel has gone out, false while it still needs to ship. shipped = false IS the open shipping queue. Beware: there is no dispatch timestamp, so 'when did it ship' can only be approximated by updated_at.

dimensions.label: sale id
dimensions.description: Foreign key to the sale being shipped. Sentinel 0 (read as NULL) on rows that anchor to an individual sale line instead, which is the live norm. A shipping report joined only on sale_id silently loses most of its rows.

dimensions.label: updated at
dimensions.description: Last modification of the shipment record. There is no dedicated shipped-at field, so for rows with shipped = true this is the closest available proxy for the dispatch date — it is a proxy, not a fact, and later edits move it.

dimensions.label: contact id
dimensions.description: Id of the destination contact block; join to ls_contacts.contact_id where owner_object = 'ShipTo' for a normalised address. Only present when the Contact relation was requested.

dimensions.label: custom field id
dimensions.description: Unique numeric id of the custom field definition. Referenced by ls_customer_custom_field_values.custom_field_id and ls_custom_field_choices.custom_field_id.

dimensions.label: type
dimensions.description: The declared data type, which controls both the validation applied on write and how the stored value must be parsed on read. Load-bearing: a 'float' value and a 'single_choice' value both arrive as untyped JSON, and reading a choice id as a number produces a plausible but meaningless average.

dimensions.label: name
dimensions.description: The label staff see for the field. Free text and editable, so it is a display label, not a stable key — always key on custom_field_id, since renaming a field would silently break any name-based filter.

dimensions.label: uom
dimensions.description: Unit of measure for the field, up to four characters (e.g. 'kg', 'cm'). Purely descriptive — the API stores no conversion and applies no validation, so values are only comparable within one field.

dimensions.label: archived
dimensions.description: True when the field definition is archived. Archived definitions keep their historic values, so a field can disappear from the POS while its values still populate ls_customer_custom_field_values — exclude archived definitions from 'what can we record' questions but not from historic analysis.

dimensions.label: default value
dimensions.description: The default CustomFieldValue applied when the field is first set, typed according to type (so it may be a scalar or a CustomFieldChoice object — stored as JSON to preserve either). A value equal to the default may mean 'staff chose it' or 'nobody touched it'; the two are indistinguishable.

dimensions.label: custom field choice id
dimensions.description: Unique numeric id of the choice. This is the value that actually appears inside a stored single_choice/multi_choice CustomFieldValue, which is why this table is mandatory for reading those values.

dimensions.label: custom field id
dimensions.description: Foreign key to the owning custom field definition in ls_custom_fields. Choices are scoped to one field — the same option text under two different fields is two different ids.

dimensions.label: name
dimensions.description: The label shown to staff for this option. When no separate value is set, the name is also the stored value, and uniqueness within the field is enforced on the name in that case.

dimensions.label: value
dimensions.description: An optional stored string value that differs from the display name (e.g. name 'Gold Member', value 'GOLD'). Documented as optional, so it is frequently empty — read COALESCE(NULLIF(value,''), name) to get the effective value. Uniqueness is enforced on this field when it is set.

dimensions.label: can be deleted
dimensions.description: False when the choice is in use somewhere and therefore cannot be removed. A useful in-use signal: can_be_deleted = false implies at least one record currently references it, though it does not say how many or on which object type.

dimensions.label: updated at
dimensions.description: Last modification of the choice. Moves when the label or value is edited, which means historic values referencing this choice silently take on the new label.

dimensions.label: custom field value id
dimensions.description: Primary key of this individual value record. Distinct from custom_field_id (the definition) — confusing the two collapses every customer's answers into one row.

dimensions.label: custom field id
dimensions.description: Foreign key to the field definition in ls_custom_fields. The stable key for 'which question is this the answer to' — always filter on this rather than on name.

dimensions.label: name
dimensions.description: The field's name copied onto the value for convenience. Documented as updatable only on the CustomField object, so it is a read-time snapshot of the label — do not filter on it, since a rename changes it everywhere at once.

dimensions.label: type
dimensions.description: The field's type copied onto the value, also only updatable on the definition. Load-bearing: it is the only in-row signal telling you whether value_raw is a literal, a date, a boolean or a CustomFieldChoice object.

dimensions.label: choice id
dimensions.description: For single_choice fields, the selected choice id lifted out of value_raw so it can be joined to ls_custom_field_choices. NULL for every non-choice type and for multi_choice (which holds several, and must be read from value_raw).

dimensions.label: deleted
dimensions.description: The delete flag: setting it true on an update of the parent is how a value is removed. Rows seen with deleted = true are tombstones and must be excluded from every count, or answered questions look more complete than they are.

dimensions.label: updated at
dimensions.description: Last modification of this value. The only per-attribute audit trail available; it does not record the previous value, so attribute history cannot be reconstructed.

dimensions.label: note id
dimensions.description: Unique numeric id of the note. The only stable handle on a note — the text itself is editable and duplicated freely between customers.

dimensions.label: is public
dimensions.description: True when the note is shown on receipts and other customer-facing output; false when it is internal-only. Load-bearing for privacy: internal notes are written on the assumption the customer never sees them, so any customer-facing surface must filter is_public = true.

dimensions.label: updated at
dimensions.description: Last modification of the note. There is no created-at and no author field, so this is the only temporal signal and it overwrites itself on every edit — note history cannot be reconstructed.

dimensions.label: workorder id
dimensions.description: Unique numeric id of the job, account-scoped. The join key for ls_workorder_lines.workorder_id, ls_workorder_items.workorder_id and ls_workorder_images.workorder_id. This is NOT the job number staff read off the tag (see gotchas re: the undocumented systemSku).

dimensions.label: time in
dimensions.description: When the item was received/booked in. The immutable intake event date and the ONLY correct basis for 'how many jobs came in this month'. Store-local wall time with no reliable offset — do not convert timezones. Commonly confused with updated_at (last modification), which drifts every time anyone touches the job.

dimensions.label: eta out
dimensions.description: The promise date: when the job is expected to be finished. Basis for 'due today / overdue' questions. VERIFIED LIVE: Lightspeed writes eta_out = time_in when staff never set an ETA, so equality with time_in is a 'no promise recorded' sentinel, not a same-day promise — treating it as real manufactures a mountain of fake overdue jobs.

dimensions.label: warranty
dimensions.description: True when the WHOLE job is warranty work and the customer will not be charged. Job-level override: quoted value of a warranty job is zero revenue no matter what prices sit on its lines. Individual lines carry their own warranty flag, so a non-warranty job can still contain free lines.

dimensions.label: tax
dimensions.description: Documented as 'does this workorder have tax charged on it'. VERIFIED LIVE: unreliable — jobs are seen with tax = false while every one of their item and labour lines carries tax = true. Never derive tax treatment from this column; use the line-level tax flags.

dimensions.label: archived
dimensions.description: True when the job is archived: hidden in the POS and explicitly excluded from every total Lightspeed reports. Current-workload and open-board questions MUST filter archived = false; historical/lifetime questions must not, or they silently drop most of the store's history.

dimensions.label: hook in
dimensions.description: Free-text storage location (hook/rack/bay number) where the item waits for work to START. VERIFIED LIVE: empty at stores that do not run a hook system, so blank means 'feature unused', not 'item missing'.

dimensions.label: hook out
dimensions.description: Free-text storage location where the finished item waits for customer PICKUP. Same 'blank means unused' caveat as hook_in. A non-empty hook_out is a decent proxy for 'physically finished and racked' at stores that use it.

dimensions.label: save parts
dimensions.description: True when the customer asked to keep the parts removed from the item, to be handed back with the job. A customer-service instruction only — it has no effect on pricing, stock or the charges on the job.

dimensions.label: assign employee to all
dimensions.description: Admin behaviour flag: when true the job's employee_id is auto-stamped onto every line. Consequence for analysis — when true, the employee_id on lines is inherited rather than a real statement of who did that task, so per-mechanic productivity from lines is only trustworthy where this is false.

dimensions.label: discount id
dimensions.description: FK to a job-level Discount applied to the whole workorder. 0/NULL means none. The discount's percentage/amount lives in the discounts reference table; nothing on this row tells you the discounted value.

dimensions.label: employee id
dimensions.description: FK to the employee IN CHARGE of the job (service writer / owner), not necessarily the person who performed the tasks. Per-mechanic workload must come from ls_workorder_lines.employee_id; using this column instead silently attributes an entire job to one name. 0 means unassigned.

dimensions.label: serialized id
dimensions.description: FK to the Serialized entry for the customer's item being worked on (the bike/machine, tracked by serial). This is a customer-owned item record, NOT a catalog product and NOT stock on hand. 0 when the job is not tied to a serialized item.

dimensions.label: shop id
dimensions.description: FK to the Shop (physical location) where the work is to be performed. For multi-location accounts this is the correct location axis for workshop capacity questions; it is the job's shop, which can differ from the shop of the sale that eventually bills it.

dimensions.label: sale id
dimensions.description: FK to the Sale this job was checked out and paid on. NULL/0 until checkout, which makes 'sale_id IS NULL' the cleanest test for an unbilled job. The money for the job lives on THAT sale's lines, not here; joining through it is the only way to get recognised workshop revenue.

dimensions.label: sale line id
dimensions.description: FK to the single SaleLine that represents this job on the register once billed. Note this is the job-level line; each labour task and part also carries its own sale_line_id, so do not assume one job equals one sale line.

dimensions.label: workorder status id
dimensions.description: FK to the store's current status for this job. The whole pipeline lives here — there are no separate opened/closed/completed booleans on a workorder. Join ls_workorder_statuses and filter on system_value for anything that must be correct across stores.

dimensions.label: status name
dimensions.description: Denormalised current status display name. Merchant-configured free text can include custom boards alongside system states, so filtering on a guessed name silently returns zero rows. Read ls_workorder_statuses first, or filter status_system_value.

dimensions.label: status system value
dimensions.description: Denormalised stable status identifier for system-defined statuses. The only cross-store-safe way to say 'finished' or 'paid'. VERIFIED LIVE: it is an EMPTY STRING (not NULL) for store-created statuses, so 'is a custom board' is status_system_value = '' — an IS NOT NULL test matches everything and quietly does nothing.

dimensions.label: item description
dimensions.description: Denormalised description of the customer's item being worked on (e.g. the bike make/model) from the Serialized relation. The everyday answer to 'what is this job on'. NULL unless the scan requests load_relations=Serialized.

dimensions.label: item serial
dimensions.description: Denormalised serial/frame number of the customer's item. VERIFIED LIVE: frequently blank because staff skip it, so absence does not mean the item is unidentified.

dimensions.label: updated at
dimensions.description: Last modification of the record, store-local. Moves whenever anyone edits the job, adds a line or changes status — so it is a change-feed cursor, NOT a completion date and NOT an intake date. Using it as 'when the job happened' produces plausible but wrong monthly volumes.

dimensions.label: workorder line id
dimensions.description: Unique numeric id of the task/charge, account-scoped (not per-workorder), so it is safe as a standalone primary key.

dimensions.label: workorder id
dimensions.description: FK to the parent job. Always populated — a line cannot exist without a workorder.

dimensions.label: done
dimensions.description: True when this individual task is complete. Task-level only: a job is finished when its workorder status says so, not when every line is done, and jobs routinely ship with lines left false. Counting 'done = false' as outstanding work is fine; counting it as unfinished JOBS is not.

dimensions.label: approved
dimensions.description: True when the customer approved this charge. VERIFIED LIVE: stores commonly skip the approval workflow entirely and leave it false even on completed, billed work — so false means 'not recorded', never 'declined'. Filtering quoted value on approved = true can zero out a real backlog.

dimensions.label: warranty
dimensions.description: True when this task is covered by warranty and the customer will NOT be charged for it. Its price still appears in unit_price_override, so any quoted/expected-revenue sum must exclude warranty = true or it inflates by the whole warranty book.

dimensions.label: tax
dimensions.description: True when this charge is taxed. Line-level and more trustworthy than the header flag on ls_workorders (VERIFIED LIVE: they disagree). Says only WHETHER tax applies — the rate comes from tax_class_id and the store's tax configuration; no tax amount is stored on this row.

dimensions.label: employee id
dimensions.description: FK to the employee responsible for this task — the correct grain for per-mechanic workload and throughput. Caveat: when the parent job has assign_employee_to_all = true this value is auto-stamped from the header and reflects assignment, not who turned the spanner. 0 means unassigned.

dimensions.label: sale line id
dimensions.description: FK to the SaleLine that represents this task on the register once checked out. NULL/0 before checkout. This is the bridge from a quoted task to its recognised revenue row.

dimensions.label: sale id
dimensions.description: FK to the Sale where this task was billed and paid. NULL/0 = not yet billed. Denormalised from the parent job, but check it per line: lines added after a partial checkout can be unbilled on an otherwise billed job.

dimensions.label: item id
dimensions.description: FK to the Non-Inventory / TaxClass=Labor Item used to create this task — i.e. the store's service-menu entry ('Full Service', 'Puncture Repair'). NULL/0 for ad-hoc labour typed in free-form, so grouping by it silently drops bespoke work. It is a catalog item id, but it holds no stock and must never be counted as a product sale.

dimensions.label: discount id
dimensions.description: FK to a Discount applied to this charge. 0/NULL means none. The discounted amount is not stored here — unit_price_override is the pre-discount price, so quoted sums overstate any discounted line.

dimensions.label: tax class id
dimensions.description: FK to the TaxClass governing this line — for genuine labour this is the store's 'Labor' class, which is also the routing signal that put the charge on this table rather than ls_workorder_items.

dimensions.label: updated at
dimensions.description: When this task/charge was last modified. The ONLY date on the row — there is no task start, completion or performed-on date anywhere in the API. Any time series of workshop labour must join ls_workorders.time_in; using this instead reports when records were touched, not when work happened.

dimensions.label: workorder item id
dimensions.description: Unique numeric id of the part line. Documented under the workorder path but unique account-wide, so it stands alone as a primary key.

dimensions.label: workorder id
dimensions.description: FK to the parent job. Always populated. The only route to the job's date, customer, status and archived flag — none of which exist on this row.

dimensions.label: approved
dimensions.description: True when the customer has approved this part charge. VERIFIED LIVE: stores frequently skip the approval workflow, so false means 'never recorded', not 'customer declined'. Do not gate parts value on it.

dimensions.label: warranty
dimensions.description: True when this part is supplied under warranty and the customer is NOT charged for it. The price still populates unit_price, so warranty rows must be excluded from any quoted-value or expected-revenue sum — the part is still consumed and still costs the business.

dimensions.label: tax
dimensions.description: True when this part line is taxed. Line-level and more reliable than the header flag on ls_workorders (VERIFIED LIVE: they disagree). Unlike the labour table there is no tax_class_id here, so the applicable rate must come from the underlying item's tax class.

dimensions.label: is special order
dimensions.description: True when the part is not in stock and is being special-ordered for this job; Lightspeed then creates a special order reached through the linked sale line. The operational meaning is 'this job is blocked waiting on a part', which is usually the real question behind 'what is waiting on parts'.

dimensions.label: note
dimensions.description: Free-text note on the part line. VERIFIED LIVE: staff sometimes type task descriptions here rather than on a labour line, so it is not safe to assume this text describes a product.

dimensions.label: employee id
dimensions.description: FK to the employee responsible for this part line — usually whoever added the part rather than who fitted it. 0 means unassigned; inherited from the header when the job has assign_employee_to_all = true.

dimensions.label: sale line id
dimensions.description: FK to the SaleLine this part becomes on the register at checkout. NULL/0 until then. Also the route to the special order record when is_special_order is true.

dimensions.label: sale id
dimensions.description: FK to the Sale where the part was billed. NULL/0 = not yet billed and therefore not yet deducted from stock or recognised as revenue.

dimensions.label: item id
dimensions.description: FK to the catalog Item this charge is for — the actual product. Join it for description, category, supplier and cost, none of which are on this row. 0/NULL for a free-text charge with no catalog product behind it.

dimensions.label: discount id
dimensions.description: FK to a Discount applied to this part charge. 0/NULL means none. unit_price is the pre-discount price and no discounted amount is stored, so quoted sums overstate discounted lines.

dimensions.label: updated at
dimensions.description: When this part line was last modified. The only date on the row: there is no added-on or fitted-on date. Time series of parts consumption must use ls_workorders.time_in, or the sale date once billed.

dimensions.label: workorder status id
dimensions.description: Unique numeric id of the status. Join target for ls_workorders.workorder_status_id. Account-specific — the same id means different things at different stores, so never hardcode one.

dimensions.label: name
dimensions.description: Display name shown in the POS. Fully merchant-configurable free text. Matching on a guessed name returns zero rows silently rather than erroring, so inspect tenant values first.

dimensions.label: sort order
dimensions.description: Position in POS dropdowns and boards — a display ordering, not a pipeline stage number, and not monotonic with progress. Documented as a string but VERIFIED LIVE numeric; end-of-pipeline system statuses sit at the top of the range (finished = 65000, paid = 65001), so ORDER BY sort_order roughly reproduces the POS board order. Values are not unique.

dimensions.label: html color
dimensions.description: Hex colour the POS paints this status with (e.g. #FF0000). Empty string when unset — cosmetic only, carries no semantics about urgency or completion despite red/green conventions staff may assume.

dimensions.label: system value
dimensions.description: Stable internal identifier for statuses Lightspeed defines and locks (the store cannot rename or delete them). The ONLY status identifier safe to hardcode. VERIFIED LIVE: it is an EMPTY STRING for store-created statuses, never NULL — so 'custom board' is system_value = '' and an IS NOT NULL filter matches every row and does nothing.

dimensions.label: workorder image id
dimensions.description: Unique numeric id of the image attachment. Identifies the attachment record, not the underlying asset — see public_id for the stored asset.

dimensions.label: workorder id
dimensions.description: FK to the job the image is attached to. The only context this row has; every date, customer and status question requires the join.

dimensions.label: filename
dimensions.description: Stored filename of the image. Often an opaque upload name (IMG_1234.jpg) rather than anything meaningful; do not parse it for dates or content.

dimensions.label: ordering
dimensions.description: Display position of this image within the job's image list — a rank, not a count and not a quantity. Never sum it. Ties are possible, so add workorder_image_id for deterministic ordering.

dimensions.label: base image url
dimensions.description: Base/CDN URL the image is served from. Not a complete link on its own: the usable URL is composed from this plus public_id (and any size transform the client applies).

dimensions.label: size
dimensions.description: Documented only as 'the size of the image' with no unit — conventionally bytes for a stored asset, but the docs do not state it and it could be a pixel dimension. Do not present it as MB without verifying against a known file; summing it yields storage volume at best.

dimensions.label: create time
dimensions.description: When the image was uploaded. The genuine event date for the attachment and the right basis for 'were intake photos taken on arrival' — compare it with ls_workorders.time_in. Distinct from updated_at, which moves on any metadata edit.

dimensions.label: updated at
dimensions.description: When the attachment record was last modified (caption edits, reordering). A sync cursor, not the upload date — use create_time for that.

dimensions.label: shop id
dimensions.description: Unique numeric id for the store location. This is the join target for sale.shopID, register.shopID, employee_hours.shop_id, item-shop quantities and orders. Stable forever; archived shops keep their id and keep owning their history.

dimensions.label: name
dimensions.description: Store name as it appears on receipts, labels and in the POS shop picker. Free text set by the merchant, not guaranteed unique across shops and not a slug or code.

dimensions.label: time zone
dimensions.description: The store's IANA timezone. Load-bearing for the entire layer: every 'today', 'this week' and daily bucket must be computed in THIS tenant value, not UTC, server time, the querier's zone, or an example timezone. On multi-shop accounts spanning zones, a single account-wide date bucket is arithmetically wrong.

dimensions.label: tax labor
dimensions.description: True when service/labour lines at this shop attract sales tax. Silently changes the tax base: if you assume labour is untaxed on a shop where this is true (typical for AU/GST and most CA provinces), every tax-vs-net reconciliation on service revenue will be off by the labour tax. Applies to the labour line type, not to goods.

dimensions.label: label title
dimensions.description: What heading is printed at the top of product labels for this shop. Pure print configuration -- carries no analytical meaning. Note the enum values are human-readable strings with spaces, not codes, so match them literally.

dimensions.label: label msrp
dimensions.description: True when a product label should also print the MSRP, but only for items where MSRP is filled in AND MSRP exceeds this shop's own selling price. Conditional on both, so a true value does not mean every label shows an MSRP. Print config only.

dimensions.label: archived
dimensions.description: True when the location has been archived (closed down / retired). Archived shops STILL own all their historical sales, orders and inventory movements, so filtering archived = false when attributing past revenue silently deletes a whole store's history. Filter it only when listing currently-trading locations.

dimensions.label: contact id
dimensions.description: Foreign key to the Contact record holding the store's street address, phone, email and website. Comes back as 0 (not null) when unset -- normalise 0 to NULL on ingest. The Contact object itself lives in the customers/contacts domain; the payload is duplicated into contact_json here for convenience.

dimensions.label: tax category id
dimensions.description: Foreign key to the TaxCategory this shop applies to new sales by default (/Account/{accountID}/TaxCategory/{taxCategoryID}). Load-bearing because the category carries the isTaxInclusive flag and the actual rates -- read the wrong one and every tax-exclusive/inclusive split is wrong. This is the DEFAULT only; an individual sale can carry a different tax category.

dimensions.label: receipt setup id
dimensions.description: Foreign key to the ReceiptSetup record (header/footer text and logo) used by this shop. Joins ls_receipt_setups. Cosmetic print config; returned as 0 when unset.

dimensions.label: price level id
dimensions.description: Foreign key to the default PriceLevel this shop sells at (/Account/{accountID}/PriceLevel/{priceLevelID}). Load-bearing for any 'discount vs list price' analysis: the baseline you compare against is this tier, not necessarily MSRP. A customer or an individual sale can override it.

dimensions.label: register id
dimensions.description: Unique numeric id for the till. Join target for sale.registerID, RegisterCount.registerID and RegisterWithdraw.registerID. Stable across open/close cycles.

dimensions.label: name
dimensions.description: Human label for the till as shown in the POS, e.g. 'Front Register', 'Counter'. Merchant-editable free text, not unique, not a code. Group on register_id, display this.

dimensions.label: is open
dimensions.description: True when the till is open for trading AT THE MOMENT THE ROW WAS FETCHED. This is live mutable state, not a historical fact: a snapshot taken overnight shows every till closed. Never use it to reason about whether a till was open when a past sale was rung -- that requires RegisterCount sessions.

dimensions.label: opened at
dimensions.description: When the CURRENT session was opened, in the shop's timezone. Only meaningful while is_open is true; when the till is closed this retains the stale value from the last open, so 'hours open' arithmetic on a closed till produces a nonsense multi-day number. Not the open time of any past session.

dimensions.label: tip enabled
dimensions.description: True when the Tipping feature is permitted on this register. Documented but frequently absent from live payloads -- treat NULL as 'the account did not report it', which is NOT the same as false. Controls whether tips can be taken, not whether any were.

dimensions.label: open employee id
dimensions.description: Foreign key to the Employee who opened the current session (/Account/{accountID}/Employee/{openEmployeeID}). Comes back as 0 when unset. This is who UNLOCKED the drawer, not who rang up the sales on it and not who will close it.

dimensions.label: shop id
dimensions.description: Foreign key to the Shop this register physically sits in (/Account/{accountID}/Shop/{shopID}). The only reliable way to attribute a register to a location -- register names are often reused across stores ('Counter' at every branch), so grouping tills by name across a multi-shop account silently merges different physical drawers.

dimensions.label: employee id
dimensions.description: Unique numeric id for the staff login. Join target for sale.employeeID, EmployeeHours.employeeID, Register.openEmployeeID and RegisterCount open/close employees. Survives archiving, so historical attribution never breaks.

dimensions.label: lock out
dimensions.description: True when the employee is locked out of the system and cannot log in to the POS. Distinct from archived: a locked-out employee still counts towards the account's employee limit and is still an active staff record, just suspended. Common for temporary suspension or a forgotten PIN.

dimensions.label: archived
dimensions.description: True for former staff. Archived employees do NOT count towards the account's employee limit (that is the documented purpose of the flag). Critically, archived staff still own every sale they ever rang: filtering archived = false when attributing historical revenue silently erases departed staff and makes the remaining team's numbers look larger.

dimensions.label: contact id
dimensions.description: Foreign key to the Contact record with the employee's phone, email and address. Returned as 0 when unset. Often empty for staff even when populated for customers.

dimensions.label: clock in employee hours id
dimensions.description: Foreign key to the EmployeeHours record the employee is CURRENTLY clocked in under (/Account/{accountID}/EmployeeHours/{clockInEmployeeHoursID}). Non-zero means clocked in right this second; 0/NULL means clocked out. This is live state, so it is the only correct source for 'who is on shift now' -- deriving it from EmployeeHours.checkOut IS NULL also catches stale never-closed entries from months ago.

dimensions.label: employee role id
dimensions.description: Foreign key to the employee's role, which specifies their rights.
