Load-bearing because of the fallback rule: when this is 0/NULL the employee's OWN rights (ls_employee_rights) apply instead of the role's. Any permissions query that ignores the fallback reports the wrong effective rights for exactly the staff who are configured individually.

dimensions.label: limit to shop id
dimensions.description: Foreign key to the single Shop this login is restricted to (/Account/{accountID}/Shop/{limitToShopID}). 0/NULL means the opposite of restricted: the employee may work at ANY shop. Reading 0 as 'shop 0' or as 'no shop access' inverts the meaning.

dimensions.label: last shop id
dimensions.description: The shop the employee is currently -- or was most recently -- attached to (/API/Account/Shop/{lastShopID}). Transient live POS state that changes every time they log in somewhere. Never use it for historical attribution: 'sales by employee home store' computed from this column reassigns a person's entire history the moment they cover a shift elsewhere.

dimensions.label: last sale id
dimensions.description: The sale the employee is currently, or was last, working on (/Account/{accountID}/Sale/{lastSaleID}). Transient POS state -- typically an open, incomplete sale on the screen in front of them. It is not 'their most recent completed sale' and must never be used to count sales per employee.

dimensions.label: last register id
dimensions.description: The register the employee is currently, or was last, attached to (/Account/{accountID}/Register/{lastRegisterID}). Transient POS state, overwritten on every till switch. Not a history of which drawer they worked.

dimensions.label: updated at
dimensions.description: When the employee record was last modified, in the shop's timezone. This is the ONLY sortable/filterable change marker on this object, so it is the incremental-sync key. It ticks on any edit including the transient last* pointers, so it changes constantly during trading and is useless as a proxy for HR events like hire or termination date.

dimensions.label: employee role id
dimensions.description: Unique numeric id for the role. Join target for Employee.employeeRoleID. Because roles arrive nested per employee, the same role id appears once for every employee holding it -- de-duplicate on this column when building the catalogue.

dimensions.label: name
dimensions.description: Display name of the role as configured by the merchant (e.g. 'Manager', 'Cashier'). Free text, not a fixed enum and not guaranteed unique across ids -- a merchant can create two roles with the same label and different rights.

dimensions.label: employee role id
dimensions.description: The role conferring this right, carried down from the parent EmployeeRole object during the explode. Not a field on the EmployeeRight element itself -- without it the exploded rows are unattributable.

dimensions.label: employee right id
dimensions.description: Unique numeric id of the right/privilege. Stable across roles and accounts, so it is the safe key for 'does this role include right N' checks -- safer than matching the name string.

dimensions.label: name
dimensions.description: The right's name as Lightspeed defines it (e.g. discount-application, void, price-override, reporting access). Load-bearing for permission audits because these are the only human-readable handle on what a role can do, yet the docs publish no enumeration of the value set -- do not hard-code an exhaustive list, and use ILIKE matching with care since similarly-named rights differ in scope.

dimensions.label: employee id
dimensions.description: The employee the right is attached to directly, carried down from the parent Employee object. Load-bearing because the row is only MEANINGFUL when that same employee's employee_role_id is NULL -- rows for role-holding employees are inert configuration that the POS ignores.

dimensions.label: employee right id
dimensions.description: Unique numeric id of the right/privilege, from the same catalogue as ls_employee_role_rights.employee_right_id. The two tables can be compared on this id to diff individual against role permissions.

dimensions.label: name
dimensions.description: The right's name as Lightspeed defines it. Same undocumented value set as the role-scoped table; no enumeration is published, so treat any hard-coded list as account-specific.

dimensions.label: employee hours id
dimensions.description: Unique numeric id of the clock entry (/Account/{accountID}/EmployeeHours/{employeeHoursID}). Employee.clockInEmployeeHoursID points here to mark the one entry that is currently open.

dimensions.label: check in
dimensions.description: Start of the clock-in entry, in the shop's timezone. This is the date to bucket a shift by; a shift that crosses midnight belongs to the check_in day under this convention, so evening-shift hours land on the earlier date. Always present.

dimensions.label: check out
dimensions.description: End of the clock-in entry, in the shop's timezone. NULL while the shift is still open -- and also NULL forever when staff simply forgot to clock out, which is common. Every duration aggregate must exclude NULLs or SUM silently returns NULL/short; every 'still working' query must cross-check ls_employees.clock_in_employee_hours_id to distinguish a live shift from an abandoned one.

dimensions.label: employee id
dimensions.description: Foreign key to the Employee this entry belongs to (/Account/{accountID}/Employee/{employeeID}). Returned as 0 when unset. The person who clocked in -- not necessarily the person who rang up sales during that window, since any logged-in employee can use any till.

dimensions.label: shop id
dimensions.description: Foreign key to the Shop where the clock in/out physically happened (/Account/{accountID}/Shop/{shopID}). Recorded per entry, so a person covering another branch produces entries against that branch -- this is the correct column for labour-hours-by-location, unlike Employee.lastShopID which is transient.

dimensions.label: employee id
dimensions.description: Foreign key to the Employee who granted the access token (/Account/{accountID}/Employee/{employeeID}). This is the identity the integration ACTS AS -- every write the integration makes is attributed to this employee, which is why an integration's sales can pollute a staff leaderboard.

dimensions.label: system customer id
dimensions.description: The account ID (/Account/{accountID}). Despite the 'customer' in the name this has NOTHING to do with retail customers -- it is Lightspeed's internal identifier for the merchant account and it is the {accountID} path segment in every other endpoint URL. Confusing it with a Customer record is the classic misread; confusing it with Account.accountID is safe, they are the same value.

dimensions.label: system user id
dimensions.description: The employee's identifier at the Lightspeed platform level, unique ACROSS ALL ACCOUNTS -- unlike employeeID, which is only unique within one account. The right key for recognising the same human across multiple merchant accounts; useless as a join key inside a single account.

dimensions.label: system api client id
dimensions.description: Unique identifier of the API client (the registered application) associated with the access token. Identifies WHICH integration is calling, not who authorised it. Constant for all tokens issued to the same app.

dimensions.label: system api key id
dimensions.description: Unique identifier of the access token itself. Changes when the token is rotated or re-authorised, so it is the natural key for 'which credential is this' and for detecting that a stored token was replaced.

dimensions.label: ecom url
dimensions.description: URL of the associated Lightspeed eCom (C-Series) store, if the account has one linked. Empty/null means no eCom link -- which in turn means online-order questions cannot be answered from this account at all. Its presence is the cheapest test for whether a merchant is omnichannel.

dimensions.label: shop count
dimensions.description: Number of shops on the account, as counted by the platform. Useful as a cheap cross-check that a Shop scan paginated fully, but it does not state whether archived shops are included, so a mismatch against COUNT(*) FROM ls_shops WHERE archived = false is expected and not an error.

dimensions.label: account id
dimensions.description: The account's unique id. This is the {accountID} path segment in every other R-Series URL and is the same value as Session.systemCustomerID. Type inferred from the example payload; the docs publish no field table for this object.

dimensions.label: name
dimensions.description: The merchant account name, i.e. the business as Lightspeed bills it. Commonly but not always identical to Shop.name -- on multi-shop accounts the account name is the parent business and each shop has its own trading name. Do not use it as a store label.

dimensions.label: link
dimensions.description: Self-referencing API URL for this account resource, as returned in the example payload. Plumbing for HATEOAS-style navigation; carries no analytical meaning and should not be shown to users.

dimensions.label: system customer id
dimensions.description: Lightspeed's platform-level identifier for the merchant, the same value as Session.systemCustomerID. Again: NOT a retail customer id. Load-bearing because integrations that key their own storage on the wrong one of accountID/systemCustomerID cross-wire tenants.

dimensions.label: status
dimensions.description: Subscription/lifecycle state of the account. Load-bearing because a suspended, trial or cancelled account can still serve historical data through the API while no longer reflecting live trading -- a silent source of 'the numbers stopped moving'. The docs publish no enumeration of the possible values, so read the live value rather than assuming 'active'.

dimensions.label: unique subscription identifier
dimensions.description: Opaque identifier of the billing subscription behind the account, from the example payload. Useful for correlating with Lightspeed billing records; meaningless for retail analytics and not a join key to anything inside the API.

dimensions.label: default currency code
dimensions.description: ISO code of the account's BASE currency (USD, CAD, AUD...). The single most load-bearing value for money: every amount in every other table in the layer -- sale totals, costs, Shop.serviceRate, register counts -- is denominated in this currency and carries no currency tag of its own. Foreign amounts only ever appear via the purchasing-currency and CurrencyRate mechanisms.

dimensions.label: default currency symbol
dimensions.description: Display symbol for the base currency ($, £, €). Presentation only -- symbols are ambiguous across currencies ($ is used by USD, CAD, AUD and more), so never infer the currency from the symbol; use default_currency_code.

dimensions.label: account id
dimensions.description: The account these purchasing currencies belong to, carried down from the parent Account object. Constant on a single-tenant token but required to keep the grain well-defined in a multi-account warehouse.

dimensions.label: currency code
dimensions.description: ISO code of a currency the account may raise purchase orders in (USD, EUR...). Distinct from Account.defaultCurrency.code, which is the currency everything is REPORTED in. A currency listed here does not mean the merchant sells in it.

dimensions.label: currency symbol
dimensions.description: Display symbol for the purchasing currency. Ambiguous across currencies; always label with currency_code, never with the symbol alone.

dimensions.label: name
dimensions.description: Name of the locale. The endpoint publishes no numeric id of any kind, so this string is the only available key -- which makes it fragile: if Lightspeed renames a locale, every reference to it breaks silently.

dimensions.label: country
dimensions.description: Country the locale belongs to. The docs do not state whether this is an ISO-3166 code or a display name, so do not join it to country codes from other systems without inspecting a live value first.

dimensions.label: states
dimensions.description: States/provinces within the locale, published as a string rather than a structured collection. Expect a delimited list needing parsing; the delimiter is not documented. Relevant because state-level tax setups vary within a country.

dimensions.label: currency symbol
dimensions.description: Currency symbol used for display in this locale. Presentation only; $ is shared by many currencies, so never infer the currency from it.

dimensions.label: currency code
dimensions.description: ISO currency code of the locale. Note this is the locale's currency, NOT the account's -- the account's base currency is Account.defaultCurrency.code and takes precedence for every stored amount.

dimensions.label: include tax on labels
dimensions.description: Whether product labels in this locale print tax-inclusive prices. Load-bearing as a signal of the region's pricing convention: tax-inclusive regions (most of EU/AU/NZ) enter and display prices with tax in them, which changes what a 'price' means before you touch a single sale record. The authoritative per-sale flag is TaxCategory.isTaxInclusive, not this.

dimensions.label: language tag
dimensions.description: Language tag per ISO 639-1 (e.g. 'en', 'fr'). Drives POS and receipt language. Note ISO 639-1 is the two-letter LANGUAGE standard -- it carries no region, so 'en' does not distinguish en-US from en-AU; use country for that.

dimensions.label: date format
dimensions.description: Date format string for the locale, in the API's own format syntax (e.g. 'd/m/Y' style PHP tokens, not strftime and not ISO). Presentation only -- never parse API datetimes with it; API datetimes are returned offset-stamped regardless of locale.

dimensions.label: datetime format
dimensions.description: Date-and-time format string for the locale, same token syntax caveat as date_format. Display formatting only.

dimensions.label: tax name1
dimensions.description: Name of the locale's first tax (GST, VAT, State Tax, TPS...). Explains WHY a TaxCategory is named what it is; the rates themselves live on TaxCategory, never here.

dimensions.label: tax name2
dimensions.description: Name of the locale's second tax, for two-tier regimes such as Canadian GST + PST/QST. Empty in single-tax regions. Its presence is the tell that a region needs two-rate tax handling.

dimensions.label: currency denominations json
dimensions.description: The locale's note and coin denominations, kept as a JSON blob. Deliberately NOT split into its own table: the V3 documentation publishes the collection but no field table for its elements, so any child columns would have to be invented. Inspect a live response before reading paths out of it.

dimensions.label: industry id
dimensions.description: Unique numeric id for the industry vertical. Global to Lightspeed, so the same id means the same vertical on every account -- unlike most ids in this API, which are account-scoped.

dimensions.label: name
dimensions.description: Name of the industry vertical (Bicycles, Skateboards, Motorcycles...). Lightspeed-defined, not merchant-editable, so it is safe to match on -- though the docs publish no closed list of values.

dimensions.label: enabled
dimensions.description: True when the vertical is switched on for THIS account. Load-bearing because the endpoint returns the full global catalogue regardless: listing rows without filtering on enabled reports every industry Lightspeed offers as though the merchant used them all. Typically exactly one is true.

dimensions.label: cc gateway id
dimensions.description: Unique numeric id of the gateway configuration. Shop.ccGatewayID joins here. Because gateways arrive nested per shop, the same id repeats once per shop sharing it -- de-duplicate to reach the declared grain.

dimensions.label: gateway
dimensions.description: Name of the payment gateway/processor this shop is wired to. Load-bearing for reconciliation: it tells you WHICH processor's statement the card takings should be matched against. A populated row does not imply the shop actually uses it -- check enabled and test_mode.

dimensions.label: enabled
dimensions.description: True when the gateway is switched on. A configured-but-disabled gateway is common after a processor migration, and reading the config as active is how you end up reconciling against the wrong processor.

dimensions.label: test mode
dimensions.description: True when the gateway is in test/sandbox mode. Load-bearing and dangerous: card charges taken while this is true are NOT real money, yet they still appear as completed payments in the POS. A shop left in test mode produces fully plausible revenue that never settles.

dimensions.label: allow credits
dimensions.description: Whether credit-card charges (credits back to a card) are permitted through this gateway. When false, refunds cannot be returned to the original card and staff must use another tender -- which is why refund tender mix sometimes fails to mirror sale tender mix.

dimensions.label: market type
dimensions.description: Market type value sent in the transaction XML (retail, e-commerce, MOTO and similar processor-defined categories). It influences interchange pricing at the processor. Processor-defined value set; the docs publish no enumeration.

dimensions.label: device type
dimensions.description: Numeric code for the type of device used to process card transactions. The code set is processor-specific and undocumented here, so treat the number as an opaque tag rather than decoding it.

dimensions.label: terminal num
dimensions.description: Terminal ID sent in the transaction XML. Identifies the physical/logical terminal to the processor and is usually the key on the processor's own settlement report -- the most useful column here for reconciliation. Not the same as Lightspeed's registerID.

dimensions.label: visa payment type id
dimensions.description: PaymentType id that Visa transactions on this gateway are recorded against (/Account/{accountID}/PaymentType/{visaPaymentTypeID}). This mapping is the ONLY documented way to split card revenue by brand on gateway-integrated accounts; 0 means unmapped, in which case Visa falls into a generic card tender and brand mix is unanswerable.

dimensions.label: master payment type id
dimensions.description: PaymentType id used for MasterCard transactions on this gateway (/Account/{accountID}/PaymentType/{masterPaymentTypeID}). 0 when unmapped.

dimensions.label: discover payment type id
dimensions.description: PaymentType id used for Discover Card transactions (/Account/{accountID}/PaymentType/{discoverPaymentTypeID}). 0 when unmapped, which is normal outside North America.

dimensions.label: american payment type id
dimensions.description: PaymentType id used for American Express transactions (/Account/{accountID}/PaymentType/{americanPaymentTypeID}). 0 when unmapped. Amex is often deliberately unmapped where the merchant does not accept it.

dimensions.label: debit payment type id
dimensions.description: PaymentType id used for debit-card transactions (/Account/{accountID}/PaymentType/{debitPaymentTypeID}). Debit is priced very differently from credit at the processor, so a null mapping here means the cheap and expensive card volume are indistinguishable in the tender mix.

dimensions.label: receipt setup id
dimensions.description: Unique numeric id of the receipt configuration. Shop.receiptSetupID joins here. Repeats once per shop using it in the nested payload, so de-duplicate to reach the declared grain.

dimensions.label: header
dimensions.description: Text printed at the TOP of the receipt. Documented fallback behaviour matters: when left blank, the POS prints the shop's contact information instead, so an empty header does not mean receipts print headerless.

dimensions.label: general msg
dimensions.description: General text printed at the end of ALL receipts (return policy, thanks, opening hours). Applies unconditionally, unlike the workorder and credit-card texts which are conditional.

dimensions.label: workorder agree
dimensions.description: Text printed at the end of workorder receipts, invoices and quotes only. Load-bearing in the legal sense rather than the numeric one: this is the customer agreement wording for service work (liability, storage, abandonment terms), so an audit of what a customer agreed to must read this and not general_msg.

dimensions.label: creditcard agree
dimensions.description: Text printed at the end of a sales receipt that includes credit-card charges -- the cardholder agreement/signature wording. Printed conditionally on the presence of a card charge, so it is absent from cash receipts.

dimensions.label: logo
dimensions.description: RELATIVE URL of the logo image file, not an absolute URL and not the image bytes. It must be resolved against the account's asset host before it can be fetched; empty when no logo is configured.

dimensions.label: logo height
dimensions.description: Logo image height in PIXELS as stored, not print millimetres. Used with logo_width to lay the image out on the receipt; 0 when no logo is set.

dimensions.label: logo width
dimensions.description: Logo image width in PIXELS. Paired with logo_height; a width exceeding the printer's dot width is the usual cause of clipped receipt logos.

dimensions.label: currency rate id
dimensions.description: Unique numeric id of the rate record (/Account/{accountID}/CurrencyRate/{currencyRateID}). Identifies the ROW, not the currency -- prefer currency_code as the business key since the id can change if a merchant deletes and re-adds a currency.

dimensions.label: currency code
dimensions.description: ISO currency code the rate applies to (USD, CAD...). The account's own base currency is normally absent from this table; if it appears, its rate should be 1 and anything else indicates a misconfiguration.

dimensions.label: created at
dimensions.description: When the currency-rate record was created, in the shop's timezone. On migrated accounts this is frequently a bulk backfill value identical across every row, so it is not evidence of when the merchant started trading in that currency.

dimensions.label: updated at
dimensions.description: When the rate record was last modified, in the shop's timezone. Effectively the rate's AS-OF date and the only staleness signal available: since Lightspeed never refreshes these automatically, a rate last touched two years ago is being applied to today's transactions. Always surface this alongside any converted figure.

dimensions.label: locale id
dimensions.description: Owning locale. Join to ls_locales to resolve the currency and formatting rules this denomination belongs to.

dimensions.label: value
dimensions.description: Face value of the note or coin in the locale currency. Documented only as a collection on Locale, so the per-denomination shape is confirmed at probe time rather than from the reference.

dimensions.label: register count id
dimensions.description: Unique id of this close-out. The ONLY documented sortable field on the endpoint, so backfill must page by it ascending. Child tender lines in ls_register_count_amounts join here.

dimensions.label: closed at
dimensions.description: The moment the till was CLOSED and the count submitted. Despite the createTime name this is the END of the session, not a record-creation date — use it, never opened_at, to attribute a close-out to a trading day. Store-local wall time with no timezone offset; do not shift it.

dimensions.label: opened at
dimensions.description: When this till session was opened. Session length = closed_at - opened_at. Store-local wall time, no offset. Misreading this as the count date inverts every duration calculation.

dimensions.label: notes
dimensions.description: Free text typed by staff at close. In practice this is where discrepancies and float resets get explained (e.g. 'removed cash to reset the float'). Usually an empty string, not NULL, for routine closes — test with NULLIF(TRIM(notes),'') rather than IS NOT NULL.

dimensions.label: register id
dimensions.description: The till that was counted. Joins ls_registers.register_id (org/location domain). Arrives as 0 when unset; normalise 0 to NULL at ingest so joins do not silently attach to a phantom register.

dimensions.label: open employee id
dimensions.description: Employee who OPENED the session. The docs give the resolution URL as /Register/{openEmployeeID}, which is a documentation typo — this is an Employee id and resolves against the Employee endpoint. 0 means unset; normalise to NULL.

dimensions.label: close employee id
dimensions.description: Employee who submitted the count and closed the till. Same documentation typo (/Register/{closeEmployeeID}) — it is an Employee id. This, NOT open_employee_id, is the person accountable for any over/short on this close-out; attributing variance to the opener is the classic mistake. 0 means unset; normalise to NULL.

dimensions.label: register count amount id
dimensions.description: Unique id for this one tender line of one close-out. Sortable, so backfill pages by it ascending.

dimensions.label: register count id
dimensions.description: The close-out this tender line belongs to. Joins ls_register_counts.register_count_id, which is where the date, register and employee live — this table has no time column of its own. Also documented as sortable, so it doubles as the pushdown key for fetching one count's lines. 0 means unset; normalise to NULL.

dimensions.label: payment type id
dimensions.description: The tender being counted (Cash, Credit Card, Gift Card, ...). Joins ls_payment_types.payment_type_id. The documented meaning is a truncated sentence ('The this count is for'); it is the payment type foreign key. 0 means unset; normalise to NULL.

dimensions.label: register withdraw id
dimensions.description: Unique id for this add/payout. The only documented sortable field, so backfill pages by it ascending.

dimensions.label: created at
dimensions.description: When the add/payout was recorded, store-local wall time with no timezone offset. This is the only time column on the object; there is no separate modification timestamp.

dimensions.label: notes
dimensions.description: Reason staff typed for the movement. Documented as 'a note for this payout' but it applies equally to adds. Frequently an empty string for routine floats, so any 'reason for payouts' analysis has poor coverage — test with NULLIF(TRIM(notes),'').

dimensions.label: employee id
dimensions.description: Employee who made the add/payout. Joins ls_employees.employee_id (workforce domain). 0 means unset; normalise to NULL. This is the accountability column for unexplained payouts.

dimensions.label: payment type id
dimensions.description: Tender that moved. Virtually always Cash in practice, but the field exists because Lightspeed permits adds and payouts of any configured tender — do not hardcode the cash assumption in aggregates. Joins ls_payment_types.payment_type_id. 0 means unset; normalise to NULL.

dimensions.label: register id
dimensions.description: Till the movement happened at. Joins ls_registers.register_id. There is no link to a register count — attributing a movement to a session requires this id plus a created_at BETWEEN opened_at AND closed_at predicate. 0 means unset; normalise to NULL.

dimensions.label: register id
dimensions.description: The register these running totals belong to. NOT present in the response body — it comes from the request path and must be stamped onto every row at ingest, otherwise a multi-register store's rows are indistinguishable. Joins ls_registers.register_id.

dimensions.label: payment type id
dimensions.description: The tender this running total is for. Harvested from the documented example payload only — no field table is published for this endpoint — but by R-Series convention it is an integer payment type id and joins ls_payment_types.payment_type_id.

dimensions.label: tax category id
dimensions.description: Unique id of the sales-tax configuration; the join target for Sale.taxCategoryID, Shop.taxCategoryID and ls_report_taxes_by_day.tax_category_id. Routinely confused with tax_class_id: a CATEGORY is the rate/authority (who you remit to), a CLASS is the item grouping (what is being taxed). The two id spaces overlap numerically, so a mistaken join silently returns plausible rows.

dimensions.label: is tax inclusive
dimensions.description: true when prices under this category are entered and displayed WITH tax already inside them (AU/NZ/UK convention), false when tax is added on top at the register (US convention). Wrong reading shifts every revenue figure by the whole rate: with true, ex-tax = price / (1 + rate); with false, ex-tax = price. It is a property of the CATEGORY, not of the shop or the item, so one account can legitimately mix both conventions across categories.

dimensions.label: tax1 name
dimensions.description: Label of the first component rate as printed on receipts and reports (e.g. 'GST', 'Sales Tax', 'State'). Cosmetic only - the remitting authority is implied by the category, never parsed from this string. Do not key logic on it; stores rename it freely.

dimensions.label: tax2 name
dimensions.description: Label of the second component rate (e.g. 'PST', 'County'). Empty string rather than NULL on single-tax accounts. A non-empty tax2_name paired with tax2_rate = 0 means the label was configured and then zeroed, not that a second tax applies.

dimensions.label: updated at
dimensions.description: When the category record was last modified, in store-local time. A change marker, NOT an effective-from date: there is no rate history table, so a rate edit silently rewrites the apparent past. Never restate historical tax by multiplying old sales by today's tax1_rate - use ls_report_taxes_by_day, which records what was actually collected.

dimensions.label: tax category id
dimensions.description: The owning tax category. The nested payload does not repeat the parent id, so the loader must stamp it onto each exploded child row; without it the override cannot be attributed and every rate lookup collapses to the wrong category.

dimensions.label: tax category class id
dimensions.description: Surrogate id of the override row itself. Its only real use is addressing the override for deletion (TaxCategory/{taxCategoryID}/TaxCategoryClass/{taxCategoryClassID}); it has no analytical meaning and should never be grouped on. Nullable if a given account's payload omits it.

dimensions.label: tax class id
dimensions.description: The tax class this override applies to. Joins ls_tax_classes.tax_class_id. Together with tax_category_id it forms the real grain: one override per (category, class) pair.

dimensions.label: tax class id
dimensions.description: Unique id of the tax class. Joined from Item.taxClassID, SaleLine.taxClassID, ls_report_tax_class_sales_by_day.tax_class_id and ls_report_orders_by_tax_class.tax_class_id. Do not confuse with tax_category_id - the id spaces overlap numerically and a crossed join returns rows rather than an error.

dimensions.label: name
dimensions.description: Human label of the class, e.g. 'Item', 'Labor', 'Gift Card'. Frequently EMPTY: Lightspeed auto-creates unnamed classes, so a raw class list shown to a human is full of blanks. 'Labor' (or its local equivalent) is the class that makes service-vs-retail margin analysis possible in ls_report_tax_class_sales_by_day.

dimensions.label: updated at
dimensions.description: When the class record was last modified, in store-local time. A change marker only; renaming a class rewrites its label everywhere retroactively, including in report rows fetched afterwards, so historical reports keyed on tax_class_name can shift meaning.

dimensions.label: payment type id
dimensions.description: Unique id of the tender method; the join target for SalePayment.paymentTypeID, RegisterWithdraw, RegisterCount and ls_report_payments_by_day.payment_type_id. Also the referent of refund_as_payment_type_id on other rows in this same table.

dimensions.label: name
dimensions.description: Display name of the tender as staff see it at the register ('Cash', 'Credit Card', 'Debit Card', 'Gift Card', 'Check'). This is the only place a store's own naming survives - `type` collapses several distinct tenders into one family, so card-brand or acquirer splits must be driven from this string.

dimensions.label: require customer
dimensions.description: true when a customer record must be attached to the sale before this tender may be used. Practically this flags account-bearing tenders (store credit, on-account, loyalty), so it is a decent proxy for 'this payment creates or settles a customer balance' when no ledger data is available.

dimensions.label: archived
dimensions.description: true when the tender has been retired from the register. Archiving does NOT remove history: past payments keep referencing the archived id. Filtering `archived = false` inside a join to payments therefore silently deletes historical takings and makes old months look smaller. Filter it only when listing tenders currently available for use.

dimensions.label: internal reserved
dimensions.description: true for predefined system tenders that a store cannot edit or delete (the set published in the API's Defined Values section). Useful for separating Lightspeed-managed plumbing - gift card, credit account, eCom, adjustment - from tenders the store created itself. Not a proxy for 'real money': system tenders carry genuine takings.

dimensions.label: type
dimensions.description: The tender FAMILY, used for grouping takings into cash/card/gift/account buckets. It is NOT the card network and NOT the acquirer: a row named 'Debit Card' carries type 'credit card'. Grouping tender mix by this column merges debit with credit and hides the store's own tender naming, which produces a plausible but wrong tender-mix chart.

dimensions.label: refund as payment type id
dimensions.description: The tender that refunds of this tender must be issued as (e.g. Gift Card refunds as Gift Card, Credit Account as Credit Account). ZERO IS A SENTINEL meaning 'any tender may be used for the refund' - it is NOT a foreign key to payment type 0. Joining it raw drops or mis-attributes every unrestricted tender; convert with NULLIF(refund_as_payment_type_id, 0) before joining.

dimensions.label: day
dimensions.description: The aggregation day these payments were taken on. The docs type it datetime, but the value is a day bucket, not an instant - there is no time-of-day detail here at all, so intraday or shift-level takings questions cannot be answered from this table.

dimensions.label: shop id
dimensions.description: The shop where the money was taken. Joins ls_shops.shop_id (location). Multi-shop accounts get one row per shop per tender per day, so omitting shop_id from a GROUP BY silently blends stores.

dimensions.label: is layaway
dimensions.description: true when the row totals payments taken against a LAYAWAY (a deposit toward goods not yet handed over), false for ordinary sale payments. It splits the grain: the same tender on the same day at the same shop can appear twice. Treating layaway deposits as revenue overstates the period, and filtering them out understates cash banked - decide which question is being asked.

dimensions.label: payment type name
dimensions.description: Denormalised tender name as of report generation. Convenient for grouping without a join, but it reflects the CURRENT name - a renamed tender changes historical labels. Group on payment_type_id when the series must stay stable.

dimensions.label: payment type id
dimensions.description: The tender this total is for. Joins ls_payment_types.payment_type_id to reach the family (`type`), archived flag and refund routing.

dimensions.label: day
dimensions.description: The aggregation day the taxes were collected on. Typed datetime in the docs but the value is a day bucket. Collection day, not liability date: a sale on the last day of a period lands in that period regardless of when the goods ship.

dimensions.label: shop id
dimensions.description: The shop where the tax was collected. Joins ls_shops.shop_id (location). On multi-shop accounts that remit separately, this is the column that splits the liability.

dimensions.label: tax category id
dimensions.description: The tax category (rate/authority) the total belongs to. Joins ls_tax_categories.tax_category_id. This is the CATEGORY axis, not the class axis - it answers 'who do I remit to', not 'what got taxed'.

dimensions.label: tax category name
dimensions.description: Denormalised category name as of report generation. Reflects the current label, so renaming a category retroactively relabels history; group on tax_category_id for stable series.

dimensions.label: day
dimensions.description: The aggregation day the discounts were given on. Typed datetime in the docs but the value is a day bucket. Days with no discounts may be absent rather than zero, so a time series must be joined against a generated calendar to avoid gaps reading as continuity.

dimensions.label: shop id
dimensions.description: The shop where the discounts were given. Joins ls_shops.shop_id (location). This is the only dimension besides day, so it is the finest cut available.

dimensions.label: day
dimensions.description: The aggregation day of these sale totals. Typed datetime in the docs but the value is a day bucket - no time-of-day, so no trading-hour or shift analysis is possible from this table.

dimensions.label: shop id
dimensions.description: The shop these sales were rung at. Joins ls_shops.shop_id (location). Omitting it from a GROUP BY blends stores with different pricing and cost bases.

dimensions.label: tax class id
dimensions.description: The tax class the totals belong to. Joins ls_tax_classes.tax_class_id. This is the CLASS axis (what was sold), not the category axis (who is remitted) - this report carries no tax figure at all, so it cannot answer remittance questions.

dimensions.label: tax class name
dimensions.description: Denormalised class name as of report generation ('Item', 'Labor', 'Gift Card'). Reflects the current label, so a renamed class retroactively relabels history; group on tax_class_id for stable series. May be empty for the auto-created unnamed classes that still carry money.

dimensions.label: received date
dimensions.description: The day the order was RECEIVED, not the day it was placed. Typed datetime in the docs but the value is a day bucket. Because the report is keyed on receipt, orders that are open, in transit or cancelled never appear at all - this table cannot measure purchase commitments, only arrivals.

dimensions.label: shop id
dimensions.description: The shop the order belongs to. Joins ls_shops.shop_id (location). On multi-shop accounts this is how restocking spend is attributed to a store.

dimensions.label: vendor id
dimensions.description: The vendor (supplier) this line is for. Joins ls_vendors.vendor_id. Note the docs phrase it per LINE, but the grain is order x tax class, so every row of one order carries the same vendor.

dimensions.label: vendor name
dimensions.description: Denormalised vendor name as of report generation. Convenient for grouping without a join, but it reflects the current name - a renamed or merged vendor retroactively relabels history. Group on vendor_id when the series must stay stable.

dimensions.label: tax class id
dimensions.description: The tax class the cost subtotal belongs to. Joins ls_tax_classes.tax_class_id. This is the axis that repeats within an order and therefore the axis that makes order-level columns dangerous to sum.

dimensions.label: tax class name
dimensions.description: Denormalised tax class name for this subtotal. Same retroactive-rename caveat as elsewhere; may be empty for auto-created unnamed classes that still carry cost.

dimensions.label: order id
dimensions.description: The purchase order this row is part of. Joins ls_orders.order_id. It REPEATS across the order's tax-class rows, so COUNT(*) counts subtotals rather than orders - use COUNT(DISTINCT order_id) for an order count.

dimensions.label: report year
dimensions.description: Tax year of the parent report; half of the composite key. A contact reappears each year it has reportable payments — always filter or group by year.

dimensions.label: contact id
dimensions.description: The Xero contact this 1099 row summarizes (spec spells it ContactId, lowercase d). Joins xero_contacts for the live record — which may have changed since this snapshot was computed.

dimensions.label: box2
dimensions.description: Amount in box 2 for the year; box semantics depend on the form revision for that year. Null/zero means nothing was bucketed there, not that the vendor is non-reportable.

dimensions.label: box3
dimensions.description: Amount in box 3 for the year; see box1 for the year-dependence caveat on box meanings.

dimensions.label: box4
dimensions.description: Amount in box 4 for the year — on common revisions this is federal income tax withheld, but verify against the year's form before reporting it as withholding.

dimensions.label: box5
dimensions.description: Amount in box 5 for the year; box semantics are form-revision dependent.

dimensions.label: box6
dimensions.description: Amount in box 6 for the year; box semantics are form-revision dependent.

dimensions.label: box8
dimensions.description: Amount in box 8 for the year; box semantics are form-revision dependent.

dimensions.label: box9
dimensions.description: Amount in box 9 for the year; box semantics are form-revision dependent.

dimensions.label: box10
dimensions.description: Amount in box 10 for the year; box semantics are form-revision dependent.

dimensions.label: box11
dimensions.description: Amount in box 11 for the year; box semantics are form-revision dependent.

dimensions.label: box13
dimensions.description: Amount in box 13 for the year. Note the payload has no Box12 at all — the numbering gap is verbatim from the API, not a load failure.

dimensions.label: box14
dimensions.description: Amount in box 14 for the year; box semantics are form-revision dependent.

dimensions.label: business name
dimensions.description: Trading/business name when it differs from the legal name. Blank for individuals operating under their own name.

dimensions.label: federal tax id type
dimensions.description: Kind of federal tax ID supplied (EIN vs SSN style). With tax_id it determines whether the TIN is personal data of an individual — treat the pair with W-9 handling rules.

dimensions.label: federal tax classification
dimensions.description: W-9 entity classification of the payee. Drives reportability rules (e.g. most C_CORP/S_CORP payments are exempt from 1099-NEC) — useful for explaining why a large vendor is absent from a year's report.

dimensions.label: report year
dimensions.description: Tax year this report covers, minted from the reportYear query parameter because the Report shape carries no identifier of its own. Partition key and the join key to xero_1099_contacts.

dimensions.label: report name
dimensions.description: Display name of the report as served. The spec's field documentation ('See Prepayment Types') is a copy-paste artifact — expect 1099 naming in real payloads.

dimensions.label: report type
dimensions.description: Report type discriminator of the shared Report envelope. The declared enum (AgedPayablesByContact) is itself a spec artifact of that shared shape — 1099 payloads flow through the same envelope. Never filter on this column; the year partition already isolates 1099 data.

dimensions.label: report title
dimensions.description: Human title rendered above the report. Presentation only.

dimensions.label: report date
dimensions.description: Date Xero generated this rendering of the report — generation time, not the tax period. The period is report_year.

dimensions.label: updated date utc
dimensions.description: When Xero last recomputed the report. If this moves for a past year, that year's box amounts have changed since you last read them — re-sync the child rows.

dimensions.label: account id
dimensions.description: Xero's immutable account identifier and the row key — the durable join target for journal lines, budget lines and every document line's AccountCode lookup.

dimensions.label: code
dimensions.description: Customer-defined alphanumeric code (max 10, e.g. '200' or 'SALES'). Editable and re-usable over time — join by account_id, present by code. Some system accounts have no code at all.

dimensions.label: name
dimensions.description: Current display name (max 150). Historical journal lines carry the name as at posting — after renames the two differ; this one is 'now'.

dimensions.label: type
dimensions.description: Granular account behavior. Use for operational slices (BANK accounts, DIRECTCOSTS vs OVERHEADS cost split); do NOT use for statement membership — SALES, REVENUE and OTHERINCOME are distinct Types inside one Class, and filtering type = 'REVENUE' silently drops sales accounts.

dimensions.label: status
dimensions.description: ACTIVE accounts are usable today; ARCHIVED/DELETED ones persist on history. Filter status for 'what can we post to now' questions only — historical aggregates must keep all statuses or old balances vanish.

dimensions.label: description
dimensions.description: Free-text purpose of the account (max 4000); valid for all types except bank accounts.

dimensions.label: bank account type
dimensions.description: Sub-kind of a BANK account — CREDITCARD spend behaves as liability-side cash, PAYPAL as a clearing wallet. Non-bank accounts return NONE or empty string; treat both as 'not a bank account'.

dimensions.label: currency code
dimensions.description: Currency of a bank account (bank accounts only; other accounts follow the org's base currency). Join xero_currencies for the display name. The spec's enum is the ISO-4217 set; the extracted list is truncated at HRK — treat values beyond it as valid ISO codes.

dimensions.label: tax type
dimensions.description: The account's DEFAULT tax rate (join to xero_tax_rates). Lines can override it — tax analysis of actual activity reads the line's tax_type, not this default.

dimensions.label: enable payments to account
dimensions.description: Whether payments may be applied directly to this account — how non-bank clearing accounts show up inside xero_payments.account_id.

dimensions.label: show in expense claims
dimensions.description: Whether the account is offered for expense-claim receipt coding — a UI availability flag, not evidence any claims exist.

dimensions.label: class
dimensions.description: Read-only statement classification and THE split for financial statements: REVENUE + EXPENSE classes form the P&L, ASSET + LIABILITY + EQUITY form the balance sheet. Every P&L query in this connector filters on this column — not on type.

dimensions.label: system account
dimensions.description: Set when Xero itself manages the account: DEBTORS is the AR control, CREDITORS the AP control, GST the tax control, RETAINEDEARNINGS the rollup. Non-system accounts return empty string or null — treat both as 'not system'. Exclude control accounts when analyzing discretionary spend, or AR/AP movements masquerade as activity.

dimensions.label: reporting code
dimensions.description: Regional statutory reporting code (e.g. NZ/AU report codes); shown only if set — null does not mean unclassified in Xero's own reports.

dimensions.label: reporting code name
dimensions.description: Read-only display name for the reporting code; shown only if set.

dimensions.label: has attachments
dimensions.description: True when files are attached to the account — pre-filter before org_meta's per-account attachments fan-out (rate-budgeted).

dimensions.label: updated date utc
dimensions.description: Last-modified audit stamp; the If-Modified-Since watermark for incremental account syncs.

dimensions.label: add to watchlist
dimensions.description: Whether the account appears in the Xero dashboard watchlist widget — a personalization flag with no accounting meaning.

dimensions.label: validation errors
dimensions.description: Write-response validation payload (ValidationError messages); null in read scans, kept verbatim for payload fidelity.

dimensions.label: singleton id
dimensions.description: Constant synthetic row key for the per-organisation singleton; the platform's tenant scoping makes the row unique. Exists only so the table has a declared grain key.

dimensions.label: asset number prefix
dimensions.description: Prefix Xero stamps onto new asset_number values ('FA-' by default). Strip it before sorting register numbers numerically.

dimensions.label: asset number sequence
dimensions.description: The NEXT sequence number Xero will issue, stored as text. A high-water mark, not a count of assets — deleted drafts consume numbers, so arithmetic on it misestimates register size.

dimensions.label: asset start date
dimensions.description: The date depreciation calculations started on registered fixed assets in Xero. Assets acquired earlier were migrated with an opening balance in prior_accum_depreciation_amount — expect no depreciation journals before this date.

dimensions.label: last depreciation date
dimensions.description: Through-date of the most recent depreciation run — the freshness bound for accounting_book_value and both accumulated-depreciation fields on every asset. If it lags today, book values are stale by exactly that gap; state the as-of date rather than presenting them as current.

dimensions.label: default gain on disposal account id
dimensions.description: GL account that ordinary disposal GAINS (recovery above book value, capped at original cost) default-post to; join xero_accounts for code and name. A default — individual disposals can be redirected in the UI.

dimensions.label: default loss on disposal account id
dimensions.description: GL account disposal LOSSES default-post to — the loss twin of the gain account. A disposal hits one or the other (plus possibly the capital-gain account), never both gain and loss.

dimensions.label: default capital gain on disposal account id
dimensions.description: GL account for the capital-gain slice (proceeds above original cost) on profitable disposals. Distinct from the ordinary gain account — conflating them mislabels the P&L line the gain lands on.

dimensions.label: opt in for tax
dimensions.description: Whether the organisation opted into Xero's tax depreciation calculation. Even when true, this connector revision carries no tax-book values (no taxValues object) — the flag records the election, not data availability.

dimensions.label: asset type id
dimensions.description: Xero's UUID for the asset type; the classification key xero_assets.asset_type_id points at.

dimensions.label: asset type name
dimensions.description: Name of the depreciation class ('Motor Vehicles', 'Office Equipment') and the natural label for register breakdowns. Editable — group by asset_type_id when identity over time matters.

dimensions.label: fixed asset account id
dimensions.description: GL account holding these assets' capitalised COST on the balance sheet; join to xero_accounts. The debit side of registration — not where depreciation expense goes.

dimensions.label: depreciation expense account id
dimensions.description: P&L account each depreciation run debits for assets of this type. 'Depreciation expense by class' resolves through this mapping into journal lines (ledger_config), not from register snapshots.

dimensions.label: accumulated depreciation account id
dimensions.description: Contra-asset balance-sheet account credited by depreciation runs; cost account plus this equals net book value in the GL. Same run as the expense account, different financial statement — confusing the two misstates both.

dimensions.label: book depreciation setting depreciation method
dimensions.description: Depreciation method handed to NEW assets of this type as a default. The asset's own depreciation_method is what actually runs — reporting the register from this column mislabels overridden assets.

dimensions.label: book depreciation setting averaging method
dimensions.description: Default first/last-period proration (whole-month vs daily) seeded onto new assets of this type; the operative value is xero_assets.averaging_method.

dimensions.label: book depreciation setting depreciation rate
dimensions.description: Default annual rate (decimal fraction, 0.05 = 5%) offered at registration when the calculation method is 'Rate'. A ratio and only a default — the operative rate is the asset's own depreciation_rate.

dimensions.label: book depreciation setting effective life years
dimensions.description: Default life in years for 'Life'-method assets of this type; the asset's own effective_life_years wins once registered.

dimensions.label: book depreciation setting depreciation calculation method
dimensions.description: Which default input this type hands to new assets: 'Rate' (default_depreciation_rate), 'Life' (default_effective_life_years) or 'None' for methods needing neither.

dimensions.label: book depreciation setting depreciable object id
dimensions.description: Xero's internal identifier for the object this default setting binds to (the asset type itself). Depreciation-engine plumbing, not an analytical join key.

dimensions.label: book depreciation setting depreciable object type
dimensions.description: Type discriminator for default_depreciable_object_id; engine plumbing.

dimensions.label: book depreciation setting book effective date of change id
dimensions.description: Identifier of the effective-dated change record if the type's default setting was amended; evidence of a policy change whose history stays inside Xero.

dimensions.label: locks
dimensions.description: Nonzero when assets of this type carry accumulated depreciation, which deletion-locks the type in Xero. Zero means deletable — such types can hard-delete and disappear from a later scan without a tombstone.

dimensions.label: asset id
dimensions.description: Xero's immutable UUID for the asset and the row key; stable across renames, status transitions and disposal.

dimensions.label: asset name
dimensions.description: Human-readable label shown in Xero's register and the natural display column. Editable at any time and not unique — asset_number is the stable human reference, asset_id the join key.

dimensions.label: asset type id
dimensions.description: Classifies the asset into its depreciation profile and, through xero_asset_types, the GL account trio (cost, accumulated depreciation, expense). Optional in the API, so Draft rows can be null; a Registered asset always has one.

dimensions.label: asset number
dimensions.description: Unique human-facing register reference, auto-issued as the settings prefix plus sequence (e.g. FA-0104) unless a custom number was typed at registration. Deleted drafts still consume sequence numbers, so gaps are normal and are not missing data.

dimensions.label: purchase date
dimensions.description: Acquisition date and the axis for capex-by-period questions. Not necessarily when depreciation begins — depreciation_start_date can trail it (delivered vs placed in service), so asset-age and remaining-life math should anchor on depreciation_start_date.

dimensions.label: disposal date
dimensions.description: Date the asset was sold, scrapped or written off; null unless asset_status = 'Disposed'. 'Disposals in period' filters this date — filtering purchase_date instead silently reports acquisitions.

dimensions.label: asset status
dimensions.description: Lifecycle gate for every aggregate: Draft exists only in the register (no GL impact yet), Registered is live and depreciating, Disposed is history with frozen figures. Net-book-value and depreciation totals filter 'Registered'; capex totals usually exclude only 'Draft'. Stored values are mixed-case — the API's status query filter uses uppercase DRAFT/REGISTERED/DISPOSED, but SQL against staging matches 'Registered'.

dimensions.label: warranty expiry date
dimensions.description: Warranty end date for maintenance and replacement planning. Spec-typed as a free string in YYYY-MM-DD form rather than a date field; staged as date. Null means unrecorded, not in or out of warranty.

dimensions.label: serial number
dimensions.description: Manufacturer serial recorded for physical identification, insurance and audit trails. Free text, not enforced unique — never a join key.

dimensions.label: book depreciation setting depreciation method
dimensions.description: The asset's OWN depreciation method, seeded from the type default at registration but overridable per asset — report from this column, not the type's default. NoDepreciation holds book value flat; FullDepreciation expenses the whole cost immediately; the DiminishingValue variants encode the declining-balance multiplier (100/150/200% of the straight-line rate).

dimensions.label: book depreciation setting averaging method
dimensions.description: How first and last depreciation periods are prorated: FullMonth books a whole month regardless of the in-month day, ActualDays prorates daily. Explains small differences when reconciling recomputed depreciation to Xero's own figures.

dimensions.label: book depreciation setting effective life years
dimensions.description: Asset life in whole years, operative only when depreciation_calculation_method = 'Life'. Exactly one of this and depreciation_rate drives the calculation — reading the inoperative one misexplains the expense.

dimensions.label: book depreciation setting depreciation calculation method
dimensions.description: Selector for WHICH input drives depreciation: 'Rate' uses depreciation_rate, 'Life' uses effective_life_years, 'None' means neither applies (NoDepreciation / FullDepreciation methods). Read the operative field, not both.

dimensions.label: book depreciation setting depreciable object id
dimensions.description: Xero's internal identifier for the depreciable object this setting binds to (the asset itself here). Depreciation-engine plumbing — analytical joins use asset_id.

dimensions.label: book depreciation setting depreciable object type
dimensions.description: Type discriminator for depreciable_object_id (which object class the setting attaches to). Engine plumbing, not an analytical dimension.

dimensions.label: book depreciation setting book effective date of change id
dimensions.description: Identifier of the effective-dated change record created when the depreciation setting was amended mid-life. Evidence that policy changed — the history itself is not exposed by this API.

dimensions.label: book depreciation detail depreciation start date
dimensions.description: Date book depreciation began — can trail purchase_date (delivered vs placed in service) and can also precede xero_asset_settings.asset_start_date for assets migrated into Xero, whose pre-Xero depreciation arrives as an opening balance in prior_accum_depreciation_amount. The anchor for asset age and remaining-life projections; using purchase_date instead overstates elapsed depreciation for assets placed in service late.

dimensions.label: book depreciation detail business use capital gain
dimensions.description: New Zealand organisations only: the business-use share of the disposal capital gain (NZ splits mixed-use assets). Null outside NZ — a jurisdictional null, not missing data.

dimensions.label: book depreciation detail business use current gain loss
dimensions.description: New Zealand only: disposal gain or loss attributable to the asset's business-use portion. Pair with private_use_current_gain_loss to reconstruct the full outcome of a mixed-use disposal.

dimensions.label: book depreciation detail private use capital gain
dimensions.description: New Zealand only: the private (non-business) share of the disposal capital gain, typically treated differently for tax than the business share. Null outside NZ.

dimensions.label: book depreciation detail private use current gain loss
dimensions.description: New Zealand only: disposal gain or loss on the private-use portion. Excluding it understates the economic result of mixed-use disposals; folding it into deductible P&L overstates the business result.

dimensions.label: book depreciation detail initial deduction percentage
dimensions.description: New Zealand only: the Investment Boost immediate-deduction percentage claimed on the asset. A rate, never summed; null outside NZ or when no boost was claimed.

dimensions.label: can rollback
dimensions.description: True when Xero can roll this asset's depreciation back individually (no 'legacy' journal entries and no lock period in the way). An operational capability flag — irrelevant to totals, but a hint that figures could still be restated.

dimensions.label: is delete enabled for date
dimensions.description: Whether Xero would currently allow this asset to be deleted (a server-computed UI affordance, mainly true for Drafts). Deletion is hard: a deleted asset disappears from the API rather than gaining a status, so absence from a fresh scan is the only tombstone.

dimensions.label: parent endpoint
dimensions.description: Namespace half of the polymorphic parent key. parent_id is meaningless without it: the same table mixes invoices, receipts, journals and contacts, so every query filters or groups by parent_endpoint before joining parent_id anywhere.

dimensions.label: parent id
dimensions.description: UUID of the record the file is attached to; join it to the endpoint's staging table (xero_invoices.invoice_id when parent_endpoint = 'Invoices', and so on).

dimensions.label: attachment id
dimensions.description: Xero's unique id for this attachment instance; the tie-breaking key when one parent carries several files.

dimensions.label: file name
dimensions.description: Original filename as uploaded. The only human-meaningful label — but user-typed, so 'scan001.pdf' tells you nothing; do not classify documents from names alone.

dimensions.label: url
dimensions.description: Link to the file on xero.com. It requires an authenticated Xero session and API fetches of the content are separately rate-budgeted — this is not a public, shareable download link.

dimensions.label: mime type
dimensions.description: Declared content type (application/pdf, image/png...). Set at upload and more trustworthy than the file_name extension for typing documents.

dimensions.label: content length
dimensions.description: File size in bytes. Safe to SUM for storage estimates at this table's grain — each row is a distinct uploaded copy.

dimensions.label: include online
dimensions.description: True when the file is exposed on the customer-facing online invoice. Only meaningful for invoice-family parents; elsewhere it is noise.

dimensions.label: bank transaction id
dimensions.description: Bank transaction whose line carries this assignment; lets department/region cuts of direct cash skip a hop when line detail is not needed.

dimensions.label: line index
dimensions.description: Zero-based position of the parent line in the bank transaction's LineItems array — pairs with bank_transaction_id to reach xero_bank_transaction_line_items.

dimensions.label: tracking index
dimensions.description: Zero-based position within the line's Tracking array; Xero permits at most two entries, one per active tracking category, so values are 0 or 1.

dimensions.label: tracking category id
dimensions.description: The tracking category (e.g. Department, Region) this assignment belongs to — join xero_tracking_categories. Aggregate WITHIN one category at a time or line amounts double across categories.

dimensions.label: tracking option id
dimensions.description: The chosen option under that category — join xero_tracking_options for governed, rename-proof labels.

dimensions.label: name
dimensions.description: Tracking category name as frozen at write time. Renames only reach rows written afterwards — group by tracking_category_id and label from xero_tracking_categories for consistent series.

dimensions.label: option
dimensions.description: Option label as frozen at write time; same rename caveat as name — filter by tracking_option_id when history must stay consistent.

dimensions.label: bank transaction id
dimensions.description: Owning bank transaction. A line means nothing alone: direction, status, date, currency and tax treatment all live on the parent — join it before aggregating anything.

dimensions.label: line index
dimensions.description: Zero-based position of the line in the parent's LineItems array. Completes the primary key and preserves order even if Xero ever omits or regenerates line_item_id.

dimensions.label: line item id
dimensions.description: Xero's identifier for the line. Some edit paths regenerate it, so treat it as an opaque handle — (bank_transaction_id, line_index) is the durable key across syncs.

dimensions.label: description
dimensions.description: Free-text narrative of what the money was for — usually the only human explanation on directly-coded cash and the richest signal for classifying spend.

dimensions.label: quantity
dimensions.description: Optional unit count; bank transaction lines frequently omit it because LineAmount is entered directly. Guard for null before dividing or multiplying with it.

dimensions.label: unit amount
dimensions.description: Optional per-unit price in the parent's currency (4dp requested). A price, not a total — never sum it; line_amount is the authoritative line value.

dimensions.label: item code
dimensions.description: User-defined code of the inventory/service Item when the line was coded to one; join xero_items on its code column. This is the mutable code, not the immutable ItemID.

dimensions.label: account code
dimensions.description: Chart-of-accounts CODE the line posts to. Some rows carry only this and not account_id — spend-by-account queries that ignore the code fallback silently drop lines.

dimensions.label: account id
dimensions.description: AccountID the line posts to — the durable join to xero_accounts and the 'where did the money go' dimension for direct cash coding. Fall back to account_code when null.

dimensions.label: tax type
dimensions.description: Tax rate code applied to the line — join xero_tax_rates.tax_type for the rate's name and percentage. Filter here for GST/VAT-exempt analysis instead of inferring from amounts.

dimensions.label: bank transaction id
dimensions.description: Xero's immutable identifier for this money movement and the row key; also the target of xero_bank_transfers' from/to leg pointers.

dimensions.label: type
dimensions.description: Direction plus provenance in one vocabulary. SPEND and RECEIVE are directly coded cash; RECEIVE-TRANSFER/SPEND-TRANSFER are the two legs every bank transfer mints (one per account); the -PREPAYMENT/-OVERPAYMENT types are bank-side shadows of prepayment and overpayment documents. Income/expense analysis must restrict to SPEND and RECEIVE — the shadow types restate money that already lives in xero_bank_transfers, xero_prepayments or xero_overpayments, and summing across all types double-counts it.

dimensions.label: contact contact id
dimensions.description: Who the money was received from or paid to, when the bookkeeper coded one — join to xero_contacts. Frequently null on feed-coded rows; null means 'no counterparty recorded', not 'no counterparty'.

dimensions.label: bank account account id
dimensions.description: The Xero BANK account the cash moved through — join to xero_accounts. Per-account cash analyses group by this, and it is why one transfer lands as two rows (one per account).

dimensions.label: bank account code
dimensions.description: User-assigned chart-of-accounts code of the bank account, denormalized for display. Codes are editable — the durable join is bank_account_id.

dimensions.label: bank account name
dimensions.description: Bank account display name as returned with the transaction; convenient for labels, but rename-proof reporting joins xero_accounts on bank_account_id.

dimensions.label: is reconciled
dimensions.description: True once the row is matched against an imported bank statement line. Unreconciled AUTHORISED rows are provisional bookkeeping — not less real, just unverified against the bank; reconciliation-status questions read this, never status.

dimensions.label: date
dimensions.description: Business date of the cash movement (YYYY-MM-DD, not when it was keyed in) — the axis for every cash-flow time series. Use updated_date_utc only for sync watermarks, never for business timing.

dimensions.label: reference
dimensions.description: Free-text reference. Per the spec it is only supported for plain SPEND and RECEIVE transactions — it cannot be set directly on transfer/prepayment/overpayment shadow rows, whose narrative lives on the source document (a transfer's Reference sits on xero_bank_transfers and propagates to its legs). Never use presence/absence of a reference to classify row types; type is the classifier.

dimensions.label: currency code
dimensions.description: ISO 4217 currency (Xero's CurrencyCode enum, ~170 values — not enumerated here) of every monetary field on this row. Summing totals across rows with different currency_code produces a number in no currency; convert via currency_rate first.

dimensions.label: url
dimensions.description: Deep link to the source document in a connected app (rendered as 'Go to App Name' in Xero); a provenance breadcrumb, not analytical data.

dimensions.label: status
dimensions.description: AUTHORISED rows are live; DELETED and VOIDED rows keep being returned by the API and keep landing in staging. Every aggregate filters status = 'AUTHORISED' or reversed history re-inflates cash totals.

dimensions.label: line amount types
dimensions.description: Declares whether LINE-level amounts include tax (Inclusive), exclude it (Exclusive) or carry none (NoTax). Header sub_total/total_tax/total are already normalized regardless; line-level analysis must consult this or tax double-counts on Inclusive documents.

dimensions.label: prepayment id
dimensions.description: Non-null exactly on RECEIVE-PREPAYMENT/SPEND-PREPAYMENT rows: the Prepayment document this row is the bank-side shadow of. Join xero_prepayments — and count the money in one table, never both.

dimensions.label: overpayment id
dimensions.description: Non-null exactly on RECEIVE-OVERPAYMENT/SPEND-OVERPAYMENT rows: the Overpayment document this row shadows. Join xero_overpayments — the credit's allocations live there, the cash movement lives here; sum one side only.

dimensions.label: updated date utc
dimensions.description: Xero's last-modified audit stamp and the incremental-sync watermark. Meaningless for business timing — an edit bumps it years after date; never use it in cash-flow series.

dimensions.label: has attachments
dimensions.description: True when at least one attachment (receipt scan, source doc) exists. The ingester uses it to gate per-transaction attachment fan-out (org_meta's xero_attachments) under Xero's 60-calls/min budget.

dimensions.label: status attribute string
dimensions.description: Write-time validation marker (e.g. ERROR/WARNING) echoed on batch upsert responses; effectively always null on read scans. Never encode business logic on it — status is the lifecycle field.

dimensions.label: validation errors
dimensions.description: Array of write-rejection messages the API echoes on failed upserts; empty on read scans. Kept verbatim for mechanical completeness — analysts should never filter on it.

dimensions.label: contact
dimensions.description: BankTransaction.Contact as returned by the pinned OpenAPI. Retained verbatim so the founding canonical mapper keeps reading the column it was written against.

dimensions.label: line items
dimensions.description: See LineItems Retained verbatim so the founding canonical mapper keeps reading the column it was written against.

dimensions.label: bank account
dimensions.description: BankTransaction.BankAccount as returned by the pinned OpenAPI. Retained verbatim so the founding canonical mapper keeps reading the column it was written against.

dimensions.label: bank transfer id
dimensions.description: Xero's immutable identifier for the transfer instruction; each such instruction also mints exactly two rows in xero_bank_transactions.

dimensions.label: from bank account account id
dimensions.description: Source bank account the money left — join xero_accounts; the SPEND-TRANSFER leg lands in this account.

dimensions.label: from bank account code
dimensions.description: Chart code of the source bank account, denormalized for display; codes are editable, so durable joins use from_bank_account_id.

dimensions.label: from bank account name
dimensions.description: Display name of the source bank account as returned with the transfer; label convenience only — rename-proof reporting joins xero_accounts.

dimensions.label: to bank account account id
dimensions.description: Destination bank account the money entered — join xero_accounts; the RECEIVE-TRANSFER leg lands in this account.

dimensions.label: to bank account code
dimensions.description: Chart code of the destination bank account, denormalized for display; the durable join is to_bank_account_id.

dimensions.label: to bank account name
dimensions.description: Display name of the destination bank account as returned with the transfer; prefer the id join to xero_accounts for governed labels.

dimensions.label: date
dimensions.description: Business date the transfer is recorded on (YYYY-MM-DD, carried by both legs) — the axis for movement-over-time questions; not the settlement date at the real-world bank.

dimensions.label: from bank transaction id
dimensions.description: Points at the SPEND-TRANSFER bank transaction minted in the source account — the join that proves a bank transaction row is a transfer leg rather than real spend.

dimensions.label: to bank transaction id
dimensions.description: Points at the RECEIVE-TRANSFER bank transaction minted in the destination account — with from_bank_transaction_id, the pair to exclude from income/expense analysis.

dimensions.label: from is reconciled
dimensions.description: Whether the source-account leg has been matched to an imported statement line; 'transfer in flight' checks read both reconciliation flags.

dimensions.label: to is reconciled
dimensions.description: Whether the destination-account leg has been matched to an imported statement line; false here with from_is_reconciled true is the classic in-transit signature.

dimensions.label: reference
dimensions.description: Free-text reference for the transfer — the spec's plural ('Reference for the transactions') covers the two leg transactions the transfer mints. Narrative only, no lifecycle or matching semantics.

dimensions.label: has attachments
dimensions.description: True when the transfer carries attachments; gates org_meta's per-parent attachment fan-out under Xero's 60-calls/min rate budget.

dimensions.label: created date utc
dimensions.description: Creation audit stamp — the only timestamp BankTransfer exposes, so it doubles as the append watermark. A later deletion bumps nothing; only full rescans with includeDeleted=true catch it.

dimensions.label: status
dimensions.description: AUTHORISED is live; DELETED transfers are only returned when the scan passes includeDeleted=true, and must be filtered from every total or reversed internal moves count as real.

dimensions.label: from tracking
dimensions.description: Up to two tracking category/option references applied to the source side, verbatim as [{TrackingCategoryID, TrackingOptionID, Name, Option}]. Rarely used; unnest with jsonb_array_elements when a category cut of transfers is genuinely needed.

dimensions.label: to tracking
dimensions.description: Up to two tracking category/option references applied to the destination side, same shape and caveats as from_tracking; the two sides may legitimately differ.

dimensions.label: validation errors
dimensions.description: Array of write-rejection messages echoed on failed upserts; empty on read scans and kept only for mechanical completeness — never filter on it.

dimensions.label: batch payment id
dimensions.description: Xero's read-only identifier for the batch and the row key; the value member payments carry in xero_payments.batch_payment_id.

dimensions.label: type
dimensions.description: Direction of the whole batch: PAYBATCH pays supplier bills, RECBATCH collects customer invoices. Filter it on every batched-cash question — mixing types nets disbursements against receipts into a meaningless figure.

dimensions.label: status
dimensions.description: AUTHORISED is live; DELETED batches (removed in the Xero UI — the API cannot delete them) keep returning with their members intact. Filter status = 'AUTHORISED' everywhere or deleted batches inflate cash movement.

dimensions.label: account account id
dimensions.description: The bank account the single consolidated movement hits, from the embedded Account stub. Join xero_accounts for code/name; the batch appears on this account's statement as ONE line.

dimensions.label: date
dimensions.description: The date the batch is paid or collected — the business axis for batched cash flow. Member payments carry their own dates which normally match but are independently editable.

dimensions.label: date string
dimensions.description: String twin of date as returned by the API. Redundant — read date.

dimensions.label: amount
dimensions.description: Header-level amount slot whose spec text is copied verbatim from Payment.Amount (a documented spec quirk) — it is a write-side field, not the reconciled batch figure. Report batched cash from total_amount, the read-only sum Xero computes from the member payments; never let this column and total_amount both feed a metric.

dimensions.label: is reconciled
dimensions.description: Whole-batch reconciliation state against the bank feed: the batch lands on the statement as one line, and this flag says whether that line has been matched. Member payments carry their own is_reconciled in xero_payments — read the level you are actually asking about; do not treat this header flag as a per-payment guarantee.

dimensions.label: reference
dimensions.description: (NZ orgs only) Optional reference shown with the batch on the bank reconciliation Find & Match screen and possibly the imported bank statement. Region-specific: null outside NZ.

dimensions.label: particulars
dimensions.description: (NZ orgs only) Bank 'particulars' code accompanying the batch on statements and bank rec. Null outside NZ.

dimensions.label: code
dimensions.description: (NZ orgs only) Bank 'code' reference accompanying the batch. Null outside NZ; not an account code — do not join it to anything.

dimensions.label: details
dimensions.description: (Non-NZ orgs) Reference sent to the org's bank with the batch transaction, max 18 chars. Free text for statement matching.

dimensions.label: narrative
dimensions.description: (UK orgs only) Statement-line text shown in Xero only, max 18 chars. Null outside the UK.

dimensions.label: payments
dimensions.description: Verbatim member-payment stubs exactly as the BatchPayments endpoint returned them, kept for payload-level reconciliation. The queryable membership edge is xero_payments.batch_payment_id — always use that join; these stubs are partial and go stale.

dimensions.label: updated date utc
