dimensions.description: Owning organisation; inherited from the parent profile row during the same scan.

dimensions.label: address type
dimensions.description: Which slot this row fills. 'The org's address' is ambiguous until you pick one: statements and invoices show the postal (POBOX) address, while STREET is the physical location. Choosing the wrong slot puts the wrong address on generated documents.

dimensions.label: city
dimensions.description: Town/city component (max 255). Free text — normalize casing before grouping.

dimensions.label: region
dimensions.description: State/region/county component. Free text, not a controlled state code — 'NSW' and 'New South Wales' both occur.

dimensions.label: country
dimensions.description: Country as letters-only free text (max 50) — NOT guaranteed to be an ISO code ('New Zealand', not 'NZ'). For reliable country grouping use xero_organisations.country_code instead.

dimensions.label: organisation id
dimensions.description: The organisation whose CIS settings these are — the fan-out path parameter, minted onto the row because the CISOrgSetting payload carries no id of its own.

dimensions.label: cis contractor enabled
dimensions.description: True when the org files CIS as a contractor — it deducts tax from subcontractor labour, and CIS-labour line items on its bills carry those deductions.

dimensions.label: cis sub contractor enabled
dimensions.description: True when the org is itself a CIS subcontractor — customers withhold the deduction from ITS invoices, so cash received legitimately undershoots invoiced totals by the CIS rate.

dimensions.label: organisation id
dimensions.description: Owning organisation; inherited from the parent profile row during the same scan.

dimensions.label: ordinal
dimensions.description: Minted array position — stable only within a single sync because the source has no link id. Never persist references to it across refreshes.

dimensions.label: link type
dimensions.description: Which service the link points at. Values are mixed-case exactly as the enum spells them ('Website', not 'WEBSITE') — filters are case-sensitive.

dimensions.label: url
dimensions.description: Public profile/website URL as entered by the org — marketing surface, not verified or normalized.

dimensions.label: description
dimensions.description: Optional free-text label for the link; usually null.

dimensions.label: organisation id
dimensions.description: Owning organisation; inherited from the parent profile row during the same scan.

dimensions.label: term scope
dimensions.description: Which side of the business the default applies to: SALES governs new receivable invoices you issue, BILLS governs new payables you record. Reading the BILLS row as customer terms inverts the direction of the policy.

dimensions.label: bills type
dimensions.description: The due-date formula day plugs into. DAYSAFTERBILLDATE: day days after the document date; DAYSAFTERBILLMONTH: day days after the end of the document's month; OFCURRENTMONTH/OFFOLLOWINGMONTH: due on the day-th of this/next month. Note the spec's branch type is named 'Bill' (a payment-term shape), unrelated to supplier bills. Projection reads PaymentTerm.Bills.Type for the BILLS row and PaymentTerm.Sales.Type for the SALES row (term_scope selects the branch).

dimensions.label: organisation id
dimensions.description: Owning organisation; inherited from the parent profile row during the same scan.

dimensions.label: phone type
dimensions.description: Slot key from Xero's fixed phone-type set (DEFAULT, DDI, MOBILE, FAX, OFFICE — the shared Phone schema's enum, which lives in contacts_dir's ground truth). DEFAULT is the primary number to display.

dimensions.label: organisation id
dimensions.description: Xero's immutable identifier for the organisation and the row key. For ORGANISATION-type tenants it is the same UUID presented as the xero-tenant-id header, i.e. it equals xero_connections.tenant_id — that equality is the join between authorization metadata and the profile.

dimensions.label: api key
dimensions.description: Xero-to-Xero network key displayed in org settings. It is an operational credential, not an analytical attribute — never surface it in generated answers; it lands in staging only for settings-snapshot completeness.

dimensions.label: name
dimensions.description: Display name shown inside Xero and the label to use in multi-org answers. Routinely differs from legal_name after rebrands — do not treat the two as interchangeable.

dimensions.label: legal name
dimensions.description: The name Xero prints on reports and statutory-style documents. Prefer it for formal output, name for conversational labels.

dimensions.label: pays tax
dimensions.description: Whether the org is registered with its local tax authority (GST/VAT registered). When false, zero tax amounts across documents are expected behaviour — a 'missing tax' finding on a non-registered org is not a data gap.

dimensions.label: version
dimensions.description: Regional edition the org was provisioned on; each *ONRAMP value pairs with the plain region its name prefixes (AUONRAMP with AU, and so on), so group them with their base region for regional analysis. This — not country_code alone — decides how tax_number reads (TFN vs GST vs VAT vs Tax ID), which payroll region can exist, and which tax bases are plausible. Key regional logic off it.

dimensions.label: organisation type
dimensions.description: One of the record's two identically-enumerated legal-form classifications (the other is organisation_entity_type); the spec documents no precedence between them and in practice they carry the same value. Segment on one column consistently — mixing the two across queries splits cohorts whenever they disagree.

dimensions.label: base currency
dimensions.description: The currency every journal line and base-converted total resolves to (spec enum CurrencyCode, ISO 4217; the full value list is larger than the extract inlines, so it is deliberately not enumerated here). Documents carry their own CurrencyCode plus a CurrencyRate back to THIS currency — summing raw document amounts across orgs with different base currencies produces a number in no currency at all.

dimensions.label: country code
dimensions.description: ISO 3166 alpha-2 home country (spec enum CountryCode, not inlined in full). Use for geographic grouping; use version for behavioural semantics — a GLOBAL-version org can sit in any country.

dimensions.label: is demo company
dimensions.description: True for Xero's sample company. Its invoices, payments and contacts are fabricated but look real in every downstream table — exclude demo orgs from any aggregate that reaches a human, or the rollup reports revenue that does not exist.

dimensions.label: organisation status
dimensions.description: ACTIVE when the API can address the org. Anything else means the tenant is not currently reachable, so expect stale staging data downstream — not fresh zeros.

dimensions.label: registration number
dimensions.description: Companies-register number, shown for NZ/AU/UK orgs. Public company identifier and the anchor for matching the org to external registries; not personal data.

dimensions.label: sales tax basis
dimensions.description: Accounting basis used for tax returns; the enum mixes regional vocabularies (PAYMENTS/INVOICE are NZ-style, CASH/ACCRUAL AU/US, FLATRATE* UK schemes). It changes when tax is reported, not what documents say — do not use it to reinterpret invoice tax fields.

dimensions.label: sales tax period
dimensions.description: Filing frequency for tax returns, again a regionally-mixed vocabulary. Useful for anticipating filing/lock cadence; never a transformation input for amounts.

dimensions.label: default sales tax
dimensions.description: Default LineAmountTypes label applied to NEW sales documents ('Tax Exclusive' etc.). A UI default only — every document carries its own LineAmountTypes, which is what governs that document's line maths. Never apply this org default to interpret existing lines.

dimensions.label: default purchases tax
dimensions.description: Default LineAmountTypes label for new purchase documents. Same warning as default_sales_tax: a default for data entry, not a fact about stored documents.

dimensions.label: period lock date
dimensions.description: Standard users cannot edit transactions dated on or before this date. Numbers before the lock are closed for reporting; a restatement before the lock implies an adviser-level edit. Null when no lock is set.

dimensions.label: end of year lock date
dimensions.description: The adviser-level year-end lock. Anything before it is effectively published accounts; treat pre-lock movements in staging as re-sync artifacts to investigate, not business changes to report.

dimensions.label: created date utc
dimensions.description: When the org was created in Xero. Documents DATED before this are conversion/migration balances from a prior system, not live trading history — a useful tripwire when 'first year' growth looks impossible.

dimensions.label: timezone
dimensions.description: Org display timezone (spec enum TimeZone, not inlined in full). Xero business dates (Date, DueDate) are calendar dates unaffected by it; use it only when bucketing UTC audit timestamps (UpdatedDateUTC, history DateUTC) into local days.

dimensions.label: organisation entity type
dimensions.description: Legal-form classification (company, partnership, trust, sole trader...) — the attribute to segment a portfolio by entity type. Shares its exact vocabulary with organisation_type and normally agrees with it; the spec declares no precedence, so pick one column for segmentation and coalesce to the other only when it is null.

dimensions.label: short code
dimensions.description: Short identifier used in Xero deep links (Go URLs). Handy for constructing links back into the Xero UI; never a join key.

dimensions.label: class
dimensions.description: Subscription plan family. LEDGER and *_CASHBOOK classes are adviser-managed books with reduced feature sets — empty invoicing or payroll tables under those classes are plan limitations, not sync failures. DEMO/TRIAL classes corroborate is_demo_company-style exclusions.

dimensions.label: edition
dimensions.description: BUSINESS or PARTNER. PARTNER-edition orgs are sold through accounting partners with restricted functionality — some have no invoicing at all. Check this before diagnosing missing documents as an ingestion bug.

dimensions.label: line of business
dimensions.description: Free-text industry description typed by the org owner. Uncontrolled vocabulary — group with care and never treat as an enum.

dimensions.label: external links
dimensions.description: Verbatim ExternalLinks array (social/website profile links). Present only when the org has updated Organisation settings; the normalized surface is xero_organisation_external_links.

dimensions.label: payment terms
dimensions.description: Verbatim PaymentTerms object ({Bills:{Day,Type}, Sales:{Day,Type}}) — the org-level DEFAULT due-date rules. The queryable form is xero_organisation_payment_terms; neither overrides a document's own DueDate.

dimensions.label: overpayment overpayment id
dimensions.description: Parent overpayment whose credit this row consumes. Populated by the ingester from the parent scan context; provenance is the Allocation shape's source-document echo slot, which the API rarely materializes inline.

dimensions.label: allocation ordinal
dimensions.description: Array position within the parent payload, minted because older payloads omit AllocationID. Stable only within one parent version — the set is replaced whenever the parent re-syncs; never diff ordinals across syncs.

dimensions.label: allocation id
dimensions.description: Xero's allocation identifier when returned (used for allocation deletes upstream). Not the row key because legacy payloads omit it; prefer it for entity resolution when present.

dimensions.label: invoice invoice id
dimensions.description: The invoice this slice of credit paid down. Customer-side credit lands on ACCREC invoices, supplier-side on ACCPAY bills; direction comes from the parent overpayment's type. Join xero_invoices for what got settled.

dimensions.label: date
dimensions.description: When the credit was applied — the settlement date for invoices paid by overpayment credit. Distinct from, and often later than, the parent's own date.

dimensions.label: is deleted
dimensions.description: The spec's delete-acknowledgement flag, seen on delete responses. On reads a removed allocation simply vanishes from the parent's array — detect unwound applications by set comparison across syncs, not by this flag.

dimensions.label: status attribute string
dimensions.description: Write-response artefact indicating payload status. Ignore for analytics.

dimensions.label: validation errors
dimensions.description: API validation messages retained verbatim; empty on healthy reads.

dimensions.label: overpayment id
dimensions.description: Xero's immutable identifier for the overpayment and the row key; allocations and refund payments point back to it.

dimensions.label: type
dimensions.description: Direction of the credit. RECEIVE-OVERPAYMENT/AROVERPAYMENT: a customer paid you too much (you owe it back). SPEND-OVERPAYMENT: you overpaid a supplier. Pick a side in every question — netting the two hides both the liability and the asset. Note the spec lists no AP* alias here; supplier-side rows arrive as SPEND-OVERPAYMENT.

dimensions.label: contact contact id
dimensions.description: The counterparty who over- or was over-paid, from the embedded Contact stub. Join xero_contacts for names and merge survivorship.

dimensions.label: date
dimensions.description: The date the overpayment was created — when the excess cash actually moved. Allocation dates on the child table are when the credit was later consumed.

dimensions.label: status
dimensions.description: AUTHORISED still carries credit; PAID means fully applied or refunded; VOIDED is cancelled but still returned by the API. Exclude VOIDED from every total or outstanding credit is overstated.

dimensions.label: line amount types
dimensions.description: How amounts inside line_items relate to tax (Exclusive/Inclusive/NoTax). Overpayment lines are typically NoTax because the excess is pure settlement, but do not assume — the header sub_total/total_tax/total are always normalized regardless.

dimensions.label: line items
dimensions.description: Verbatim ordered line array, auto-generated when the excess was banked. Kept as payload: document totals answer overpayment questions, and the coding here is mechanical (a receivable/payable suspense line), not analyst-facing. Interpret raw LineAmount only with line_amount_types.

dimensions.label: total tax
dimensions.description: Total tax on the overpayment; normally 0.00 because an overpayment is settlement excess, not a taxable supply. Non-zero values deserve investigation before they enter any tax report.

dimensions.label: currency code
dimensions.description: Document currency for every monetary column on this row. The extracted spec enum truncates mid-alphabet (ends at HRK) — treat the value set as open ISO-4217 (USD, NZD, SGD and others occur constantly); never validate against the enum list. Summing across currencies without converting via currency_rate is meaningless.

dimensions.label: applied amount
dimensions.description: Credit consumed against invoices so far, as a current-state figure. Per-invoice, per-date detail lives in xero_overpayment_allocations — use that for any time-based analysis.

dimensions.label: allocations
dimensions.description: Verbatim allocation array for payload-level audit. The analytic surface is xero_overpayment_allocations, exploded one row per application — query that, not this.

dimensions.label: payments
dimensions.description: Refund-payment stubs returned inline. Canonical refund rows live in xero_payments with overpayment_id set and payment_type AROVERPAYMENTPAYMENT/APOVERPAYMENTPAYMENT — use that join.

dimensions.label: reference
dimensions.description: Optional free-text description of the overpayment. Display and matching material only.

dimensions.label: has attachments
dimensions.description: True when files are attached; the rows come from org_meta's xero_attachments fan-out (rate-budgeted).

dimensions.label: attachments
dimensions.description: Attachment stubs if included inline (usually absent on list reads). Governed attachment data lives in xero_attachments.

dimensions.label: updated date utc
dimensions.description: Audit watermark for incremental sync; moves when allocations or refunds change, which keeps the child table fresh. Not a business date.

dimensions.label: updated date utc string
dimensions.description: ISO-8601 string twin of updated_date_utc. Redundant — read the timestamp column.

dimensions.label: payment service id
dimensions.description: Xero's identifier for the configured service and the row key.

dimensions.label: payment service name
dimensions.description: Display name of the service ('Stripe', 'PayPal', a custom gateway). Free text chosen by the org — do not key provider logic off it.

dimensions.label: payment service url
dimensions.description: The custom payment URL customers are sent to from online invoices, usually templated with invoice placeholders. Configuration, not evidence a payment happened.

dimensions.label: pay now text
dimensions.description: Label on the Pay Now button in Xero Online Invoicing; defaults to 'Pay by credit card' when unset. Presentation only.

dimensions.label: payment service type
dimensions.description: Service kind. The spec declares no enum but states API-created services are always CUSTOM; natively integrated gateways configured in the UI may surface other values — treat as open vocabulary.

dimensions.label: validation errors
dimensions.description: API validation messages retained verbatim; empty on healthy reads.

dimensions.label: payment id
dimensions.description: Xero's immutable payment identifier and the row key. Stable across edits; deleting a payment flips status to DELETED rather than removing this row from the API.

dimensions.label: payment type
dimensions.description: What kind of application this is. ACCRECPAYMENT is a customer paying an invoice; ACCPAYPAYMENT is you paying a bill; the six *CREDIT/*OVERPAYMENT/*PREPAYMENT types are refunds of credit documents — money moving in the OPPOSITE direction to the ordinary payment on the same AR/AP side. Collections analysis must whitelist ACCRECPAYMENT: including refund types overstates receipts, and including ACCPAYPAYMENT mixes directions.

dimensions.label: status
dimensions.description: AUTHORISED is a live application; DELETED is a reversed one that Xero keeps returning forever. Every cash total must filter status = 'AUTHORISED' — deleted payments otherwise resurrect settled history and un-paid invoices look paid.

dimensions.label: date
dimensions.description: The business date the cash applied — the axis for collections, DSO and cash-timing questions. It is user-keyed and can be backdated into closed periods, so 'cash collected in March' can change after March; use updated_date_utc to detect that drift.

dimensions.label: reference
dimensions.description: Free-text remittance description ('Direct Debit', cheque number). Reconciliation matching material — never a join key and never unique.

dimensions.label: is reconciled
dimensions.description: True once the payment is matched to a bank statement line. An unreconciled AUTHORISED payment is a real application whose cash is not yet confirmed by the bank feed — state which basis (book vs bank-confirmed) a cash answer uses.

dimensions.label: account account id
dimensions.description: The bank or clearing account the cash touched, from the embedded Account stub. Join xero_accounts for code, name and class; do not assume it is a BANK-class account — clearing and current-asset accounts appear here too.

dimensions.label: code
dimensions.description: Code of the account used to make the payment, echoed flat beside the Account stub. Not all accounts carry codes — join on account_id, not on this.

dimensions.label: invoice invoice id
dimensions.description: Set when this payment settles an invoice. The invoice may be a sale (ACCREC) or a bill (ACCPAY) — direction comes from payment_type or Invoice.Type after the join. Exactly one of invoice_id, credit_note_id, prepayment_id, overpayment_id is non-null per row.

dimensions.label: invoice number
dimensions.description: Human-readable number of the settled invoice, denormalized for display. Numbers are org-editable and not guaranteed unique across drafts — join on invoice_id for correctness.

dimensions.label: credit note credit note id
dimensions.description: Set when this row is a CASH REFUND of a credit note (payment_type ARCREDITPAYMENT/APCREDITPAYMENT). The credit note's non-cash applications to invoices live in xero_credit_note_allocations, not here.

dimensions.label: credit note number
dimensions.description: Display number of the refunded credit note. Same caveat as invoice_number: join on credit_note_id, not the number.

dimensions.label: prepayment prepayment id
dimensions.description: Set when this row refunds unapplied prepayment credit back to the counterparty (payment_type ARPREPAYMENTPAYMENT/APPREPAYMENTPAYMENT). The ORIGINAL prepayment cash arrived as a bank transaction, not as a row here — counting both directions as collections cancels real cash.

dimensions.label: overpayment overpayment id
dimensions.description: Set when this row refunds overpayment credit (payment_type AROVERPAYMENTPAYMENT/APOVERPAYMENTPAYMENT). Overpayment credit consumed against invoices is in xero_overpayment_allocations; only the cash-out refund appears here.

dimensions.label: batch payment id
dimensions.description: Present iff the payment was created inside a batch; groups member payments into the single bank movement on xero_batch_payments. Null for individually entered payments. This is the join key for batch membership.

dimensions.label: batch payment
dimensions.description: Verbatim embedded stub of the parent batch (id, type, status, totals) exactly as the Payments endpoint returned it, kept for payload-level audit only. Query batch attributes through the batch_payment_id join to xero_batch_payments, where they are typed and current — this stub goes stale when the batch is edited.

dimensions.label: details
dimensions.description: Remittance text that appears on the supplier's bank statement (non-NZ orgs; 18-char limit at write time). Free text for reconciliation, never a key.

dimensions.label: has account
dimensions.description: API-mechanics flag from the write path (the spec ties it to validation problems on the payload). No analytic meaning — never filter business questions on it.

dimensions.label: has validation errors
dimensions.description: True when the API attached validation messages to this record on a write response. Ingestion diagnostics only.

dimensions.label: status attribute string
dimensions.description: Write-response artefact ('OK'/'ERROR'-style) meaningful only on rows echoed back from a create/update call. Ignore for analytics.

dimensions.label: validation errors
dimensions.description: Array of API validation messages, populated on error responses and retained verbatim for ingestion debugging. Empty on healthy reads.

dimensions.label: warnings
dimensions.description: Array of API warning messages returned with the record, verbatim. Diagnostics only; carries no business signal.

dimensions.label: updated date utc
dimensions.description: Audit watermark driving incremental sync; moves when a payment is edited or deleted. Use date for business time — this timestamp is when the RECORD changed, not when cash moved.

dimensions.label: updated date utc string
dimensions.description: ISO-8601 string twin of updated_date_utc returned by the API for convenience. Redundant — always read updated_date_utc.

dimensions.label: invoice
dimensions.description: Payment.Invoice as returned by the pinned OpenAPI. Retained verbatim so the founding canonical mapper keeps reading the column it was written against.

dimensions.label: credit note
dimensions.description: Payment.CreditNote as returned by the pinned OpenAPI. Retained verbatim so the founding canonical mapper keeps reading the column it was written against.

dimensions.label: prepayment
dimensions.description: Payment.Prepayment as returned by the pinned OpenAPI. Retained verbatim so the founding canonical mapper keeps reading the column it was written against.

dimensions.label: overpayment
dimensions.description: Payment.Overpayment as returned by the pinned OpenAPI. Retained verbatim so the founding canonical mapper keeps reading the column it was written against.

dimensions.label: account
dimensions.description: Payment.Account as returned by the pinned OpenAPI. Retained verbatim so the founding canonical mapper keeps reading the column it was written against.

dimensions.label: deduction type id
dimensions.description: Xero's immutable deduction pay item identifier; payslip deduction lines reference it.

dimensions.label: name
dimensions.description: Admin-chosen label of the deduction (the spec's doc-string wrongly says 'earnings rate'). Display only; behaviour flags below carry the semantics.

dimensions.label: account code
dimensions.description: GL account code the withheld money is posted to (typically a liability until remitted). Join xero_accounts on code.

dimensions.label: reduces tax
dimensions.description: True marks a PRE-TAX deduction that shrinks the PAYG base. The flag that separates salary packaging from ordinary after-tax deductions — effective-tax comparisons that ignore it misread packaged employees as under-taxed.

dimensions.label: reduces super
dimensions.description: True when the deduction also reduces the super guarantee base — rare and usually deliberate. If SGC looks low for some employees, check their deductions for this flag before suspecting error.

dimensions.label: is exempt from w1
dimensions.description: Whether amounts on this deduction sit outside BAS label W1. Only matters when reconciling payroll to a lodged BAS, and that is exactly when it matters most: a W1 figure built from gross wages without honouring this flag will not tie to what was reported to the ATO.

dimensions.label: updated date utc
dimensions.description: Last-modified audit stamp on the pay item and the incremental sync watermark for the PayItems scan. Ticks on configuration edits only — it says nothing about when deductions were actually taken.

dimensions.label: deduction category
dimensions.description: STP classification: UNIONFEES and WORKPLACEGIVING are separately reported to the ATO; NONE is everything else. The filter for charitable-giving and union-fee questions.

dimensions.label: current record
dimensions.description: Active flag. Filter true for configuration listings; never filter when joining from historical deduction lines.

dimensions.label: earnings rate id
dimensions.description: Xero's immutable pay item identifier; earnings lines and timesheet lines reference it.

dimensions.label: name
dimensions.description: Admin-chosen label ('Ordinary Hours', 'Sat Overtime'). Display only — classification logic must use earnings_type, since orgs name items inconsistently.

dimensions.label: account code
dimensions.description: GL expense account code this pay item posts wages to; join xero_accounts on code to tie payroll to the P&L.

dimensions.label: type of units
dimensions.description: The unit label ('Hours') for RATEPERUNIT items. Tells you what a line's number_of_units means — summing units across items with different unit types is meaningless.

dimensions.label: is exempt from tax
dimensions.description: True when payments on this item escape PAYG withholding. Effective-tax-rate analyses must exclude exempt items from the taxable base.

dimensions.label: is exempt from super
dimensions.description: True when this pay does not attract superannuation guarantee. Explains why SGC is less than 'rate x total wages' whenever exempt items (some allowances, overtime) are in the mix.

dimensions.label: is reportable as w1
dimensions.description: Whether payments on this item count in BAS label W1 (gross wages reported to the ATO). W1 reconciliation must filter on this — total wages and W1 wages legitimately differ.

dimensions.label: is qualifying earnings
dimensions.description: Whether this item counts as qualifying earnings for the superannuation guarantee calculation base. The precise SG-base flag, distinct from is_exempt_from_super's blunt exclusion.

dimensions.label: allowance contributes to annual leave rate
dimensions.description: For RATEPERUNIT allowances only: whether the allowance feeds the annual-leave pay rate. Configuration nuance for leave-cost modelling; null/false elsewhere.

dimensions.label: allowance contributes to overtime rate
dimensions.description: For RATEPERUNIT allowances only: whether this allowance is rolled into the base used to compute overtime rates. When true the allowance's cost is already reflected inside a richer overtime rate on the payslip lines, so adding an 'allowance uplift' on top of overtime spend counts it twice.

dimensions.label: earnings type
dimensions.description: The ATO classification of this pay item and the primary split key for all wage analysis: ordinary time vs overtime vs allowances vs bonuses vs termination payments (ETP/Lump sums) vs paid parental leave vs workers comp. Termination-related types distort averages — exclude them from run-rate wage metrics.

dimensions.label: rate type
dimensions.description: How the item is valued: FIXEDAMOUNT (see amount), MULTIPLE of the employee's ordinary rate (see multiplier), or RATEPERUNIT (see rate_per_unit). Tells you which default column is meaningful; the actual paid value is on the payslip line.

dimensions.label: rate per unit
dimensions.description: DEFAULT rate per unit for RATEPERUNIT items (the spec transmits it as a string; staged numeric). Employees and payslip lines can override it — cost calculations must use the line-level rate, not this default.

dimensions.label: multiplier
dimensions.description: For MULTIPLE items, the factor applied to the employee's ordinary rate (1.5 = time-and-a-half). A rate parameter — never summed.

dimensions.label: accrue leave
dimensions.description: For MULTIPLE items: whether hours paid on this item also accrue leave. Explains accrual differences between ordinary and overtime hours.

dimensions.label: amount
dimensions.description: Optional default amount for FIXEDAMOUNT items. A configured default, not money paid — paid amounts live on payslip earnings lines.

dimensions.label: employment termination payment type
dimensions.description: For EMPLOYMENTTERMINATIONPAYMENT items: ATO ETP code O (other) or R (redundancy/invalidity-related). Drives ETP tax treatment; only relevant on termination analysis.

dimensions.label: updated date utc
dimensions.description: Last-modified audit stamp on the pay item and the incremental sync watermark for the PayItems scan. It ticks when someone edits the item's rate or flags — it says nothing about when anyone was paid on it, so never use it as an activity date for the earnings it classifies.

dimensions.label: current record
dimensions.description: True for the org's active pay items; false for retired ones kept for history. Filter true when listing configurable items; do NOT filter when joining from payslip lines, or historical wages lose their classification.

dimensions.label: allowance type
dimensions.description: STP allowance classification (CAR, MEALS, TRAVEL...) for ALLOWANCE items; null otherwise. The ATO reporting split for allowance spend.

dimensions.label: allowance category
dimensions.description: STP Phase 2 sub-categorisation of OTHER-type allowances (uniform, private vehicle, home office...). Null for non-allowance items.

dimensions.label: employee id
dimensions.description: Owning employee (inherited key from the parent scan).

dimensions.label: line index
dimensions.description: Ordinal within the employee's bank account array. Order matters operationally: fixed-amount splits are taken in order and the remainder account absorbs what is left.

dimensions.label: statement text
dimensions.description: The narration that appears on the employee's bank statement for the pay credit — employer-chosen text like 'Salary'. Cosmetic; no analytical content.

dimensions.label: remainder
dimensions.description: True on the split that receives whatever net pay is left after fixed-amount splits. Exactly one row per employee should be true; the remainder row's amount is null/meaningless.

dimensions.label: employee id
dimensions.description: Owning employee and the row key — Xero stores exactly one home address per employee, so this is 1:1 with the parent.

dimensions.label: employee id
dimensions.description: Owning employee (inherited key from the parent scan); half of the row key.

dimensions.label: leave type id
dimensions.description: The leave type this balance belongs to (resolves to PayItems leave types in the payroll config domain); the other half of the row key.

dimensions.label: leave name
dimensions.description: Display name of the leave type, denormalised onto the balance by Xero. It is the only human-readable handle inside this domain, so 'annual leave' questions inevitably pattern-match on it — but it is admin-editable free text, and ILIKE '%annual%' also catches 'Annual Leave Loading' and cashed-out variants, quietly inflating the balance. Key and group on leave_type_id, use this only as a label, and resolve the real leave type through the payroll config domain whenever the number matters.

dimensions.label: type of units
dimensions.description: The unit the balance is denominated in, as declared by the leave type (typically Hours). Never aggregate balances across rows with different units — 152 hours plus 5 days is not 157 of anything.

dimensions.label: super membership id
dimensions.description: Xero's identifier for this employee-fund enrolment and the row key; what super lines point at.

dimensions.label: employee id
dimensions.description: Owning employee (inherited from the parent scan). One employee can hold several memberships — e.g. after changing funds — so employee-level rollups must expect >1 row.

dimensions.label: super fund id
dimensions.description: The destination fund; joins xero_payroll_au_super_funds for name, type (REGULATED vs SMSF) and USI.

dimensions.label: employee id
dimensions.description: Owning employee and row key (1:1 with the parent). The OpenAPI doc-string for this field is a copy-paste error ('Address line 1...'); it is the employee identifier.

dimensions.label: employment basis
dimensions.description: Full-time/part-time/casual basis as declared to the ATO. This is the declared basis for tax, and can drift from reality — FTE analysis should prefer the pay template's ordinary hours; CASUAL here plus leave accruals on payslips is a compliance smell worth surfacing, not hiding.

dimensions.label: tfn exemption type
dimensions.description: Why no TFN is quoted: NOTQUOTED (top-rate withholding applies), PENDING (28-day grace), PENSIONER, UNDER18. Null when a real TFN exists — so 'employees without a TFN' is tfn_exemption_type IS NOT NULL, not tax_file_number checks.

dimensions.label: abn
dimensions.description: Australian Business Number, populated (and mandatory) only when the employee's income type is NONEMPLOYEE — i.e. this row belongs to a contractor-style payee. A populated ABN is a strong 'not an employee' signal.

dimensions.label: australian resident for tax purposes
dimensions.description: Tax residency as declared. Tax residency is not citizenship or visa status; pair with residency_status, which carries the three-way STP2 vocabulary.

dimensions.label: residency status
dimensions.description: STP2 residency basis for withholding: AUSTRALIANRESIDENT, FOREIGNRESIDENT (no tax-free threshold, so withholding starts at the first dollar), WORKINGHOLIDAYMAKER (its own concessional ATO schedule, valid only for a registered WHM employer). Drives which tax table applies and is the first field to check for 'why is this person's tax different'. The rates behind each basis are legislated and change by financial year — never hardcode a percentage into a projection from this column.

dimensions.label: tax scale type
dimensions.description: Which ATO tax scale applies: REGULAR for most; special scales for entertainers, horticulturists/shearers, seniors/pensioners, working holiday makers and foreign residents. Non-REGULAR values explain 'unusual' withholding — check here before flagging a payroll error.

dimensions.label: work condition
dimensions.description: Sub-condition for the entertainer tax scale (promotional work, fewer than three performances a week, or none). Only meaningful when tax_scale_type = ACTORSARTISTSENTERTAINERS.

dimensions.label: tax free threshold claimed
dimensions.description: Whether the employee claims the tax-free threshold with this employer. An employee can only validly claim it with one employer at a time; false usually means this is a second job, which explains higher withholding.

dimensions.label: tax offset estimated amount
dimensions.description: Employee-estimated annual tax offset in whole dollars, used to reduce per-pay withholding. An estimate declared by the employee — not an entitlement and not an amount withheld.

dimensions.label: has help debt
dimensions.description: Legacy HECS/HELP debt flag from the pre-STP2 declaration. Under STP2 the consolidated has_loan_or_student_debt supersedes the individual loan flags — test the consolidated flag first and fall back to these for older records.

dimensions.label: has sfss debt
dimensions.description: Legacy Student Financial Supplement Scheme debt flag — a closed loan scheme, so on current data it survives only on long-tenured employees and is a poor proxy for study debt generally. Superseded by has_loan_or_student_debt on STP2-updated records; combining the two is safe only after COALESCE, because a raw NULL makes the whole OR predicate NULL and the row vanishes from the count.

dimensions.label: has trade support loan debt
dimensions.description: Legacy Trade Support Loan flag, likewise folded into has_loan_or_student_debt under STP2.

dimensions.label: upward variation tax withholding amount
dimensions.description: Extra dollars the employee asked to have withheld each pay run, in whole dollars. Additional to scale withholding — explains payslips whose tax looks 'too high'.

dimensions.label: eligible to receive leave loading
dimensions.description: Whether the employee gets leave loading (typically 17.5% on top of annual leave). Affects withholding calculation and leave cost projections — an employee with this true costs more per leave hour than their rate suggests.

dimensions.label: approved withholding variation percentage
dimensions.description: ATO-approved downward withholding variation (0-100). When set, scale-based withholding is overridden — the definitive explanation for an employee whose tax percentage looks wrong.

dimensions.label: has student startup loan
dimensions.description: Student Start-up Loan flag; one of the loan types consolidated into has_loan_or_student_debt under STP2.

dimensions.label: has loan or student debt
dimensions.description: STP2 consolidated flag: true when the employee has any HELP/HECS, VSL, FS, SSL or TSL debt. The authoritative study-debt indicator on STP2-updated records — use this, not an OR over the legacy flags, or you double-count.

dimensions.label: updated date utc
dimensions.description: Last-modified stamp of the declaration itself. Declarations change rarely; a recent stamp usually marks the STP2 migration touch, not a new TFN declaration.

dimensions.label: include leave loading in qualifying earnings
dimensions.description: Whether leave loading counts as ordinary-time earnings for Superannuation Guarantee purposes. Changes the SGC base — super-cost projections that ignore it understate liability for leave-loading-eligible staff.

dimensions.label: employee id
dimensions.description: Xero's immutable employee identifier and the row key. Every child table in this domain and every AU payslip carries it.

dimensions.label: title
dimensions.description: Salutation (Mr/Ms/Dr...), free text. Presentation only — never a gender or seniority signal.

dimensions.label: start date
dimensions.description: Employment start date — the opening of the employment episode. Tenure = start_date to COALESCE(termination_date, today). Null for some contractor-style records; exclude nulls from tenure math rather than defaulting to an epoch.

dimensions.label: termination date
dimensions.description: The end of the employment episode; null while employed. Headcount-as-at-date questions must test start_date <= d AND (termination_date IS NULL OR termination_date >= d) — filtering only on status gives today's answer for every historical date.

dimensions.label: termination reason
dimensions.description: ATO STP2 cessation code: V voluntary, I ill health, D deceased, R redundancy, F dismissal, C contract cessation, T transfer. Attrition analysis should split V (resignation-like) from employer-initiated R/F — lumping them together hides the story. It is an STP Phase 2 code, so expect it null on employees terminated before the org's STP2 upgrade even though termination_date is set; a null is 'not stated', never 'voluntary'.

dimensions.label: status
dimensions.description: ACTIVE or TERMINATED. Terminated employees are returned by the API forever — every current-workforce aggregate must filter status = 'ACTIVE' or the answer counts ghosts. For point-in-time headcount use the date columns instead; status only reflects now.

dimensions.label: job title
dimensions.description: Free-text job title. Uncontrolled vocabulary — do not GROUP BY it and present the result as an org structure without normalisation.

dimensions.label: classification
dimensions.description: Award/agreement classification (e.g. a modern-award level), free text set by the payroll admin. Useful for award-compliance slicing when populated; often blank.

dimensions.label: employee group name
dimensions.description: The employee's tracking-option under the org's employee-group tracking category — Xero's mechanism for splitting payroll expense by department/team. This is the join-by-name bridge to xero_payroll_au_settings.tracking_categories and to xero_tracking_options; it is how per-department payroll cost questions resolve. Name, not id — renames break history.

dimensions.label: is authorised to approve leave
dimensions.description: Grant of the Xero Me permission to approve other employees' leave requests. It is an access right, not a reporting line — payroll admins and office managers routinely hold it with no direct reports — so counting approvers as managers inflates the management layer and understates span of control.

dimensions.label: is authorised to approve timesheets
dimensions.description: Grant of the Xero Me permission to approve submitted timesheets. Independent of the leave-approval grant — an employee may hold either, both or neither — so a 'who can approve anything' question must test both flags rather than assuming they are set together, and neither implies a reporting relationship.

dimensions.label: ordinary earnings rate id
dimensions.description: The earnings rate that defines this employee's ordinary hours (the basis for leave accrual and SGC ordinary-time earnings). Resolves against the pay-items earnings rates owned by the payroll config domain.

dimensions.label: payroll calendar id
dimensions.description: The pay calendar (weekly/fortnightly/monthly cycle) this employee is paid on. Determines which pay runs can contain their payslips; 'per-period' template amounts mean per this calendar's period.

dimensions.label: income type
dimensions.description: STP2 income stream type. SALARYANDWAGES is a normal employee; WORKINGHOLIDAYMAKER changes tax treatment; NONEMPLOYEE and LABOURHIRE are paid through payroll but are not employees — exclude them from headcount and leave-liability questions; CLOSELYHELDPAYEES are family/director payees with relaxed STP timing.

dimensions.label: employment type
dimensions.description: EMPLOYEE or CONTRACTOR. Contractors flow through payroll for super/ABN reasons but are not employees: any 'employees', 'headcount' or 'leave' question must filter EMPLOYEE (and usually income_type) or it silently counts contractors.

dimensions.label: country of residence
dimensions.description: Two-letter country of residence carried for STP2 reporting of foreign residents and working holiday makers. Almost always AU, and it changes no withholding by itself — the tax consequence lives in the tax declaration (residency_status/tax_scale_type), so never infer a tax treatment from this column. The value list published in the spec is alphabetically truncated (it stops at DJ), so treat the enums string as illustrative, not as a validation whitelist that would reject real countries.

dimensions.label: is stp2 qualified
dimensions.description: Whether the employee record has been upgraded for STP Phase 2 compliance. A data-migration flag: false means STP2 fields (income_type, termination_reason codes, disaggregated tax flags) may be missing or stale — it does not mean the employee is unpayable.

dimensions.label: updated date utc
dimensions.description: Server-side last-modified stamp and the incremental-sync watermark (paired with If-Modified-Since). An audit timestamp — never a proxy for hire, termination or pay events.

dimensions.label: validation errors
dimensions.description: API validation messages echoed on the record, kept verbatim for debugging failed writes. Presentation-only payload; never filter or aggregate on it.

dimensions.label: pay template
dimensions.description: Verbatim PayTemplate object — all five line families in their original order — from the per-employee fetch; the audit copy the xero_payroll_au_pay_template_* tables are exploded from. Analysis belongs in those tables (they carry the calculation_type branching guidance); this blob exists to preserve line ordering and to reconcile template changes between syncs.

dimensions.label: opening balances
dimensions.description: Verbatim OpeningBalances object — the conversion header plus all six migrated-YTD line arrays — exactly as the per-employee fetch delivered it. The xero_payroll_au_opening_balance* tables are the queryable form; keep this copy for conversion audits, because opening balances change rarely and a diff here pinpoints when a migration correction landed.

dimensions.label: leave balances
dimensions.description: Verbatim LeaveBalances array behind xero_payroll_au_employee_leave_balances. Snapshot semantics apply to the blob exactly as to the table: it is the balance at last sync, not history — do not mine stale payload copies for a time series; historical balances require payslip leave lines from the processing domain.

dimensions.label: earnings lines
dimensions.description: Retained verbatim as the raw array Xero returned: the declared element order is part of the document and is lost by flattening. Fully normalised into xero_payroll_au_pay_template_earnings_lines (one row per element) — join there for anything you filter or aggregate on, and read this column only when the original ordering or an unflattened payload matters.

dimensions.label: deduction lines
dimensions.description: Retained verbatim as the raw array Xero returned: the declared element order is part of the document and is lost by flattening. Fully normalised into xero_payroll_au_pay_template_deduction_lines (one row per element) — join there for anything you filter or aggregate on, and read this column only when the original ordering or an unflattened payload matters.

dimensions.label: super lines
dimensions.description: Retained verbatim as the raw array Xero returned: the declared element order is part of the document and is lost by flattening. Fully normalised into xero_payroll_au_pay_template_super_lines (one row per element) — join there for anything you filter or aggregate on, and read this column only when the original ordering or an unflattened payload matters.

dimensions.label: reimbursement lines
dimensions.description: Retained verbatim as the raw array Xero returned: the declared element order is part of the document and is lost by flattening. Fully normalised into xero_payroll_au_pay_template_reimbursement_lines (one row per element) — join there for anything you filter or aggregate on, and read this column only when the original ordering or an unflattened payload matters.

dimensions.label: leave lines
dimensions.description: Retained verbatim as the raw array Xero returned: the declared element order is part of the document and is lost by flattening. Fully normalised into xero_payroll_au_pay_template_leave_lines (one row per element) — join there for anything you filter or aggregate on, and read this column only when the original ordering or an unflattened payload matters.

dimensions.label: leave application id
dimensions.description: Xero's immutable identifier for the application and the row key (the spec doc-string mislabels it as an employee id).

dimensions.label: employee id
dimensions.description: The employee taking the leave; join xero_payroll_au_employees. The grouping key for absence-per-person analysis.

dimensions.label: leave type id
dimensions.description: What kind of leave this is; join xero_payroll_au_leave_types for the LeaveCategoryCode (annual vs personal/sick vs long-service...) and paid/unpaid flag. Absence analyses that skip the join conflate paid holidays with unpaid or statutory leave.

dimensions.label: start date
dimensions.description: First calendar day of the requested span. Calendar days, not working days: (end_date - start_date) overstates leave consumed — use the periods' NumberOfUnits for actual units.

dimensions.label: end date
dimensions.description: Last calendar day of the requested span (inclusive). Overlap tests against a window need the usual start <= window_end AND end >= window_start pattern.

dimensions.label: pay out type
dimensions.description: DEFAULT is leave taken as absence; CASHED_OUT converts balance to money with the employee still at work. Absence and headcount-coverage analyses must exclude CASHED_OUT applications.

dimensions.label: updated date utc
dimensions.description: Last-modified audit stamp and the incremental sync watermark for leave. It moves when the request is approved, rejected or edited, so it is a processing timestamp, not a lodgement date — the record carries no 'applied on' field, and using this as one dates old leave to whenever it was last touched.

dimensions.label: validation errors
dimensions.description: Write-response diagnostic payload from the API; null on every read. Never analytical — present only so the staging row is a faithful copy of the record, and a non-null value here means a write was replayed, not that the business record is invalid.

dimensions.label: leave application id
dimensions.description: Parent application key, inherited on explode; the path to employee, leave type and pay-out type.

dimensions.label: leave periods
dimensions.description: Zero-based position of this period in the application's LeavePeriods array; periods have no id of their own. Periods are also uniquely addressed by their pay-period dates within an application, but the ordinal is the stable key.

dimensions.label: leave periods pay period start date
dimensions.description: Start of the pay period this slice of leave falls into — aligns with a pay run's period dates, which is how leave joins back to the run that paid it.

dimensions.label: leave periods pay period end date
dimensions.description: End of the pay period for this slice. The natural time axis for leave trend analysis, since it is when the leave hits payroll.

dimensions.label: leave periods leave period status
dimensions.description: Lifecycle of this slice: REQUESTED (awaiting approval), SCHEDULED (approved, future), PROCESSED (paid on a posted run), REJECTED (never happened). 'Leave taken to date' = PROCESSED only; 'committed leave' = PROCESSED + SCHEDULED; REJECTED must always be excluded.

dimensions.label: leave type id
dimensions.description: Xero's immutable leave type identifier; applications and accrual lines reference it.

dimensions.label: name
dimensions.description: Admin-chosen label (the spec's doc-string wrongly says 'earnings rate'). Display only — categorize via leave_category_code.

dimensions.label: type of units
dimensions.description: The unit leave is tracked in (usually Hours). Governs what every NumberOfUnits on periods and accrual lines means — mixing types with different units in one SUM is a unit error.

dimensions.label: normal entitlement
dimensions.description: Units a full-time employee is entitled to per year (e.g. 152 hours annual leave). A policy parameter for expected-accrual modelling; actual accruals are on the payslip accrual lines.

dimensions.label: leave loading rate
dimensions.description: Extra percentage paid on top of ordinary earnings when this leave is taken (typically 17.5 for loaded annual leave). Explains why leave pay exceeds base rate x units; null/zero when no loading applies.

dimensions.label: updated date utc
dimensions.description: Last-modified audit stamp on the leave type and the incremental sync watermark for the PayItems scan. An entitlement or loading edit refreshes it — not evidence any leave was accrued or taken.

dimensions.label: is paid leave
dimensions.description: Whether taking this leave generates pay. Unpaid leave types produce absence without wages — absence cost models must branch on this.

dimensions.label: show on payslip
dimensions.description: Whether this leave type's balance is printed on employee payslips. A presentation setting with no bearing on accrual or entitlement — a false here means employees cannot see the balance, not that the type stopped accruing, so never read it as 'inactive'.

dimensions.label: current record
dimensions.description: Active flag. Filter true for configuration listings; keep false rows joinable from historical leave.

dimensions.label: leave category code
dimensions.description: Statutory classification (STP Phase 2) of the leave type — the canonical split for absence analysis and the only safe way to compare leave across orgs whose custom names differ.

dimensions.label: sgc exempt
dimensions.description: True when pay for this leave is exempt from the superannuation guarantee. Another contributor to SGC-vs-wages gaps.

dimensions.label: is qualifying earnings
dimensions.description: Whether pay for this leave counts inside the superannuation-guarantee earnings base. It is the precise counterpart to the blunt sgc_exempt flag and the two can disagree, so an 'SGC vs wages' ratio computed without checking both is the usual reason a perfectly correct super figure looks like an underpayment.

dimensions.label: employee id
dimensions.description: Owning employee (inherited key from the parent scan).

dimensions.label: line index
dimensions.description: Ordinal within the opening-balance deduction array; forms the key with employee_id.

dimensions.label: deduction type id
dimensions.description: The deduction pay item the migrated YTD amount sits under — the axis conversion-year reconciliation matches on: pair it with the same DeductionTypeID on Xero payslip deduction lines, or the year's total silently splits across two rows for one deduction.

dimensions.label: calculation type
dimensions.description: Inherited from the shared DeductionLine shape. A migrated deduction is a completed total, so no calculation basis is recorded and this is normally null. Critically, a stray PRETAX/POSTTAX value here does NOT tell you the tax treatment of the migrated dollars — the pre-tax/post-tax split of pre-conversion deductions is not carried across, so do not use this column to adjust migrated taxable income.

dimensions.label: percentage
dimensions.description: Percentage slot on the shared shape. Migrated deductions arrive as dollar totals, so this is null even for employees whose current deduction is percentage-based — its emptiness says nothing about how the deduction was configured before conversion.

dimensions.label: number of units
dimensions.description: Unit slot on the shared shape, unused for migrated totals. Null here means 'not recorded at migration', not zero units — never coalesce it to 0 and multiply.

dimensions.label: employee id
dimensions.description: Owning employee (inherited key from the parent scan).

dimensions.label: line index
dimensions.description: Ordinal within the opening-balance earnings array; forms the key with employee_id.

dimensions.label: earnings rate id
dimensions.description: The earnings rate the migrated YTD amount belongs to — reconciliation must match it to the same rate on Xero payslips.

dimensions.label: calculation type
dimensions.description: Inherited from the shared EarningsLine shape. An opening balance records money the previous system already calculated, so there is no live calculation basis and this is normally null; where a migration tool did populate it, it describes how the OLD system derived the figure, never how Xero will pay this employee. Branching on it as if this were a pay template misreads settled history as a standing instruction.

dimensions.label: annual salary
dimensions.description: The shared shape carries an annual-salary slot, but an opening balance states what was already paid, not a forward rate, so expect null. Even when populated it is the salary in force at conversion — historical context only; the current salary is on the pay-template earnings line.

dimensions.label: number of units per week
dimensions.description: Contracted weekly units on the shared shape. Opening balances migrate dollar totals, not work schedules, so this is effectively always null — do not try to reconstruct pre-conversion FTE or hours from it.

dimensions.label: rate per unit
dimensions.description: Per-unit rate slot on the shared shape. Migrated YTD figures arrive as totals with no rate decomposition, so this is null; an implied historical rate would need units this table does not carry, and inventing one from amount alone is guesswork.

dimensions.label: normal number of units
dimensions.description: Ordinary-units basis used by MULTIPLE-type rates on the shared shape; meaningless for a settled total and null in practice. Its emptiness is not evidence that no overtime or penalty rates were paid before conversion.

dimensions.label: number of units
dimensions.description: Unit count from the shared shape. Opening balances migrate dollars, never hours, so hours-worked questions about the pre-conversion period cannot be answered from this domain at all — say the data does not exist rather than returning null as zero hours.

dimensions.label: fixed amount
dimensions.description: The FIXEDAMOUNT-rate slot on the shared shape; null for migrated balances, because every migrated dollar lands in amount regardless of how the previous system classified it. Never add it to amount hoping for a fuller total — you would be adding an empty column to a complete one.

dimensions.label: employee id
dimensions.description: Owning employee (inherited key from the parent scan).

dimensions.label: line index
dimensions.description: Ordinal within the opening-balance leave array; forms the key with employee_id.

dimensions.label: leave type id
dimensions.description: The leave type whose balance was carried over — the join to the matching xero_payroll_au_employee_leave_balances row and to the leave type's unit declaration in the payroll config domain. Without resolving it, number_of_units has no unit.

dimensions.label: employee id
dimensions.description: Owning employee (inherited key from the parent scan).

dimensions.label: line index
dimensions.description: Ordinal within the paid-leave earnings array; forms the key with employee_id.

dimensions.label: leave type id
dimensions.description: The leave type under which the migrated paid-leave dollars are categorised for STP2. The loading-split columns only populate when this resolves to an annual-leave-category type in the payroll config domain — check the category before reading their nulls as zero loading.

dimensions.label: sgc applied leave loading amount
dimensions.description: Migrated leave loading that WAS subject to Super Guarantee, only for annual-leave-category types. Splitting loading by SGC treatment is what makes conversion-year super reconciliation possible.

dimensions.label: sgc exempted leave loading amount
dimensions.description: Migrated leave loading exempt from Super Guarantee, only for annual-leave-category types. Its presence explains why migrated super is lower than a flat SGC-rate estimate over gross.

dimensions.label: reset stp categorisation
dimensions.description: Write-side control flag to reset STP categorisation for the leave type (annual-leave categories only). Ingested for fidelity; carries no analytical signal.

dimensions.label: employee id
dimensions.description: Owning employee (inherited key from the parent scan).

dimensions.label: line index
dimensions.description: Ordinal within the opening-balance reimbursement array; forms the key with employee_id.

dimensions.label: reimbursement type id
dimensions.description: The reimbursement pay item the migrated YTD amount belongs to; resolve against the payroll config domain's reimbursement types for the name, and match on this id (not the free-text description) when reconciling against payslip reimbursement lines.

dimensions.label: description
dimensions.description: Free-text narration inherited from the shared shape, usually null because migration tools carry totals per reimbursement type without the original wording. Reconcile against payslip reimbursement lines on reimbursement_type_id — matching on this text loses every row where the narration was dropped or reworded at conversion.

dimensions.label: expense account
dimensions.description: Expense-code slot on the shared shape. Migrated reimbursements were already expensed in the previous system, so nothing posts to a Xero account and this is null — pre-conversion reimbursement spend cannot be attributed to a GL account from this table, and a report that groups by it will show everything under one empty bucket.

dimensions.label: employee id
dimensions.description: Owning employee (inherited key from the parent scan).

dimensions.label: line index
dimensions.description: Ordinal within the opening-balance super array; forms the key with employee_id.

dimensions.label: super membership id
dimensions.description: Which of the employee's fund memberships received the migrated contributions — the join through xero_payroll_au_employee_super_memberships to the fund. Can be null on old conversions; treat null as 'fund unknown at migration', not as a broken join.

dimensions.label: contribution type
dimensions.description: Which contribution stream the YTD amount belongs to — SGC vs salary sacrifice vs voluntary matters for concessional-cap reconciliation.

dimensions.label: calculation type
dimensions.description: Inherited from the shared SuperLine shape. The migrated figure is a settled contribution total, so no basis is recorded and this is normally null; the basis actually in force (STATUTORY / PERCENTAGEOFEARNINGS / FIXEDAMOUNT) lives on the pay-template super line, and reading it from here would describe the previous system, not Xero.

dimensions.label: minimum monthly earnings
dimensions.description: Earnings-floor slot on the shared shape, irrelevant once a contribution has been made and null here. Do not read a null as proof no earnings threshold was applied before conversion — the migrated amount is the only evidence of what was actually contributed.

dimensions.label: expense account code
dimensions.description: GL expense-code slot on the shared shape. Migrated balances raise no Xero journal — they are opening figures, not postings — so this is null, and pre-conversion super expense cannot be split by account or department from this table.

dimensions.label: liability account code
dimensions.description: GL liability-code slot on the shared shape, null for the same reason as expense_account_code. Any super owed at conversion sits in the org's opening balance sheet, not against a code recorded here, so do not reconcile the super payable account to this table.

dimensions.label: percentage
dimensions.description: Contribution-percentage slot on the shared shape; null for migrated totals. Dividing amount by migrated earnings yields an average across the whole pre-conversion period, not the rate in force at any point — do not present it as the employee's super rate.

dimensions.label: employee id
dimensions.description: Owning employee and row key (at most one opening-balance set per employee).

dimensions.label: opening balance date
dimensions.description: The as-at date of the migrated YTD figures — the boundary between 'paid in the old system' and 'paid in Xero'. YTD reconstructions for the conversion year must add opening balances to Xero payslips only up to this year, and never for later years.

dimensions.label: tax
dimensions.description: YTD PAYG tax withheld in the old system at conversion. The API delivers it as a string — cast to numeric before arithmetic, and expect blanks rather than zeros for employees without migrated tax.

dimensions.label: pay run id
dimensions.description: Xero's immutable pay run identifier and the row key; the parent key for every payslip in the run.

dimensions.label: payroll calendar id
dimensions.description: The payroll calendar this run was generated from (the spec's doc-string mislabels it 'pay run'). It determines the run's frequency — join xero_payroll_au_payroll_calendars for WEEKLY/MONTHLY etc. Comparing costs across calendars of different frequencies without normalizing to a common period is a classic wrong answer.

dimensions.label: pay run period start date
dimensions.description: First day of the period the employees are being paid FOR. Use with the end date for accrual-style period attribution; not the day money moved.

dimensions.label: pay run period end date
dimensions.description: Last day of the period worked. The natural axis for 'payroll cost of period X' questions; a run's payment can land in a later calendar month than its period.

dimensions.label: pay run status
dimensions.description: DRAFT is an unposted work-in-progress whose totals still move; POSTED is committed payroll. Every cost, tax, super or headcount figure must filter POSTED — a draft's totals are provisional and may never post at those numbers, so including them books payroll that has not happened.

dimensions.label: payment date
dimensions.description: The day employees are actually paid. Cash-timing questions (PAYG remitted, wages paid in month X) group by this; period-cost questions use the period dates. The two conventions split a run across months whenever payment falls after period end.

dimensions.label: payslip message
dimensions.description: Free-text note printed on every payslip in the run. Presentation only; never a filter for analysis.

dimensions.label: reimbursement
dimensions.description: Total expense reimbursements paid through payroll. Not wages, not taxed, not super-bearing — exclude from remuneration analyses but include in cash-out.

dimensions.label: updated date utc
dimensions.description: Xero's last-modified audit stamp and the incremental sync watermark. A run edited after posting refreshes this — not evidence of a new pay event.

dimensions.label: validation errors
dimensions.description: Write-response diagnostic payload from the API; null on reads. Never analytical — present only so the staging row is a faithful record.

dimensions.label: employee id
dimensions.description: Owning employee (inherited key from the parent scan).

dimensions.label: line index
dimensions.description: Ordinal within the template's deduction lines; forms the key with employee_id.

dimensions.label: deduction type id
dimensions.description: The deduction pay item applied. The type (in the payroll config domain) carries the name and whether it reduces super or W1 — this line only carries the employee-specific quantum.

dimensions.label: calculation type
dimensions.description: FIXEDAMOUNT uses amount; PRETAX/POSTTAX are percentage-based and use percentage. Branch on this before reading the numerics — and remember PRETAX shrinks taxable income while POSTTAX does not, which changes any net-pay modelling.

dimensions.label: amount
dimensions.description: Fixed deduction per pay period, populated for FIXEDAMOUNT lines. Per-period money — annualise via the employee's payroll calendar before comparing across employees.

dimensions.label: percentage
dimensions.description: Percentage of earnings deducted, for PRETAX/POSTTAX lines. A rate: never summed, and meaningless without the earnings base on the eventual payslip.

dimensions.label: number of units
dimensions.description: Units for unit-based deduction setups; rarely populated on templates. Treat null as 'not unit-based', not zero.

dimensions.label: employee id
dimensions.description: Owning employee (inherited key from the parent scan).

dimensions.label: line index
dimensions.description: Ordinal within the pay template's earnings lines; with employee_id it forms the row key because one earnings rate can appear on multiple lines.

dimensions.label: earnings rate id
dimensions.description: The earnings rate (pay item) this line applies — ordinary hours, overtime, allowances. Resolves against the payroll config domain's earnings rates; the rate, not this line, carries the name and STP category.

dimensions.label: calculation type
dimensions.description: Decides which numeric columns on this row are authoritative: ANNUALSALARY uses annual_salary + number_of_units_per_week; ENTEREARNINGSRATE uses rate_per_unit x number_of_units; USEEARNINGSRATE takes the rate's own default. Reading the wrong column for the type yields nulls or nonsense — always branch on this first.

dimensions.label: number of units per week
dimensions.description: Contracted units (hours) per week for salaried lines — the numerator for FTE (divide by the org's full-time week, commonly 38). Null on rate-based lines.

dimensions.label: rate per unit
dimensions.description: Dollar rate per unit for ENTEREARNINGSRATE lines — an hourly rate, never a total. Never SUM this column; multiply by units first.

dimensions.label: normal number of units
dimensions.description: Base ordinary units used when the earnings rate is a multiple of another rate (RateType MULTIPLE, e.g. overtime at 1.5x). Only meaningful for those rates.

dimensions.label: amount
dimensions.description: Per-period template amount where the line is expressed as a flat amount. Per pay period of the employee's calendar — comparing employees on different calendars without normalising to annual mixes weekly against monthly numbers.

dimensions.label: number of units
dimensions.description: Template units per pay period for rate-based lines (hours per period, not per week). Pairs with rate_per_unit or the rate's default rate.

dimensions.label: fixed amount
dimensions.description: Per-period amount used only when the underlying earnings rate's RateType is FIXEDAMOUNT (e.g. a flat allowance). Distinct from amount; check both when hunting a template's flat components.

dimensions.label: employee id
dimensions.description: Owning employee (inherited key from the parent scan).

dimensions.label: line index
dimensions.description: Ordinal within the template's leave lines; forms the key with employee_id.

dimensions.label: leave type id
dimensions.description: The leave type accruing (annual, personal, long service...). Names and unit types live on the leave types in the payroll config domain; this id is also the join to the employee's balance rows.

dimensions.label: calculation type
dimensions.description: How the accrual is computed: BASEDONORDINARYEARNINGS accrues proportionally to hours worked; FIXEDAMOUNTEACHPERIOD adds a constant; ENTERRATEINPAYTEMPLATE uses this line's units; NOCALCULATIONREQUIRED means no automatic accrual (e.g. unpaid leave). Determines which unit columns below mean anything.

dimensions.label: entitlement final pay payout type
dimensions.description: Whether the accrued balance pays out on termination (PAIDOUT) or lapses (NOTPAIDOUT). The switch that decides if this leave type belongs in the leave-liability provision — NOTPAIDOUT balances are an operational fact, not a monetary liability.

dimensions.label: employment termination payment type
dimensions.description: ETP classification if the payout forms an Employment Termination Payment: O (other/ordinary) or R (redundancy-related, concessionally taxed). Only meaningful when the payout routes through an ETP.

dimensions.label: include superannuation guarantee contribution
dimensions.description: Whether pay for this leave attracts super guarantee contributions (the spec doc-string 'amount of leave line' is wrong — this is a boolean SGC switch). Affects the super cost of every hour of this leave taken.

dimensions.label: is qualifying earnings
dimensions.description: Whether this leave line counts as qualifying (ordinary-time) earnings for superannuation guarantee calculations. Together with the SGC flag it decides the super base — misreading either understates SGC liability.

dimensions.label: number of units
dimensions.description: Per-period accrual units when the calculation type takes units from this template line. Units are hours or days per the leave type — check before aggregating.

dimensions.label: full time number of units per period
dimensions.description: Full-time-equivalent ordinary units per period used to pro-rata BASEDONORDINARYEARNINGS accruals for part-timers. A scaling basis, not an accrual amount.

dimensions.label: employee id
dimensions.description: Owning employee (inherited key from the parent scan).

dimensions.label: line index
dimensions.description: Ordinal within the template's reimbursement lines; forms the key with employee_id.

dimensions.label: reimbursement type id
dimensions.description: The reimbursement pay item applied; the type (payroll config domain) names it and fixes its default expense account.

dimensions.label: description
dimensions.description: Free-text line description (max 50 chars) shown on the payslip. Display only.

dimensions.label: expense account
dimensions.description: Expense account code the reimbursement posts against (visible as a code once a pay run posts). Joins xero_accounts on code for P&L attribution.

dimensions.label: employee id
dimensions.description: Owning employee (inherited key from the parent scan).

dimensions.label: line index
dimensions.description: Ordinal within the template's super lines; forms the key with employee_id.

dimensions.label: super membership id
dimensions.description: Which of the employee's fund memberships this contribution pays into — the join to xero_payroll_au_employee_super_memberships and from there to the fund. Null on STATUTORY lines created before a membership was set.

dimensions.label: contribution type
dimensions.description: SGC is the compulsory employer guarantee; SALARYSACRIFICE is employee pre-tax money (reduces their taxable income and counts toward their concessional cap); EMPLOYERADDITIONAL is employer money above SGC; EMPLOYEE is post-tax voluntary. Employer super EXPENSE above salary is SGC + EMPLOYERADDITIONAL only — SALARYSACRIFICE and EMPLOYEE are the employee's own money that the employer merely remits, so folding them into 'employer super cost' overstates on-costs.

dimensions.label: calculation type
dimensions.description: STATUTORY applies the legislated SGC rate to ordinary-time earnings; PERCENTAGEOFEARNINGS uses percentage; FIXEDAMOUNT uses amount. STATUTORY lines carry no rate here — the rate is legislated and changes by financial year, so do not hardcode it in projections.

dimensions.label: minimum monthly earnings
dimensions.description: Monthly earnings floor below which this super line does not apply — a legacy of the (since-abolished) $450/month SGC threshold. Non-zero values on current data are stale config worth flagging, not applying.

dimensions.label: expense account code
dimensions.description: GL account code the super expense posts to (joins xero_accounts on code, not id). Where payroll meets the P&L — super cost by department resolves through this account plus tracking.

dimensions.label: liability account code
dimensions.description: GL account code for the accrued super payable until remitted to the fund. The balance on this account is super owed, not super cost.

dimensions.label: percentage
dimensions.description: Contribution percentage for PERCENTAGEOFEARNINGS lines. A rate — never summed; null on STATUTORY and FIXEDAMOUNT lines.

dimensions.label: amount
dimensions.description: Fixed contribution per pay period for FIXEDAMOUNT lines. Per-period money on the employee's calendar; annualise before comparing.

dimensions.label: payroll calendar id
dimensions.description: Xero's immutable calendar identifier; pay runs and employees reference it.

dimensions.label: name
dimensions.description: Admin-chosen label ('Weekly Wages', 'Monthly Salaries'). Display only — frequency logic must use calendar_type, names lie.

dimensions.label: calendar type
dimensions.description: The pay frequency. The normalization key for comparing costs across calendars: a WEEKLY calendar posts ~4.33 runs per month, so per-run comparisons across types are meaningless without annualizing.

dimensions.label: start date
dimensions.description: Start of the UPCOMING (next unposted) pay period — a rolling pointer, not the calendar's creation date and not history. Never use it to date past payroll.

dimensions.label: payment date
dimensions.description: When the upcoming period will be paid; rolls forward like start_date. Useful for 'when is the next pay day', useless for history.

dimensions.label: reference date
dimensions.description: The anchor date from which the period sequence was originally generated. Fixed at setup; explains period boundary alignment.

dimensions.label: updated date utc
dimensions.description: Last-modified stamp; ticks every time the rolling dates advance, so expect it to churn with each posted run.

dimensions.label: validation errors
dimensions.description: Write-response diagnostic payload from the API; null on every read. Never analytical — present only so the staging row is a faithful copy of the record, and a non-null value here means a write was replayed, not that the business record is invalid.

dimensions.label: payslip id
dimensions.description: Parent payslip the deduction was withheld on, inherited on explode. It repeats across the payslip's deduction lines, and the two things every deduction total needs — the employee and the run's POSTED status — are both reached through it (payslip -> run), so no aggregate here is trustworthy until that two-hop join is made.

dimensions.label: deduction lines
dimensions.description: Zero-based position of this line in the payslip's DeductionLines array, minted at explode time; the source line has no id of its own.

dimensions.label: deduction type id
