dimensions.description: Which deduction pay item this is; join xero_payroll_au_deduction_types for name, ReducesTax and category. Without the join, 'deductions by kind' is unanswerable — the line carries no label.

dimensions.label: calculation type
dimensions.description: Whether the line was computed as a fixed amount or as a percentage of earnings. It governs whether amount or percentage is the configured driver — amount is always the resulting dollars, so measures should read amount whatever this says. The spec publishes no value list here: discover the values present in the tenant rather than hard-coding literals.

dimensions.label: percentage
dimensions.description: The configured percentage for percentage-calculated lines (null for fixed). A parameter, not a measure — averaging or summing it is meaningless.

dimensions.label: number of units
dimensions.description: Units behind a unit-priced deduction — rare, since most deductions are a flat dollar figure or a percentage — and null otherwise. These are not hours worked and must never feed a labour-hours measure; amount is the only money on the line.

dimensions.label: payslip id
dimensions.description: Parent payslip key, inherited on explode. Run status and pay dates are two joins away (payslip -> run).

dimensions.label: earnings lines
dimensions.description: Zero-based position of this line in the payslip's EarningsLines array, minted at explode time to preserve presentation order; the source line has no id of its own.

dimensions.label: earnings rate id
dimensions.description: Which pay item produced this line. Join xero_payroll_au_earnings_rates for EarningsType (ORDINARYTIMEEARNINGS vs OVERTIMEEARNINGS vs ALLOWANCE...) — the line itself does not say what kind of earnings it is.

dimensions.label: calculation type
dimensions.description: How the line's amount was computed — from the employee's standard rate, a rate typed onto the payslip, or an annual salary. It decides which of annual_salary / rate_per_unit x number_of_units / amount is the operative value, so reading the wrong one yields nulls or nonsense. The spec publishes no value list for this field: discover the values present in the tenant instead of hard-coding literals into a filter.

dimensions.label: rate per unit
dimensions.description: The per-unit (usually hourly) rate actually applied on this line. A rate, not an amount — never SUM it; the line's cost is rate x units.

dimensions.label: normal number of units
dimensions.description: The employee's standard units for the period (their normal hours), as opposed to the units actually paid. Compare with number_of_units to spot over/under-standard periods; do not use it as hours worked.

dimensions.label: payslip id
dimensions.description: Parent payslip that granted this accrual, inherited on explode. One payslip accrues several leave types, so the column repeats; it is also the only thing that dates the accrual, because the line carries no period of its own — 'leave accrued in Q3' is a filter on the run behind this payslip, never on anything in this table.

dimensions.label: leave accrual lines
dimensions.description: Zero-based position of this line in the payslip's LeaveAccrualLines array, minted at explode time; the source line has no id of its own.

dimensions.label: leave accrual lines leave type id
dimensions.description: The leave type being accrued; join xero_payroll_au_leave_types for name and LeaveCategoryCode (annual vs personal vs long service...). Accrual analysis without the join lumps incompatible entitlements together.

dimensions.label: leave accrual lines auto calculate
dimensions.description: True when Xero computed the accrual from the leave type's entitlement settings; false when it was manually entered on the payslip. Manual overrides are where accrual anomalies hide — segment on this before declaring an entitlement misconfigured.

dimensions.label: payslip id
dimensions.description: Parent payslip whose leave pay this line prices, inherited on explode. Many rows share it, so a payslip measure (wages, net_pay) joined against this table is repeated once per leave line — collapse to one row per payslip before mixing the two grains. It is also the only route to the pay period, since the line itself carries no date.

dimensions.label: leave earnings lines
dimensions.description: Zero-based position of this line in the payslip's LeaveEarningsLines array, minted at explode time; the source line has no id of its own.

dimensions.label: leave earnings lines earnings rate id
dimensions.description: The earnings rate the leave was paid at. Join xero_payroll_au_earnings_rates; note leave paid at a loading-inflated rate still points at the base rate item.

dimensions.label: leave earnings lines pay out type
dimensions.description: DEFAULT is leave taken as time off; CASHED_OUT converts balance to money with no absence. 'Days off taken' must exclude CASHED_OUT; 'leave balance drawdown' includes both. Ignoring this flag inflates absence metrics at every cash-out event.

dimensions.label: payslip id
dimensions.description: Parent payslip that carried this reimbursement, inherited on explode. It repeats per line, and the payslip's own reimbursements column already totals these rows — join through it for the run's POSTED filter and pay date, but never add the two grains together.

dimensions.label: reimbursement lines
dimensions.description: Zero-based position of this line in the payslip's ReimbursementLines array, minted at explode time; the source line has no id of its own.

dimensions.label: reimbursement type id
dimensions.description: Which reimbursement pay item this is; join xero_payroll_au_reimbursement_types for the name and its expense account.

dimensions.label: description
dimensions.description: Free-text note on the line ('parking, client visit'). Useful for eyeballing, unreliable for classification — the type id is the categorical field.

dimensions.label: expense account
dimensions.description: GL account code the reimbursement expense posts to. Join xero_accounts on its code (not account_id) to land these in the P&L alongside other expenses.

dimensions.label: payslip id
dimensions.description: Parent payslip the contribution was calculated on, inherited on explode. It repeats once per fund-and-contribution-type line, so joining payslips here fans the payslip's Super total out across its own components; the employee identity and the run's POSTED status both arrive only through this key.

dimensions.label: superannuation lines
dimensions.description: Zero-based position of this line in the payslip's SuperannuationLines array, minted at explode time; the source line has no id of its own.

dimensions.label: superannuation lines super membership id
dimensions.description: The employee's super fund membership this contribution goes to (memberships live on the employee record in the payroll employees domain). Group by it to see per-fund flows; one employee can contribute to multiple lines in one payslip.

dimensions.label: superannuation lines contribution type
dimensions.description: The single most important filter in AU super analysis. SGC is the statutory employer guarantee; EMPLOYERADDITIONAL is voluntary employer cost; SALARYSACRIFICE is employee remuneration redirected pre-tax; EMPLOYEE is post-tax employee money. 'Employer super cost' = SGC + EMPLOYERADDITIONAL only — adding the other two overstates cost with the employees' own money.

dimensions.label: superannuation lines calculation type
dimensions.description: How the amount was derived: STATUTORY follows the SG rate rules, PERCENTAGEOFEARNINGS uses the percentage column, FIXEDAMOUNT is a set dollar figure. Explains why percentage or amount is null on some rows.

dimensions.label: superannuation lines minimum monthly earnings
dimensions.description: The monthly earnings floor configured for this contribution, echoed from the employee's super setup onto the line. A threshold parameter, not money: SUM or AVG over it means nothing. Its real use is explaining a zero or absent contribution in a light month — check this before reporting an SG underpayment.

dimensions.label: superannuation lines expense account code
dimensions.description: GL account code the super EXPENSE posts to (employer-funded lines). Join xero_accounts on code to tie payroll super to the P&L.

dimensions.label: superannuation lines liability account code
dimensions.description: GL account code the unpaid-super LIABILITY sits in until remitted to the fund. Balance-sheet reconciliation of super payable joins here on code.

dimensions.label: superannuation lines payment date for this period
dimensions.description: The scheduled date for remitting this contribution to the fund — the axis for super CASH-OUT timing, distinct from the payslip's pay date. Accrued-vs-paid super gaps come from confusing the two.

dimensions.label: superannuation lines percentage
dimensions.description: The contribution percentage for percentage/statutory lines (e.g. the SG rate). A rate — never SUM; use it to sanity-check amount against wages.

dimensions.label: payslip id
dimensions.description: Parent payslip the PAYG was withheld on, inherited on explode. Usually one tax line per payslip, but never assume it: ETP and manual-schedule payslips add more, so treat this as a repeating foreign key and de-duplicate before combining it with payslip-level measures.

dimensions.label: tax lines
dimensions.description: Zero-based position of this line in the payslip's TaxLines array; kept as the key for uniformity with the sibling line tables even though tax lines also carry their own id.

dimensions.label: tax lines payslip tax line id
dimensions.description: Xero's identifier for the tax line — the only payslip line family with a native id. Stable across re-fetches; use it for change tracking rather than the ordinal.

dimensions.label: tax lines tax type name
dimensions.description: Human label of the withholding type ('PAYG'). A display string, not a stable enum — filter on manual_tax_type for schedule logic.

dimensions.label: tax lines description
dimensions.description: Free-text explanation of the withholding as printed on the payslip. Presentation only and org-authored, so it is not a classification: parsing it for 'ETP' or 'HELP' instead of reading manual_tax_type produces a rule that breaks the first time an admin retypes the wording.

dimensions.label: tax lines manual tax type
dimensions.description: Set only when someone overrode automatic PAYG with a manual schedule amount (ETP, Schedule 4/5 variants). Null means Xero calculated the tax. Manually-taxed payslips are exactly where withholding anomalies concentrate — segment on this before flagging outliers.

dimensions.label: tax lines liability account
dimensions.description: GL account code holding the PAYG payable until remitted; populated for posted runs. Join xero_accounts on code for balance-sheet reconciliation.

dimensions.label: payslip id
dimensions.description: Parent payslip this timesheet-derived line belongs to, inherited on explode. It is NOT unique here — a payslip normally has several timesheet lines — so joining payslips to this table repeats every payslip-level total once per line. Aggregate the lines first, then join, never the reverse.

dimensions.label: timesheet earnings lines
dimensions.description: Zero-based position of this line in the payslip's TimesheetEarningsLines array, minted at explode time; the source line has no id of its own.

dimensions.label: earnings rate id
dimensions.description: The earnings rate the timesheet hours were paid at; join xero_payroll_au_earnings_rates to classify. The rate here comes from the timesheet line's rate selection, not necessarily the employee's default.

dimensions.label: calculation type
dimensions.description: How the amount was computed; for timesheet-generated lines this is effectively rate x units, which is why amount is usually null here and the cost has to be multiplied out. The spec publishes no value list for this field — discover the values present in the tenant rather than hard-coding literals.

dimensions.label: annual salary
dimensions.description: The employee's annual salary, rarely populated on a timesheet-generated line since these are priced from hours. When present it is a yearly rate of pay sitting on a per-period row: never SUM it, and never treat it as this line's cost.

dimensions.label: rate per unit
dimensions.description: The rate the timesheet units were paid at, which is the earnings rate's rate as resolved for this employee — not necessarily the pay item's default. A rate, not money: never SUM it, and never average it across lines as 'average hourly rate' without weighting by number_of_units.

dimensions.label: normal number of units
dimensions.description: The employee's standard units for the period, carried onto the line as a reference point — it is what they would normally be paid, not what the timesheet recorded. Use it only as the denominator when measuring over- or under-standard periods; using it as hours worked reports a contract, not a timesheet.

dimensions.label: payslip id
dimensions.description: Xero's immutable payslip identifier, the row key, and the fan-out parameter that fetched this row.

dimensions.label: pay run id
dimensions.description: Inherited from the parent run whose roster listed this payslip — the Payslip payload itself does not carry it. The only path to run status and pay dates, so effectively mandatory in every query.

dimensions.label: employee id
dimensions.description: The employee being paid; join xero_payroll_au_employees for current identity, employment dates and classifications. Group by this, not by name — names duplicate.

dimensions.label: payslips employee group
dimensions.description: The employee-group (tracking) name carried from the pay run's embedded summary roster — the full Payslip payload omits it. The AU-payroll way orgs encode department/cost-centre; null when the org does not group employees.

dimensions.label: reimbursements
dimensions.description: Expense money returned to the employee through this payslip. Not remuneration: exclude from wage, tax and super analyses.

dimensions.label: updated date utc
dimensions.description: Last-modified audit stamp on the payslip record; drives re-fetching an edited payslip. Not a payment date — pay dates live on the run.

dimensions.label: earnings lines
dimensions.description: Retained verbatim as the raw array Xero returned: the declared element order is part of the document and is lost by flattening. Fully normalised into xero_payroll_au_payslip_earnings_lines (one row per element) — join there for anything you filter or aggregate on, and read this column only when the original ordering or an unflattened payload matters.

dimensions.label: timesheet earnings lines
dimensions.description: Retained verbatim as the raw array Xero returned: the declared element order is part of the document and is lost by flattening. Fully normalised into xero_payroll_au_payslip_timesheet_earnings_lines (one row per element) — join there for anything you filter or aggregate on, and read this column only when the original ordering or an unflattened payload matters.

dimensions.label: deduction lines
dimensions.description: Retained verbatim as the raw array Xero returned: the declared element order is part of the document and is lost by flattening. Fully normalised into xero_payroll_au_payslip_deduction_lines (one row per element) — join there for anything you filter or aggregate on, and read this column only when the original ordering or an unflattened payload matters.

dimensions.label: reimbursement lines
dimensions.description: Retained verbatim as the raw array Xero returned: the declared element order is part of the document and is lost by flattening. Fully normalised into xero_payroll_au_payslip_reimbursement_lines (one row per element) — join there for anything you filter or aggregate on, and read this column only when the original ordering or an unflattened payload matters.

dimensions.label: reimbursement type id
dimensions.description: Xero's immutable reimbursement pay item identifier; payslip reimbursement lines reference it.

dimensions.label: name
dimensions.description: Admin-chosen label ('Travel reimbursement'; the spec's doc-string wrongly says 'earnings rate'). The only categorical handle this small dimension offers.

dimensions.label: account code
dimensions.description: Default GL expense account code for this reimbursement type; join xero_accounts on code. Payslip lines can override it via their own expense_account.

dimensions.label: updated date utc
dimensions.description: Last-modified audit stamp on the reimbursement pay item and the incremental sync watermark for the PayItems scan. Configuration recency only — it says nothing about when money was reimbursed.

dimensions.label: current record
dimensions.description: Active flag for the pay item. Filter true when listing what the org can currently reimburse; never filter it inside a join from historical reimbursement lines, or retired types drop their rows and reimbursement spend silently shrinks in older periods.

dimensions.label: settings scope
dimensions.description: Minted singleton key so the row has a stable identity across syncs.

dimensions.label: employees are stp2
dimensions.description: Whether the org has been enabled for STP Phase 2 employee editing. False means STP2-only fields across the employee tables (income types, disaggregated flags) may be systematically absent — an ingestion-wide data-quality signal, not an employee attribute.

dimensions.label: tracking categories
dimensions.description: Which tracking category classifies employee groups and which classifies timesheets. Kept verbatim because the spec types this as a bare object and declares no keys at all: the EmployeeGroups / TimesheetCategories shape is a runtime observation, not a contract, so probe with jsonb_object_keys before hardcoding a path — a wrong key returns NULL silently instead of erroring, and that NULL reads as 'no tracking configured' when it means 'wrong key'. Resolve the ids inside against xero_tracking_categories to name the dimensions, then match employee_group_name to that category's options.

dimensions.label: accounts
dimensions.description: Verbatim Settings.Accounts array — the payroll control-account wiring exactly as returned, normalized into xero_payroll_au_settings_accounts. Query that table for the role filters (WAGESEXPENSE, PAYGLIABILITY, ...); this copy exists so a re-wire of the payroll GL accounts is diffable between syncs.

dimensions.label: settings scope
dimensions.description: Parent key copied down from xero_payroll_au_settings so this explode table joins to its header on a real column instead of a bare literal. Constant within a tenant, and deliberately so: the value is uninteresting, but without it the header-to-lines join degenerates into a cross join that would multiply rows the moment a second scope ever appeared.

dimensions.label: account id
dimensions.description: GL account identifier — the same UUID as xero_accounts.account_id, making the cross-domain join exact. Part of the key, not the whole key: the same account can be wired to more than one payroll role.

dimensions.label: type
dimensions.description: Account type including the payroll-specific roles (PAYGLIABILITY, PAYG, SUPERANNUATIONEXPENSE, SUPERANNUATIONLIABILITY, WAGESEXPENSE, WAGESPAYABLELIABILITY) alongside standard ledger types. The payroll roles are the reason this table exists — filter on them to find where each payroll obligation posts. Key member: one GL account may carry several roles, so (settings_scope, account_id, type) is the grain.

dimensions.label: code
dimensions.description: Customer-defined account code — the value payroll template lines store in their *account_code columns, so this is the hop that turns codes back into account ids.

dimensions.label: name
dimensions.description: Human label of the wired GL account, echoed from the chart of accounts at sync time. Use it to sanity-check the wiring in a report; for anything durable resolve account_id against xero_accounts, because admins rename accounts and this echo goes stale between syncs.

dimensions.label: abn
dimensions.description: ABN of the entity offering the product and half the row key. One ABN typically fronts many USIs, so it never identifies a product on its own — never join funds to products on ABN alone or you fan a fund out across every product that ABN offers. Text, because an ABN is an 11-digit identifier rather than a quantity and can arrive spaced or unspaced.

dimensions.label: usi
dimensions.description: Unique Superannuation Identifier of the product; the other half of the key and the join back to xero_payroll_au_super_funds.usi.

dimensions.label: product name
dimensions.description: The official registered product name — the label to prefer over the admin-typed fund name when presenting regulated funds.

dimensions.label: super fund id
dimensions.description: Xero's fund identifier and the row key; what super memberships reference.

dimensions.label: type
dimensions.description: REGULATED (APRA fund, identified by USI) or SMSF (self-managed, identified by ABN with its own BSB/account for direct payment). This decides which columns are populated — querying usi on an SMSF or bank details on a regulated fund returns nulls by design.

dimensions.label: name
dimensions.description: Fund display name. For REGULATED funds prefer the product name resolved via USI from xero_payroll_au_super_fund_products — this field is whatever the payroll admin typed.

dimensions.label: abn
dimensions.description: Australian Business Number — the spec documents it as the ABN of the self-managed super fund, i.e. the SMSF's primary identifier (SMSFs have no USI). Identify REGULATED funds by usi, not this column. Keep as text; ABNs are 11 digits and not arithmetic.

dimensions.label: electronic service address
dimensions.description: The SMSF's SuperStream electronic service address (ESA) for receiving contribution messages. SMSF-only, operational plumbing.

dimensions.label: employer number
dimensions.description: The employer number some funds assign to this organisation — identifies the EMPLOYER to the fund, not any employee.

dimensions.label: usi
dimensions.description: Unique Superannuation Identifier of the regulated fund product — the canonical join to xero_payroll_au_super_fund_products and the identifier SuperStream payments route on. Null for SMSFs.

dimensions.label: updated date utc
dimensions.description: Last-modified stamp and incremental watermark for the fund registry scan.

dimensions.label: validation errors
dimensions.description: API validation messages echoed on the record, verbatim for debugging. Presentation-only.

dimensions.label: timesheet id
dimensions.description: Parent timesheet key, inherited on explode; status, employee and period dates live on the parent.

dimensions.label: timesheet lines
dimensions.description: Zero-based position of this line in the timesheet's TimesheetLines array, minted at explode time; lines have no id of their own.

dimensions.label: earnings rate id
dimensions.description: The earnings rate these hours will be paid at (ordinary vs overtime vs allowance); join xero_payroll_au_earnings_rates. The split key for overtime-hours analysis at entry time.

dimensions.label: tracking item id
dimensions.description: Despite the name, this is a tracking OPTION id (from the tracking category the org designated for timesheets) — join xero_tracking_options.tracking_option_id, not the category table. The cost-centre/department axis for labor hours; null when the org does not track timesheets.

dimensions.label: number of units
dimensions.description: ARRAY of daily hour values, one element per day of the timesheet period, ordered from the timesheet's StartDate (element 0 = start day, weekends included as 0 or null). Total line hours = SUM over jsonb_array_elements_text(number_of_units)::numeric; day-of-week analysis uses the element index added to start_date. Reading it as a single number, or taking the first element, silently drops most of the hours.

dimensions.label: updated date utc
dimensions.description: Last-modified stamp on the line itself; the parent timesheet's stamp is the sync watermark, this one localizes which line changed.

dimensions.label: timesheet id
dimensions.description: Xero's immutable timesheet identifier and the row key — the only thing that is actually unique here, since the same employee and period can carry a rejected submission and its replacement.

dimensions.label: employee id
dimensions.description: Whose hours these are; join xero_payroll_au_employees. Do not treat employee + period as unique: a refused submission and its replacement both persist, so 'hours for employee X in week W' must filter status before summing or the rejected copy is added back in.

dimensions.label: start date
dimensions.description: First day of the timesheet period; also the anchor for reading the daily units arrays on the lines (element 0 = this day).

dimensions.label: end date
dimensions.description: Last day of the timesheet period (inclusive). Period length fixes the expected length of each line's daily units array.

dimensions.label: status
dimensions.description: The trust filter. DRAFT/REQUESTED hours are unvetted; APPROVED is signed off but unpaid; PROCESSED is in a posted pay run; REJECTED never counts. 'Hours worked' analyses usually mean APPROVED + PROCESSED — including drafts turns typos into labor cost.

dimensions.label: updated date utc
dimensions.description: Last-modified audit stamp and the incremental sync watermark for timesheets. It ticks on every status transition (submit, approve, reject) as well as on hour edits, so it dates the last administrative touch, not the work — never use it as the date hours were worked; that is start_date/end_date.

dimensions.label: validation errors
dimensions.description: Write-response diagnostic payload from the API; null on every read. Never analytical — present only so the staging row is a faithful copy of the record, and a non-null value here means a write was replayed, not that the business record is invalid.

dimensions.label: timesheet lines
dimensions.description: Retained verbatim as the raw array Xero returned: the declared element order is part of the document and is lost by flattening. Fully normalised into xero_payroll_au_timesheet_lines (one row per element) — join there for anything you filter or aggregate on, and read this column only when the original ordering or an unflattened payload matters.

dimensions.label: deduction id
dimensions.description: Xero's identifier for the deduction type (lower-cased 'deductionId' in this v2 API); referenced by payslip deduction lines.

dimensions.label: deduction name
dimensions.description: The label the org gave this deduction, shown on payslips and in the pay-run UI. Free text edited in place, so historical payslip lines render under today's name — classify with deduction_category and join on deduction_id. Grouping deductions by name silently merges two types an org renamed to the same string and splits one it renamed mid-year.

dimensions.label: deduction category
dimensions.description: Statutory-reporting bucket. PayrollGiving earns tax credits; KiwiSaverVoluntaryContributions is voluntary top-up saving (NOT the standard 3-10 percent employee contribution); Superannuation is non-KiwiSaver schemes; NzOther is everything else. Classifying deductions in payslip analysis starts here.

dimensions.label: liability account id
dimensions.description: GL liability account the withheld money accrues to until paid out; joins to xero_accounts.account_id for reconciling payroll liabilities against the ledger.

dimensions.label: current record
dimensions.description: True when the deduction type is active. Inactive types persist because historical payslips reference them — filter current_record for 'available deductions' but keep all rows when decoding history.

dimensions.label: standard amount
dimensions.description: Default NZD amount suggested when the deduction is added to a payslip; a default, not what was actually deducted anywhere.

dimensions.label: earnings rate id
dimensions.description: Xero's identifier for the earnings rate; the foreign key on timesheet lines, salary records and pay-template lines.

dimensions.label: name
dimensions.description: Display name ('Ordinary Hours', 'Time and a Half'...). Names are org-chosen — classify by earnings_type, not by string-matching names.

dimensions.label: earnings type
dimensions.description: Statutory classification of the earning. RegularEarnings is base pay; OvertimeEarnings feeds overtime metrics; HolidayPay is the 8-percent casual payout; WithholdingIncome flags schedular-contractor pay that is NOT employee wages and must be excluded from wage-bill answers; the two Tips values contain parentheses and need exact-string matching.

dimensions.label: rate type
dimensions.description: Calculation mechanics: RatePerUnit uses rate_per_unit x units; MultipleOfOrdinaryEarningsRate scales the employee's own ordinary rate by multiple_of_ordinary_earnings_rate (so the dollar rate differs per employee); FixedAmount pays fixed_amount flat. Exactly one of the three amount columns is meaningful per row.

dimensions.label: type of units
dimensions.description: Unit label for quantities recorded against this rate (typically Hours). Timesheet units inherit this meaning — summing units across rates with different unit types is meaningless.

dimensions.label: current record
dimensions.description: True when the rate is active for new pay; retired rates persist because historical lines reference them.

dimensions.label: expense account id
dimensions.description: GL expense account this earning posts to — the bridge from payroll to P&L wage-cost lines; joins to xero_accounts.account_id.

dimensions.label: rate per unit
dimensions.description: Default NZD rate per unit, only when rate_type = RatePerUnit; per-employee salary records override it. Null here does not mean unpaid.

dimensions.label: fixed amount
dimensions.description: Flat NZD amount per occurrence, only when rate_type = FixedAmount.

dimensions.label: employee id
dimensions.description: Owning employee, inherited from the fan-out path parameter.

dimensions.label: bank accounts
dimensions.description: Zero-based position in the parent's bankAccounts array (accounts carry no id); provenance is the array itself. Order matters to Xero's split logic — fixed-amount accounts are taken before the Balance account.

dimensions.label: particulars
dimensions.description: First of NZ banking's three free-text annotation fields (particulars / code / reference) that print on both parties' statements — conventionally the payer or 'Wages'. Set per destination account, so a split-pay employee can see different text against each credit. A label only: it carries no amount, date or identifier the platform can compute from.

dimensions.label: code
dimensions.description: Second of the NZ particulars/code/reference statement triplet, conventionally a short payroll or employee code the payer uses to recognise the credit. Org-chosen free text with no referential integrity to anything in Xero — resist the temptation to join or group on it, and never treat a matching code as evidence two rows are the same person.

dimensions.label: reference
dimensions.description: Third of the NZ particulars/code/reference triplet — the statement text the employee sees against the credit, often the pay period or 'Salary'. Static configuration reused on every pay, so it does not identify a specific payment and cannot be used to reconcile an individual wage transfer to a pay run.

dimensions.label: calculation type
dimensions.description: FixedAmount takes dollar_amount each pay; Balance receives whatever net pay remains. Exactly one Balance account should exist per employee — more than one indicates misconfiguration worth flagging, not averaging.

dimensions.label: leave id
dimensions.description: Xero's identifier for this leave request and the row key (the spec's description mislabels it 'LeaveType' — it is the leave record's own id).

dimensions.label: employee id
dimensions.description: Employee taking the leave, inherited from the fan-out path parameter.

dimensions.label: leave type id
dimensions.description: Which kind of leave. Join xero_payroll_nz_leave_types for the name and whether it is paid — 'annual leave taken' without this join silently mixes sick, bereavement and unpaid leave.

dimensions.label: start date
dimensions.description: First calendar day of the leave span. Calendar span, not units: a Friday-to-Monday request spans 4 days but may consume 2 units — quantity questions go to the periods table.

dimensions.label: end date
dimensions.description: Last calendar day of the leave span, inclusive. Filter leave overlapping window [a,b] with start_date <= b AND end_date >= a.

dimensions.label: updated date utc
dimensions.description: Audit stamp of the last change to this request; sync watermark, not a business date.

dimensions.label: employee id
dimensions.description: Employee holding the balance, inherited from the fan-out path parameter.

dimensions.label: leave type id
dimensions.description: Leave type of the balance; join xero_payroll_nz_leave_types for accrual rules.

dimensions.label: name
dimensions.description: Leave type name denormalized by Xero onto the balance; convenient for display but the id is the join key.

dimensions.label: type of units
dimensions.description: Unit of the balance (Hours for most types, Weeks for NZ annual leave entitlement). Summing balances across unit types produces a meaningless number — always group or filter by this.

dimensions.label: leave id
dimensions.description: Parent leave request this period slice belongs to.

dimensions.label: periods
dimensions.description: Zero-based position of this slice within the parent request's periods array (the slices carry no id of their own); provenance is the periods array itself. Chronological order follows period_start_date, which is the safer sort key.

dimensions.label: employee id
dimensions.description: Employee on leave, denormalized from the fan-out path so leave-by-person queries skip a join.

dimensions.label: period start date
dimensions.description: Start of the PAY period this slice falls in — the payroll calendar's boundary, not the leave's own start date.

dimensions.label: period end date
dimensions.description: End of the pay period this slice falls in. Bucket leave into months by this date (or the parent's dates) consistently — mixing conventions splits one request across months twice.

dimensions.label: type of units
dimensions.description: Unit for number_of_units (Hours, Days, Weeks as Xero spells them). NZ statutory leave mixes hour- and week-based types — never SUM units across different type_of_units values.

dimensions.label: type of units taken
dimensions.description: Unit for number_of_units_taken; normally equals type_of_units but is carried separately by the API — check both before aggregating.

dimensions.label: period status
dimensions.description: Approved = confirmed for a pay run; Completed = paid in a finalized run; Estimated = Xero's forecast split that no pay run has confirmed. Actual-leave metrics must exclude Estimated or future forecast leave inflates history.

dimensions.label: employee id
dimensions.description: Employee this accrual configuration applies to, inherited from the fan-out path parameter.

dimensions.label: leave type id
dimensions.description: The org-level leave type being configured for this employee; join xero_payroll_nz_leave_types for its name.

dimensions.label: schedule of accrual
dimensions.description: How this employee accrues the type. AnnuallyAfter6Months and OnAnniversaryDate grant lump entitlements; PercentageOfGrossEarnings accrues per pay (casual holiday pay); NoAccruals means the type never self-accrues (sick leave granted by statute events). Determines which of the quantity columns below is meaningful.

dimensions.label: type of units to accrue
dimensions.description: Unit of units_accrued_annually (Hours/Days/Weeks). Comparing entitlements across employees requires equal units first.

dimensions.label: maximum to accrue
dimensions.description: Cap on accrued units; null means uncapped. Balances at the cap accrue nothing further — relevant when projecting future liability.

dimensions.label: opening balance
dimensions.description: Units granted when the type was first assigned to the employee (migration or enrolment); a one-time seed, already reflected in the current balance — never add it on top.

dimensions.label: opening balance type of units
dimensions.description: Unit of the opening balance; can differ from the accrual unit for annual leave (weeks vs hours).

dimensions.label: include holiday pay every pay
dimensions.description: Holiday-pay-specific: true means the 8 percent is paid out in every pay run instead of banked — such employees accrue no annual-leave balance, so their zero balance is correct, not missing data.

dimensions.label: show annual leave in advance
dimensions.description: Annual-leave-specific payslip display flag: include leave available in advance in the shown balance. Presentation only — does not change the stored balance.

dimensions.label: schedule of accrual date
dimensions.description: The date the employee next/first becomes entitled to the accrual (anniversary-based schedules). A future date means the entitlement has not landed yet.

dimensions.label: employee id
dimensions.description: Owning employee, inherited from the fan-out path parameter.

dimensions.label: balance ordinal
dimensions.description: Minted array position — the source rows carry no identifier of their own. Stable only within one sync; use employee_id + period_end_date for human-facing ordering.

dimensions.label: period end date
dimensions.description: End date of the historical pay period this line covers. Periods predate the org's first Xero pay run — a line dated after go-live indicates a data-entry error, not a real pay period.

dimensions.label: days paid
dimensions.description: Number of days paid in the period; feeds NZ 'ordinary weekly pay' divisors. Zero with positive gross usually means a lump sum, which distorts averages.

dimensions.label: unpaid weeks
dimensions.description: Whole weeks unpaid within the period; subtracted from the divisor in average-weekly-earnings calculations, so ignoring it understates the true weekly average.

dimensions.label: employee id
dimensions.description: Employee the template belongs to; the API also echoes it inside the pay template body, which is the provenance used here.

dimensions.label: pay template earning id
dimensions.description: Xero's identifier for this template line; the stable line key.

dimensions.label: earning templates
dimensions.description: Zero-based position in the template's earningTemplates array, preserving Xero's display order; provenance is the array itself.

dimensions.label: earnings rate id
dimensions.description: Which earnings rate the line applies; join xero_payroll_nz_earnings_rates to learn whether the line is RatePerUnit or FixedAmount and which columns below are live.

dimensions.label: name
dimensions.description: Read-only display name of the template line, echoing the earnings rate name at assignment time; the live name is on the joined earnings rate.

dimensions.label: employee id
dimensions.description: Employee this payment method belongs to, inherited from the fan-out path parameter.

dimensions.label: payment method
dimensions.description: Electronically means net pay leaves in the bank file, split across the accounts in the bank-accounts child table; Cheque and Manual are settled outside that file, so those employees normally carry no bank-account rows at all. An employee with an empty child set and a non-electronic method is correctly configured, not missing data — treat the two facts together before flagging a payroll setup gap.

dimensions.label: employee id
dimensions.description: Owning employee, inherited from the fan-out path parameter; one tax record per employee.

dimensions.label: tax code
dimensions.description: NZ PAYE tax code. M is the common primary-income code; codes containing SL (MSL, SBSL...) carry student-loan deductions; WT is schedular/withholding income (contractor-like); ND is no-declaration emergency rate. Segmenting 'employees with student loans' means tax codes containing SL OR has_student_loan_balance — not either alone.

dimensions.label: special tax rate percentage
dimensions.description: IR-issued special tax rate (STC tax code); a percentage, only meaningful when the tax code is a special-rate code. Never average across employees.

dimensions.label: has special student loan rate
dimensions.description: True when IR granted a non-standard student loan deduction rate; pairs with special_student_loan_rate_percentage.

dimensions.label: special student loan rate percentage
dimensions.description: The IR-approved non-standard student-loan deduction rate for this employee, as a percentage of earnings. Only live when has_special_student_loan_rate is true — a value sitting here with the flag false is a leftover from a lapsed IR variation, and applying it inflates modelled deductions. Gate on the flag, never on the value being non-null.

dimensions.label: is eligible for kiwi saver
dimensions.description: Whether the employee is eligible for KiwiSaver at all. Eligibility is not membership — kiwisaver_contributions holds the actual participation state.

dimensions.label: kiwi saver contributions
dimensions.description: KiwiSaver participation state. MakeContributions is the only state where per-pay contributions actually occur; OptOut, OnAContributionsHoliday, OnASavingsSuspension and NotCurrentlyAKiwiSaverMember all mean zero current contributions even though the rate columns may still hold values. Any 'KiwiSaver participation' metric filters this, not the rate columns.

dimensions.label: kiwi saver employer salary sacrifice contribution rate percentage
dimensions.description: Portion of the employer contribution funded by salary sacrifice. Part of, not additional to, the package — adding it on top of the employer rate double-counts.

dimensions.label: kiwi saver opt out date
dimensions.description: Date an opt-out from KiwiSaver took effect; populated alongside kiwisaver_contributions = 'OptOut'. Presence of a date is not a current-state test — someone who opted out and later re-joined keeps the historical date while their state moves to MakeContributions. Read kiwisaver_contributions for participation and use this only to date the event.

dimensions.label: kiwi saver contribution holiday end date
dimensions.description: When a contributions holiday / savings suspension expires; after this date contributions resume, so 'currently suspended' checks this date as well as the state.

dimensions.label: has student loan balance
dimensions.description: True when IR notified a remaining student-loan balance, which caps final deductions. Distinct from having an SL tax code — an employee can carry SL deductions with no balance letter on file.

dimensions.label: student loan as at
dimensions.description: Date of the IR student-loan letter that student_loan_balance was copied from.

dimensions.label: payee working pattern id
dimensions.description: Xero's identifier for the working pattern (spelled payeeWorkingPatternID in the API); the key the working-weeks detail hangs off.

dimensions.label: employee id
dimensions.description: Employee the pattern belongs to, inherited from the fan-out path parameter.

dimensions.label: effective from
dimensions.description: Date the pattern takes effect. Multiple patterns per employee form a history — 'current pattern' is the max effective_from <= today, not the latest row synced.

dimensions.label: payee working pattern id
dimensions.description: Parent working pattern, from the detail record's own id field.

dimensions.label: working weeks
dimensions.description: Zero-based week position in the repeating cycle (weeks carry no id); provenance is the workingWeeks array. Week 0 then week 1 alternate for a two-week roster.

dimensions.label: effective from
dimensions.description: Effective date denormalized from the detail record so the grid is usable without joining back to the header.

dimensions.label: employee id
dimensions.description: Xero's immutable employee identifier; the join key every per-employee fan-out table (tax, leave, pay templates, salary) hangs off.

dimensions.label: start date
dimensions.description: Employment start date as at the time the record was requested. Headcount as-of-date D is start_date <= D AND (end_date IS NULL OR end_date >= D) — counting rows without the date window overstates headcount with future starters and leavers.

dimensions.label: end date
dimensions.description: Employment end date; null while employed. Non-null means terminated (or a scheduled termination) — every 'current headcount' or 'active staff' answer must filter end_date IS NULL OR end_date >= CURRENT_DATE, or ex-employees inflate the count.

dimensions.label: payroll calendar id
dimensions.description: The pay-run calendar this employee is paid on. Join to xero_payroll_nz_pay_run_calendars for frequency (Weekly/Monthly...); employees on different calendars are paid on different cycles, so 'this pay period' is per-calendar, not org-wide.

dimensions.label: updated date utc
dimensions.description: Audit stamp of the last change to the employee record; the incremental-sync watermark. Not an employment event date — never use it for tenure math.

dimensions.label: created date utc
dimensions.description: When the record was created in Xero — a data-entry timestamp that can postdate start_date by years for migrated employees. Tenure comes from start_date, never from this.

dimensions.label: job title
dimensions.description: Free-text job title; uncontrolled vocabulary ('Dev', 'Developer', 'Software Developer' are three values). Group with care or via mapping, not raw equality.

dimensions.label: engagement type
dimensions.description: Xero's classification of the employment agreement behind the role. The spec declares NO value set for this field, so the org's actual strings must be inspected before it is used as a segment — never hard-code labels or assume a fixed vocabulary. Rows whose engagement is fixed-term also carry fixed_term_end_date, and employees engaged casually typically have no working pattern at all, so averaging contracted hours across engagement types without segmenting blends incomparable populations.

dimensions.label: fixed term end date
dimensions.description: Contractual end of a fixed-term engagement. It is a plan, not a termination: the actual leaving date is end_date, and the two can differ when a contract ends early or is extended.

dimensions.label: leave type id
dimensions.description: Xero's identifier for the leave type; the join key from leave requests, balances and per-employee configurations.

dimensions.label: name
dimensions.description: Display name ('Annual Leave', 'Sick Leave'...). Statutory NZ types have conventional names but custom types are free text — prefer id-based logic.

dimensions.label: is paid leave
dimensions.description: Whether taking this leave pays the employee. Absence-cost questions must split paid from unpaid — unpaid leave reduces pay rather than costing it, the exact opposite effect on the wage bill.

dimensions.label: show on payslip
dimensions.description: Payslip display flag for the balance; presentation only, no effect on accrual or payment.

dimensions.label: updated date utc
dimensions.description: Audit stamp of the last change to the type; sync watermark.

dimensions.label: is active
dimensions.description: True when the type can be used on new leave; the ActiveOnly request parameter filters on this, so the sync must NOT pass it or retired types referenced by history disappear.

dimensions.label: type of units
dimensions.description: Unit leave of this type is paid in (Hours for most; Weeks for NZ annual leave entitlement under the Holidays Act). The reason a blanket SUM over leave units is wrong.

dimensions.label: type of units to accrue
dimensions.description: Unit the type accrues in; can differ from type_of_units (accrue weeks, take hours) — conversion happens via the employee's working pattern.

dimensions.label: payroll calendar id
dimensions.description: Xero's identifier for the calendar; employees and pay runs reference it.

dimensions.label: name
dimensions.description: The org's own label for the pay cycle ('Weekly Wages', 'Monthly Salaries'). Free text that is not kept in step with the cadence, so a calendar still named 'Fortnightly' can legitimately be Monthly after the org changed its cycle — read calendar_type for the frequency and never infer it from this string.

dimensions.label: calendar type
dimensions.description: Pay frequency. Annualizing a per-period amount multiplies by the periods-per-year this implies (Weekly 52, Fortnightly 26, FourWeekly 13, Monthly 12, TwiceMonthly 24, Quarterly 4, Annual 1) — using 26 for FourWeekly is the classic annualization bug.

dimensions.label: period start date
dimensions.description: Start of the calendar's current/next open period; rolls forward each posted run. Not the calendar's inception date.

dimensions.label: period end date
dimensions.description: End of the current/next open period; with period_start_date defines the window timesheets and leave will fall into for the next run.

dimensions.label: payment date
dimensions.description: The date wages for the current period hit bank accounts — cash-flow forecasting reads this, and it can fall in a different month than the period it pays for (accrual vs cash timing).

dimensions.label: updated date utc
dimensions.description: Audit stamp; changes every time the period rolls, so it is noisy as a change signal.

dimensions.label: pay run id
dimensions.description: Xero's immutable identifier for the pay run and the row key; the fan-out parameter for pulling this run's payslips.

dimensions.label: payroll calendar id
dimensions.description: The payroll calendar (pay frequency schedule) this run was generated from. Group by it to separate the weekly wage cycle from the monthly salary cycle — mixing calendars in a per-run average produces a meaningless blended figure. The calendar entity itself is owned by the NZ payroll settings domain.

dimensions.label: period start date
dimensions.description: First day of the earnings period this run pays for. Use the period dates for labour-cost accrual questions ('what did March labour cost'), not paymentDate — a run paid on 3 April can cover work done in March.

dimensions.label: period end date
dimensions.description: Last day of the earnings period. Periods of different calendars overlap freely; do not treat (period_start_date, period_end_date) as unique — unscheduled runs reuse the same period.

dimensions.label: payment date
dimensions.description: The day employees are paid — the cash-basis date, and the date that fixes the PAYE filing period with IRD. Cash-flow questions bucket by this; accrual questions bucket by the period dates. The two commonly straddle a month boundary.

dimensions.label: pay run status
dimensions.description: Draft runs are in-progress and mutable — their totals and payslips change or vanish entirely if the draft is discarded. Every aggregate in this domain must filter to 'Posted' (directly here, via a join from the payslip and line tables) or drafts inflate and destabilise history.

dimensions.label: pay run type
dimensions.description: Scheduled runs follow the calendar; Unscheduled runs are legitimate off-cycle pay (bonuses, corrections, final pay) and belong in cost totals; EarlierYearUpdate runs restate a prior tax year and will distort period-over-period trend lines if bucketed by their payment_date — exclude or handle them explicitly in time series.

dimensions.label: calendar type
dimensions.description: Pay frequency of the calendar behind this run. Needed to annualise correctly: a Weekly run's totals ×52, a Monthly run's ×12 — averaging per-run amounts across mixed frequencies without this column is the classic wrong answer for 'average pay run size'.

dimensions.label: posted date time
dimensions.description: When the run was posted (finalised); null while Draft, which makes it the cheapest test for 'has this run actually been committed'. Audit stamp, not a business date — bucket money by payment_date or the period dates, never by this. Expect true here on inspection, but verify before filtering on it; a report that filters this to true will return nothing if the field is unpopulated, which reads as 'no timesheet wages' rather than 'flag absent'.

dimensions.label: last edited

dimensions.label: payment method

'Electronically' payslips fan out into payment lines per bank account; Cheque/Manual payslips may carry no meaningful payment-line split at all. Load-bearing because bank-feed reconciliation is only valid over Electronically payslips — including Cheque/Manual rows makes expected outflow exceed what the bank file actually paid, and excluding them from a 'net pay' total understates wages.

dimensions.label: tax settings period type

It reflects the tax calculation, not the calendar: read pay frequency from the run's calendar_type instead, because a fortnightly calendar reports here as 2 weeks and grouping headcount by this column collapses distinct calendars together.

dimensions.label: tax settings lump sum tax code

dimensions.label: tax settings lump sum amount

A Holidays Act input feeding average-daily-pay calculations — use it as a divisor (gross / days_paid), never as an additive headcount-days measure across employees with different calendars.

dimensions.label: gross earnings history unpaid weeks

dimensions.description: The ordinary-earnings rate this arrangement pays through (normally the org's Ordinary Hours rate); join xero_payroll_nz_earnings_rates for its GL expense account.

dimensions.label: number of units per day
dimensions.description: Standard hours per working day; used by leave-in-days conversions. Hours-per-week / hours-per-day gives implied days-per-week when days_per_week is null.

dimensions.label: days per week
dimensions.description: Standard working days per week for the arrangement; can be fractional for alternating patterns.

dimensions.label: effective from
dimensions.description: Date the arrangement takes effect. Point-in-time salary at date D is the row with the greatest effective_from <= D per employee — status alone cannot answer historical questions.

dimensions.label: status
dimensions.description: Active is the one current arrangement; Pending is future-dated (a scheduled raise); History is superseded. Payroll-cost baselines filter Active; raise-tracking compares consecutive rows ordered by effective_from.

dimensions.label: payment type
dimensions.description: Salary (annual amount drives pay) vs Hourly (rate x timesheet/pattern hours drives pay). Hourly employees' annual_salary is notional — actual earnings vary with hours worked.

dimensions.label: work pattern type
dimensions.description: Whether standard time is expressed as DaysAndHours (units-per-day/days-per-week here) or a RegularWeek working pattern (see xero_payroll_nz_employee_working_patterns for the per-day hours).

dimensions.label: account id
dimensions.description: GL account UUID; equals xero_accounts.account_id, which is the join to full account metadata. Not the row key — the same GL account can be assigned to more than one payroll role, so key on type.

dimensions.label: type
dimensions.description: The payroll role this account plays and the row key: PAYELIABILITY accrues PAYE owed to IR; WAGESPAYABLE holds net wages until paid; WAGESEXPENSE is the default P&L wage cost; BANK is the account wages are paid from. Reconciliation queries pick the role here, then follow account_id into journals.

dimensions.label: code
dimensions.description: The account's short code (3 digits per Xero's payroll docs); matches xero_accounts.code but the UUID is the safe join.

dimensions.label: name
dimensions.description: Account display name denormalized from the ledger at read time.

dimensions.label: id
dimensions.description: Xero's identifier for the statutory deduction type (the API calls it just 'id'; docs describe it as the earnings-order id).

dimensions.label: name
dimensions.description: The label the payroll administrator gave the order or statutory item. Free text, so it may carry an IR or court reference — and occasionally identifying detail about the employee subject to the order, which is why it should not be surfaced casually. Group by statutory_deduction_category for anything analytical; the name is a display string only.

dimensions.label: statutory deduction category
dimensions.description: Legal category driving deduction-priority rules: PriorityOrder/NonPriorityOrder/TableBased govern attachment-order sequencing when net pay can't cover everything; ChildSupport, CourtFines, InlandRevenueArrears, MsdRepayments are specific order kinds; the three StudentLoan variants and KiwiSaver round out the statutory set. KiwiSaver appearing HERE (the standard employee contribution) and in the voluntary deductions catalogue (top-ups) is the classic double-count trap.

dimensions.label: liability account id
dimensions.description: GL liability account holding withheld statutory amounts pending remittance to the Crown agency; joins to xero_accounts.account_id.

dimensions.label: current record
dimensions.description: True when the type is active for new payslips; inactive rows remain for decoding history.

dimensions.label: id
dimensions.description: Xero's identifier for the superannuation scheme (field name is just 'id' on the Benefit object).

dimensions.label: name
dimensions.description: The org's label for the scheme as it prints on payslips. Editable free text, so historical payslip lines display today's name and a rename rewrites the apparent history — read category for what the scheme actually is and join on superannuation_id.

dimensions.label: category
dimensions.description: KiwiSaver (the national scheme), ComplyingFund (KiwiSaver-equivalent registered fund) or Other. Employer-contribution analysis usually wants KiwiSaver + ComplyingFund together since both attract ESCT and satisfy auto-enrolment.

dimensions.label: liability account id
dimensions.description: GL liability account accruing contributions until remitted to the fund/IRD; joins to xero_accounts.account_id.

dimensions.label: expense account id
dimensions.description: GL expense account carrying the employer's contribution cost; this is where super shows up in P&L wage-cost questions.

dimensions.label: calculation type nz
dimensions.description: FixedAmount pays standard_amount per period; PercentageOfTaxableEarnings pays percentage of the employee's taxable earnings. Determines which of standard_amount/percentage is live — the other is noise.

dimensions.label: standard amount
dimensions.description: Default per-period NZD contribution for FixedAmount schemes; a default rate card, not an amount contributed.

dimensions.label: percentage
dimensions.description: Default contribution percentage of taxable earnings for percentage schemes. Per-employee KiwiSaver rates in xero_payroll_nz_employee_tax override this default.

dimensions.label: company max
dimensions.description: Employer contribution cap for the scheme; contributions computed above it are clipped, so modelling employer cost from raw percentages without this cap overstates spend for high earners.

dimensions.label: current record
dimensions.description: True when the scheme is active; inactive schemes remain for historical payslip decoding.

dimensions.label: timesheet line id
dimensions.description: Xero's identifier for the line; the row key.

dimensions.label: timesheet id
dimensions.description: Parent timesheet, inherited during explode; the required route to employee, period and status.

dimensions.label: timesheet lines
dimensions.description: Zero-based position within the parent's timesheetLines array, preserving entry order; provenance is the array itself.

dimensions.label: employee id
dimensions.description: Employee who worked the units, denormalized from the parent so per-person hour queries skip a join — but status filtering still requires the parent.

dimensions.label: date
dimensions.description: The calendar day worked (renamed from 'date' to avoid the SQL keyword). Daily-hours series group on this; it always falls inside the parent's period.

dimensions.label: earnings rate id
dimensions.description: Which earnings rate the units are claimed at. Overtime vs ordinary lives here: join xero_payroll_nz_earnings_rates and split on earnings_type before pricing hours.

dimensions.label: tracking item id
dimensions.description: Tracking option (a xero_tracking_options row) tagging the line to a department/region/job when the org enabled a timesheet tracking category (see xero_payroll_nz_tracking_categories). Null when tracking is off — labour-allocation reports must state the untracked remainder.

dimensions.label: timesheet id
dimensions.description: Xero's identifier for the timesheet; the parent key of its lines.

dimensions.label: payroll calendar id
dimensions.description: Pay calendar whose period this timesheet covers; start/end dates below are that calendar's period boundaries.

dimensions.label: employee id
dimensions.description: Employee the hours belong to — carried on the record itself here, unlike the fan-out employee tables.

dimensions.label: start date
dimensions.description: First day of the timesheet's pay period. One timesheet per employee per period — a second one for the same window signals a resubmission, not extra hours.

dimensions.label: end date
dimensions.description: Last day of the timesheet's pay period, INCLUSIVE — so a containment test is work_date BETWEEN start_date AND end_date, and a half-open range silently drops the final day of every period. It mirrors the pay calendar's window, not the range of days the employee actually entered hours for.

dimensions.label: status
dimensions.description: Lifecycle: Draft (being entered), Requested (awaiting approval), Approved (payable), Completed (paid in a posted run). Worked-hours facts filter Approved+Completed; payroll-pending queues filter Requested.

dimensions.label: updated date utc
dimensions.description: Audit stamp of the last edit; the incremental sync watermark for timesheets and their lines.

dimensions.label: settings key
dimensions.description: Minted singleton key so the row has a stable identity across syncs.

dimensions.label: employee groups tracking category id
dimensions.description: The accounting tracking category whose options group EMPLOYEES (e.g. by department) for wage-cost reporting; joins to xero_tracking_categories.tracking_category_id. Null = employee grouping not configured.

dimensions.label: timesheet tracking category id
dimensions.description: The accounting tracking category whose options tag TIMESHEET LINES; xero_payroll_nz_timesheet_lines.tracking_item_id values are options of this category. Null = timesheet tracking off, so every tracking_item_id will be null too.

dimensions.label: id
dimensions.description: Xero's identifier for the benefit pay item; payslip benefit lines reference it.

dimensions.label: name
dimensions.description: The org's label for the scheme as it appears on payslips (typically the pension provider). The only human-readable way to tell two schemes apart, since category collapses everything to StakeholderPension or Other — but it is free text, so an org running one scheme under two items (different contribution tiers) will show near-identical names that must not be merged.

dimensions.label: category
dimensions.description: StakeholderPension marks a pension scheme; Other is the catch-all. Pension-specific analyses (auto-enrolment coverage) should filter StakeholderPension.

dimensions.label: liability account id
dimensions.description: GL account the accrued contribution liability posts to; join xero_accounts to trace payroll postings into the ledger.

dimensions.label: expense account id
dimensions.description: GL account the employer contribution expense posts to — where pension cost lands in the P&L.

dimensions.label: standard amount
dimensions.description: Default per-period amount — only meaningful when calculation_type = 'FixedAmount'; ignore it for percentage schemes or you will misquote the default.

dimensions.label: calculation type
dimensions.description: Selects which of standard_amount / percentage drives the contribution. Read this before quoting either figure.

dimensions.label: current record
dimensions.description: FALSE means retired configuration kept for history — filter TRUE for 'what schemes do we run today', keep FALSE rows to decode old payslip lines.

dimensions.label: subject to nic
dimensions.description: Whether the benefit value attracts National Insurance — changes the true employer cost of the scheme beyond the contribution itself.

dimensions.label: subject to pension
dimensions.description: Whether the amount counts into pensionable earnings for other pension calculations.

dimensions.label: subject to tax
dimensions.description: Whether the benefit is taxable on the employee; affects net-pay expectations, not employer cost.

dimensions.label: is calculating on qualifying earnings
dimensions.description: TRUE applies the percentage to the auto-enrolment qualifying-earnings band rather than full gross — the same percentage yields materially less contribution, so cost models must branch on this.

dimensions.label: show balance to employee
dimensions.description: Payslip presentation toggle; no analytical meaning.

dimensions.label: deduction id
dimensions.description: Xero's identifier for the deduction pay item; payslip deduction lines reference it.

dimensions.label: deduction name
dimensions.description: The org-configured label employees see on payslips ('AE Pension', 'Cycle to Work'...). Free text and org-specific: two orgs (or one org over time) can name the same kind of deduction differently, so never classify deductions by parsing this string — deduction_category is the reliable classifier; this column is for display and disambiguating multiple items within one category.

dimensions.label: deduction category
dimensions.description: The functional category. SalarySacrifice and StakeholderPension are pre-tax pension routes; StakeholderPensionPostTax is relief-at-source; StudentLoanDeductions/PostgraduateLoanDeductions are HMRC loans. Categorise payslip deduction lines through this, not by parsing names.

dimensions.label: liability account id
dimensions.description: GL account the withheld amount is owed from until paid over; join xero_accounts to reconcile payroll liabilities.

dimensions.label: current record
dimensions.description: FALSE = retired configuration. Filter TRUE for today's deduction menu; keep FALSE to decode historical payslips.

dimensions.label: standard amount
dimensions.description: Default per-period amount, meaningful only when calculation_type = 'FixedAmount'.

dimensions.label: reduces super liability
dimensions.description: Cross-region flag (super = AU pension terminology) exposed by the shared schema; not meaningful for UK deductions — ignore rather than interpret.

dimensions.label: reduces tax liability
dimensions.description: TRUE means the deduction comes out before tax — the employee's taxable pay shrinks. This flag is why gross pay minus visible deductions does not equal taxable pay.

dimensions.label: calculation type
dimensions.description: FixedAmount uses standard_amount; PercentageOfGross uses percentage. Read before quoting a default.

dimensions.label: percentage
dimensions.description: Percentage of gross for percentage-type deductions. A rate; never summed.

dimensions.label: subject to nic
dimensions.description: Whether the deducted amount remains inside NIC-able pay. FALSE on salary sacrifice is exactly where employer NIC savings come from.

dimensions.label: subject to tax
dimensions.description: Whether the deducted amount remains inside taxable pay; the companion to reduces_tax_liability for classifying pre- vs post-tax deductions.

dimensions.label: is reduced by basic rate
dimensions.description: TRUE for relief-at-source pensions: the employee pays the net-of-basic-rate amount and the provider reclaims the rest — the payslip deduction understates the gross contribution by 20%.

dimensions.label: apply to pension calculations
dimensions.description: Whether the deduction feeds into pensionable-pay calculations for other items.

dimensions.label: is calculating on qualifying earnings
dimensions.description: TRUE applies percentage deductions to the auto-enrolment qualifying-earnings band instead of full gross — same percentage, smaller base.

dimensions.label: is pension
dimensions.description: Marks the EMPLOYEE side of pension contributions (the employer side is xero_payroll_uk_benefits). Total pension cost questions must combine both tables, not pick one.

dimensions.label: id
dimensions.description: Xero's identifier for the earnings order pay item.

dimensions.label: name
dimensions.description: The org's label for this order item as it appears on payslips. Orgs routinely name these after the individual case or the issuing court, so the value can itself identify an employee's debt or child-support arrangement — treat it as sensitive when listing, and classify with statutory_deduction_category rather than by reading this string.

dimensions.label: statutory deduction category
dimensions.description: The legal category of the order. Only UK-relevant values (ChildSupport, CourtFines, Creditor, PriorityOrder, NonPriorityOrder, TableBased, StudentLoan variants...) occur in UK tenants; KiwiSaver/USChildSupport/MsdRepayments belong to other regions sharing this enum.

dimensions.label: liability account id
dimensions.description: GL account holding withheld order amounts until remitted to the court/agency; join xero_accounts.

dimensions.label: current record
dimensions.description: FALSE = retired configuration; filter TRUE for the active menu, keep FALSE to decode historical payslip lines.

dimensions.label: earnings rate id
dimensions.description: Xero's identifier for the earnings rate; referenced by payslip earnings lines, timesheet lines, pay templates and salary records.

dimensions.label: name
dimensions.description: Display name ('Regular Hours', 'Overtime 1.5x'...). Classify by earnings_type, not by parsing names.

dimensions.label: earnings type
dimensions.description: The semantic class of the earning, and the only reliable way to split gross pay into regular, premium and statutory components. The Statutory* family does not behave uniformly: family-related statutory pay (maternity, paternity, adoption, shared parental, bereavement, neonatal care) is largely recoverable from HMRC, and more than fully recoverable for small employers, so it costs the business far less than its gross; Statutory SICK Pay is NOT recoverable at all and costs the business every penny. Treating the whole Statutory* prefix as one recoverable bucket gets employer cost wrong in both directions. NonPensionable variants are the same payment excluded from pensionable earnings — they change the pension base, not the gross.

dimensions.label: rate type
dimensions.description: Gates the rate fields: RatePerUnit reads rate_per_unit, MultipleOfOrdinaryEarningsRate reads multiple_of_ordinary_earnings_rate (x the employee's ordinary rate), FixedAmount reads fixed_amount. The other two fields are noise for any given row.

dimensions.label: type of units
dimensions.description: What one unit means (typically Hours). Timesheet and payslip unit counts inherit this meaning — check it before converting units to hours.

dimensions.label: current record
dimensions.description: FALSE = retired rate kept for history. Filter TRUE for the active catalogue; retired rates still decode old payslips.

dimensions.label: expense account id
dimensions.description: GL account this earning's cost posts to; join xero_accounts to reconcile payroll expense lines in the P&L.

dimensions.label: rate per unit
dimensions.description: Default rate per unit — only when rate_type = 'RatePerUnit', and employees can override it. A rate; never summed.

dimensions.label: multiple of ordinary earnings rate
dimensions.description: Multiplier of the employee's ordinary rate (1.5 = time-and-a-half) — only when rate_type = 'MultipleOfOrdinaryEarningsRate'. The actual money rate differs per employee.

dimensions.label: fixed amount
dimensions.description: Default fixed amount — only when rate_type = 'FixedAmount'.

dimensions.label: employee id
dimensions.description: The employee the account belongs to. The BankAccount payload itself carries no employee reference, so the ingester stamps the fan-out path parameter onto each exploded row; equals xero_payroll_uk_employees.employee_id.

dimensions.label: ordinal
dimensions.description: Position in the bankAccounts array; the source exposes no account id, and order reflects the configured split order.

dimensions.label: employee id
dimensions.description: Parent employee; inherited from the record the contracts array was exploded from.

dimensions.label: ordinal
dimensions.description: Stable position in the employee's contracts array; part of the key because public_key is optional.

dimensions.label: public key
dimensions.description: Xero's contract identifier. May be absent on older records — hence the ordinal in the key.

dimensions.label: start date
dimensions.description: Contract start, locked once the employee has been paid. Use this for hire-date and tenure analysis; the employee row's start_date is a mutable snapshot.

dimensions.label: employment status
dimensions.description: Employee vs Worker is a UK employment-law distinction (workers lack unfair-dismissal and statutory-redundancy rights, and some statutory pay entitlements). Unspecified appears on older data — treat it as unknown, not Employee.

dimensions.label: contract type
dimensions.description: FullTime/PartTime/ZeroHour. Any FTE or average-hours metric must segment on this — averaging zero-hour staff into full-time averages produces a meaningless blended number.

dimensions.label: is fixed term
dimensions.description: TRUE for fixed-term contracts; pair with fixed_term_end_date for expiry-pipeline questions. Null/false means permanent.

dimensions.label: fixed term end date
dimensions.description: When a fixed-term contract expires. Only populated when is_fixed_term — a null here on a permanent contract is expected, not missing data.

dimensions.label: developmental role details start date
dimensions.description: Start of the developmental (apprenticeship) role window within this contract. Apprentices under 25 qualify for NI category H and apprentice National Minimum Wage rates only inside this window.

dimensions.label: developmental role details end date
dimensions.description: End of the developmental role window; after this date the person is an ordinary employee for wage-floor and NIC purposes even if the contract continues.

dimensions.label: developmental role details developmental role
dimensions.description: The role type; the spec supports only 'Apprentice' today, so treat any non-null value as an apprenticeship flag.

dimensions.label: developmental role details public key
dimensions.description: Xero's identifier for the developmental-role sub-record; only needed to correlate edits, never an analysis key.

dimensions.label: leave id
dimensions.description: Xero's identifier for the leave request and the row key.

dimensions.label: employee id
dimensions.description: The employee on leave; inherited from the fan-out path parameter.

dimensions.label: leave type id
dimensions.description: Which leave type this request draws on. Join xero_payroll_uk_leave_types for the name and the is_paid_leave flag — unpaid leave in a paid-absence total silently inflates cost estimates.

dimensions.label: start date
dimensions.description: First calendar day of the leave. Calendar span (end - start) is NOT time off — weekends and non-working days sit inside it; use period units for quantity.

dimensions.label: end date
dimensions.description: Last calendar day of the leave (inclusive). Future-dated rows are approved bookings, not absence that has happened yet.

dimensions.label: updated date utc
dimensions.description: Audit stamp of the last change; sync watermark, not the request date.

dimensions.label: periods
dimensions.description: The leave period information. The StartDate, EndDate and NumberOfUnits needs to be specified when you do not want to calculate NumberOfUnits automatically. Using incorrect period StartDate and EndDate will result in automatic computation of the NumberOfUnits. Retained verbatim as the raw array Xero returned: the declared element order is part of the document and is lost by flattening. Fully normalised into xero_payroll_uk_employee_leave_periods (one row per element) — join there for anything you filter or aggregate on, and read this column only when the original ordering or an unflattened payload matters.

dimensions.label: employee id
dimensions.description: The employee holding the balance; inherited from the fan-out path parameter.

dimensions.label: leave type id
dimensions.description: The leave type the balance belongs to; join xero_payroll_uk_leave_types for paid/statutory flags.

dimensions.label: name
dimensions.description: Denormalized leave-type name carried on the balance row; convenient for display but the join on leave_type_id is authoritative if they ever disagree.

dimensions.label: type of units
dimensions.description: Unit of measure for balance (typically Hours). Group or filter by it before any cross-employee aggregation — 'total balance' across mixed units means nothing.

dimensions.label: leave id
dimensions.description: The leave request this slice belongs to; inherited from the parent record.

dimensions.label: ordinal
dimensions.description: Stable position of the slice within the request's periods array; the source has no period id.

dimensions.label: period start date
dimensions.description: Start of the PAY period the slice falls in — payroll-calendar aligned, not month aligned. Use it (or period_end_date) as the time axis for leave-taken trends.

dimensions.label: period end date
dimensions.description: End of the pay period this slice was deducted in. Pair it with period_start_date to attribute the units to a payroll period, not to the days actually taken: the leave request's own start_date/end_date can sit anywhere inside or across these boundaries, so a slice dated to a period does not mean the absence happened evenly across it.

dimensions.label: period status
dimensions.description: Approved = scheduled/approved but not yet run through payroll; Completed = processed in a finalised pay run. 'Leave actually taken and paid' filters Completed; forward-looking liability includes Approved.

dimensions.label: employee id
dimensions.description: The enrolled employee; inherited from the fan-out path parameter.

dimensions.label: leave type id
