dimensions.description: The org leave type this enrolment configures; join xero_payroll_uk_leave_types for its name.

dimensions.label: schedule of accrual
dimensions.description: When entitlement is granted. Annual-upfront schedules (BeginningOfCalendarYear, OnAnniversaryDate) make mid-year balances look generous; EachPayPeriod and OnHourWorked accrue gradually. Compare balances only within the same schedule.

dimensions.label: maximum to accrue
dimensions.description: Cap on the accruable balance; null means uncapped. Relevant when projecting future balances.

dimensions.label: opening balance
dimensions.description: Hours granted when the type was first assigned to the employee — a setup constant, not the current balance (that is the balances table).

dimensions.label: rate accrued hourly
dimensions.description: Hours of leave earned per hour worked; normally 0 except under OnHourWorked (the 12.07% holiday-accrual pattern for casual staff appears here as ~0.1207).

dimensions.label: schedule of accrual date
dimensions.description: The anniversary date entitlement lands on; only populated when schedule_of_accrual is OnAnniversaryDate.

dimensions.label: employee id
dimensions.description: Parent employee; inherited from the record the array was exploded from.

dimensions.label: ordinal
dimensions.description: Stable position of this assignment in the employee's niCategories array; part of the key because niCategoryID is optional in the payload.

dimensions.label: ni category id
dimensions.description: Xero's identifier for the NI category assignment. Numeric (not a uuid) and optional — prefer (employee_id, ordinal) for row identity.

dimensions.label: start date
dimensions.description: When this category letter takes effect. The employee's CURRENT category is the row with MAX(start_date) not after today; historical NIC recalculations need the letter effective on the pay period's payment date.

dimensions.label: ni category
dimensions.description: The NI category letter. This single letter sets both employer and employee NIC rates: X means no NICs at all (e.g. under 16), C exempts the employee but not the employer, V/F/I/L/S/N/E/K/D carry employer reliefs. Costing 'employer NIC at 15%' uniformly across letters is wrong.

dimensions.label: date first employed as civilian
dimensions.description: Only meaningful for veteran relief (category V): the 12-month employer-NIC holiday runs from this date, not from start_date. Null for non-veterans.

dimensions.label: workplace postcode
dimensions.description: The WORKPLACE postcode that qualifies Freeport/Investment Zone category letters — not the employee's home postcode (that is on the employee row). Required by HMRC for F/I/L/S and N/E/K/D letters.

dimensions.label: employee id
dimensions.description: The employee the opening balances belong to; inherited from the fan-out path parameter.

dimensions.label: prior employee number
dimensions.description: The staff number issued by the employee's former employer (or former payroll system). A matching hint for imported HR data, never an analysis key — it is not unique in Xero.

dimensions.label: pay template earning id
dimensions.description: Xero's identifier for the standing earnings line and the row key.

dimensions.label: employee id
dimensions.description: The employee whose template this line belongs to — carried on the template record itself.

dimensions.label: earnings rate id
dimensions.description: Which org earnings rate the line applies; join xero_payroll_uk_earnings_rates for its name, type and unit semantics.

dimensions.label: rate per unit
dimensions.description: Employee-specific override of the rate per unit; null falls back to the earnings rate's default or the salary basis. A rate, never summable.

dimensions.label: number of units
dimensions.description: Default units seeded per pay run. The spec mislabels this field's description as 'the rate per unit' — it is the unit count; expected amount is number_of_units x rate_per_unit (or fixed_amount).

dimensions.label: fixed amount
dimensions.description: Fixed amount seeded per period for fixed-amount earnings; mutually exclusive in practice with rate x units. Still a template figure, not money paid.

dimensions.label: name
dimensions.description: Read-only display name of the earnings line, denormalized from the earnings rate; the join on earnings_rate_id is authoritative.

dimensions.label: employee id
dimensions.description: The employee this payment configuration belongs to; inherited from the fan-out path parameter.

dimensions.label: payment method
dimensions.description: Electronically means Xero generates bank-file lines from the child bank accounts; Cheque and Manual employees are paid outside the file. A payment-run reconciliation that assumes everyone is electronic misses them.

dimensions.label: bank accounts
dimensions.description: Retained verbatim as the raw array Xero returned: the declared element order is part of the document and is lost by flattening. Fully normalised into xero_payroll_uk_employee_bank_accounts (one row per element) — join there for anything you filter or aggregate on, and read this column only when the original ordering or an unflattened payload matters.

dimensions.label: salary and wages id
dimensions.description: Xero's identifier for this pay-basis record and the row key.

dimensions.label: employee id
dimensions.description: The employee the pay basis belongs to; inherited from the fan-out path parameter.

dimensions.label: earnings rate id
dimensions.description: The ordinary earnings rate the basis pays through — also the base rate that MultipleOfOrdinaryEarningsRate overtime rates multiply.

dimensions.label: number of units per day
dimensions.description: Contracted units per day; used for daily-rate pro-rating of starters, leavers and unpaid leave.

dimensions.label: effective from
dimensions.description: The date this basis takes effect. Point-in-time salary questions pick the record where effective_from <= the date, preferring Active/History over Pending.

dimensions.label: status
dimensions.description: Active is the one live basis per employee; Pending is future-dated; History is superseded. Every current-pay aggregate filters Active — including History double-counts, including Pending books unstarted raises.

dimensions.label: payment type
dimensions.description: Salary (fixed per period) vs Hourly (earnings follow hours). Segment cost analyses on this: hourly annual figures are projections while salaried ones are commitments.

dimensions.label: employee id
dimensions.description: The employee whose statutory balance this is; inherited from the fan-out path parameter.

dimensions.label: leave type
dimensions.description: Which statutory entitlement the balance measures. Each type has its own statutory cap (28 weeks SSP, 39 paid weeks SMP...), so compare balances within a type only.

dimensions.label: as of date
dimensions.description: The date the balance was calculated for, stamped from the request. Without it the row is undated and every 'remaining entitlement' answer silently claims to be current: a balance computed six months ago against an ongoing sickness absence is stale by construction, not by sync lag. Part of the key so a backfill that asks about several dates does not overwrite itself. Always report it alongside balance_remaining.

dimensions.label: units
dimensions.description: Always Hours per the spec — kept so unit-checking logic can be uniform across all balance tables.

dimensions.label: employee id
dimensions.description: The employee this tax record belongs to; inherited from the fan-out path parameter (the payload itself carries no id).

dimensions.label: starter type
dimensions.description: How the employee joined for PAYE purposes (e.g. P45 vs starter checklist). Explains why previous_taxable_pay is or is not populated.

dimensions.label: starter declaration
dimensions.description: The HMRC starter statement (A: first job this year, B: only job now, C: has another job/pension). C-declaration employees are commonly on BR/0T codes — a cluster of them is a second-jobs population, not a payroll error.

dimensions.label: tax code
dimensions.description: The current PAYE code (1257L, BR, 0T, K497...). K-prefixed codes ADD notional pay rather than granting allowance, so 'allowance = code x 10' arithmetic is wrong for them. This is today's code — not necessarily the code any historical payslip used.

dimensions.label: w1 m1
dimensions.description: TRUE means the code operates non-cumulatively (week 1/month 1): each period is taxed in isolation and YTD tax will not reconcile to the cumulative code-implied amount. Any 'expected tax vs actual' check must branch on this flag.

dimensions.label: previous tax paid
dimensions.description: Tax already paid in the prior employment this tax year (P45 figure); the companion to previous_taxable_pay for cumulative-code calculations.

dimensions.label: student loan deduction
dimensions.description: Which student loan plan is being deducted (Plan 1, 2, 4 and 5 style values); null/empty means no student loan is operating. Each plan has its own repayment threshold and rate, so counting 'has a loan' is safe while comparing or averaging deduction amounts across plans is not. Postgraduate loans are a separate, stacking deduction — see has_post_graduate_loans, not this field.

dimensions.label: has post graduate loans
dimensions.description: TRUE when a postgraduate loan is deducted IN ADDITION to any student loan plan — the two stack, they are not alternatives.

dimensions.label: is director
dimensions.description: TRUE for company directors, whose NICs are computed on an annual (or annualised) earnings period. Directors' per-period NIC looks 'wrong' next to regular employees by design — segment them out of NIC-rate sanity checks.

dimensions.label: directorship start date
dimensions.description: When the directorship began; pro-rates the annual NIC earnings period in the first year.

dimensions.label: nic calculation method
dimensions.description: For directors: annual vs alternative (per-period with annual true-up) NIC method. Explains large final-period NIC catch-ups under the alternative method.

dimensions.label: employee id
dimensions.description: Xero's immutable identifier for the employee and the join key for every other table in this domain, including the sibling pay-run/payslip domain.

dimensions.label: start date
dimensions.description: Employment start date as of the moment the record was fetched. For point-in-time headcount or tenure use this, but for re-hires and contract changes trust xero_payroll_uk_employee_contracts — this field is a snapshot, not a history.

dimensions.label: end date
dimensions.description: Employment end date; NULL means currently employed. Every 'current headcount' or 'active staff' filter is end_date IS NULL (optionally AND start_date <= CURRENT_DATE) — forgetting it counts every leaver ever paid.

dimensions.label: payroll calendar id
dimensions.description: The pay-run calendar this employee is paid on. Join to xero_payroll_uk_pay_run_calendars to split the workforce into weekly vs monthly payroll populations before comparing pay-period figures.

dimensions.label: updated date utc
dimensions.description: Audit stamp of the last change; the incremental-sync watermark, not a business event date.

dimensions.label: created date utc
dimensions.description: When the record was created IN XERO — for migrated orgs this is the migration date, not the hire date. Never use it for tenure; use start_date/contracts.

dimensions.label: is off payroll worker
dimensions.description: TRUE marks an IR35 off-payroll worker (deemed employee paid via an intermediary). They sit in this table and get payslips, but they are not employees for headcount, pension auto-enrolment or statutory-leave purposes — most workforce metrics should exclude them explicitly.

dimensions.label: ni categories
dimensions.description: The employee's NI categories Retained verbatim as the raw array Xero returned: the declared element order is part of the document and is lost by flattening. Fully normalised into xero_payroll_uk_employee_ni_categories (one row per element) — join there for anything you filter or aggregate on, and read this column only when the original ordering or an unflattened payload matters.

dimensions.label: contracts
dimensions.description: The employee's contracts Retained verbatim as the raw array Xero returned: the declared element order is part of the document and is lost by flattening. Fully normalised into xero_payroll_uk_employee_contracts (one row per element) — join there for anything you filter or aggregate on, and read this column only when the original ordering or an unflattened payload matters.

dimensions.label: earning templates
dimensions.description: Retained verbatim as the raw array Xero returned: the declared element order is part of the document and is lost by flattening. Fully normalised into xero_payroll_uk_employee_pay_template_earnings (one row per element) — join there for anything you filter or aggregate on, and read this column only when the original ordering or an unflattened payload matters.

dimensions.label: leave type id
dimensions.description: Xero's identifier for the leave type — the key every leave table joins on.

dimensions.label: leave id
dimensions.description: A secondary Xero identifier ('for the leave') that shadows leave_type_id in some payloads; keep for lineage, join on leave_type_id.

dimensions.label: name
dimensions.description: Display name ('Holiday', 'Sickness'...). Org-defined and not standardised across tenants — never string-match names to classify; use the flags.

dimensions.label: is paid leave
dimensions.description: Whether taking this leave pays the employee. The gate for costing absence: unpaid leave has zero direct wage cost, and paid-absence liability should filter TRUE.

dimensions.label: show on payslip
dimensions.description: Payslip presentation toggle for the balance; no cost meaning.

dimensions.label: updated date utc
dimensions.description: UTC audit stamp of the last edit to the leave-type definition and the incremental-sync watermark for this catalogue. It changes on configuration edits (rename, retirement), not when anyone takes leave — leave activity dates live on requests and periods.

dimensions.label: is active
dimensions.description: FALSE = retired type. The list op's ActiveOnly parameter can hide these at source — the ingester requests all; analysts filter here.

dimensions.label: is statutory leave
dimensions.description: TRUE marks Xero-managed statutory types (sick, maternity...). Requests against them flow through the statutory leave tables, not ordinary employee leave — a hint for which family answers the question.

dimensions.label: payroll calendar id
dimensions.description: Xero's identifier for the calendar; employees, timesheets and pay runs reference it.

dimensions.label: name
dimensions.description: The org's label for this pay schedule ('Monthly Salaries', 'Weekly Wages'...). Useful for presenting a calendar to a human, but never for inferring frequency — a calendar named 'Monthly' can be configured Fortnightly. calendar_type is the only trustworthy frequency; an org can also run several calendars of the same type (separate sites or entities), so names are not unique either.

dimensions.label: calendar type
dimensions.description: Pay frequency. Comparing per-period figures across calendars of different types compares a week of pay to a month of pay — normalise to annual or monthly first.

dimensions.label: period start date
dimensions.description: Start of the CURRENT (next unposted) period at sync time; rolls forward with each pay run. Not the calendar's inception date.

dimensions.label: period end date
dimensions.description: End of the current period at sync time; rolls forward like period_start_date.

dimensions.label: payment date
dimensions.description: When the current period pays out — the payday. For 'when is the next payroll' questions, this is the answer, freshness permitting.

dimensions.label: updated date utc
dimensions.description: UTC audit stamp of the last change to the calendar record and this table's incremental-sync watermark. Because the period dates roll forward each time a pay run posts, this timestamp moves with routine payroll activity — a recent value means the schedule is in use, not that anyone redesigned it. Never present it as a business event date; paydays come from payment_date.

dimensions.label: pay run id
dimensions.description: Xero's immutable pay run identifier and the row key; the fan-out handle for fetching this run's payslips.

dimensions.label: payroll calendar id
dimensions.description: The pay frequency calendar this run was processed under. Orgs commonly run several calendars at once (weekly wages plus monthly salaries), so 'the March payroll' is usually two or more runs — group by this id before comparing periods. This domain's ground truth contains no PayRunCalendar object, so there is no calendar dimension here and calendar_type carries the frequency inline; the id stays a stable join key if a payroll-config domain later lands one.

dimensions.label: period start date
dimensions.description: First day of the earnings period this run pays for. Use the period dates for accrual-style cost attribution (which month the work happened), not for when cash left the bank — that is payment_date.

dimensions.label: period end date
dimensions.description: Last day of the earnings period. periodStart/End come from the payroll calendar and can be identical across a Scheduled and an Unscheduled run — they are not a key.

dimensions.label: payment date
dimensions.description: The date employees are paid — the date that decides which UK tax period the run falls into for PAYE/RTI purposes. Cash-basis payroll cost and tax-year reporting bucket by this date, not by the period dates; mixing the two shifts runs across month and tax-year boundaries.

dimensions.label: pay run status
dimensions.description: Draft runs are work-in-progress: totals move, payslips get added and removed, nothing has been paid or reported to HMRC. Every financial aggregate must filter payRunStatus = 'Posted' or draft noise contaminates real history.

dimensions.label: pay run type
dimensions.description: Scheduled is the regular calendar run; Unscheduled is an off-cycle run (corrections, bonuses, leavers) that shares the same period; EarlierYearUpdate is an HMRC correction to a prior tax year. Period-cost questions include Scheduled + Unscheduled and EXCLUDE EarlierYearUpdate — EYU amounts belong to the year they amend, not the year they were posted.

dimensions.label: calendar type
dimensions.description: Pay frequency of the underlying calendar, and the reason run-level totals are not comparable row to row: a Weekly run covers roughly a quarter of what a Monthly one does (52 weeks against 12 months — not exactly four weeks per month, which is why 'weekly x4' reconciliations drift). Annualize with the factor for the VALUE, not for its position in the enum: Weekly x52, Fortnightly x26, FourWeekly x13, Monthly x12, Quarterly x4, Annual x1. An 'average pay per run' computed across mixed frequencies is a number about nothing.

dimensions.label: posted date time
dimensions.description: When the run was posted (finalized). Null/absent for Draft runs. This is an audit stamp — the business date for reporting is payment_date; the two can straddle a month end.

dimensions.label: pay slip id
dimensions.description: Parent payslip key, inherited at explode time, and the reconciliation handle: lines under one payslip_id sum to that slip's total_benefits. Benefit lines carry no employee or date, so this is also the only path to who received the benefit and in which run.

dimensions.label: benefit lines
dimensions.description: Zero-based position in the payslip's benefitLines array — the row's provenance and, with payslip_id, its key (no natural line id exists).

dimensions.label: benefit type id
dimensions.description: The configured benefit type — the stable classifier that decides what a benefit line actually means, and therefore whether its amount is employer spend or only a taxable value being payrolled. This domain's ground truth contains no BenefitType object, so nothing here names the type: pair with display_name for readability, group by this id for stability, and get the org to confirm the mapping before any of it feeds a cost number.

dimensions.label: display name
dimensions.description: Benefit name as shown on the slip ('NEST Pension', 'Private Medical'). Org-controlled free text, and the only human-readable classifier this domain carries, so pattern-matching it is the usual first pass at finding pension lines — but it is a heuristic, not a taxonomy: a scheme named after its provider will not match '%pension%', and a renamed benefit silently changes which rows a saved query returns. Confirm any name-matched set against the distinct benefit_type_id values it covers before publishing the number.

dimensions.label: fixed amount
dimensions.description: The configured flat amount for fixed benefits; an input echoed from setup, already reflected in amount. Never add the two.

dimensions.label: percentage
dimensions.description: The configured rate for percentage benefits (e.g. 3% employer pension); a rate, never summed — amount carries the resulting money.

dimensions.label: pay slip id
dimensions.description: Parent payslip key, inherited at explode time. It identifies whose pay was attached and in which run — court order lines carry neither — which is exactly why joining out through it turns an aggregate into named personal data; do that deliberately, not by habit.

dimensions.label: court order lines
dimensions.description: Zero-based position in the payslip's courtOrderLines array — the row's provenance and, with payslip_id, its key (no natural line id exists).

dimensions.label: court order type id
dimensions.description: The configured court order type — the distinction between an attachment of earnings order, a child-maintenance deduction order and a council tax attachment, which differ in priority and in who receives the money. This domain's ground truth contains no CourtOrderType object, so the raw id is the only classifier: without carrying it, every order collapses into one undifferentiated bucket.

dimensions.label: pay slip id
dimensions.description: Parent payslip key, inherited at explode time. Deduction lines carry no employee and no date, so this id is how a deduction gets attributed to a person and a pay period — and how it reaches the Posted filter that separates enforced deductions from draft ones.

dimensions.label: deduction lines
dimensions.description: Zero-based position in the payslip's deductionLines array — the row's provenance and, with payslip_id, its key (deduction lines carry no natural id).

dimensions.label: deduction type id
dimensions.description: The configured deduction type applied. This domain's ground truth contains no DeductionType object and this family carries no display name, so the raw id is the only thing separating a pension contribution from union fees or a season-ticket loan — drop it from a breakdown and every deduction collapses into one unreadable bucket. Resolving these ids to names requires the payroll-config domain.

dimensions.label: subject to tax
dimensions.description: Whether the deducted amount is still subject to tax, per the spec — in practice the pre-tax versus post-tax split of the deduction. It matters because deductions taken before tax shrink the pay that tax is calculated on, so an employee sacrificing salary looks like a lower earner on gross-based comparisons while their employer's cost is unchanged. Beware nulls: on a three-way FILTER split, rows where the flag is unset fall into neither bucket and silently vanish from the total.

dimensions.label: percentage
dimensions.description: The configured rate for percentage-based deductions (e.g. 5% employee pension); null for flat deductions. A rate, never summed — the resulting money is amount.

dimensions.label: pay slip id
dimensions.description: Parent payslip key, inherited at explode time, and the only way out of this table: an earnings line carries no employee, no date and no status of its own, so every filter that decides whether a number is real (Posted, payment_date, employee) arrives through this id.

dimensions.label: earnings lines
dimensions.description: Zero-based position of this row in the payslip's earningsLines array — the provenance of this table's rows. Forms the key with payslip_id because the spec does not guarantee earningsLineID is present; also preserves Xero's display order.

dimensions.label: earnings line id
dimensions.description: Xero's own id for this earnings line, and the only line family in this domain that has one. Use it to tell a genuinely amended line from a reordered one when a Draft run is re-scanned — line_index shifts when lines are inserted, this does not. It is deliberately not the key: the spec marks it optional, so it can be absent and cannot be relied on to be unique across a null-heavy load.

dimensions.label: earnings rate id
dimensions.description: The configured earnings rate (pay item) applied — salary, overtime, bonus and so on. This domain's ground truth contains no EarningsRate object, so there is no rate dimension to join here and display_name is the only human handle; group by this id whenever the org has renamed pay items, because names are edited in place and rewrite history in any name-keyed breakdown.

dimensions.label: display name
dimensions.description: The earnings rate's name as shown on the payslip ('Regular Hours', 'Bonus', ...). Free text controlled by the org — filtering on it ('Overtime') works only as well as the org's naming discipline; earnings_rate_id is the stable key.

dimensions.label: number of units
dimensions.description: Units paid on this line. Units are whatever the earnings rate defines (hours, days) — summing units across lines with different rate definitions mixes hours with days.

dimensions.label: fixed amount
dimensions.description: The set amount for lines whose earnings rate is Fixed type (e.g. a flat bonus); null otherwise. Do not add it to amount — amount already equals it for fixed lines.

dimensions.label: is linked to timesheet
dimensions.description: Spec-declared false in this family: timesheet-sourced pay is materialized separately in xero_payroll_uk_payslip_timesheet_earnings_lines. A true here is vendor drift — trust the family (table) membership over the flag.

dimensions.label: is average daily pay rate
dimensions.description: True when the line was priced from an average daily pay rate rather than a directly configured rate. It is the warning label on rate_per_unit: on these rows the rate is a computed average over prior pay, so reading it as the employee's contracted rate — or benchmarking rates across employees without excluding them — compares a derived figure with a real one.

dimensions.label: pay slip id
dimensions.description: Parent payslip key, inherited at explode time. Tax lines have no date, so the HMRC tax period a withholding belongs to comes from the parent run's payment_date two joins away — bucketing employee tax by anything else misfiles it across month and tax-year boundaries.

dimensions.label: employee tax lines
dimensions.description: Zero-based position in the payslip's employeeTaxLines array — the row's provenance and, with payslip_id, its key (taxLineID is not spec-required).

dimensions.label: tax line id
dimensions.description: Xero's own id for this tax line, present when supplied. Deliberately not the key — the spec marks it optional, so it cannot be relied on to identify every row — but it is what distinguishes a genuinely amended tax component from a reordered one when a run is re-scanned and line_index shifts underneath it.

dimensions.label: description
dimensions.description: Human label of the tax component ('PAYE', 'Employee NIC'). The practical way to split income tax from National Insurance — but it is display text; use global_tax_type_id when exact typing matters.

dimensions.label: is employer tax
dimensions.description: True when the employer pays this tax. Expected false throughout this table — collection membership (employeeTaxLines) is the authoritative payer signal; a true here is drift to investigate, not a row to silently reclassify.

dimensions.label: global tax type id
dimensions.description: Xero's tax type code for this component — the stable classifier behind the display description; group by it for typing that survives label edits.

dimensions.label: manual adjustment
dimensions.description: True when a payroll admin overrode the calculated tax. Flag these when auditing effective tax rates — they are corrections, and outliers usually trace here.

dimensions.label: pay slip id
dimensions.description: Parent payslip key, inherited at explode time — the only route to employee, run status and payment date, none of which an employer tax line carries. It is also what attributes an on-cost to a head: employer NI per employee only exists by grouping these lines through the slip.

dimensions.label: employer tax lines
dimensions.description: Zero-based position in the payslip's employerTaxLines array — the row's provenance and, with payslip_id, its key (taxLineID is not spec-required).

dimensions.label: tax line id
dimensions.description: Xero's own id for this tax line, present when supplied. Deliberately not the key — the spec marks it optional, so it cannot be relied on to identify every row — but it is what distinguishes a genuinely amended tax component from a reordered one when a run is re-scanned and line_index shifts underneath it.

dimensions.label: description
dimensions.description: Component label ('Employer NIC', 'Apprenticeship Levy'). Display text — the readable splitter of employer NI from levy; use global_tax_type_id for stable typing.

dimensions.label: is employer tax
dimensions.description: Expected true throughout this table; the employerTaxLines array membership is authoritative. A false here is drift to investigate, not grounds to move the row.

dimensions.label: global tax type id
dimensions.description: Xero's tax type code for this component — group by it rather than the editable description when typing matters.

dimensions.label: manual adjustment
dimensions.description: True when the calculated employer tax was overridden by an admin — the first place to look when employer NI ratios spike or dip for one slip.

dimensions.label: pay slip id
dimensions.description: Parent payslip key, inherited at explode time. An accrual row has no date of its own: what puts entitlement in a period is the parent run's payment_date, two joins away, so accrual-over-time series are only as correct as this join.

dimensions.label: leave accrual lines
dimensions.description: Zero-based position in the payslip's leaveAccrualLines array — the row's provenance and, with payslip_id, its key (no natural line id exists).

dimensions.label: leave type id
dimensions.description: The leave type the entitlement accrued under. This domain's ground truth contains no LeaveType object, so the id is the only classifier available here and it is load-bearing twice over: it separates annual leave from sick or parental schemes, and it is the boundary within which number_of_units is comparable, since different leave types are measured in different units.

dimensions.label: pay slip id
dimensions.description: Parent payslip key, inherited at explode time. Leave earnings lines are dateless — the leave was paid in the parent run, so 'when did this leave cost us' is the run's payment_date reached through this id, never a leave-taken date (there isn't one here).

dimensions.label: leave earnings lines
dimensions.description: Zero-based position in the payslip's leaveEarningsLines array — the row's provenance and, with payslip_id, its key (leave earnings lines carry no natural id).

dimensions.label: earnings rate id
dimensions.description: The leave-linked earnings rate that priced this leave — which is also all you get: unlike the regular earnings family, this one carries no displayName, so there is no readable label for what kind of leave was paid. Note this is a rate id, not a leave type id: it does not join to the accrual table's leave_type_id, so 'holiday pay versus sick pay' cannot be answered from this column alone without the org's rate configuration.

dimensions.label: number of units
dimensions.description: Units of leave paid on this line, in whatever unit the rate defines (hours or days). The paid-leave-volume measure — but confirm the unit before summing across rates.

dimensions.label: fixed amount
dimensions.description: Set amount when the underlying earnings rate is Fixed type; null otherwise. Already reflected in amount — never add the two.

dimensions.label: is linked to timesheet
dimensions.description: Spec-declared false for leave earnings lines; family membership is the authoritative signal. Treat a true as vendor drift, not a reclassification.

dimensions.label: pay slip id
dimensions.description: Parent payslip key, inherited at explode time, and the grain you must collapse to before comparing anything with the payslip: the lines under one payslip_id are the split of a single net payment, so they sum to that slip's total_pay rather than each matching it.

dimensions.label: payment lines
dimensions.description: Zero-based position in the payslip's paymentLines array — the row's provenance and, with payslip_id, its key (paymentLineID is not spec-required).

dimensions.label: payment line id
dimensions.description: Xero's own id for this payment line, present when supplied. Not the key (the spec marks it optional), but it is the stable handle on a specific bank destination: when an employee changes the split of their net pay, this id is how you tell an edited routing instruction from a newly added one.

dimensions.label: pay slip id
dimensions.description: Parent payslip key, inherited at explode time, and the reconciliation handle: the lines sharing one payslip_id sum to that slip's total_reimbursements. Also the only route to employee and payment date, which this family does not carry.

dimensions.label: reimbursement lines
dimensions.description: Zero-based position in the payslip's reimbursementLines array — the row's provenance and, with payslip_id, its key (no natural line id exists).

dimensions.label: reimbursement type id
dimensions.description: The configured reimbursement type — mileage, subsistence, equipment and so on as the org set them up. This domain's ground truth contains no ReimbursementType object, so nothing here resolves the id to a name, but it is still the only stable classifier: group by it and label from description, never the reverse, because per-line descriptions are typed fresh each run.

dimensions.label: description
dimensions.description: Free-text note entered per line ('Mileage March', 'Laptop charger'). Human context only; it is not normalized and the same expense category is spelled a dozen ways.

dimensions.label: pay slip id
dimensions.description: Parent payslip key, inherited at explode time. The hours on this row belong to whatever period the parent run paid, so this id is the only route to a date at all — and to the Posted filter that decides whether the hours were actually paid.

dimensions.label: timesheet earnings lines
dimensions.description: Zero-based position in the payslip's timesheetEarningsLines array — the row's provenance and, with payslip_id, its key (no natural line id exists).

dimensions.label: earnings rate id
dimensions.description: The earnings rate pricing these timesheet hours. Same rate ids as the other earnings families — usable to compare timesheet vs regular pay for the same rate.

dimensions.label: fixed amount
dimensions.description: Set amount for Fixed-type rates; null otherwise and already reflected in amount.

dimensions.label: is linked to timesheet
dimensions.description: Do not filter on this. The spec documents it here with the leave family's sentence ('False for leave earnings line'), which is plainly a copy-paste into the timesheet object, so neither true nor false can be trusted as a classification. Membership of the timesheetEarningsLines array — that is, being a row in this table — is what makes pay timesheet-sourced; the column is carried for fidelity only.

dimensions.label: pay slip id
dimensions.description: Xero's immutable payslip identifier and the row key; every line-family child table hangs off it. Named payslip_id (matching the PayslipID path parameter) rather than pay_slip_id — joiners take note.

dimensions.label: employee id
dimensions.description: The employee this slip pays — the only reliable identity key. Join to xero_payroll_uk_employees for demographics; never group by the embedded first/last name, which is a point-in-time snapshot and collides across namesakes.

dimensions.label: pay run id
dimensions.description: The containing run. Join it on every aggregate: it is the only route to pay_run_status (Draft vs Posted), pay_run_type (to exclude EarlierYearUpdate) and payment_date (the tax-period business date).

dimensions.label: last edited
dimensions.description: When this payslip last changed. GET /Payslips accepts only page and PayRunID — there is no modified-since filter and no If-Modified-Since contract — so this is a client-side change detector, not a server-side incremental filter: rows still have to be fetched before the watermark can be compared. Slips on Draft runs move constantly; a fresh value on a slip whose run is already Posted means a post-posting correction, and its eleven line families must be re-exploded.

dimensions.label: bacs hash
dimensions.description: Documented by the spec as the BACS Service User Number despite the field being named 'hash' — treat it as an opaque employer-level banking identifier either way, useful only for tying slips back to a submitted BACS file. It identifies the employer's service user, not the employee, so it is not a per-person attribute and never a grouping key for people.

dimensions.label: payment method
dimensions.description: How the net pay leaves the business. Only Electronically slips are expected to reconcile against paymentLines bank splits; Cheque and Manual slips settle outside the BACS file, so 'net pay vs bank file' checks must scope to Electronically.

dimensions.label: reimbursement id
dimensions.description: Xero's identifier for the reimbursement pay item; payslip reimbursement lines reference it.

dimensions.label: name
dimensions.description: The label the org gave this reimbursement item, as it appears on payslips ('Mileage', 'Expenses'...). Org-defined free text with no standard vocabulary, so it disambiguates items within a tenant but never classifies across tenants — there is no category field on Reimbursement, so if a question needs 'mileage vs everything else' the only honest handles are this name and the GL account it posts to.

dimensions.label: account id
dimensions.description: GL account the reimbursement posts to; join xero_accounts — usually an expense account, which is how these amounts reach the P&L without touching wages.

dimensions.label: current record
dimensions.description: FALSE = retired item; filter TRUE for the active menu, keep FALSE rows to decode history.

dimensions.label: account id
dimensions.description: The GL account's identifier — the same AccountID as xero_accounts, which is the whole point: it links payroll roles to ledger accounts. (The spec's docstring calls it 'the identifier for Settings'; it is the account id.) Deliberately NOT the row key: nothing stops an org pointing two payroll roles at one GL account, so this value repeats and COUNT(DISTINCT account_id) undercounts the mapping.

dimensions.label: type
dimensions.description: The payroll ROLE this account plays and the true row key — the settings payload carries at most one entry per role. WAGESEXPENSE is where gross pay hits the P&L, WAGESPAYABLE/PAYELIABILITY/NICLIABILITY are balance-sheet liabilities, BANK is the paying account, EMPLOYERSNIC the employer NIC expense, PAYEECONTRIBUTION employee contributions. Not the accounting AccountType — do not confuse with xero_accounts.type.

dimensions.label: code
dimensions.description: The GL account's short code (text — codes can have leading zeros); matches xero_accounts.code.

dimensions.label: name
dimensions.description: The GL account's display name, denormalized from the chart of accounts.

dimensions.label: statutory leave id
dimensions.description: Xero's identifier for the statutory leave episode; also the fan-out key into the SSP detail table for Sick episodes.

dimensions.label: employee id
dimensions.description: The employee on statutory leave — carried on the record itself here, unlike most fan-out payloads.

dimensions.label: start date
dimensions.description: First day of the statutory leave episode, and the only date on this row that never moves — it is what 'maternity leave started in Q2' must be measured on. Do not use it as the first PAID day: entitlement and payment windows start on their own rules per type (SSP waiting days, the maternity pay period), which is why cost questions resolve on payslip statutory earnings lines rather than on this span.

dimensions.label: end date
dimensions.description: Last day of the episode; for In-Progress episodes this is the planned end, which can move.

dimensions.label: is entitled
dimensions.description: Whether the episode qualified for statutory PAYMENT. FALSE episodes are still absence — excluding them from absence analysis is wrong, but including them in statutory-pay cost is equally wrong.

dimensions.label: status
dimensions.description: Episode lifecycle. Pending has not started paying, In-Progress is live, Completed is history. 'Currently on maternity leave' = type filter + status = 'In-Progress'.

dimensions.label: statutory leave id
dimensions.description: The SSP episode identifier; equals the summaries row's key, making the join one-to-one.

dimensions.label: employee id
dimensions.description: The employee on sick leave; join xero_payroll_uk_employees for the name and current-employment status. Episodes survive termination, so a per-employee SSP history includes leavers — filter through the employee row's end_date when the question means current staff. Also the grouping key for the shared-entitlement rule: linked episodes of the SAME employee share one 28-week SSP entitlement.

dimensions.label: leave type id
dimensions.description: Points at the 'Statutory Sick Leave (non-pensionable)' pay item used to pay the episode — a pay-item linkage, not an org leave-type classification.

dimensions.label: start date
dimensions.description: First day of the sickness absence — not the first PAID day. SSP has historically been payable only from the fourth qualifying day (three unpaid waiting days), and the waiting-day and lower-earnings rules have been subject to legislative change, so the paid window inside start_date..end_date is narrower than the calendar span by an amount that depends on the rules in force for that period and on work_pattern. Never derive SSP cost by multiplying this span by a daily rate; the payslip SSP earnings lines in the pay-run domain are what was actually paid.

dimensions.label: end date
dimensions.description: Last day of the sickness absence (planned end while the episode is open).

dimensions.label: type
dimensions.description: Statutory leave category of this record — always the sick variant here; kept for symmetry with the summaries table.

dimensions.label: status
dimensions.description: Episode lifecycle status (the spec's own description is a copy-paste of type; treat values like the summaries statuses).

dimensions.label: work pattern
dimensions.description: Ordered list of weekdays the employee was scheduled to work when the leave was taken — qualifying-day logic depends on the order and content, so the array is kept verbatim. A plain string array, no nested objects.

dimensions.label: sufficient notice
dimensions.description: Whether the employee gave the notice/evidence the employer requires; FALSE can lawfully withhold SSP for late-notified days.

dimensions.label: is entitled
dimensions.description: Whether the episode qualifies for SSP payment; FALSE rows still represent real absence with zero SSP cost.

dimensions.label: entitlement weeks requested
dimensions.description: Weeks of SSP the episode requested — demand, not what was granted.

dimensions.label: entitlement weeks qualified
dimensions.description: Weeks of the 28-week SSP maximum still available when the leave was requested — a point-in-time entitlement figure, not a balance that updates.

dimensions.label: overlaps with other leave
dimensions.description: TRUE when paternity/shared-parental leave overlaps the sick period — allowed, but payment amounts interact; flag such episodes in cost analyses.

dimensions.label: entitlement failure reasons
dimensions.description: Why a not-entitled episode failed (string array, verbatim). Populated only when is_entitled is false — the explanatory companion, not an extra filter dimension.

dimensions.label: timesheet line id
dimensions.description: Xero's identifier for the line and the row key.

dimensions.label: timesheet id
dimensions.description: Parent timesheet; inherited from the record the lines were exploded from. The approval status filter lives on the parent.

dimensions.label: date
dimensions.description: The working day the units belong to — the correct time axis for daily/weekly hours analysis (the parent's start_date is the whole period).

dimensions.label: earnings rate id
dimensions.description: Which earnings rate the units are worked under; join xero_payroll_uk_earnings_rates to split regular vs overtime and to read the unit type.

dimensions.label: tracking item id
dimensions.description: The accounting tracking OPTION (e.g. a specific department) tagged on the line — an option under the timesheet tracking category configured in xero_payroll_uk_tracking_categories. Join xero_tracking_options, not xero_tracking_categories.

dimensions.label: timesheet id
dimensions.description: Xero's identifier for the timesheet and the row key.

dimensions.label: payroll calendar id
dimensions.description: The pay calendar whose period this timesheet covers; join xero_payroll_uk_pay_run_calendars to translate periods to pay frequency.

dimensions.label: employee id
dimensions.description: The employee who worked (or at least entered) these hours; join xero_payroll_uk_employees to filter to current staff, because leavers' timesheets persist forever. Only timesheet-paid (typically hourly) employees ever appear here — COUNT(DISTINCT employee_id) is the timesheet population, not headcount.

dimensions.label: start date
dimensions.description: First day of the timesheet's payroll period — payroll-calendar aligned, not month aligned.

dimensions.label: end date
dimensions.description: Last day of the timesheet's payroll period (inclusive). Use it to place a timesheet in a period, not to place the WORK: individual lines carry their own date, so hours can fall anywhere in the span and a period straddling a month end will attribute the whole sheet to one month if you bucket on the header instead of on timesheet_lines.date.

dimensions.label: status
dimensions.description: Draft is unapproved entry, Approved is signed off and awaiting payroll, Completed is processed in a pay run. Paid-hours analyses filter Completed (or Approved+Completed for committed hours); including Draft counts unvetted numbers.

dimensions.label: updated date utc
dimensions.description: Audit stamp of the last change; the incremental-sync watermark.

dimensions.label: timesheet lines
dimensions.description: Retained verbatim as the raw array Xero returned: the declared element order is part of the document and is lost by flattening. Fully normalised into xero_payroll_uk_timesheet_lines (one row per element) — join there for anything you filter or aggregate on, and read this column only when the original ordering or an unflattened payload matters.

dimensions.label: record key
dimensions.description: Singleton key so the one-row-per-org grain has a declared primary key.

dimensions.label: employee groups tracking category id
dimensions.description: The accounting tracking category used to group EMPLOYEES (e.g. by team). Null means the org has not enabled employee-group tracking — group-level payroll splits are then impossible, not merely empty.

dimensions.label: timesheet tracking category id
dimensions.description: The accounting tracking category whose options timesheet lines are tagged with (tracking_item_id on lines is one of ITS options). Resolve line tags through this category's options in xero_tracking_options.

dimensions.label: prepayment prepayment id
dimensions.description: Parent prepayment whose credit this row consumes. Populated by the ingester from the parent scan context; provenance is the Allocation shape's source-document echo slot, which the API rarely materializes inline.

dimensions.label: allocation ordinal
dimensions.description: Array position within the parent payload, minted because older payloads omit AllocationID. Stable only within one parent version — when the parent re-syncs, the whole allocation set for that prepayment_id is replaced, so never diff ordinals across syncs.

dimensions.label: allocation id
dimensions.description: Xero's allocation identifier when the API returns it (it exists to address allocation deletes upstream). Not the row key because legacy payloads omit it — prefer it for entity resolution when present, fall back to the composite key.

dimensions.label: invoice invoice id
dimensions.description: The invoice this slice of credit paid down — AR credit lands on ACCREC invoices, AP credit on ACCPAY bills; direction comes from the parent prepayment's type, not from this row. Join xero_invoices to see what the credit settled.

dimensions.label: date
dimensions.description: When the credit was applied — the settlement date for invoices paid by credit, and the axis for time-series application analysis. Distinct from (and often much later than) the parent prepayment's own date.

dimensions.label: is deleted
dimensions.description: The spec's delete-acknowledgement flag, seen on delete responses. On ordinary reads a removed allocation simply VANISHES from the parent's array — detect unwound applications by rows disappearing on re-sync, not by this flag turning true.

dimensions.label: credit note credit note id
dimensions.description: Always null in the prepayment context: the spec reuses one Allocation shape across credit notes, prepayments and overpayments, and this echo slot only fills on credit-note allocations (invoicing's xero_credit_note_allocations). Mapped so the shared shape is fully accounted — never filter on it here.

dimensions.label: status attribute string
dimensions.description: Write-response artefact indicating payload status. Ignore for analytics.

dimensions.label: validation errors
dimensions.description: API validation messages retained verbatim; empty on healthy reads.

dimensions.label: prepayment id
dimensions.description: Xero's immutable identifier for the prepayment and the row key; the value allocations and refund payments point back to.

dimensions.label: type
dimensions.description: Direction of the credit. RECEIVE-PREPAYMENT/ARPREPAYMENT: a customer paid you in advance (you owe them goods or a refund). SPEND-PREPAYMENT/APPREPAYMENT: you paid a supplier in advance. Every prepayment question must pick a side — summing both directions nets customer liabilities against supplier assets. The hyphenated values come from the source bank transaction; the AR*/AP* values are the same documents as typed on the payments surface.

dimensions.label: contact contact id
dimensions.description: The counterparty whose credit this is, from the embedded Contact stub. Join xero_contacts; remember merged contacts point at a survivor via MergedToContactID there.

dimensions.label: date
dimensions.description: The date the prepayment was created — when the cash actually arrived or left via its source bank transaction. Use it for cash timing; allocation dates on the child table are when the credit was consumed, which can be much later.

dimensions.label: status
dimensions.description: AUTHORISED still carries credit; PAID means fully applied or refunded; VOIDED is cancelled but STILL RETURNED by the API. Exclude VOIDED from every total or credit is overstated; note there is no DRAFT state — prepayments are born posted.

dimensions.label: line amount types
dimensions.description: Declares whether amounts inside line_items include tax (Inclusive), exclude it (Exclusive) or have none (NoTax). It ONLY changes how the jsonb lines read — sub_total, total_tax and total on this row are already normalized (sub_total is always ex-tax).

dimensions.label: line items
dimensions.description: Verbatim ordered line array of the credit document — the account/tax/tracking coding, auto-generated from the source bank transaction. Kept as payload because document-level totals answer prepayment questions; interpret raw LineAmount values only together with line_amount_types. If line-level prepayment analysis becomes load-bearing, promote to an explode table in a schema revision rather than parsing ad hoc.

dimensions.label: total tax
dimensions.description: Total tax on the prepayment. Prepayments can carry tax at creation depending on org settings — do not assume zero.

dimensions.label: reference
dimensions.description: Spec quirk, read-only: for prepayments this slot returns the document's invoice-number ('Reference field isn't available'). Do not treat it as user-entered reference text.

dimensions.label: invoice number
dimensions.description: The prepayment's OWN document number, returned for receive prepayments only. It is NOT a pointer to any invoice it later offsets — that linkage lives in xero_prepayment_allocations.

dimensions.label: currency code
dimensions.description: Document currency for every monetary column on this row. The extracted spec enum truncates mid-alphabet (ends at HRK) — treat the value set as open ISO-4217 (USD, NZD, SGD and others occur constantly); never validate against the enum list. Summing across currencies without converting via currency_rate is meaningless.

dimensions.label: branding theme id
dimensions.description: Branding template applied to a receive prepayment's printable document. Join xero_branding_themes; presentation metadata, no effect on amounts.

dimensions.label: applied amount
dimensions.description: Credit consumed against invoices so far — the current-state sum of this document's allocations. Per-invoice, per-date detail is in xero_prepayment_allocations; use that table for time-series application analysis.

dimensions.label: allocations
dimensions.description: Verbatim allocation array kept for payload-level audit (reconciling remaining_credit = total - applications - refunds). The analytic surface is xero_prepayment_allocations, exploded one row per application — query that, not this.

dimensions.label: payments
dimensions.description: Refund-payment stubs returned inline on the document. Canonical refund rows live in xero_payments with prepayment_id set and payment_type ARPREPAYMENTPAYMENT/APPREPAYMENTPAYMENT — use that join; this payload is for audit only.

dimensions.label: has attachments
dimensions.description: True when files are attached. Cheap existence filter; the attachment rows themselves come from org_meta's xero_attachments fan-out (rate-budgeted).

dimensions.label: attachments
dimensions.description: Attachment stubs if the API includes them inline (usually absent on list reads). The governed attachment surface is org_meta's xero_attachments; treat this as raw payload, not a catalogue.

dimensions.label: updated date utc
dimensions.description: Audit watermark for incremental sync; also moves when allocations change, which is how the child table stays fresh. Not a business date.

dimensions.label: updated date utc string
dimensions.description: ISO-8601 string twin of updated_date_utc. Redundant — read the timestamp column.

dimensions.label: task id
dimensions.description: Xero's immutable UUID for the task and the row key; time entries reference it as task_id.

dimensions.label: project id
dimensions.description: Owning project, present on the payload itself (the ingester's per-project fan-out confirms it). Join key to xero_projects — which also supplies the currency_code every monetary column here is denominated in.

dimensions.label: name
dimensions.description: What the work is called ('Design', 'Site visit') and what appears on the invoice line when the task is billed through Projects. Not unique across projects — 'Consulting' exists everywhere — so aggregate by task_id and qualify displays with the project name.

dimensions.label: charge type
dimensions.description: How this task turns effort into money, and the column every value question must respect: TIME bills logged minutes at rate, FIXED bills the fee in total_amount regardless of minutes, NON_CHARGEABLE bills nothing ever. Utilization counts all three; revenue counts only the first two. Pricing time without filtering on this column invents revenue from free work.

dimensions.label: rate currency
dimensions.description: Currency half of the rate Amount pair, kept verbatim so the pair survives flattening. The spec asserts no link to the parent project's currencyCode: expect agreement, treat a mismatch as a payload anomaly worth chasing rather than a signal that this task is priced in another currency, and group or convert on the project's currency_code — this API publishes no rate to base currency.

dimensions.label: estimate minutes
dimensions.description: Estimated effort for the task in minutes. Overrun detection is total_minutes > estimate_minutes; null or zero means nobody estimated, not that no work was expected — exclude those rows from overrun ratios or they divide by zero.

dimensions.label: status
dimensions.description: Task lifecycle with a trap the spec spells out: only a FIXED task whose rate amount has been invoiced reaches INVOICED (after which it cannot be modified), and a TIME or NON_CHARGEABLE task can never hold that value — it stays ACTIVE (or transiently LOCKED) however much of it has been billed. 'Uninvoiced tasks' must therefore be answered from amount_to_be_invoiced or minutes_to_be_invoiced, never from status, or every hourly task looks perpetually unbilled. LOCKED means the task is mid-state-change and unmodifiable, not deleted — deleted tasks carry no status at all because they stop being returned.

dimensions.label: time entry id
dimensions.description: Xero's immutable UUID for the logged block of time and the row key.

dimensions.label: user id
dimensions.description: The Xero user who logged the time, and the grouping key for every utilization and capacity answer. Join to xero_project_users for name and email — but LEFT JOIN: the roster is current-state, so hours logged by someone since removed from Projects carry a user_id that resolves to nothing, and an inner join deletes those hours instead of showing them as unattributed.

dimensions.label: project id
dimensions.description: Project the time belongs to (the task's parent), present on the payload directly — grouping here skips the task join when chargeability doesn't matter.

dimensions.label: task id
dimensions.description: Task the minutes were logged against, and the join that gives the row its economics: charge_type and rate live on xero_project_tasks, so without it a time entry has duration and no value. Misrouting it — pricing hours against the wrong task, or dropping rows whose task is missing from a partially refreshed fan-out — changes the money answer, not just the label.

dimensions.label: date utc
dimensions.description: The date the time is logged ON — the work date, and the business axis for hours-by-week, WIP aging and utilization. The spec pairs it against dateEnteredUtc ('the date time that time entry is created'), so this one is user-supplied and freely backdated: expect it to sit earlier than date_entered_utc and never treat it as an arrival stamp. It is also the field the Time op's dateAfterUtc/dateBeforeUtc filters cut on, which makes them safe for sharding a backfill and unsafe as an incremental watermark.

dimensions.label: date entered utc
dimensions.description: When the entry was CREATED — set to server time by default per the spec, so an audit stamp in practice, not a work date. Aggregating hours on it shifts every late-logged entry into the wrong period; its legitimate use is bookkeeping hygiene, e.g. how far in arrears the team logs time (date_entered_utc - date_utc).

dimensions.label: description
dimensions.description: Free-text note of what was done. Handy for keyword slicing ('meeting', 'travel') but optional and null-heavy — never a reliable filter on its own.

dimensions.label: status
dimensions.description: ACTIVE is unbilled, INVOICED is billed, LOCKED is transiently mid-invoicing (treat as about-to-be-INVOICED, not missing). All three are real worked time — utilization sums them all; 'unbilled time' filters ACTIVE only. Deleted entries never get a status: they vanish from the API, and only a full rescan clears them from staging.

dimensions.label: user id
dimensions.description: Xero user UUID and the row key — the identity xero_project_time_entries.user_id points at. The spec calls it 'the xero user identifier', i.e. the org-level user rather than a Projects-local id, so it lines up with the org's Users collection wherever that scope was granted. It means nothing outside Xero: cross-system people matching has to go through email.

dimensions.label: project id
dimensions.description: Xero's immutable UUID for the project and the row key; xero_project_tasks and xero_project_time_entries carry it as their foreign key.

dimensions.label: contact id
dimensions.description: The client the job is delivered for — at most one per project, and nullable: name is the only field the schema requires, so internal and unassigned jobs land here with no contact. It is the org-wide Xero contact identifier, so it resolves against xero_contacts and, through it, the same client's invoices. Grouping the rollups by this id is the fastest 'value by client' in the domain — but LEFT JOIN, because an inner join silently deletes every client-less project from the total.

dimensions.label: name
dimensions.description: The human name of the job and the only label the API offers — there is no project code or number field, so answers should display this. Uniqueness is not enforced: two clients (or one) can each have a 'Website redesign', so aggregate by project_id and only ever use name for display.

dimensions.label: status
dimensions.description: Project lifecycle. INPROGRESS is open work; CLOSED projects are finished but are STILL RETURNED by the API with all their rollups intact. Pipeline, WIP and utilization-target questions must filter INPROGRESS; lifetime-revenue and history questions must NOT, or finished work disappears.

dimensions.label: currency code
dimensions.description: ISO 4217 currency the project is quoted, tracked and invoiced in (Xero's CurrencyCode enum). Every monetary column on this row — and every rate and amount on the project's tasks — is denominated in it, and the Projects API supplies no exchange rate to the org's base currency. Any sum that crosses projects must GROUP BY this column or convert externally first; a raw cross-currency SUM is a number in no currency.

dimensions.label: deadline utc
dimensions.description: When the job is due (UTC), null when no deadline was set. The overdue book is deadline_utc < now() AND status = 'INPROGRESS' — a CLOSED project past its deadline finished late, it is not overdue.

dimensions.label: estimate currency
dimensions.description: Currency half of the estimate Amount pair, kept verbatim so the pair survives flattening intact. Xero documents no relationship between it and the project's currencyCode, so do not assume one: expect them to agree, and treat a disagreement as a payload anomaly to investigate, never as an instruction to convert — this API exposes no exchange rate to convert with. Filter and group on currency_code.

dimensions.label: estimate amount value
dimensions.description: The second budget field the spec carries next to estimate; Xero publishes a description for neither, and nothing in the spec makes them different quantities. Report the budget from estimate and keep this as the cross-check: adding the two doubles every project's budget, and a row where they disagree is a data-quality flag to chase, not a second business figure.

dimensions.label: deposit currency
dimensions.description: Currency half of the deposit Amount pair, kept verbatim so the pair survives flattening. As with estimate_currency, the spec ties it to nothing: expect it to agree with the project's currency_code and treat a mismatch as a payload anomaly rather than a conversion cue — no rate to base currency exists anywhere in this API. Query on currency_code.

dimensions.label: line item id
dimensions.description: Xero's uuid for this line, useful for matching a line to itself between two snapshots — but deliberately NOT the row key: an edit that rewrites the LineItems array reissues these ids, so keying on it would strand the pre-edit rows and double the order's committed value. The grain key is (purchase_order_id, line_ordinal).

dimensions.label: purchase order id
dimensions.description: Owning purchase order and half the row key. Every aggregate must join through it to filter the parent's status — lines carry no lifecycle state of their own.

dimensions.label: line ordinal
dimensions.description: Zero-based position of the line within its order's LineItems array. The other half of the row key, and the only identity that survives an edit intact, since Xero reissues LineItemIDs when the array is replaced; it also preserves document order for rendering.

dimensions.label: description
dimensions.description: What is being ordered, in the buyer's words. On free-text lines (item_code null) this is the only evidence of what was bought, so spend-by-product analysis that keys solely on item_code silently ignores it. Description-only lines with no quantity or amounts are legal — filter quantity IS NOT NULL before computing unit economics.

dimensions.label: item code
dimensions.description: User-defined code of the catalog item this line references; null for free-text lines. Joins xero_items.code — a text, user-editable key, so renamed or deleted items orphan historical lines.

dimensions.label: account code
dimensions.description: GL account code this committed spend would post to once billed — the category axis for procurement analysis. Null when the org leaves categorization to item defaults until billing.

dimensions.label: account id
dimensions.description: Uuid of the same GL account when the API returns it. Prefer joining xero_accounts on this; fall back to account_code = xero_accounts.code on older documents where it is null.

dimensions.label: tax type
dimensions.description: Tax rate key applied to this line (joins xero_tax_rates.tax_type); drives tax_amount and the Inclusive/Exclusive arithmetic.

dimensions.label: tax amount
dimensions.description: Tax for the line in the document currency, auto-calculated from the tax rate but overridable — do not recompute it from tax_type and assume equality.

dimensions.label: discount rate
dimensions.description: Percentage discount on the line, already reflected in line_amount — applying it again understates committed spend. A ratio: never summed.

dimensions.label: discount amount
dimensions.description: Absolute discount on the line, already reflected in line_amount; the header's total_discount is the document-level sum of these.

dimensions.label: tracking
dimensions.description: Array (max 2 elements) of tracking category assignments — the org's analysis dimensions (department, region). Each element carries TrackingCategoryID, TrackingOptionID, Name, Option. Cut committed spend by dimension via CROSS JOIN LATERAL jsonb_array_elements(tracking) and match Name/Option, or the ids against xero_tracking_categories / xero_tracking_options.

dimensions.label: purchase order id
dimensions.description: Xero's immutable identifier for the purchase order and the row key; the join key for line items, attachments and history.

dimensions.label: purchase order number
dimensions.description: Human-facing alphanumeric code, auto-generated from the org's invoice settings when omitted. Unique within an org in practice but user-editable — join on purchase_order_id, display this.

dimensions.label: contact contact id
dimensions.description: The supplier the order is raised against; joins xero_contacts. Xero does not require the contact to be flagged IsSupplier — raising ACCPAY documents is what makes a contact a supplier.

dimensions.label: status
dimensions.description: Lifecycle gate for every number in this table. DRAFT/SUBMITTED are unapproved intent, AUTHORISED is an open commitment, BILLED means an ACCPAY bill now carries the real spend, DELETED rows are still returned by the API. Committed-spend questions filter AUTHORISED; there is no VOIDED state for purchase orders — DELETED covers withdrawal at every stage.

dimensions.label: date
dimensions.description: Issue date of the order (org-timezone business date, defaulted to today when omitted at creation). The DateFrom/DateTo server-side filters and all period reporting key off this, not the audit stamp.

dimensions.label: delivery date
dimensions.description: Date the goods are contractually to be delivered; null when never specified. Distinct from expected_arrival_date, which is the forecast rather than the ask.

dimensions.label: expected arrival date
dimensions.description: Forecast arrival date of the goods. Overdue-delivery reporting is AUTHORISED orders whose expected_arrival_date (or delivery_date) has passed — Xero records no goods-receipt event to close the loop.

dimensions.label: reference
dimensions.description: Free-text secondary reference (supplier quote number, project code). Not unique and not the PO number — never use as a key.

dimensions.label: line amount types
dimensions.description: Declares whether line_amount on this order's lines includes tax. Line-level rollups across mixed modes double-count tax; the header sub_total/total_tax/total are already normalized and immune.

dimensions.label: currency code
dimensions.description: ISO 4217 currency of every monetary field on this order. The spec enumerates the full ISO list (the extract truncates it, so it is deliberately not carried as a closed enum here). Summing totals across currency codes yields a number in no currency — group by this or convert via currency_rate first.

dimensions.label: total tax
dimensions.description: Tax component of the order in the document currency, normalized so that sub_total + total_tax = total whatever line_amount_types says. It is not a tax asset: a purchase order posts nothing to the ledger, so nothing here is reclaimable input VAT/GST — that exists only once the order is billed and the ACCPAY invoice's tax reaches the journals.

dimensions.label: total discount
dimensions.description: Sum of line-level discounts already reflected in the line amounts and header totals — do not subtract it again from sub_total or total.

dimensions.label: sent to contact
dimensions.description: True when the order was marked as sent to the supplier. Settable only on approved or billed orders, so drafts always read false — not evidence a draft was never emailed manually.

dimensions.label: delivery instructions
dimensions.description: Free-text delivery instructions (max 500 chars). Operational text that occasionally embeds names or phone numbers — treat with care even though it is not flagged PII.

dimensions.label: branding theme id
dimensions.description: Document template applied when sending; joins xero_branding_themes. Presentation only — no analytical meaning.

dimensions.label: has attachments
dimensions.description: True when at least one file is attached. The files themselves are in xero_attachments via the rate-budgeted per-order fan-out endpoint — use this flag to decide whether that call is worth spending.

dimensions.label: status attribute string
dimensions.description: Write-response validation indicator from batch upserts (e.g. ERROR), not part of the document lifecycle — status is the real state. Ignore for analytics.

dimensions.label: updated date utc
dimensions.description: Server-side modification stamp and the incremental-sync watermark (If-Modified-Since). An audit timestamp — never a business date for period reporting.

dimensions.label: validation errors
dimensions.description: Write-time validation messages echoed by the API, kept verbatim for payload fidelity. Empty on clean reads — never analytical.

dimensions.label: warnings
dimensions.description: Write-time warning messages — the same transport artifact as validation_errors, retained only for payload fidelity.

dimensions.label: attachments
dimensions.description: Embedded attachment descriptors (id, filename, mime type, url, size, online-invoice flag) when the API includes them. The governed home for files is xero_attachments — prefer it over parsing this payload.

dimensions.label: line items
dimensions.description: See LineItems Retained verbatim as the raw array Xero returned: the declared element order is part of the document and is lost by flattening. Fully normalised into xero_purchase_order_line_items (one row per element) — join there for anything you filter or aggregate on, and read this column only when the original ordering or an unflattened payload matters.

dimensions.label: line items line item id
dimensions.description: Xero's identifier for the quoted line; the row key.

dimensions.label: quote id
dimensions.description: Parent quote key. Join xero_quotes for status, currency and line_amount_types — quoted value only counts as pipeline under the right parent status.

dimensions.label: line items
dimensions.description: Zero-based position within the parent's LineItems array (provenance: the array itself). Presentation order; renumbered on edit.

dimensions.label: line items description
dimensions.description: Free-text description of the offered line; description-only lines (null amounts) carry narrative, not value.

dimensions.label: line items quantity
dimensions.description: Units offered; null on description-only lines.

dimensions.label: line items unit amount
dimensions.description: Per-unit offered price before discount, quote currency. A rate — never summed. Compare against invoice unit_amount to measure quote-to-invoice price erosion.

dimensions.label: line items tax type
dimensions.description: Tax rate key proposed for the line; join xero_tax_rates.tax_type.

dimensions.label: line items tax amount
dimensions.description: Tax computed on the offered line, quote currency; indicative until invoiced.

dimensions.label: line items account code
dimensions.description: GL account code the line would post to if invoiced; join xero_accounts.code. Often blank on quotes — sales users defer coding.

dimensions.label: line items account id
dimensions.description: Immutable GL account id for the prospective posting; join xero_accounts.

dimensions.label: line items item code
dimensions.description: Catalogue item code being offered; null on free-typed quote lines.

dimensions.label: line items item item id
dimensions.description: Resolved catalogue item id from the embedded Item echo; durable join to xero_items.

dimensions.label: line items item
dimensions.description: Verbatim item stub ({Code, Name, ItemID}) as quoted; prefer scalar item_id/item_code for joins.

dimensions.label: line items tracking
dimensions.description: Up to 2 tracking assignments on the quoted line ({TrackingCategoryID, TrackingOptionID, Name, Option}); expand with jsonb_array_elements to attribute pipeline to departments/regions.

dimensions.label: line items discount rate
dimensions.description: Percentage discount offered on the line; line_amount is already net of it.

dimensions.label: line items discount amount
dimensions.description: Absolute discount offered (supported on quotes per the spec); line_amount is already net of it — subtracting again understates offered value.

dimensions.label: line items repeating invoice id
dimensions.description: Repeating-template lineage on the shared line schema; effectively always null on quotes.

dimensions.label: line items taxability
dimensions.description: US automated sales tax classification; null outside US orgs.

dimensions.label: line items sales tax code id
dimensions.description: Internal id of the US sales tax code on the line; US orgs only.

dimensions.label: line items tax breakdown
dimensions.description: Per-jurisdiction US sales tax components estimated for the offered line, kept verbatim.

dimensions.label: quote id
dimensions.description: Xero's immutable identifier for the quote and the row key.

dimensions.label: quote number
dimensions.description: Human-facing quote number (max 255), auto-generated from org settings; display and lookup, not a join key.

dimensions.label: status
dimensions.description: The pipeline stage and the mandatory filter on every quote metric: DRAFT/SENT = open, DECLINED = lost, ACCEPTED = won awaiting billing, INVOICED = converted, DELETED = removed but still returned by the API. 'Pipeline value' that ignores status counts dead and already-billed offers.

dimensions.label: contact contact id
dimensions.description: The prospect/customer quoted; join xero_contacts.

dimensions.label: reference
dimensions.description: Free-text reference on the quote (customer RFQ number etc.).

dimensions.label: terms
dimensions.description: Terms text printed on the quote; presentation only.

dimensions.label: title
dimensions.description: Title text printed on the quote; presentation only.

dimensions.label: summary
dimensions.description: Summary text printed on the quote; presentation only.

dimensions.label: date
dimensions.description: Issue date of the quote (org-timezone business date); the axis for quoting-activity and win-rate cohorts.

dimensions.label: date string
dimensions.description: String twin of date as returned by the API; prefer the typed date column.

dimensions.label: expiry date
dimensions.description: Date the offer lapses. Expired-but-still-SENT quotes remain status SENT — 'live pipeline' should also require expiry_date >= CURRENT_DATE (or null).

dimensions.label: expiry date string
dimensions.description: String twin of expiry_date; prefer the typed date column.

dimensions.label: currency code
dimensions.description: ISO 4217 currency of the quote's monetary fields (spec CurrencyCode enum; extraction truncates the full list). Convert before summing across currencies.

dimensions.label: currency rate
dimensions.description: Rate to the org's base currency for a multicurrency quote; multiply monetary fields by it for base-currency pipeline.

dimensions.label: line amount types
