dimensions.description: Whether quote line amounts include tax — NOTE the quote enum is UPPERCASE (EXCLUSIVE/INCLUSIVE/NOTAX) unlike the invoice enum (Exclusive/...). String filters written with invoice casing silently match nothing.

dimensions.label: total tax
dimensions.description: Tax estimated on the offer, quote currency.

dimensions.label: total discount
dimensions.description: Sum of line discounts offered; already reflected in totals — do not subtract again.

dimensions.label: branding theme id
dimensions.description: Template/branding used for the quote; join xero_branding_themes.

dimensions.label: updated date utc
dimensions.description: Last-modified audit stamp and incremental watermark (If-Modified-Since); not a business date.

dimensions.label: status attribute string
dimensions.description: Batch-response status indicator accompanying validation messages; ignore for analytics.

dimensions.label: validation errors
dimensions.description: API validation error messages carried verbatim ({Message} objects); data-quality triage only.

dimensions.label: line item id
dimensions.description: Xero's uuid for this line, kept for matching a line to itself between snapshots — deliberately not the row key, because an edit that rewrites the receipt's LineItems array reissues these ids and keying on them would leave the pre-edit rows behind, doubling the receipt's spend. The grain key is (receipt_id, line_ordinal).

dimensions.label: receipt id
dimensions.description: Owning receipt and half the row key. Every aggregate must join through it for status, spend date and the capturing employee — lines have no lifecycle of their own.

dimensions.label: line ordinal
dimensions.description: Zero-based position of the line within its receipt's LineItems array — the other half of the row key and the only identity that survives an edit, since Xero reissues LineItemIDs when the array is replaced. Also preserves the order the employee keyed the lines in.

dimensions.label: description
dimensions.description: What the employee bought, in their own words — the only textual evidence on hand-keyed receipts; description-only lines with no amounts are legal.

dimensions.label: quantity
dimensions.description: Units purchased, up to 4dp; often 1 or null on expense receipts — filter nulls before unit-economics math.

dimensions.label: unit amount
dimensions.description: Per-unit price in org base currency (unitdp=4). A rate — sum line_amount, never this.

dimensions.label: item code
dimensions.description: Catalog item code when the employee coded the line to an item; usually null on expense receipts. Joins xero_items.code.

dimensions.label: account code
dimensions.description: The GL expense account this spend is coded to — the category axis for employee-spend analysis. This is a categorization, not a posting: the ledger truth materializes as journal lines when the claim is processed.

dimensions.label: account id
dimensions.description: Uuid of the same GL account when returned; prefer it for joins to xero_accounts, falling back to account_code = xero_accounts.code.

dimensions.label: tax type
dimensions.description: Tax rate key applied to the line (joins xero_tax_rates.tax_type) — the basis for reclaimable-tax analysis on employee spend.

dimensions.label: tax amount
dimensions.description: Tax on the line in org base currency. Xero derives it from tax_type but it is overridable on write, so recomputing it from the rate and asserting equality manufactures false mismatches; it is also the term subtracted from line_amount when the parent receipt is Inclusive.

dimensions.label: tracking
dimensions.description: Array (max 2 elements) of tracking category assignments carrying TrackingCategoryID, TrackingOptionID, Name, Option — cut employee spend by department/region via CROSS JOIN LATERAL jsonb_array_elements(tracking), matching ids to xero_tracking_categories / xero_tracking_options.

dimensions.label: receipt id
dimensions.description: Xero's immutable identifier for the receipt and the row key; the join key for line items and the claim link table.

dimensions.label: receipt number
dimensions.description: Xero-generated sequence number scoped to the capturing user's current claim — NOT unique across the org. Display only; never a join key.

dimensions.label: date
dimensions.description: The date the employee spent the money — the spend-period axis. Reimbursement timing lives on the claim and its payments, not here.

dimensions.label: contact contact id
dimensions.description: The merchant/supplier the employee paid; joins xero_contacts. Frequently an ad-hoc, loosely-managed contact created from the receipt itself — expect duplicates of real suppliers.

dimensions.label: user user id
dimensions.description: The employee (org user) who captured and owns this receipt; joins xero_users — the person axis for employee-spend analysis.

dimensions.label: reference
dimensions.description: Free-text reference for the purchase (order number, trip name); matching aid only, no analytical meaning.

dimensions.label: line amount types
dimensions.description: Declares whether line_amount on this receipt's lines includes tax; drives the same Inclusive/Exclusive CASE arithmetic as invoices. Header totals here are already normalized.

dimensions.label: total tax
dimensions.description: Tax component of the receipt, normalized so sub_total + total_tax = total whatever line_amount_types says. It is the input VAT/GST the org may recover on employee spend — but only for AUTHORISED receipts: summing it over DRAFT, SUBMITTED or DECLINED rows claims tax on spend the business has not accepted.

dimensions.label: status
dimensions.description: Receipt workflow state: DRAFT is captured-not-claimed, SUBMITTED is on a claim awaiting approval, AUTHORISED is approved spend, DECLINED was rejected by the approver (a state unique to receipts), VOIDED is dead. Approved-spend numbers count AUTHORISED only.

dimensions.label: url
dimensions.description: Deep link to the source document in a connected app (rendered as 'Go to [appName]' in Xero). Set by API integrations; null for hand-keyed receipts.

dimensions.label: has attachments
dimensions.description: True when a scanned image or file is attached; the files live in xero_attachments via the rate-budgeted per-receipt fan-out.

dimensions.label: updated date utc
dimensions.description: Server-side modification stamp and the incremental-sync watermark (If-Modified-Since); audit metadata only.

dimensions.label: validation errors
dimensions.description: Write-time validation messages echoed by the API; kept verbatim for payload fidelity, empty on clean reads.

dimensions.label: warnings
dimensions.description: Write-time warning messages; transport artifact retained for fidelity, never analytical.

dimensions.label: attachments
dimensions.description: Embedded attachment descriptors (id, filename, mime type, url, size, online flag) when included; prefer the governed xero_attachments table over parsing this payload.

dimensions.label: line items
dimensions.description: Retained verbatim as the raw array Xero returned: the declared element order is part of the document and is lost by flattening. Fully normalised into xero_receipt_line_items (one row per element) — join there for anything you filter or aggregate on, and read this column only when the original ordering or an unflattened payload matters.

dimensions.label: line items line item id
dimensions.description: Xero's identifier for the template line; the row key.

dimensions.label: repeating invoice id
dimensions.description: Parent template key. Join xero_repeating_invoices for type, status, currency and the schedule needed to normalize any amount on this row.

dimensions.label: line items
dimensions.description: Zero-based position within the template's LineItems array (provenance: the array itself). Presentation order; renumbered on edit.

dimensions.label: line items description
dimensions.description: Line description copied onto every generated invoice; description-only lines carry narrative, not value.

dimensions.label: line items quantity
dimensions.description: Units billed per occurrence; null on description-only lines.

dimensions.label: line items unit amount
dimensions.description: Per-unit price billed each occurrence, template currency. A rate — never summed.

dimensions.label: line items tax type
dimensions.description: Tax rate key applied each occurrence; join xero_tax_rates.tax_type.

dimensions.label: line items tax amount
dimensions.description: Tax per occurrence on this line, template currency.

dimensions.label: line items account code
dimensions.description: GL account code each occurrence posts to; join xero_accounts.code — this is where recurring revenue/spend lands in the P&L.

dimensions.label: line items account id
dimensions.description: Immutable GL account id for the recurring posting; durable join to xero_accounts.

dimensions.label: line items item code
dimensions.description: Catalogue item code billed each cycle; null on free-typed template lines.

dimensions.label: line items item item id
dimensions.description: Resolved catalogue item id from the embedded Item echo; durable join to xero_items.

dimensions.label: line items item
dimensions.description: Verbatim item stub ({Code, Name, ItemID}) on the template line; prefer scalar item_id/item_code for joins.

dimensions.label: line items tracking
dimensions.description: Up to 2 tracking assignments stamped onto every generated invoice line ({TrackingCategoryID, TrackingOptionID, Name, Option}); expand with jsonb_array_elements to see which departments/regions recurring billing is committed to.

dimensions.label: line items discount rate
dimensions.description: Percentage discount applied each occurrence (ACCREC templates only); line_amount is already net of it.

dimensions.label: line items discount amount
dimensions.description: Absolute discount applied each occurrence (ACCREC templates only); line_amount is already net of it.

dimensions.label: line items taxability
dimensions.description: US automated sales tax classification; null outside US orgs.

dimensions.label: line items sales tax code id
dimensions.description: Internal id of the US sales tax code on the template line; US orgs only.

dimensions.label: line items tax breakdown
dimensions.description: Per-jurisdiction US sales tax components estimated for the template line, kept verbatim.

dimensions.label: repeating invoice id
dimensions.description: Xero's identifier for the template and the row key; xero_invoices.repeating_invoice_id points here from every generated document.

dimensions.label: id
dimensions.description: Verbatim duplicate of the template identifier returned by the API as ID; always equals repeating_invoice_id — kept for payload fidelity, use repeating_invoice_id.

dimensions.label: type
dimensions.description: Direction of the recurring flow: ACCREC templates generate sales invoices (recurring revenue), ACCPAY templates generate bills (recurring spend). Recurring-revenue metrics must filter ACCREC or subscription MRR silently absorbs rent and utilities.

dimensions.label: status
dimensions.description: Template state: only AUTHORISED templates generate invoices; DRAFT templates are configured but dormant; DELETED templates are removed yet still returned by the API. Run-rate = AUTHORISED only.

dimensions.label: contact contact id
dimensions.description: The customer billed (ACCREC) or supplier paid (ACCPAY) each cycle; join xero_contacts.

dimensions.label: reference
dimensions.description: Free-text reference stamped onto generated documents; ACCREC only.

dimensions.label: line amount types
dimensions.description: Whether the template's line amounts include tax (Exclusive/Inclusive/NoTax); inherited by every generated invoice.

dimensions.label: currency code
dimensions.description: ISO 4217 currency the template bills in (spec CurrencyCode enum; extraction truncates the full list). Normalize per-currency before comparing run-rates.

dimensions.label: schedule unit
dimensions.description: Cadence unit of the schedule (WEEKLY or MONTHLY). The other half of run-rate normalization alongside schedule_period.

dimensions.label: schedule due date
dimensions.description: Integer day used with schedule_due_date_type to derive each generated invoice's due date (e.g. 20 of the following month).

dimensions.label: schedule due date type
dimensions.description: Payment-terms rule that interprets schedule_due_date (days after invoice/bill date or month, or a day of the current/following month).

dimensions.label: schedule start date
dimensions.description: Date the first invoice of the CURRENT version of the schedule was generated — it resets when the template is edited, so it is not the customer's original subscription start.

dimensions.label: schedule next scheduled date
dimensions.description: Calendar date the next invoice will be generated; the forward-looking billing calendar.

dimensions.label: schedule end date
dimensions.description: Date the template stops generating; only returned when an end date is set — null means it runs indefinitely, not that it is ending.

dimensions.label: branding theme id
dimensions.description: Template/branding applied to generated documents; join xero_branding_themes.

dimensions.label: approved for sending
dimensions.description: True when generated invoices are auto-approved and emailed to the contact; false means each occurrence lands as a draft for manual handling — a workflow split that shows up as billing lag.

dimensions.label: send copy
dimensions.description: Whether Xero emails the sending user a copy of each generated invoice — an internal-notification preference with no financial meaning; never a proxy for whether the customer was billed.

dimensions.label: mark as sent
dimensions.description: Whether generated invoices display as 'sent' in Xero regardless of actual delivery.

dimensions.label: include pdf
dimensions.description: Whether the email sent for each occurrence carries the invoice as a PDF attachment — a delivery-format preference only; it says nothing about approval, sending or payment state.

dimensions.label: has attachments
dimensions.description: True when the template carries attachments (copied onto generated invoices); files are catalogued in xero_attachments (org_meta).

dimensions.label: attachments
dimensions.description: Attachment stubs occasionally echoed on the template payload; the catalogued inventory is xero_attachments (org_meta).

dimensions.label: tax type
dimensions.description: The owning tax rate's systemwide code — inherited from the parent scan and the join back to xero_tax_rates. Components have no identity of their own in Xero; this code plus array position IS the row key, so any question about a component starts by resolving the rate through this column, not by matching component names (which repeat across rates, e.g. 'GST').

dimensions.label: tax components
dimensions.description: Zero-based position in the rate's TaxComponents array — the provenance anchor for the exploded container and, with compounding, the application order.

dimensions.label: name
dimensions.description: Component label (e.g. 'GST', 'PST') — the granularity tax authorities are remitted at, finer than the parent rate's name.

dimensions.label: is compound
dimensions.description: True when this component applies on top of the base PLUS prior components' tax — the mechanism that makes effective_rate exceed the plain sum. Any true value here forbids naive rate addition.

dimensions.label: is non recoverable
dimensions.description: True when the component cannot be claimed back — applicable to Canadian organisations only; elsewhere expect false/null. Affects whether the tax is a cost or a pass-through.

dimensions.label: tax type
dimensions.description: The systemwide tax code (e.g. OUTPUT2, NONE) and the row key — the value every TaxType column elsewhere joins on. Xero addresses rates by this code, not by uuid.

dimensions.label: name
dimensions.description: Human label ('20% (VAT on Income)'). Editable and non-unique over time — never join on it; frozen copies on old lines will not match.

dimensions.label: status
dimensions.description: ACTIVE rates are offered for new coding; DELETED/ARCHIVED persist on history; PENDING rates are scheduled (e.g. legislated future changes). Do not drop non-ACTIVE rows — historical joins need them.

dimensions.label: report tax type
dimensions.description: Which box of the regional tax return the rate feeds (INPUT vs OUTPUT sides, EC*, MOSS, flat-rate schemes…). The right slicer for 'tax collected vs tax paid' questions — rate names are too free-form to classify.

dimensions.label: can apply to assets
dimensions.description: Read-only applicability flag: whether asset-class accounts may use this rate. Configuration surface, not usage evidence.

dimensions.label: can apply to equity
dimensions.description: Whether equity-class accounts may use this rate (read-only).

dimensions.label: can apply to expenses
dimensions.description: Whether expense-class accounts may use this rate (read-only).

dimensions.label: can apply to liabilities
dimensions.description: Whether liability-class accounts may use this rate (read-only).

dimensions.label: can apply to revenue
dimensions.description: Whether revenue-class accounts may use this rate (read-only).

dimensions.label: tax components
dimensions.description: See TaxComponents Retained verbatim so the founding canonical mapper keeps reading the column it was written against.

dimensions.label: tracking category id
dimensions.description: Xero's identifier for the dimension and the row key — what every tracking assignment (journal, document, budget) joins on.

dimensions.label: name
dimensions.description: Current dimension name (max 100, e.g. 'Region'). Renameable — assignments frozen on immutable journals keep the old spelling, so resolve dimensions by id and use this for display.

dimensions.label: status
dimensions.description: ACTIVE categories (max two) are assignable today; ARCHIVED/DELETED ones persist on history. 'Current dimensions' questions filter ACTIVE; historical segmentation must not.

dimensions.label: options
dimensions.description: See Tracking Options Retained verbatim so the founding canonical mapper keeps reading the column it was written against.

dimensions.label: tracking option id
dimensions.description: The Xero identifier for a tracking option e.g. dc54c220-0140-495a-b925-3246adc0075f Retained verbatim so the founding canonical mapper keeps reading the column it was written against.

dimensions.label: option
dimensions.description: The option name of the tracking option e.g. East, West (max length = 100) Retained verbatim so the founding canonical mapper keeps reading the column it was written against.

dimensions.label: tracking option id
dimensions.description: Xero's identifier for the option and the row key — the stable segment key assignments join on.

dimensions.label: tracking category id
dimensions.description: Owning category — an option name like 'North' is only unique within its category, never globally.

dimensions.label: options
dimensions.description: Zero-based position in the category's Options array — provenance anchor for the exploded container; display order in Xero.

dimensions.label: name
dimensions.description: Current option label (max 100). Renames leave stale spellings on immutable journal history — group by tracking_option_id, decorate with this.

dimensions.label: status
dimensions.description: ACTIVE options are assignable; ARCHIVED/DELETED remain on history. Segment breakdowns over past periods must include non-ACTIVE options.

dimensions.label: user id
dimensions.description: Xero's immutable identifier for the user within this org and the row key. Note: document History events reference actors by free-text display name, not by this id, so audit-trail attribution never joins on it; the few accounting payloads that do embed a user (expense-claim Receipts) carry the full User object rather than a bare id.

dimensions.label: updated date utc
dimensions.description: Audit stamp of the last change to the user record (role change, rename) and the incremental-sync watermark. Not a login/activity timestamp — Xero does not expose last-login.

dimensions.label: is subscriber
dimensions.description: True for the person who owns and pays for the Xero subscription — the escalation/billing contact, one per org in practice, and not necessarily an accountant or admin of the books.

dimensions.label: organisation role
dimensions.description: Permission tier controlling what the login can do in Xero and via API. REMOVED marks ex-users that the API keeps returning — every 'how many users / who has access' answer must exclude it. FINANCIALADVISER, MANAGEDCLIENT and CASHBOOKCLIENT flag practice-side or adviser-managed logins rather than the org's own staff.

measures.label: Gross takings (inc GST)
measures.description: Completed sales including GST, net of refunds on the refund date.

measures.label: Captured POS tenders
measures.description: Captured POS tender value, net of tender refunds, on the operational trading date.

measures.label: Sell price realisation

measures.grain: one_sales_or_refund_event

measures.label: Active customers
measures.description: Distinct identified customers purchasing inside the tenant-defined active window.

measures.label: New customers

measures.label: Repeat purchase rate

measures.label: sales rows
measures.description: Count of source rows at the documented grain: one row per Sale record — one register ticket/transaction, in any state (open, completed, voided, archived). Refunds are NOT a separate resource: a refund is a Sale whose lines carry negative unitQuantity and whose payments carry negative amount, so it is also one row here.. This is a discoverability measure, not a business KPI.
measures.grain: one row per Sale record — one register ticket/transaction, in any state (open, completed, voided, archived). Refunds are NOT a separate resource: a refund is a Sale whose lines carry negative unitQuantity and whose payments carry negative amount, so it is also one row here.

measures.label: tax1 rate
measures.description: Exploratory aggregation of Default first tax rate for the sale, expressed as a FRACTION (0.1 = 10%, not 10). Lines without a specific TaxClass rate fall back to this. Reading it as a percentage is a 100x error; deriving tax as calc_subtotal * tax1_rate is also wrong on any mixed basket because lines override it. measures.grain: one row per Sale record — one register ticket/transaction, in any state (open, completed, voided, archived). Refunds are NOT a separate resource: a refund is a Sale whose lines carry negative unitQuantity and whose payments carry negative amount, so it is also one row here.

measures.label: calc total
measures.description: Exploratory aggregation of The grand total the customer pays: after discounts, INCLUDING tax. The canonical per-sale revenue figure and the one the POS UI shows. Refund sales carry a negative value so SUM() nets refunds out automatically. Never pair it with the cost columns (which are ex-tax) — use calc_subtotal for margin. The aggregation is constrained by the documented source grain and is not a certified business KPI.

measures.label: calc subtotal
measures.description: Exploratory aggregation of Sale total EXCLUDING tax, after discounts. The correct revenue base for gross-margin arithmetic because calc_avg_cost and calc_fifo_cost are also ex-tax. Mixing calc_total with cost overstates margin by roughly the tax rate (about 9% of revenue at 10% GST). The aggregation is constrained by the documented source grain and is not a certified business KPI.
measures.grain: one row per Sale record — one register ticket/transaction, in any state (open, completed, voided, archived). Refunds are NOT a separate resource: a refund is a Sale whose lines carry negative unitQuantity and whose payments carry negative amount, so it is also one row here.

measures.label: calc avg cost

The cost-basis choice silently changes reported profit: Lightspeed's own profit reporting uses FIFO, so pick one basis and never blend the two within a report. The aggregation is constrained by the documented source grain and is not a certified business KPI.

measures.label: calc fifo cost

Can be 0 on migrated history and on non-inventory/service lines, in which case gross profit is silently reported as 100% — fall back to calc_avg_cost when this is 0 and subtotal is not. The aggregation is constrained by the documented source grain and is not a certified business KPI.
measures.grain: one row per Sale record — one register ticket/transaction, in any state (open, completed, voided, archived). Refunds are NOT a separate resource: a refund is a Sale whose lines carry negative unitQuantity and whose payments carry negative amount, so it is also one row here.

measures.label: total

Reads as a near-duplicate of calc_total but is derived differently, so the two can disagree depending on whether calc_subtotal is already net of discount on your account. Choose ONE total column for reporting (calc_total is what the POS shows) and never mix them within a query. The aggregation is constrained by the documented source grain and is not a certified business KPI.

The aggregation is constrained by the documented source grain and is not a certified business KPI.

measures.label: unit quantity

measures.label: discount percent

measures.label: avg cost
measures.description: Exploratory aggregation of Weighted-average cost of the product on this line, ex tax. The reference calls it the current average UNIT cost, but VERIFIED LIVE it behaves as the LINE total cost. Multiplying it by unit_quantity therefore double counts COGS and can halve reported margin — validate against a known line on your own account before doing any arithmetic with it. The aggregation is constrained by the documented source grain and is not a certified business KPI.

It is 0 on non-inventory/service lines and on some migrated history, which silently reports those lines at 100% margin; fall back to avg_cost when this is 0 and calc_subtotal is not. measures.label: calc subtotal
measures.description: Exploratory aggregation of Line revenue excluding tax. TRAP: the reference defines it as unitQuantity * unitPrice — i.e. GROSS of the line discount — whereas displayableSubtotal explicitly subtracts the discount. Confirm on your own account which behaviour you get before using it as the margin base; the gap is exactly calc_line_discount. The aggregation is constrained by the documented source grain and is not a certified business KPI.
measures.grain: one row per SaleLine — one charge on one sale. That is a catalog item line, a miscellaneous/non-inventory charge, an item-fee surcharge line, or a refund line (negative unitQuantity). Layaway, special-order and workorder lines share this same grain.

measures.grain: one inventory change event — one item's stock level changing in one shop, for one reason, at one moment

measures.label: qoh change
measures.description: Exploratory aggregation of Units added (positive) or removed (negative) by this event. The ONLY summable measure in this table. Rows with qoh_change = 0 exist (cost-only corrections, cancelled reservations) so filter qoh_change <> 0 when counting real movements. The aggregation is constrained by the documented source grain and is not a certified business KPI.
measures.grain: one inventory change event — one item's stock level changing in one shop, for one reason, at one moment

measures.label: cost change
measures.description: Exploratory aggregation of Despite the '-Change' name this is NOT a delta: documented as 'the updated unit cost for the Item', i.e. the item's unit cost AFTER this event, ex tax, in store currency. SUM() of it is meaningless. Contrast ls_inventory_count_reconciles.cost_change, which uses the same name for a genuine value delta. The aggregation is constrained by the documented source grain and is not a certified business KPI.
measures.grain: one inventory change event — one item's stock level changing in one shop, for one reason, at one moment

measures.label: inventory count calcs rows
measures.description: Count of source rows at the documented grain: one item within one inventory count (the system-vs-physical rollup for that item/count pair). This is a discoverability measure, not a business KPI.
measures.grain: one item within one inventory count (the system-vs-physical rollup for that item/count pair)

measures.label: calc qoh
measures.description: Exploratory aggregation of What the system believed the business should have in stock — the 'book' side of the variance. Frozen at the moment the last count entry landed for this item, so stock that moved between counting and reading this number is not reflected. Can be negative if the item was already oversold. The aggregation is constrained by the documented source grain and is not a certified business KPI.
measures.grain: one item within one inventory count (the system-vs-physical rollup for that item/count pair)

measures.label: counted qoh
measures.description: Exploratory aggregation of The physical amount counted — the sum of every ls_inventory_count_items.qty entry for this item in this count. The 'physical' side of the variance. Zero here means counted-and-found-none only if a count entry exists; an item never scanned may still show 0. The aggregation is constrained by the documented source grain and is not a certified business KPI.
measures.grain: one item within one inventory count (the system-vs-physical rollup for that item/count pair)

measures.label: inventory count items rows
measures.description: Count of source rows at the documented grain: one physical counting act — one item counted once by one employee at one moment (counting the same item three times creates three rows). This is a discoverability measure, not a business KPI.
measures.grain: one physical counting act — one item counted once by one employee at one moment (counting the same item three times creates three rows)

measures.label: qty
measures.description: Exploratory aggregation of The quantity found in this one counting act. An absolute observation of what was on the shelf at that spot, NOT a change — it must never enter a stock-movement sum. Multiple entries for one item accumulate to ls_inventory_count_calcs.counted_qoh. The aggregation is constrained by the documented source grain and is not a certified business KPI.
measures.grain: one physical counting act — one item counted once by one employee at one moment (counting the same item three times creates three rows)

measures.label: inventory count reconciles rows
measures.description: Count of source rows at the documented grain: one reconcile posting — one item's stock and cost adjustment applied when a count was reconciled. This is a discoverability measure, not a business KPI.
measures.grain: one reconcile posting — one item's stock and cost adjustment applied when a count was reconciled

measures.label: cost change
measures.description: Exploratory aggregation of The cost VALUE of the adjustment: the amount lost (negative) or gained (positive) to the books for this item, ex tax, in store currency. Unlike InventoryLog.costChange — same field name, different object — this really is a delta and really is summable. It is a total for the adjustment, not a unit cost. The aggregation is constrained by the documented source grain and is not a certified business KPI.
measures.grain: one reconcile posting — one item's stock and cost adjustment applied when a count was reconciled

measures.label: qoh change
measures.description: Exploratory aggregation of The stock-level change applied by the reconcile: negative means the count found FEWER units than the books claimed (shrinkage written off), positive means it found more (stock found). A genuine, summable delta. The aggregation is constrained by the documented source grain and is not a certified business KPI.
measures.grain: one reconcile posting — one item's stock and cost adjustment applied when a count was reconciled

measures.label: transfers rows
measures.description: Count of source rows at the documented grain: one inter-shop transfer document (header), with its origin-side and destination-side records flattened in. This is a discoverability measure, not a business KPI.
measures.grain: one inter-shop transfer document (header), with its origin-side and destination-side records flattened in

measures.label: transfer items rows
measures.description: Count of source rows at the documented grain: one line on one transfer — one item on one inter-shop transfer document. This is a discoverability measure, not a business KPI.
measures.grain: one line on one transfer — one item on one inter-shop transfer document

measures.label: to send
measures.description: Exploratory aggregation of The quantity the origin shop INTENDS to send — the picking instruction. Aspirational: to_send > sent on a dispatched transfer means the picker could not find them all. The aggregation is constrained by the documented source grain and is not a certified business KPI.
measures.grain: one line on one transfer — one item on one inter-shop transfer document

measures.label: to receive
measures.description: Exploratory aggregation of The quantity the receiving shop has counted as received during check-in. The destination's claim, which is what you compare against sent to catch a discrepancy before it is posted. The aggregation is constrained by the documented source grain and is not a certified business KPI.
measures.grain: one line on one transfer — one item on one inter-shop transfer document

measures.label: sent
measures.description: Exploratory aggregation of The actual number dispatched from the origin shop. A QUANTITY — not the boolean ls_transfers.is_sent. Documented: sent - received is the number still in transit. The aggregation is constrained by the documented source grain and is not a certified business KPI.
measures.grain: one line on one transfer — one item on one inter-shop transfer document

measures.label: received
measures.description: Exploratory aggregation of The actual number that landed at the destination. sent - received > 0 on an old, supposedly-complete transfer is stock that left one shop and never arrived: the classic in-transit shrinkage signal. The aggregation is constrained by the documented source grain and is not a certified business KPI.
measures.grain: one line on one transfer — one item on one inter-shop transfer document

measures.label: sent value
measures.description: Exploratory aggregation of TOTAL inventory cost value of the quantity sent, ex tax, in store currency — not a unit cost. Implied unit cost = sent_value / NULLIF(sent, 0). This is the cost basis leaving the origin shop's balance sheet. The aggregation is constrained by the documented source grain and is not a certified business KPI.
measures.grain: one line on one transfer — one item on one inter-shop transfer document

measures.label: received value
measures.description: Exploratory aggregation of TOTAL inventory cost value of the quantity received, ex tax. Diverges from sent_value when quantities differ or the cost basis moved in transit; sent_value - received_value on a closed transfer is the dollar value of the loss. The aggregation is constrained by the documented source grain and is not a certified business KPI.
measures.grain: one line on one transfer — one item on one inter-shop transfer document

measures.label: special orders rows
measures.description: Count of source rows at the documented grain: one special order — one item a named customer asked the shop to bring in, tracked from the sale line it was raised on to the purchase order line or transfer that fulfils it. This is a discoverability measure, not a business KPI.
measures.grain: one special order — one item a named customer asked the shop to bring in, tracked from the sale line it was raised on to the purchase order line or transfer that fulfils it

measures.label: unit quantity
measures.description: Exploratory aggregation of How many units the customer asked the shop to bring in. Current requested quantity, restated when staff edit the order — this is customer DEMAND, not units sold. What was actually sold lives on the linked sale line. The aggregation is constrained by the documented source grain and is not a certified business KPI.
measures.grain: one special order — one item a named customer asked the shop to bring in, tracked from the sale line it was raised on to the purchase order line or transfer that fulfils it

measures.label: transfer from rows
measures.description: Count of source rows at the documented grain: one origin record for one stock transfer. This is a discoverability measure, not a business KPI.
measures.grain: one origin record for one stock transfer

measures.label: transfer to rows
measures.description: Count of source rows at the documented grain: one destination record for one stock transfer. This is a discoverability measure, not a business KPI.
measures.grain: one destination record for one stock transfer

measures.label: purchase orders rows
measures.description: Count of source rows at the documented grain: one purchase order raised with one vendor for one shop (Lightspeed resource `Order`). This is a discoverability measure, not a business KPI.
measures.grain: one purchase order raised with one vendor for one shop (Lightspeed resource `Order`)

measures.label: ship cost
measures.description: Exploratory aggregation of Freight the vendor added to the order, in the MERCHANT's default currency. Order-level: whether it is spread down to the lines depends on shipping_cost_method. Part of landed cost, not of goods cost. The aggregation is constrained by the documented source grain and is not a certified business KPI.
measures.grain: one purchase order raised with one vendor for one shop (Lightspeed resource `Order`)

measures.label: ship cost vendor currency
measures.description: Exploratory aggregation of The same freight expressed in the VENDOR's currency. Equals ship_cost for domestic suppliers; for import POs the pair differs by vendor_currency_rate. Adding it to ship_cost mixes currencies and doubles the freight. The aggregation is constrained by the documented source grain and is not a certified business KPI.
measures.grain: one purchase order raised with one vendor for one shop (Lightspeed resource `Order`)

measures.label: other cost
measures.description: Exploratory aggregation of Other vendor-added costs (handling, surcharges, duty recharges) in merchant currency. CAN BE NEGATIVE, in which case it is a discount — so it must be added, never ABS()'d or summed as a cost-only bucket. The aggregation is constrained by the documented source grain and is not a certified business KPI.
measures.grain: one purchase order raised with one vendor for one shop (Lightspeed resource `Order`)

measures.label: other cost vendor currency
measures.description: Exploratory aggregation of Other vendor-added costs in the vendor's currency; same negative-means-discount convention as other_cost. The vendor-currency twin, not an additional charge. The aggregation is constrained by the documented source grain and is not a certified business KPI.
measures.grain: one purchase order raised with one vendor for one shop (Lightspeed resource `Order`)

measures.label: total discount
measures.description: Exploratory aggregation of Total MONEY value of all discounts on the order, merchant currency — the realised sum, whichever discount family produced it. It is a rollup, so adding it to the per-line discount_money_value allocations double counts the same money. The aggregation is constrained by the documented source grain and is not a certified business KPI.
measures.grain: one purchase order raised with one vendor for one shop (Lightspeed resource `Order`)

measures.label: total quantity
measures.description: Exploratory aggregation of Total units ORDERED across all lines — a header rollup of ls_purchase_order_lines.quantity, and never units received. Summing this alongside line quantities in the same query double counts. The aggregation is constrained by the documented source grain and is not a certified business KPI.
measures.grain: one purchase order raised with one vendor for one shop (Lightspeed resource `Order`)

measures.label: vendor currency rate
measures.description: Exploratory aggregation of Exchange rate captured on the PO, defaulting to the vendor's rate: multiply vendor-currency amounts by this to reach merchant currency. VERIFIED LIVE: domestic suppliers show 0 or 1 — a 0 here means 'not applicable', NOT a zero-valued currency, so guard every division and never revalue an old PO at today's rate. The aggregation is constrained by the documented source grain and is not a certified business KPI.
measures.grain: one purchase order raised with one vendor for one shop (Lightspeed resource `Order`)

measures.label: discount money value
measures.description: Exploratory aggregation of The order-level discount expressed as MONEY in the merchant's currency. Populated regardless of how it was entered (Lightspeed resolves a percentage into money here), so this is the field to sum for 'discount received from suppliers'. Do not also subtract discount_percent_value. The aggregation is constrained by the documented source grain and is not a certified business KPI.
measures.grain: one purchase order raised with one vendor for one shop (Lightspeed resource `Order`)

measures.label: discount money vendor value
measures.description: Exploratory aggregation of The same order-level discount in the VENDOR's currency. The twin of discount_money_value, not an extra discount; summing both double counts across two currencies. The aggregation is constrained by the documented source grain and is not a certified business KPI.
measures.grain: one purchase order raised with one vendor for one shop (Lightspeed resource `Order`)

measures.label: discount percent value
measures.description: Exploratory aggregation of Order-level discount percentage in whole-percent units (5 = 5%, not 0.05). Applies to the goods cost of the lines, not to freight or other costs. The aggregation is constrained by the documented source grain and is not a certified business KPI.
measures.grain: one purchase order raised with one vendor for one shop (Lightspeed resource `Order`)

measures.label: purchase order lines rows
measures.description: Count of source rows at the documented grain: one product line on one purchase order (one row per OrderLine). This is a discoverability measure, not a business KPI.
measures.grain: one product line on one purchase order (one row per OrderLine)

measures.label: quantity
measures.description: Exploratory aggregation of Units ORDERED on this line. Not units received and not units still to come: outstanding = quantity - qty_checked_in - qty_received_not_checked_in. Editing a PO changes this in place, so it is the current ask, not the original ask. The aggregation is constrained by the documented source grain and is not a certified business KPI.
measures.grain: one product line on one purchase order (one row per OrderLine)

measures.label: unit cost
measures.description: Exploratory aggregation of Unit COST in the merchant's default currency, ALREADY adjusted for any order-level discount. Despite the API name 'price' this is what we pay the supplier, never what the customer pays; pairing it with retail price from the products domain is how margin is computed, and confusing the two inverts margin entirely. The aggregation is constrained by the documented source grain and is not a certified business KPI.
measures.grain: one product line on one purchase order (one row per OrderLine)

measures.label: unit cost original
measures.description: Exploratory aggregation of Unit cost in merchant currency BEFORE any order-level discount. unit_cost_original - unit_cost is the per-unit discount the supplier gave. Using this as cost of goods overstates cost by the whole discount. The aggregation is constrained by the documented source grain and is not a certified business KPI.
measures.grain: one product line on one purchase order (one row per OrderLine)

measures.label: unit cost vendor currency
measures.description: Exploratory aggregation of Unit cost BEFORE order discount in the VENDOR's currency — the vendor-currency counterpart of unit_cost_original, and per the docs it should be used instead of, not alongside, that field. VERIFIED LIVE: 0 for domestic suppliers, where 0 means 'not applicable', not free. The aggregation is constrained by the documented source grain and is not a certified business KPI.
measures.grain: one product line on one purchase order (one row per OrderLine)

measures.label: qty checked in
measures.description: Exploratory aggregation of Units checked in, meaning ADDED TO INVENTORY — the stock is on the shelf and counted in quantity-on-hand. A cumulative running counter overwritten on every receipt, so it answers 'how many have landed in total', never 'how many landed in June'. The aggregation is constrained by the documented source grain and is not a certified business KPI.
measures.grain: one product line on one purchase order (one row per OrderLine)

measures.label: qty received not checked in
measures.description: Exploratory aggregation of Units received at the door but NOT yet added to inventory — physically present, invisible to stock-on-hand. Usually 0 on finished POs. Adding it to qty_checked_in gives units physically arrived; treating it as available stock overstates what staff can sell. The aggregation is constrained by the documented source grain and is not a certified business KPI.
measures.grain: one product line on one purchase order (one row per OrderLine)

measures.label: line total
measures.description: Exploratory aggregation of Documented as quantity x price, so it is the discounted goods cost of the line in merchant currency and EXCLUDES the allocated shipping_cost. Landed cost of the line = line_total + shipping_cost (the discount is already inside line_total via unit_cost). The aggregation is constrained by the documented source grain and is not a certified business KPI.
measures.grain: one product line on one purchase order (one row per OrderLine)

measures.label: shipping cost
measures.description: Exploratory aggregation of This line's share of the PO-level freight, calculated down from the header in merchant currency. Empty/zero when the order's shipping_cost_method is 'total' (freight stays at header level), which is the usual reason per-line landed cost looks too cheap. The aggregation is constrained by the documented source grain and is not a certified business KPI.
measures.grain: one product line on one purchase order (one row per OrderLine)

measures.label: shipping cost vendor currency
measures.description: Exploratory aggregation of The same allocated freight share expressed in the vendor's currency. A currency twin of shipping_cost, not an additional charge. The aggregation is constrained by the documented source grain and is not a certified business KPI.
measures.grain: one product line on one purchase order (one row per OrderLine)

measures.label: discount money value
measures.description: Exploratory aggregation of This line's share of the order-level discount as money in merchant currency. Already reflected in unit_cost and line_total, so subtracting it again from line_total double-discounts the line. The aggregation is constrained by the documented source grain and is not a certified business KPI.
measures.grain: one product line on one purchase order (one row per OrderLine)

measures.label: discount money vendor value
measures.description: Exploratory aggregation of This line's allocated discount share in the vendor's currency — the currency twin of discount_money_value, not a second discount. The aggregation is constrained by the documented source grain and is not a certified business KPI.
measures.grain: one product line on one purchase order (one row per OrderLine)

measures.label: order shipments rows
measures.description: Count of source rows at the documented grain: one shipment (receiving event) against one purchase order. This is a discoverability measure, not a business KPI.
measures.grain: one shipment (receiving event) against one purchase order

measures.label: total qty received
measures.description: Exploratory aggregation of Total units received in THIS delivery, summing its items. SUM over an order_id gives what has arrived so far on that PO; comparing that against ls_purchase_orders.total_quantity gives true fill rate. The aggregation is constrained by the documented source grain and is not a certified business KPI.
measures.grain: one shipment (receiving event) against one purchase order

measures.label: total vendor cost
measures.description: Exploratory aggregation of Total LANDED cost of everything in this shipment expressed in the VENDOR's currency — goods plus allocated freight, net of allocated discount. The vendor-currency twin of total_cost; adding both mixes currencies. The aggregation is constrained by the documented source grain and is not a certified business KPI.
measures.grain: one shipment (receiving event) against one purchase order

measures.label: total cost
measures.description: Exploratory aggregation of Total LANDED cost of this shipment in the merchant's default currency — goods plus allocated freight, net of allocated discount. This, not `cost`, is what the inventory was actually valued at on arrival; choosing `cost` instead moves gross margin by the entire freight bill. The aggregation is constrained by the documented source grain and is not a certified business KPI.
measures.grain: one shipment (receiving event) against one purchase order

measures.label: vendor currency rate
measures.description: Exploratory aggregation of Exchange rate from vendor currency to merchant currency CAPTURED AT SHIPMENT CREATION. Multiply vendor-currency amounts by it to reach merchant currency; it is frozen history, so revaluing an old receipt at today's rate is wrong. VERIFIED LIVE (on the Order twin of this field): domestic suppliers can carry 0 or 1, and 0 means 'not applicable' — guard against dividing by it. The aggregation is constrained by the documented source grain and is not a certified business KPI.
measures.grain: one shipment (receiving event) against one purchase order

measures.label: shipping cost vendor currency
measures.description: Exploratory aggregation of Freight allocated to THIS shipment, in the vendor's currency. The per-delivery share, not the PO's total freight — that is shipping_cost_order_full_vendor_value. The aggregation is constrained by the documented source grain and is not a certified business KPI.
measures.grain: one shipment (receiving event) against one purchase order

measures.label: shipping cost
measures.description: Exploratory aggregation of Freight allocated to THIS shipment, in merchant currency, and already included inside total_cost. This is the column to SUM for freight spend by period; summing the *_order_full_* columns instead multiplies the bill by the number of deliveries. The aggregation is constrained by the documented source grain and is not a certified business KPI.
measures.grain: one shipment (receiving event) against one purchase order

measures.label: shipping cost order full value
measures.description: Exploratory aggregation of The FULL freight applied to the whole purchase order, in merchant currency, repeated on every shipment row of that order as context. It is not this delivery's share — SUM()ing it across shipments multiplies the PO's freight by the number of deliveries. The biggest double-count trap in this domain. The aggregation is constrained by the documented source grain and is not a certified business KPI.
measures.grain: one shipment (receiving event) against one purchase order

measures.label: shipping cost order full vendor value
measures.description: Exploratory aggregation of The full whole-PO freight in the vendor's currency, repeated on every shipment row. Same double-count hazard as shipping_cost_order_full_value, in the other currency. The aggregation is constrained by the documented source grain and is not a certified business KPI.
measures.grain: one shipment (receiving event) against one purchase order

measures.label: discount money vendor value
measures.description: Exploratory aggregation of Discount allocated to THIS shipment in the vendor's currency. Already netted off total_vendor_cost. The aggregation is constrained by the documented source grain and is not a certified business KPI.
measures.grain: one shipment (receiving event) against one purchase order

measures.label: discount money value
measures.description: Exploratory aggregation of Discount allocated to THIS shipment in merchant currency, already netted off total_cost. Subtracting it from total_cost double-discounts the delivery. The aggregation is constrained by the documented source grain and is not a certified business KPI.
measures.grain: one shipment (receiving event) against one purchase order

measures.label: discount order full money value
measures.description: Exploratory aggregation of The FULL discount applied to the whole purchase order in merchant currency, repeated on every shipment row as context. Not this delivery's share; SUM()ing it across shipments inflates supplier discounts by the number of deliveries. The aggregation is constrained by the documented source grain and is not a certified business KPI.
measures.grain: one shipment (receiving event) against one purchase order

measures.label: discount order full money vendor value
measures.description: Exploratory aggregation of The full whole-PO discount in the vendor's currency, repeated on every shipment row. Same double-count hazard, other currency. The aggregation is constrained by the documented source grain and is not a certified business KPI.
measures.grain: one shipment (receiving event) against one purchase order

measures.label: cost
measures.description: Exploratory aggregation of Goods cost of the items in this shipment BEFORE freight and discount, merchant currency. The pre-landed figure: total_cost - cost is roughly the net freight/discount effect. Reporting `cost` as cost of goods received omits freight entirely. The aggregation is constrained by the documented source grain and is not a certified business KPI.
measures.grain: one shipment (receiving event) against one purchase order

measures.label: vendor cost
measures.description: Exploratory aggregation of Goods cost of the items in this shipment before freight and discount, in the VENDOR's currency. Note the name collision: on ls_purchase_order_lines `vendorCost` is a UNIT cost, here it is a shipment total. The aggregation is constrained by the documented source grain and is not a certified business KPI.
measures.grain: one shipment (receiving event) against one purchase order

measures.label: order shipment items rows
measures.description: Count of source rows at the documented grain: one product's receipt within one shipment (one row per ShipmentItem). This is a discoverability measure, not a business KPI.
measures.grain: one product's receipt within one shipment (one row per ShipmentItem)

measures.label: qty received
measures.description: Exploratory aggregation of Units of this item received in THIS delivery — a per-delivery event quantity, safe to sum over time, unlike the running counters on ls_purchase_order_lines. The denominator for landed unit cost. The aggregation is constrained by the documented source grain and is not a certified business KPI.
measures.grain: one product's receipt within one shipment (one row per ShipmentItem)

measures.label: vendor cost
measures.description: Exploratory aggregation of Item cost in the VENDOR's currency before freight and discount. The docs say only 'item cost' and do not state whether it is per unit or extended for qty_received — verify against total_vendor_cost / qty_received on live data before treating it as a unit cost. Note the collision: the same API name on OrderLine is definitively a unit cost. The aggregation is constrained by the documented source grain and is not a certified business KPI.
measures.grain: one product's receipt within one shipment (one row per ShipmentItem)

measures.label: cost
measures.description: Exploratory aggregation of Item cost in the merchant's default currency before freight and discount. Same documented ambiguity as vendor_cost about per-unit vs extended; resolve it empirically against total_cost before publishing any unit-cost figure. The aggregation is constrained by the documented source grain and is not a certified business KPI.
measures.grain: one product's receipt within one shipment (one row per ShipmentItem)

measures.label: total vendor cost
measures.description: Exploratory aggregation of Total LANDED cost of this item within this shipment, in the vendor's currency — goods plus allocated freight, net of allocated discount. Vendor-currency twin of total_cost, not an additional amount. The aggregation is constrained by the documented source grain and is not a certified business KPI.
measures.grain: one product's receipt within one shipment (one row per ShipmentItem)

measures.label: total cost
measures.description: Exploratory aggregation of Total LANDED cost of this item within this shipment in merchant currency — the true inventory value added by this receipt, and the numerator for real landed unit cost (total_cost / qty_received). Summing this across a shipment reproduces the shipment header's total_cost, so never add the two. The aggregation is constrained by the documented source grain and is not a certified business KPI.
measures.grain: one product's receipt within one shipment (one row per ShipmentItem)

measures.label: shipping cost
measures.description: Exploratory aggregation of Freight allocated to this item in merchant currency, already included in total_cost. Zero when the parent shipment's shipping_cost_method is 'total' — the freight then exists only at shipment level. The aggregation is constrained by the documented source grain and is not a certified business KPI.
measures.grain: one product's receipt within one shipment (one row per ShipmentItem)

measures.label: shipping cost vendor currency
measures.description: Exploratory aggregation of Freight allocated to this item in the vendor's currency; the currency twin of shipping_cost, not an extra charge. The aggregation is constrained by the documented source grain and is not a certified business KPI.
measures.grain: one product's receipt within one shipment (one row per ShipmentItem)

measures.label: discount money value
measures.description: Exploratory aggregation of Discount allocated to this item in merchant currency, already netted off total_cost. Subtracting it again double-discounts the receipt. The aggregation is constrained by the documented source grain and is not a certified business KPI.
measures.grain: one product's receipt within one shipment (one row per ShipmentItem)

measures.label: discount money vendor value
measures.description: Exploratory aggregation of Discount allocated to this item in the vendor's currency — currency twin of discount_money_value. The aggregation is constrained by the documented source grain and is not a certified business KPI.
measures.grain: one product's receipt within one shipment (one row per ShipmentItem)

measures.label: vendor currency rate
measures.description: Exploratory aggregation of Exchange rate from vendor to merchant currency captured AT SHIPMENT CREATION — historic and frozen, so re-converting old receipts at a current rate is wrong. Can be 0 or 1 for domestic suppliers, where 0 means 'not applicable' rather than a real rate. The aggregation is constrained by the documented source grain and is not a certified business KPI.
measures.grain: one product's receipt within one shipment (one row per ShipmentItem)

measures.label: vendors rows
measures.description: Count of source rows at the documented grain: one supplier the account buys from. This is a discoverability measure, not a business KPI.
measures.grain: one supplier the account buys from

measures.label: purchasing currency rate
measures.description: Exploratory aggregation of The vendor's CURRENT default exchange rate, used to seed new purchase orders. It is a live default, not history: the rate that priced any given PO is ls_purchase_orders.vendor_currency_rate, captured at order time. Restating past spend with this rate silently rewrites history. The aggregation is constrained by the documented source grain and is not a certified business KPI.
measures.grain: one supplier the account buys from

measures.label: vendor returns rows
measures.description: Count of source rows at the documented grain: one vendor return document raised at one shop for one vendor. This is a discoverability measure, not a business KPI.
measures.grain: one vendor return document raised at one shop for one vendor

measures.label: ship cost
measures.description: Exploratory aggregation of Shipping cost incurred on the return, in the shop's currency. A cost to us that reduces the net benefit of the return; per the total field's definition it is an adjustment already reflected in total, so do not add it again. The aggregation is constrained by the documented source grain and is not a certified business KPI.
measures.grain: one vendor return document raised at one shop for one vendor

measures.label: other cost
measures.description: Exploratory aggregation of Other costs on the return (restocking fees, handling). Treated as an adjustment inside total; by analogy with the Order object a negative value would be a credit rather than a charge. The aggregation is constrained by the documented source grain and is not a certified business KPI.
measures.grain: one vendor return document raised at one shop for one vendor

measures.label: subtotal
measures.description: Exploratory aggregation of Cost value of the goods being returned, before ship_cost/other_cost adjustments. This is inventory COST leaving the building, never retail value and never a customer refund. The aggregation is constrained by the documented source grain and is not a certified business KPI.

measures.description: Exploratory aggregation of Number of decimal places the currency is stored/displayed to. Load-bearing for rounding: rounding to a fixed 2 decimals is wrong for zero-decimal currencies (JPY) and for three-decimal ones (KWD, BHD), producing totals that drift from the POS by a cent per line. Documented as a float even though it is conceptually an integer count. The aggregation is constrained by the documented source grain and is not a certified business KPI.

measures.description: Exploratory aggregation of Smallest unit of currency actually used in CASH transactions -- e.g. 0.05 where 1c and 2c coins were withdrawn (AU, CA, NZ). Load-bearing and routinely missed: cash-tendered totals are rounded to this increment while card totals are not, so cash-vs-card reconciliation shows a systematic few-cent gap that is correct behaviour, not an error. Distinct from currency_precision, which governs storage. The aggregation is constrained by the documented source grain and is not a certified business KPI.
measures.grain: one row per locale Lightspeed publishes globally (a global catalogue, not the account's own setting)

measures.label: calculated
measures.description: Exploratory aggregation of The 'should have' side: what the system computed the drawer holds for this tender, built from payments taken on it during the session PLUS the signed register adds/payouts (including the opening float, which arrives as a positive RegisterWithdraw). Documented as float; store as numeric so cent-level variance sums do not drift. Never add ls_register_withdraws.amount on top of this — it is already included. measures.label: actual
measures.description: Exploratory aggregation of The physical amount a human counted for this tender at close. Zero is AMBIGUOUS: it means either a genuinely empty drawer or — far more often on card and gift-card tenders — that nobody bothered to count it. There is no documented 'was counted' flag, so 0 must be treated as unknown for non-cash tenders. Documented as float; store as numeric. The aggregation is constrained by the documented source grain and is not a certified business KPI.
measures.grain: one payment type's expected-versus-counted pair inside one register close-out

measures.label: register withdraws rows
measures.description: Count of source rows at the documented grain: one cash add or payout at one register (a single signed drawer movement outside of sales). This is a discoverability measure, not a business KPI.
measures.grain: one cash add or payout at one register (a single signed drawer movement outside of sales)

measures.label: amount
measures.description: Exploratory aggregation of SIGNED drawer movement. POSITIVE = money INTO the drawer (opening float, change top-up); NEGATIVE = money OUT (payout, safe drop). Documented as float; store as numeric. Because it is signed, a naive SUM(amount) NETS floats against payouts and lands near zero — that number answers no real question. The aggregation is constrained by the documented source grain and is not a certified business KPI.
measures.grain: one cash add or payout at one register (a single signed drawer movement outside of sales)

measures.label: register calculated rows
measures.description: Count of source rows at the documented grain: one payment type's live running total for one register's CURRENTLY OPEN session, as at the instant the endpoint was called. This is a discoverability measure, not a business KPI.
measures.grain: one payment type's live running total for one register's CURRENTLY OPEN session, as at the instant the endpoint was called

measures.label: payment total
measures.description: Exploratory aggregation of Running total of PAYMENTS taken on this tender since the register was opened — the sales-driven component of the expected drawer. Type is undocumented (example payload only); treat as a money value and stage as numeric. Expected to be positive for takings. The aggregation is constrained by the documented source grain and is not a certified business KPI.
measures.grain: one payment type's live running total for one register's CURRENTLY OPEN session, as at the instant the endpoint was called

measures.label: add total
measures.description: Exploratory aggregation of Running total of the POSITIVE register-withdraw rows since open: the opening float plus any change top-ups. Corresponds to SUM(amount) WHERE amount > 0 on ls_register_withdraws for the same session. Type undocumented (example payload only); expect a positive number. Named add_total rather than 'add' because ADD is a SQL keyword. The aggregation is constrained by the documented source grain and is not a certified business KPI.
measures.grain: one payment type's live running total for one register's CURRENTLY OPEN session, as at the instant the endpoint was called

measures.label: withdraw total
measures.description: Exploratory aggregation of Running total of the NEGATIVE register-withdraw rows since open: payouts and safe drops. The SIGN IS UNDOCUMENTED — the example payload publishes no worked figure, so it is unknown whether this arrives already-negative (matching RegisterWithdraw.amount) or as a positive magnitude. Probe a live account before adding or subtracting it. Named withdraw_total to pair with add_total. The aggregation is constrained by the documented source grain and is not a certified business KPI.
measures.grain: one payment type's live running total for one register's CURRENTLY OPEN session, as at the instant the endpoint was called

measures.label: tax categories rows
measures.description: Count of source rows at the documented grain: one sales-tax configuration (TaxCategory, labelled "Sales Tax" in the Lightspeed UI) on the account. This is a discoverability measure, not a business KPI.
measures.grain: one sales-tax configuration (TaxCategory, labelled "Sales Tax" in the Lightspeed UI) on the account

measures.label: tax1 rate
measures.description: Exploratory aggregation of First component rate as a FRACTION OF 1, not a percentage: 0.1 means 10%. Multiply by 100 before displaying. This is the category DEFAULT - it is not necessarily the rate applied to any given sale line, because ls_tax_category_classes may override it for that line's tax class. In most single-tax jurisdictions this is the only rate used. The aggregation is constrained by the documented source grain and is not a certified business KPI.
measures.grain: one sales-tax configuration (TaxCategory, labelled "Sales Tax" in the Lightspeed UI) on the account

measures.label: tax2 rate
measures.description: Exploratory aggregation of Second component rate, also a fraction of 1; 0 on single-tax accounts. The headline rate equals tax1_rate + tax2_rate only where the jurisdiction stacks the two additively. Jurisdictions that compound tax2 on top of tax1 cannot be expressed by this model, and jurisdictions with three or more components cannot be expressed at all. The aggregation is constrained by the documented source grain and is not a certified business KPI.
measures.grain: one sales-tax configuration (TaxCategory, labelled "Sales Tax" in the Lightspeed UI) on the account

It REPLACES ls_tax_categories.tax1_rate for lines in this class - it is not an increment and must never be added to the default. 0 here means genuinely zero-rated, which is materially different from the row being absent. The aggregation is constrained by the documented source grain and is not a certified business KPI.

measures.label: tax2 rate override

measures.grain: one per-tax-class rate override inside one tax category

measures.label: amount
measures.description: Exploratory aggregation of Total money taken under this payment type on this day at this shop (the docs call it the subtotal for the payment type). This is takings, not revenue: gift-card loads, layaway deposits and on-account settlements all land here on the day cash moved. The docs do not state the sign convention for refunded tenders, so do not assume every value is positive. measures.label: tax amount
measures.description: Exploratory aggregation of Total tax collected for this category on this day at this shop. It is a COMBINED figure: even though a category can define two component rates (tax1/tax2), this report does not split them, so GST-plus-PST jurisdictions cannot separate the components here. This figure will not equal subtotal x tax1_rate because per-class overrides, exempt lines and per-line rounding all intervene - trust this number over any recomputation. The aggregation is constrained by the documented source grain and is not a certified business KPI.
